ct:SB 444.summary: Lets municipal employees serve on their town's board of finance if any stipend they receive is under $10,000 in a rolling 12-month period.

ct:SB 449.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE INTERGOVERNMENTAL POLICY AND PLANNING DIVISION WITHIN THE OFFICE OF POLICY AND MANAGEMENT.
ct:SB 449.summary: Requires OPM to identify state property qualifying as PA 490 land so towns classify and value it that way, ends a child care zoning certification, repeals the Intertown equipment incentive program, and delays school repair grant notices to April 1.

ct:SB 452.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE RELEASE OF LIGHTER-THAN-AIR BALLOONS.
ct:SB 452.summary: Bans knowingly releasing helium or other lighter-than-air balloons into the atmosphere, replacing the nine-balloon allowance, and from 2027 requires retailers to attach weights to balloons they sell, with a $20 civil penalty per violation.

ct:SB 457.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE STATE'S BOTTLE BILL.
ct:SB 457.summary: Sets misdemeanor or felony penalties, by volume from 5,000 containers, for willfully collecting refunds on containers not bought in Connecticut, and ends reduced redemption-center handling fees by July 1, 2027 or once scanning technology is used.

ct:SB 458.title: AN ACT DESIGNATING VARIOUS DAYS AND MONTHS.
ct:SB 458.summary: Requires the governor to proclaim days and months including Hartford Whalers Day (January 11), Good Neighbor Day (September 28), Ovarian Cancer Awareness Month (September) and Military Suicide Remembrance and Awareness Day (September 30).

ct:SB 470.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE LEGISLATIVE COMMISSIONERS' RECOMMENDATIONS FOR TECHNICAL AND MINOR REVISIONS TO THE GOVERNMENT ADMINISTRATION STATUTES.
ct:SB 470.summary: Allows certain contracts of state higher-education units made or amended after passage, rather than after July 1, 2026, to include either the state nondiscrimination contract text or a nondiscrimination affirmation, and makes technical changes to government administration statutes.

ct:SB 472.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE ELECTRONIC SURVEILLANCE OF EMPLOYEES.
ct:SB 472.summary: Requires employers that electronically monitor employees to name the specific monitored locations in their notice and post it there, with exceptions for security reasons and airports, and to give new hires a plain-language statement on monitoring permitted without notice.

ct:SB 473.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE REVISOR'S TECHNICAL REVISIONS TO THE GENERAL STATUTES.
ct:SB 473.summary: Corrects statutory references and makes other technical changes throughout the general statutes.

ct:SB 477.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE FAILURE TO FILE FOR CERTAIN GRAND LIST EXEMPTIONS, A MUNICIPAL OPTION TO ABATE DELINQUENT PROPERTY TAXES ON CERTAIN PARCELS OF LAND, ALLOCATIONS OF CERTAIN STATE FUNDS AND ITEMS IMPLEMENTING THE STATE BUDGET FOR THE BIENNIUM ENDING JUNE 30, 2027.
ct:SB 477.summary: Lets taxpayers in certain towns claim property tax exemptions despite missed filing deadlines, lets towns abate delinquent taxes on qualifying land on the 2013 and 2014 grand lists, raises judges' pay about 4.4% in FY 27, and revises many other budget-bill provisions.

ct:SB 478.title: AN ACT CONCERNING CONSUMER SAFEGUARDS FOR LONG-TERM CARE POLICIES.
ct:SB 478.summary: Requires long-term care insurers and the Insurance Department to report annually on policy losses, and lets the insurance commissioner investigate and discipline insurers that violate long-term care insurance laws.

ct:SB 483.title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE CRIME OF DIGITAL DEFRAUDING.
ct:SB 483.summary: Makes it larceny to make and share a digitally forged image, video or audio recording of a person, without their consent, with intent to financially injure someone. Allows a defense if the defendant took reasonable steps to disclose the forgery. Effective October 1, 2026.

ct:SB 484.title: AN ACT CONCERNING DISTRACTED DRIVING AND THE SAFE OPERATION OF A MOTOR VEHICLE IN A HIGHWAY WORK ZONE.
ct:SB 484.summary: Makes driving in a highway work zone while doing anything the distracted driving law prohibits a per se reckless driving violation, a criminal offense, and bars prosecuting the same act as both reckless and distracted driving.

ct:SB 488.title: AN ACT IMPLEMENTING THE TREASURER'S RECOMMENDATIONS FOR REVISIONS TO THE UNCLAIMED PROPERTY PROGRAM AND SECOND INJURY FUND.
ct:SB 488.summary: Changes unclaimed property laws, including ways to show interest in property, early transfers to the treasurer and ending required automatic returns of property under $50, and limits the Second Injury Fund's liability for reimbursing employers and insurers.

ct:SB 5.title: AN ACT CONCERNING ONLINE SAFETY.
ct:SB 5.summary: Bars AI subscription providers from signing or renewing without written disclosure of key terms, restricts AI companions for minors, requires notices and self-harm detection, adds whistleblower rules for frontier AI developers, regulates automated employment decisions, and creates a Connecticut AI Academy.

ct:SB 508.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE SUSPENSION OF AN OPERATOR'S LICENSE FOR REPEATEDLY FAILING TO STOP FOR A SCHOOL BUS.
ct:SB 508.summary: Requires the motor vehicles commissioner to suspend a driver's license for six months, without a hearing, after a third or subsequent violation of the law on stopping for a school bus.

ct:SB 509.title: AN ACT CONCERNING ADDRESS VERIFICATION REFORMS FOR REGISTRANTS.
ct:SB 509.summary: As amended, creates an affirmative defense to sex offender registration violations if circumstances beyond the person's control, which they did not cause, prevented compliance and they comply within 20 business days; requires registrants to submit proof of residency to the emergency services and public protection department 75 to 90 days after registering.

ct:SB 518.title: AN ACT AMENDING A CONVEYANCE OF A PARCEL OF STATE LAND IN THE CITY OF MIDDLETOWN.
ct:SB 518.summary: Changes the reversion condition on a ten-acre Middletown parcel conveyed to Shiloh Baptist Community Development Corporation: the land reverts to the state unless construction starts or a financing loan is signed by June 30, 2029, rather than unless it is used by then.

ct:SB 519.title: AN ACT AMENDING A PRIOR CONVEYANCE OF STATE LAND TO THE BRIDGEPORT PORT AUTHORITY.
ct:SB 519.summary: Amends a prior act conveying about 1.008 acres of state land in Bridgeport to the Bridgeport Port Authority, setting the price of any sale or lease at $119,000 instead of appraised value.

ct:SB 520.title: AN ACT REPEALING A CONVEYANCE OF A PARCEL OF STATE LAND TO THE TOWN OF CANTON.
ct:SB 520.summary: Repeals Special Act 24-20, a prior act conveying a parcel of state land to the town of Canton.

ct:SB 521.title: AN ACT CONVEYING A PARCEL OF STATE LAND TO THE NORTHWEST RESOURCE RECOVERY AUTHORITY.
ct:SB 521.summary: Directs the Administrative Services commissioner to convey a roughly four-acre Torrington parcel with the Torrington Transfer Station to the Northwest Resource Recovery Authority for administrative costs. The authority must use it as a public transfer station or it reverts to the state.

ct:SB 87.title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A NONPROFIT PROVIDER ADVISORY BOARD AND PROHIBITING AUTO INSURANCE PENALTIES ON VOLUNTEER DRIVERS PROVIDING TRANSPORTATION TO NONPROFIT ORGANIZATIONS.
ct:SB 87.summary: Creates a 23-member Nonprofit Provider Advisory Board within the Office of Policy and Management and bars auto insurers from refusing to renew or raising rates solely because a driver is an unpaid volunteer driver for nonprofits.

ct:SB 89.title: AN ACT UPDATING PRISON RAPE ELIMINATION STANDARDS.
ct:SB 89.summary: Requires state agencies and local governments that hold offenders to comply with the federal Prison Rape Elimination Act as of January 1, 2024, adds duty-to-intervene and sexual assault crisis-service standards, and requires sexual assault reports be copied to the Correction Ombuds.

ct:SB 9.title: AN ACT SUPPORTING COMMUTERS AND MICROTRANSIT SERVICES AND CONCERNING PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION.
ct:SB 9.summary: Allows employers tax credits for commuting benefits, extends the DOT microtransit pilot from two to three years, sets aside $4 million for Shore Line East and $3 million for added service, and creates free bus passes for students and veterans.

ct:SB 90.title: AN ACT REVISING AND CONSOLIDATING THE HATE CRIMES STATUTES.
ct:SB 90.summary: Combines Connecticut's bias-crime laws into one protected-category framework, labels bias-motivated offenses as hate crimes, extends persistent-offender status to them, and allows hate-crimes diversion programs for offenders.

dc:B 26-0016.title: Strategic Parking Enforcement Enhancement Act of 2025
dc:B 26-0016.summary: As amended by substitute, creates a Department of Public Works reimbursable detail program assigning overtime parking enforcement officers to businesses, nonprofits, universities, business improvement districts and others under written agreements, and lets campus police who opt in and certify training issue parking citations in set areas around their campuses.

dc:B 26-0047.title: Funeral Directors Licensing Reform Amendment Act of 2025
dc:B 26-0047.summary: Changes funeral director licensing requirements, creates a separate embalmer's license, revises apprenticeship and supervision rules, and updates the Board of Funeral Directors' composition. Existing licensed funeral directors automatically receive an embalmer's license.

dc:B 26-0174.title: Enhancing Consumer Protection Procedures Amendment Act of 2025
dc:B 26-0174.summary: Expands D.C. consumer protection enforcement, including fines and fees for not complying with investigative subpoenas, asset freezes, treating failure to post prices as an unfair trade practice, bans on retaliation for complaints, and added authority for the Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection.

dc:B 26-0181.title: Short-Term Disability Insurance Benefit Protection Clarification Amendment Act of 2025
dc:B 26-0181.summary: Clarifies that the existing ban on insurers reducing short-term disability benefits because of District paid leave benefits applies regardless of where the policy was issued, and makes the ban enforceable under District insurance law.

dc:B 26-0243.title: Automatic Enrollment for Utility Affordability Programs Act of 2025
dc:B 26-0243.summary: As drafted in the committee print, requires the Department of Energy and Environment to implement, within one year of the act's applicability date, a process to automatically identify households eligible for utility affordability programs; utilities then confirm eligibility and enroll them.

dc:B 26-0244.title: Micromobility Fire Safety Standards Act of 2025
dc:B 26-0244.summary: Amends the micromobility fire safety bill to name Global Accreditation Cooperation as the accrediting body, correct a battery standard citation, let any certification body test products, and give shared-fleet operators six months for alternate e-bike testing.

dc:B 26-0245.title: Personal Delivery Device Weight Limit Amendment Act of 2025
dc:B 26-0245.summary: Raises the weight limit for personal delivery devices to 275 pounds, excluding cargo, or a higher limit set by the Department of Transportation through rulemaking, and repeals the earlier temporary weight-limit act.

dc:B 26-0285.title: Climatizing Our Overheated Living Spaces Regulation Amendment Act of 2025
dc:B 26-0285.summary: Moves the applicability date of the D.C. rental heating and cooling bill from May 1 to April 1, 2027. The bill sets heat and air conditioning season dates and indoor temperature ranges for rental housing.

dc:B 26-0422.title: Glazier Licensing Standards and Certification Act of 2025
dc:B 26-0422.summary: Establishes licensing and certification requirements for glaziers and glazing contractors in D.C. and adds two glazier and glazing contractor members to the Board of Industrial Trades.

dc:B 26-0427.title: Cybersecurity and Accountability Act of 2025
dc:B 26-0427.summary: Changes the insurance cybersecurity bill's confidentiality section: submitted documents are not subject to subpoena or discovery requests to the insurance commissioner, but no privilege bars private civil-damages plaintiffs from seeking them directly from a licensee.

dc:B 26-0436.title: Fair Initiatives Lend Transparency to Every Resident Amendment Act of 2025
dc:B 26-0436.summary: Requires the Board of Elections to reject initiatives covering more than one subject, extends the advisory-opinion deadline from 15 to 30 days, and adds fiscal impact statements, public comment, a public meeting, and fiscal impact summaries on petitions and ballots.

dc:B 26-0444.title: Food Policy Council Procurement Amendment Act of 2025
dc:B 26-0444.summary: Changes the Food Policy Council's report from annual to every three years starting September 30, 2027, and has the Food Policy Director's office oversee and advise on food purchasing by District agencies and contractors that regularly buy food.

dc:B 26-0494.title: Accountancy Practice Amendment Act of 2025
dc:B 26-0494.summary: Authorizes 4-year basic business licenses and fee refunds, exempts motor clubs doing private towing from identifying a storage lot, lets the Mayor add CPA licensure requirements by rule, and changes degree, experience and out-of-state practice-privilege rules for accountants.

dc:B 26-0526.title: Leading Education Access for Reentry and Necessary Success (LEARNS) Amendment Act of 2025
dc:B 26-0526.summary: Requires the Department of Corrections to provide special education to eligible detained people from age 18, expands eligibility for special education evaluations, and requires an online portal to track grievances and service requests.

dc:B 26-0547.title: Green Death Care Option Amendment Act of 2025 (now known as "Posthumous Care Modernization Amendment Act of 2026")
dc:B 26-0547.summary: Allows funeral establishments to reduce human remains by alkaline hydrolysis (water, alkaline chemicals and heat), defines cremation as incineration, and, like cremation ashes, excludes its product from the vital records definition of human remains.

dc:B 26-0548.title: Washington Commanders Motor Vehicle Identification Tags Amendment Act of 2025
dc:B 26-0548.summary: Authorizes the Mayor to design and issue Washington Commanders motor vehicle tags. Residents pay a $25 application fee and $20 annual display fee, or amounts set by rule, deposited in the State Athletic Activities, Programs, and Office Fund.

dc:B 26-0554.title: Commercial Driver’s License Amendment Act of 2025
dc:B 26-0554.summary: Updates D.C. commercial driver's license law to current federal code citations and revises disqualification standards, including disqualifying drivers convicted of fraud tied to commercial licenses or permits or who fail required retests after suspected fraud.

dc:B 26-0564.title: Food & Friends Property Tax Exemption Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0564.summary: Exempts the property at 219 Riggs Road NE from District real property tax while it is owned by Food & Friends, Inc. and used for charitable food distribution or related services, applying as of October 1, 2025.

dc:B 26-0619.title: Eric’s ID Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0619.summary: Requires the DMV to offer license, permit and ID card applicants an optional nonapparent-disability indicator, designated as a butterfly symbol; bars requiring proof; and requires police to train sworn officers on interactions with people who carry the indicator.

dc:B 26-0641.title: Archdiocese of Washington Parish Real Property, Deed Recordation, and Transfer Tax Exemption Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0641.summary: Confirms listed parcels owned by the Archbishop of Washington or named parishes are exempt from deed recordation and transfer taxes, and, for most, real property tax while used for religious, charitable or educational services; treats no-cost transfers to parishes as supplemental deeds.

dc:B 26-0663.title: Fiscal Year 2026 Revised Local Budget Temporary Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0663.summary: Temporarily adjusts the FY2026 local budget, decreasing it by $101,257,922 overall, with changes to agency allocations that reflect revenue and cost changes.

dc:B 26-0700.title: Reservoir District Tax Exemption Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0700.summary: Defines the one-third affordable set-aside of rental units for the Reservoir District tax exemption in Square 3128 under the federal tax-credit definition (26 U.S.C. 42(g)(2)(A)), with units open to households within HUD's 80 percent Multifamily Tax Subsidy income limit.

dc:B 26-0711.title: Entertainment Establishment Employee Safety Extension Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0711.summary: Allows, on a temporary basis, retail establishments with on-premises Class C or D retailer licenses, and restaurants open 24 hours or at 3 a.m. at least two days a week, to refuse cash if a conspicuous notice is posted on the door or menu.

dc:B 26-0713.title: Comprehensive Policing and Justice Reform Technical Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0713.summary: Temporarily expands the Police Complaints Board to nine members, lets the Office of Police Complaints' executive director open complaints over unalleged abuse or misuse of police powers, including failure to intervene in or report excessive force, and limits certain provisions to victims under 18.

dc:B 26-0716.title: Public Service Commission Term Holdover Extension Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0716.summary: On a temporary basis, extends to 270 days after term expiration the period a Public Service Commission commissioner may keep serving in a holdover capacity.

dc:B 26-0722.title: Language Access Rulemaking Authority Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0722.summary: Temporarily requires the Mayor to issue rules implementing the Language Access Act of 2004, applying as of June 19, 2004.

dc:B 26-0729.title: Private Vehicle-for-Hire Operator Clarification Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0729.summary: Temporarily redefines a private vehicle-for-hire operator as an individual who uses a company's digital dispatch to drive a motor vehicle providing passenger transportation. Applies retroactively to March 1, 2024.

dc:B 26-0733.title: Prearrest Diversion Task Force Recommendations Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0733.summary: Temporarily resets deadlines for the Prearrest Diversion Task Force to issue recommendations on diverting certain misdemeanor offenses and categories of people from arrest, to June 2025 for initial recommendations and July 31, 2026 for the next set.

dc:B 26-0735.title: Special Education for Young Adults in the Custody of the Department of Corrections Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0735.summary: Temporarily designates the Department of Corrections to provide a free appropriate public education under federal and D.C. special education law, during school years 2025-2026 and 2026-2027, to detained individuals with disabilities in its custody from age 18.

dc:B 26-0752.title: Health and Human Service Programs and Benefits Eligibility and Delivery Data-Sharing Clarifications Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0752.summary: Temporarily clarifies that the Department of Human Services may share records within the department and with other District agencies to determine eligibility for federal and District health and human service programs, subject to existing data-sharing law.

dc:B 26-0760.title: Medical Cannabis Licensing and Unlicensed Establishment Enforcement Clarification Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0760.summary: Temporarily extends medical cannabis conditional licenses by one year, treats establishments selling Schedule I substances as unlicensed, authorizes enforcement against all unlicensed establishments from April 1, 2025, and lets summary closures continue while the danger persists or is likely to recur.

dc:B 26-0764.title: The Omnibus Barry Farm Redevelopment Clarification Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0764.summary: Temporarily lets the Surveyor record Barry Farm street and alley closing and dedication plats in phases, with deadlines running from December 2028 for Phase 1A to December 2034 for Phases 2A and 2B.

dc:B 26-0766.title: Restoration of Covenanted Roads and Alleys by the District Government Clarification Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0766.summary: Temporarily lets the Mayor repair private rights-of-way used for District trash removal, with owner consent, a liability release and indemnification, when the owner has no duty to maintain them and they are not in good repair.

dc:B 26-0768.title: Net Zero Continuity Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0768.summary: Temporarily exempts District-owned or funded temporary buildings and additions under 10,000 square feet from net-zero-energy standards, and delays certain energy requirements for public safety facilities, aquatics centers with natatoriums and new residential projects until the Mayor's final regulations take effect.

dc:B 26-0779.title: Ballpark Bonds Loan Repayment Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0779.summary: Temporarily directs FY2027 sports facilities fee revenue, up to $49,505,000, to pay debt service on ballpark early-redemption borrowing and RFK infrastructure bonds, with the remainder going to the General Fund.

dc:B 26-0780.title: Food & Friends Property Tax Exemption Emergency Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0780.summary: On an emergency basis, exempts from real property tax the 219 Riggs Road NE property owned by Food & Friends, Inc., as long as it is used for charitable food distribution or related services. Applies to 100% of the land as of October 1, 2025.

dc:B 26-0781.title: Food & Friends Property Tax Exemption Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0781.summary: On a temporary basis, exempts from real property tax the 219 Riggs Road NE property owned by Food & Friends, Inc., as long as it is used for charitable food distribution or related services, applying to 100% of the land.

dc:B 26-0782.title: Broadband Price Transparency Regulation Emergency Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0782.summary: On an emergency basis, deems broadband internet sellers that follow the federal broadband consumer label rules in effect January 1, 2026 compliant with D.C.'s requirement that advertised prices include all mandatory fees.

dc:B 26-0783.title: Broadband Price Transparency Regulation Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0783.summary: On a temporary basis, deems broadband internet sellers that follow the federal broadband consumer label rules in effect January 1, 2026 compliant with D.C.'s requirement that advertised prices include all mandatory fees.

dc:B 26-0784.title: Comprehensive Policing and Justice Reform Technical Congressional Review Emergency Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0784.summary: On an emergency basis, expands the Police Complaints Board from five to nine members, lets the Office of Police Complaints' executive director open complaints over unalleged abuse or misuse of police powers, and limits certain provisions to victims under 18.

dc:B 26-0785.title: Peer-to-Peer Car Sharing Rental Vehicle Sales Tax Clarification Emergency Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0785.summary: On an emergency basis, restates the rental vehicle sales tax rates, 9.25% through September 30, 2026 and 11% afterward, and reverts the FY2027 budget act's peer-to-peer car sharing wording to prior language.

dc:B 26-0786.title: Peer-to-Peer Car Sharing Rental Vehicle Sales Tax Clarification Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0786.summary: Temporarily restates the rental vehicle sales tax rates, 9.25% through September 30, 2026 and 11% afterward, in the FY2027 budget support laws and reverts their peer-to-peer car sharing wording to prior language.

dc:B 26-0787.title: Community Schools Grant Program Emergency Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0787.summary: Amends, on an emergency basis, the Community Schools Incentive Act so Community Schools Task Force appointees must be "individuals" rather than "District residents." The act lasts up to 90 days.

dc:B 26-0788.title: Community Schools Grant Program Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0788.summary: Temporarily removes the requirement that Community Schools Task Force appointees be District residents, allowing any individuals to be appointed.

dc:B 26-0790.title: Duke District BID Grantmaking Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0790.summary: Requires, on a temporary basis, the Department of Small and Local Business Development to award a $1 million grant in the first quarter of Fiscal Year 2027 to the Duke District Business Improvement District for the Greater Shaw/U Street area.

dc:B 26-0791.title: Extension of Substance Use and Targeted Outreach Grants Emergency Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0791.summary: Requires, on an emergency basis, the Department of Behavioral Health to give Fiscal Year 2027 grants to the Fiscal Year 2026 Targeted Outreach pilot grantees to continue services, and authorizes Opioid Abatement Fund spending on them. The act lasts up to 90 days.

dc:B 26-0792.title: Extension of Substance Use and Targeted Outreach Grants Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0792.summary: Requires, on a temporary basis, the Department of Behavioral Health to give Fiscal Year 2027 grants to the Fiscal Year 2026 Targeted Outreach pilot grantees to continue services, and allows it to spend Opioid Abatement Fund money on the program.

dc:B 26-0793.title: Modification Nos. M0008, M0009 and M0010 to Contract No. CW110323 with Tag-B Parking, LLC Approval and Payment Authorization Emergency Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0793.summary: On an emergency basis, approves modifications to a contract with Tag-B Parking, LLC for private student transportation and attendant services, exercises the rest of option year three, and authorizes payment up to $18,710,208.

dc:B 26-0794.title: Modification Nos. M0010, M0011, and M0012 to Contract No. CW110212 with USA Guided Tours DC, LLC Approval and Payment Authorization Emergency Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0794.summary: On an emergency basis, approves modifications to a contract with USA Guided Tours DC, LLC for transportation of students with disabilities, exercises the third option year, and authorizes payment up to $7,722,000.

dc:B 26-0795.title: Modification Nos. M0007 and M0008 to Contract No. CW110321 with Miles Away Charter, LLC Approval and Payment Authorization Emergency Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0795.summary: On an emergency basis, approves modifications to a contract with Miles Away Charter, LLC for transportation of students with disabilities, exercises the third option year, and authorizes payment up to $1,465,200.

dc:B 26-0796.title: Modification Nos. M04, M05 and M06 to Contract No. CW106884 with See Forever Foundation Approval and Payment Authorization Emergency Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0796.summary: On an emergency basis, approves modifications to a contract with See Forever Foundation for an education program for youth in the custody of the Department of Youth Rehabilitation Services, and authorizes payment up to $3,968,957.85.

dc:B 26-0797.title: Modification Nos. M0009, M00010 and M0011 to Contract No. CW110208 with Ramjay Inc., Approval and Payment Authorization Emergency Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0797.summary: On an emergency basis, approves modifications to a contract with Ramjay Inc. for transportation of students with disabilities, exercises the third option year, and authorizes payment up to $4,802,490.

dc:B 26-0800.title: Modification No. M003 to Contract No. DCRL-2026-C-0024 with Crawford Consulting and Mental Health Service, Inc. Approval and Payment Authorization Emergency Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0800.summary: On an emergency basis, approves Modification No. M003 to a contract with Crawford Consulting and Mental Health Service, Inc. for community-based residential and social services, and authorizes payment up to $1,774,850.84.

dc:B 26-0824.title: Health and Human Service Programs and Benefits Eligibility and Delivery Data-Sharing Clarifications Congressional Review Emergency Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0824.summary: On an emergency basis, makes Department of Human Services record-sharing under the Homeless Services Reform Act subject to the Data-Sharing and Information Coordination Act's uses and disclosures, and widens that act's definition of agency to include subdivisions of agencies.

dc:B 26-0825.title: Alternative Breakfast Service Model Emergency Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0825.summary: On an emergency basis, changes school breakfast rules so Title I elementary schools with low participation may serve all students grab-and-go breakfast, breakfast in the classroom, or both.

dc:B 26-0826.title: Alternative Breakfast Service Model Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0826.summary: On a temporary basis, changes school breakfast rules so Title I elementary schools with low participation may serve all students grab-and-go breakfast, breakfast in the classroom, or both.

dc:B 26-0827.title: Porchfest Permitting Emergency Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0827.summary: On an emergency basis, lets District residents apply for a block party permit to close their street for a Porchfest (a free music festival on porches or yards), and adds Porchfests to the District's policy of approving block parties.

dc:B 26-0828.title: Porchfest Permitting Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0828.summary: On a temporary basis, lets District residents apply for a block party permit to close their street for a Porchfest, a free neighborhood music festival held on residents' porches or yards.

dc:B 26-0836.title: Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority Gold Line Bus Rapid Transit Phase 1 Fiscal Year 2027 and 2028 Reimbursable Agreement Emergency Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0836.summary: On an emergency basis, approves an agreement giving the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority $5 million in District capital funds for planning, environmental review and preliminary design of Phase 1 of a Gold Line bus rapid transit route on H Street and Benning Road.

dc:B 26-0840.title: Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority Stadium-Armory Station Improvements Fiscal Year 2026 to Fiscal Year 2030 Reimbursable Agreement Emergency Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0840.summary: On an emergency basis, approves an agreement giving the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority $300 million in District capital funds to design and build improvements at the Stadium-Armory Metrorail Station.

dc:B 26-0847.title: Net Zero Continuity Congressional Review Emergency Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0847.summary: On an emergency basis, exempts certain District-owned and -funded projects, such as temporary buildings, additions under 10,000 square feet, and police and fire facilities, from net-zero-energy standards, and revises that standard's definition and the projects it covers.

dc:B 26-0848.title: Private Vehicle-for-Hire Operator Clarification Congressional Review Emergency Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0848.summary: On an emergency basis, defines a private vehicle-for-hire operator as an individual who uses a private vehicle-for-hire company's digital dispatch to drive passengers in a motor vehicle, applying as of March 1, 2024.

dc:B 26-0849.title: Language Access Rulemaking Authority Congressional Review Emergency Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0849.summary: On an emergency basis, requires the Mayor to issue rules to carry out the Language Access Act of 2004, applying as of June 19, 2004.

dc:B 26-0851.title: Homeless Services Contract Adjustment Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0851.summary: On a temporary basis, requires the Office of Contracting and Procurement to decide, within 45 calendar days of a complete request, whether a homeless services contractor is owed a contract adjustment after a federal wage determination changes.

dc:B 26-0852.title: University of the District of Columbia Multiyear Contract No. PO-GF-2026-C-0019 with Ellucian Company LLC Contract Emergency Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0852.summary: On an emergency basis, approves a multiyear contract between the University of the District of Columbia and Ellucian Company LLC to move the university's enterprise software systems to a cloud-based service.

dc:CER 26-0207.title: Dr. Tiffany L. Lancaster Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0207.summary: Honors Dr. Tiffany L. Lancaster for her contributions to the District and her public service, culture and advancement of others.

dc:CER 26-0208.title: Philip Lepanto Ceremonial Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0208.summary: Remembers and honors the life of Philip A. Lepanto, including his service as an Advisory Neighborhood Commissioner.

dc:CER 26-0209.title: 17th Street High Heel Race Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0209.summary: Celebrates the annual 17th Street High Heel Race, a District LGBTQ+ tradition that began in 1986.

dc:CER 26-0210.title: Robert A. Kennedy, Jr. Memorial Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0210.summary: Honors the life of Robert A. Kennedy Jr. and his advocacy for people with disabilities in the District.

dc:CER 26-0212.title: Battle’s Transportation, Inc. Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0212.summary: Honors Battle's Transportation, Inc., a District passenger transportation company founded in 1976, for fifty years of service.

dc:CER 26-0213.title: Robert Vinson Brannum Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0213.summary: Honors Robert Vinson Brannum, a native Washingtonian and Air Force veteran, for his civic, veterans and community service in Ward 5.

dc:CER 26-0214.title: Capital Queens Women’s Sports Week Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0214.summary: Recognizes the inaugural Capital Queens Women's Sports Week, held September 20 to 26 and established jointly by the Washington Spirit and Washington Mystics.

dc:CER 26-0215.title: Lindsey Parker Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0215.summary: Honors Lindsey Parker for her work in District government, including as Director of the Office of the Chief Technology Officer and in the Mayor's office.

dc:CER 26-0216.title: Kevin Donahue Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0216.summary: Honors Kevin Donahue for his service to District residents as City Administrator.

dc:CER 26-0217.title: Hattie Holmes Senior Wellness Center Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0217.summary: Honors the Hattie Holmes Senior Wellness Center for its commitment to and impact on the community.

dc:CER 26-0218.title: Congress Heights Senior Wellness Center Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0218.summary: Honors the Congress Heights Senior Wellness Center in Ward 8 for its programming for District adults aged 60 and older.

dc:CER 26-0219.title: Iona Senior Services Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0219.summary: Honors Iona Senior Services for its work and service to communities across the District.

dc:CER 26-0220.title: Bernice Fonteneau Senior Wellness Center Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0220.summary: Honors the Bernice Fonteneau Senior Wellness Center in Ward 1 as a community resource since 2011 serving adults aged 60 and older.

dc:CER 26-0221.title: Hayes Senior Wellness Center Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0221.summary: Honors the Hayes Senior Wellness Center in Ward 6 for its role as a community resource for adults aged 60 and older.

dc:CER 26-0222.title: Washington Home Center Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0222.summary: Honors Iona's Washington Home Center in Ward 8 for its support of older adults, caregivers and families.

dc:CER 26-0223.title: Model Cities Senior Wellness Center Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0223.summary: Honors the Model Cities Senior Wellness Center in Ward 5 for its role as a community resource for seniors.

dc:CER 26-0224.title: Vida Senior Services Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0224.summary: Honors Vida Senior Services for more than five decades of services to older adults, including free meals, health screenings and mental health support.

dc:CER 26-0225.title: DC Table Tennis Day Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0225.summary: Recognizes October 10, 2026, and the second Saturday of each October after it, as DC Table Tennis Day in the District.

dc:PR 26-0671.title: Board of Library Trustees Denise Rolark Barnes Confirmation Resolution of 2026
dc:PR 26-0671.summary: Confirms Denise Rolark Barnes to the Board of Library Trustees for a term ending January 5, 2031.

dc:PR 26-0672.title: Board of Library Trustees Mary Early Confirmation Resolution of 2026
dc:PR 26-0672.summary: Confirms Mary Early to the Board of Library Trustees for a term ending January 5, 2030.

dc:PR 26-0785.title: Ballpark Bonds Loan Repayment Emergency Declaration Resolution of 2026
dc:PR 26-0785.summary: Declares an emergency so the Council can quickly pass an act allowing FY2027 sports facilities fees to repay short-term borrowing used to pay off Nationals Ballpark bonds early and to cover RFK infrastructure bond debt service.

dc:PR 26-0786.title: Food & Friends Property Tax Exemption Emergency Declaration Resolution of 2026
dc:PR 26-0786.summary: Declares an emergency so the Council can pass, after a single reading, an act continuing a real property tax exemption for Food & Friends at 219 Riggs Road NE, as the earlier temporary act expires September 25, 2026.

dc:PR 26-0787.title: Broadband Price Transparency Regulation Emergency Declaration Resolution of 2026
dc:PR 26-0787.summary: Declares an emergency so the Council can quickly pass an act deeming broadband internet sellers that follow federal broadband consumer label rules compliant with D.C.'s requirement that advertised prices include all mandatory fees.

dc:PR 26-0788.title: Comprehensive Policing and Justice Reform Technical Congressional Review Emergency Declaration Resolution of 2026
dc:PR 26-0788.summary: Declares an emergency so the Council can adopt, after a single reading, an act expanding the Police Complaints Board, letting the Office of Police Complaints' executive director open complaints over unalleged abuse or misuse of police powers, and limiting certain provisions to victims under 18.

dc:PR 26-0789.title: Council Period 26 Committee Membership Amendment Resolution of 2026
dc:PR 26-0789.summary: Changes membership of Council committees, adding Elissa Silverman to five committees and removing Doni Crawford from four.

dc:PR 26-0790.title: Peer-to-Peer Car Sharing Rental Vehicle Sales Tax Clarification Emergency Declaration Resolution of 2026
dc:PR 26-0790.summary: Declares an emergency so the Council can quickly pass an act reverting budget-act language, so the rental vehicle sales tax applies to peer-to-peer car sharing only when the owner has five or more vehicles available.

dc:PR 26-0791.title: Community Schools Task Force Emergency Declaration Resolution of 2026
dc:PR 26-0791.summary: Declares an emergency so the Council can pass legislation immediately removing the requirement that Community Schools Task Force appointees be District residents. It states that the requirement unintentionally excluded out-of-District experts.

dc:PR 26-0792.title: Duke District BID Grantmaking Emergency Declaration Resolution of 2026
dc:PR 26-0792.summary: Declares an emergency so the Council can pass legislation immediately directing the Department of Small and Local Business Development to award a grant to the Duke District Business Improvement District for the Greater Shaw/U Street area.

dc:PR 26-0793.title: Extension of Substance Use and Targeted Outreach Grants Emergency Declaration Resolution of 2026
dc:PR 26-0793.summary: Declares an emergency so the Council can quickly pass an act continuing funding for all FY2026 grantees of the Substance Use and Behavioral Health Services Targeted Outreach Grant pilot, paid from the Opioid Abatement Fund.

dc:PR 26-0794.title: Modification Nos. M0008, M0009 and M0010 to Contract No. CW110323 with Tag-B Parking, LLC Approval and Payment Authorization Emergency Declaration Resolution of 2026
dc:PR 26-0794.summary: Declares an emergency so the Council can quickly approve modifications to the Tag-B Parking, LLC contract for private student transportation and attendant services and authorize payment for services received.

dc:PR 26-0797.title: Modification Nos. M04, M05 and M06 to Contract No.CW106884 with See Forever Foundation Approval and Payment Authorization Emergency Declaration Resolution of 2026
dc:PR 26-0797.summary: Declares an emergency so the Council can quickly approve modifications to the See Forever Foundation contract for an education program for youth in Department of Youth Rehabilitation Services custody and authorize payment.

dc:PR 26-0798.title: Modification Nos. M0009, M00010 and M0011 to Contract No. CW110208 with Ramjay Inc., Approval and Payment Authorization Emergency Declaration Resolution of 2026
dc:PR 26-0798.summary: Declares an emergency so the Council can quickly approve modifications to the Ramjay Inc. contract for transportation of students with disabilities and authorize payment.

dc:PR 26-0799.title: Modification No. M003 to Contract No. DCRL-2026-C-0024 with Crawford Consulting and Mental Health Service, Inc. Approval and Payment Authorization Emergency Declaration Resolution of 2026
dc:PR 26-0799.summary: Declares an emergency so the Council can quickly approve a modification to the Crawford Consulting and Mental Health Service, Inc. contract for community-based residential and social services and authorize payment.

dc:PR 26-0800.title: Contract No. DCAM-21-NC-RFQuals-0001C PPA-26-01 with Flywheel Development, LLC Emergency Declaration Resolution of 2026
dc:PR 26-0800.summary: Declares an emergency so the Council can quickly approve a multiyear contract with Flywheel Development, LLC to develop solar photovoltaic systems at 27 District-owned sites.

dc:PR 26-0801.title: Contract No. DCAM-21-NC-RFQuals-0001C PPA-26-01 with Flywheel Development, LLC Emergency Approval Resolution of 2026
dc:PR 26-0801.summary: On an emergency basis, approves a multiyear contract with Flywheel Development, LLC to build solar systems at 27 District-owned sites at no cost to the District, with payment in solar renewable energy credits and District purchase of all electricity generated.

dc:PR 26-0811.title: Health and Human Service Programs and Benefits Eligibility and Delivery Data-Sharing Clarifications Congressional Review Emergency Declaration Resolution of 2026
dc:PR 26-0811.summary: Declares an emergency to continue, during congressional review, clarified authority for the Department of Human Services to share data with other District agencies to determine eligibility for health and human service programs.

dc:PR 26-0812.title: Alternative Breakfast Service Model Emergency Declaration Resolution of 2026
dc:PR 26-0812.summary: Declares an emergency over administrative challenges in implementing school breakfast requirements at Title I elementary schools, which must act when breakfast participation is below 75 percent.

dc:PR 26-0813.title: Porchfest Permitting Emergency Declaration Resolution of 2026
dc:PR 26-0813.summary: Declares an emergency so the Porchfest block party permitting amendment can take effect without a gap while permanent legislation moves forward; the earlier temporary act expires October 17, 2026.

dc:PR 26-0814.title: Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority Fiscal Year 2027 to 2032 Dedicated Funding Grant Agreement Emergency Declaration Resolution of 2026
dc:PR 26-0814.summary: Declares an emergency to allow approval of a six-year grant agreement under which the District gives the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority up to $1.071 billion total, and up to $178.5 million a year, for state-of-good-repair capital improvements.

dc:PR 26-0817.title: Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority Stadium-Armory Station Improvements Fiscal Year 2026 to Fiscal Year 2030 Reimbursable Agreement Emergency Declaration Resolution of 2026
dc:PR 26-0817.summary: Declares an emergency to allow approval of a District agreement providing $300 million in local capital funds to the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority for improvements at the Stadium-Armory Metrorail Station.

dc:PR 26-0818.title: Net Zero Continuity Congressional Review Emergency Declaration Resolution of 2026
dc:PR 26-0818.summary: Declares an emergency to prevent a gap in the law during congressional review, continuing provisions that exempt certain District-owned and -funded projects from net-zero-energy standards and change how those standards apply.

dc:PR 26-0819.title: Private Vehicle-for-Hire Operator Clarification Congressional Review Emergency Declaration Resolution of 2026
dc:PR 26-0819.summary: Declares an emergency to continue, during congressional review, a clarified definition of private vehicle-for-hire operator so the Department of For-Hire Vehicles can keep enforcing registration, insurance and trade dress rules.

dc:PR 26-0820.title: Language Access Rulemaking Authority Congressional Review Emergency Declaration Resolution of 2026
dc:PR 26-0820.summary: Declares an emergency to continue, without a gap during congressional review, the Mayor's authority to issue rules enforcing the Language Access Act of 2004.

dc:PR 26-0821.title: Homeless Services Contract Adjustment Emergency Declaration Resolution of 2026
dc:PR 26-0821.summary: Declares an emergency on the need to require the Office of Contracting and Procurement to process requests to adjust homeless services contracts within 45 days after federal wage determination changes.

dc:PR 26-0822.title: University of the District of Columbia Multiyear Contract No. PO-GF-2026-C-0019 with Ellucian Company LLC Contract Emergency Declaration Resolution of 2026
dc:PR 26-0822.summary: Declares an emergency to approve a multiyear contract between the University of the District of Columbia and Ellucian Company LLC to move the university's enterprise software systems to a cloud-based service.

de:HB 122.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 10 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO FAMILY COURT'S CRIMINAL JURISDICTION.
de:HB 122.summary: Removes the in-state residency requirement from the definition of "family" and gives Family Court and the Court of Common Pleas shared criminal jurisdiction over certain offenses, including cases where a child's parentage is disputed.

de:HB 133.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 11 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO FINES, FEES, RESTITUTION, AND OTHER COURT-RELATED MONETARY OBLIGATIONS.
de:HB 133.summary: Lets courts waive, suspend, or modify criminal fines and fees, including mandatory ones, and creates a hardship-waiver process. Defendants on public benefits or represented by the Office of Defense Services presumptively qualify; people already sentenced may apply later.

de:HB 134.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 11 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO ANIMAL CRUELTY.
de:HB 134.summary: Raises penalties for animal cruelty: violations after two misdemeanors become class F felonies, violations after a first felony become class E felonies, and a second felony conviction bars owning or possessing any animal for life.

de:HB 141.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLES 11 AND 24 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO FIREARMS.
de:HB 141.summary: Requires licensed firearm dealers, importers, and manufacturers to give buyers a state-published Firearm Responsibilities Notice and have them sign a form acknowledging receipt before a sale; dealers keep the signed forms at least three years.

de:HB 145.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 11 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO REVERSE LOCATION AND REVERSE KEYWORD SEARCHES AND COURT ORDERS.
de:HB 145.summary: Prohibits government entities from seeking, and courts from issuing, orders or requests identifying unnamed people who searched a keyword, except for certain listed serious felonies when the search returns five or fewer hits; unlawfully obtained evidence is inadmissible.

de:HB 150.title: AN ACT AMENDING TITLE 10 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO CIVIL ARRESTS.
de:HB 150.summary: Bars civil (non-criminal) arrests of people going to, attending, or leaving courthouses and Industrial Accident Board hearing offices, unless a judicial order authorizes the arrest or officers give the judge or board advance written notice.

de:HB 155.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE PUBLICATION OF STATE PUBLIC INTEGRITY COMMISSION REPORTS.
de:HB 155.summary: Requires State Public Integrity Commission reports to be published on its website and requires public officers to annually disclose third-party-paid travel expenses over $250 in total, effective January 1 after enactment.

de:HB 165.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 24 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO DRY NEEDLING.
de:HB 165.summary: Authorizes physician associates, occupational therapists and advanced practice registered nurses to perform dry needling, requires a physician referral for occupational therapists, and bars them from calling themselves acupuncturists unless licensed. Takes effect at the earlier of 12 months or final regulations.

de:HB 188.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 15 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO PRIMARY ELECTIONS.
de:HB 188.summary: As amended, allows registered voters unaffiliated with a political party to vote in a party primary of their choice starting January 1, 2028; their party-ballot choice becomes public record but does not change their registration.

de:HB 190.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO GRANTS-IN-AID.
de:HB 190.summary: Sets rules for organizations seeking legislative grants-in-aid, including conflict-of-interest and whistleblower policies, audits or financial reviews, and resident testimonials, and lets the Controller General audit, withhold or reclaim grant money. Takes effect July 1, 2028.

de:HB 200.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 18, TITLE 29, AND TITLE 31 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO INSURANCE COVERAGE FOR TREATMENT TO PREVENT HIV INFECTION.
de:HB 200.summary: Requires individual, group, state employee and Medicaid health plans to cover medically necessary HIV PrEP and PEP medication and related testing and counseling without cost-sharing or prior authorization, for policies issued or renewed after December 31, 2026.

de:HB 213.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 10 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO EVIDENCE AND WITNESSES.
de:HB 213.summary: Creates a privilege for confidential communications between a crime victim and a victim advocate, which yields only to prevent harm or to report child abuse; the victim can waive it in writing.

de:HB 218.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 10 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO INTERPERSONAL AND SEXUAL VIOLENCE IN THE MILITARY.
de:HB 218.summary: Requires courts to consider a military protective order as a factor favoring an emergency protective order or temporary sexual violence protective order, and requires officers with probable cause of a violation to notify the agency that issued the military order.

de:HB 219.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 1 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO DIWALI DAY.
de:HB 219.summary: Designates Diwali Day as a ceremonial day to be commemorated annually in Delaware.

de:HB 222.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 3 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO NUTRIENT MANAGEMENT.
de:HB 222.summary: Raises the fine range for State Nutrient Management Program violations from $25-$1,000 to $125-$5,000 per violation.

de:HB 233.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 26 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO LARGE ENERGY USE FACILITIES.
de:HB 233.summary: Requires Commission-regulated electric utilities to set a separate rate class for large energy-use facilities, with Commission-approved agreements, so costs of serving them are assigned to those facilities rather than other customers.

de:HB 253.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 12 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO PERSONS QUALIFIED TO RECEIVE LETTERS TESTAMENTARY OR OF ADMINISTRATION.
de:HB 253.summary: Allows a person with a felony conviction to receive letters testamentary or of administration if the Register of Wills approves it, at the Register's discretion, for good cause shown.

de:HB 259.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 16 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO SCREENING FOR LEAD POISONING.
de:HB 259.summary: Requires the Division of Public Health to post on its website, and send to state officials, school-reported data on how many kindergartners meet the state's lead poisoning screening requirements.

de:HB 261.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 14 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO TRANSPORTATION OF PUPILS.
de:HB 261.summary: Gives the Department of Education authority to adopt rules on transporting public school students, and replaces the limit of nonpublic school transportation to within district boundaries with out-of-district transportation required under IDEA, Section 504 and other state or federal law.

de:HB 267.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 14 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO READING COMPETENCY.
de:HB 267.summary: Requires school districts and charters to report reading-deficiency screening and intervention data to the Department of Education on October 31 and June 30 each year, and sets an August 30 annual department report with longitudinal analysis of those submissions.

de:HB 276.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 11 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THEFT.
de:HB 276.summary: Allows the value of items stolen at separate times to be combined into one theft charge when the thefts were part of a defined course of conduct, which must be proven beyond a reasonable doubt.

de:HB 283.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 30 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE REALTY TRANSFER TAX.
de:HB 283.summary: Extends the realty transfer tax spousal exception to spouses generally, not only husband and wife, and adds an exception for transfers between grandparents and their grandchildren or a grandchild's spouse.

de:HB 295.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLES 21 AND 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO A DESIGNATED PARKING SPACE FOR VETERANS AT STATE BUILDINGS.
de:HB 295.summary: Requires the Office of Management and Budget director to reserve at least one parking space for veterans at certain state-owned buildings and facilities, bans parking there by others, and encourages the same at leased sites. Takes effect six months after enactment.

de:HB 297.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLES 12 AND 25 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO DECEDENTS’ ESTATES AND PROPERTY.
de:HB 297.summary: Updates Delaware trust and estate law on how multiple fiduciaries act, filling trustee vacancies, merging trusts, and exercising powers of appointment, among other technical changes.

de:HB 299.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 18 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO LIFE INSURANCE POLICY EXCLUSIONS AND RESTRICTIONS BASED ON DEATH RESULTING FROM SUICIDE.
de:HB 299.summary: Cuts from two years to one the period after issue in which a new life insurance policy may exclude suicide, and requires insurers that deny a death benefit on that basis to refund premiums. Takes effect six months after enactment.

de:HB 300.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 14 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A TITLE IX COORDINATOR WITHIN THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION.
de:HB 300.summary: Creates a Title IX Coordinator position in the Department of Education to train and assist schools, collect compliance data, maintain model policies, and support Title IX compliance in grades 6 through 12 athletics.

de:HB 305.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 16 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE DELAWARE DIABETES WELLNESS PILOT PROGRAM WITHIN THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND SOCIAL SERVICES  TO STUDY DIABETIC WELL CARE.
de:HB 305.summary: Creates a three-year observational diabetes wellness pilot program, run by the Health and Social Services secretary with a Delaware health system and a technology provider, enrolling 400 to 500 volunteer patients for regular testing and health management, funded by federal money.

de:HB 308.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 26 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION.
de:HB 308.summary: Requires Public Service Commission meetings to be livestreamed online and lets the public comment virtually.

de:HB 309.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 14 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO SERVICES FOR STUDENTS WITH AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER.
de:HB 309.summary: Updates the statewide autism program law so the Department of Education administers it directly and employs the statewide director, replacing a designated school district or other entity.

de:HB 310.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 30 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO BUSINESS TAX CREDITS AND DEDUCTIONS.
de:HB 310.summary: As amended, excludes large energy-use facilities from the "qualified facility" definition for the employment and investment tax credit and license fee reduction, unless they produce or procure 100% of annual energy from clean generation in Delaware or nearby PJM zones.

de:HB 313.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLES 14 AND 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE DEPARTMENT OF SERVICES FOR CHILDREN, YOUTH AND THEIR FAMILIES AND EDUCATIONAL SERVICES.
de:HB 313.summary: Establishes in law the Education Unit within the Department of Services for Children, Youth and Their Families, which provides educational services to children and youth living in department-run facilities.

de:HB 322.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 11 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO ARREST AND DETENTION.
de:HB 322.summary: Allows employees or security personnel of health-care institutions and licensed medical or dental practices to take into custody and reasonably detain on the premises a person presenting a security or safety risk, while summoning law enforcement.

de:HB 324.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 16 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO TATTOO PARLORS, BODY PIERCING ESTABLISHMENTS, AND HUMAN TRAFFICKING.
de:HB 324.summary: Requires tattoo parlors to post signs about human trafficking and directs the Department of Health and Social Services to encourage tattoo and body piercing workers to take free trafficking-recognition training. Takes effect one year after enactment.

de:HB 326.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 11 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THEFT BY IMPERSONATION OF A FAMILY MEMBER.
de:HB 326.summary: Creates the felony of theft by impersonating a victim's family member, graded by victim and amount stolen, from class F up to class B for $100,000 or more.

de:HB 329.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLES 20 AND 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT AND EMERGENCY REGULATIONS.
de:HB 329.summary: Limits state-of-emergency orders to 120 days, renewable once for 60 more; later renewals need a Governor's finding and the General Assembly may amend or end them. Requires written updates to the General Assembly every 30 days. Takes effect once the sitting Governor leaves office.

de:HB 332.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 16 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO KRATOM.
de:HB 332.summary: Bans selling, providing or marketing kratom products to anyone under 21 as a class B misdemeanor, and requires a report on kratom testing capabilities and retailer licensing by January 1, 2027.

de:HB 337.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 16 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO FOLIC ACID FORTIFICATION.
de:HB 337.summary: Requires corn masa flour made, sold or used in Delaware to contain 0.7 mg of folic acid per pound beginning January 1, 2027, with a folic acid declaration on the nutrition label; wet corn masa products may contain 0.4 mg per pound.

de:HB 338.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 18 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO HEALTH CARRIER COVERAGE OF IMMUNIZATIONS AND PREVENTIVE SERVICES.
de:HB 338.summary: Ties the preventive services and immunizations that health insurers must cover without cost-sharing to task force, CDC immunization committee, and HRSA recommendations in effect on January 1, 2025, and removes language letting carriers drop coverage when recommendations change.

de:HB 341.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO CHILD SUPPORT.
de:HB 341.summary: Creates a presumption that parents are not liable for the support of children committed to or served by the Department of Services for Children, Youth and Their Families, with Family Court ordering support only if it will not hinder reunification.

de:HB 342.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 11 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE POSSESSION AND PURCHASE OF DEADLY WEAPONS BY PERSONS PROHIBITED.
de:HB 342.summary: Adds people subject to out-of-state domestic violence protection orders to those barred from buying or possessing deadly weapons and ammunition, if the order bars weapons or meets the criteria of 18 U.S.C. 922(g)(8).

de:HB 343.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 13 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO METHODS TO OBTAIN JURISDICTION OVER RESPONDENT IN FAMILY COURT AND THE DUTY TO SUPPORT.
de:HB 343.summary: Allows the Division of Child Support Services to serve a non-custodial parent's Family Court summons by any mail with proof of delivery, including the U.S. Postal Service, FedEx or UPS.

de:HB 344.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLES 15 AND 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO CAMPAIGN FINANCE.
de:HB 344.summary: As amended, requires written documentation of loans to political committees, bars candidates from charging interest on loans to their own committees, extends record retention to five years, adds biennial training, and has the election commissioner refer alleged violations monthly to the Department of Justice's public trust division.

de:HB 346.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 16 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED DISEASE PREVENTION AND CONTROL.
de:HB 346.summary: Updates sexually transmitted disease law: repeals quarantine, isolation and compelled-treatment powers, removes the one-working-day reporting deadline, and requires providers caring for pregnant patients to offer STI and STD testing, which patients may refuse with the refusal documented.

de:HB 347.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 14 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE UNIFORM PUBLIC SCHOOL REGISTRATION PROCESS.
de:HB 347.summary: Removes the requirement that parents provide a birth certificate to register a child for public school; other proof of age or birth date is accepted instead.

de:HB 348.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO ELECTRIC VEHICLES.
de:HB 348.summary: Removes the $2,500 all-electric and $1,000 plug-in hybrid rebate caps and the $50,000 vehicle price limit from Delaware's electric vehicle rebate program, lets DNREC set rebates by household income and vehicle type, and adds businesses, nonprofits, and governments as eligible.

de:HB 350.title: AN ACT TO AMEND THE LAWS OF DELAWARE RELATING TO HOMESCHOOL STUDENT PARTICIPATION IN EXTRACURRICULAR ACTIVITIES.
de:HB 350.summary: Requires the Department of Education to study, with schools and homeschool groups, letting homeschool students join extracurricular activities at their local public, charter or vocational school, including whether to create a pilot program, and to report by December 31, 2027.

de:HB 351.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 21 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO VEHICLE SECURITY CIRCUMVENTION DEVICES.
de:HB 351.summary: Makes it a crime to knowingly make, sell, transfer or possess a vehicle security circumvention device, or aid or permit its use, with exceptions such as law enforcement and locksmiths; requires reporting a lost or stolen device to police within 48 hours.

de:HB 355.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 10 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO SEXUAL ASSAULT, HARASSMENT, AND DISCRIMINATION.
de:HB 355.summary: As amended, bars civil liability for communications about sexual assault, harassment or discrimination made without malice (knowing falsity or reckless disregard) by those who experienced or witnessed it, and says a prevailing defendant in a related suit may be awarded attorneys' fees and costs.

de:HB 356.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 16 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO PFAS IN FIREFIGHTING FOAM AND EQUIPMENT.
de:HB 356.summary: Bars manufacturers from making, selling, or distributing Class B firefighting foam with intentionally added PFAS from January 1, 2028, with five-year exemptions for bulk petroleum facilities; requires recalls and sets civil penalties of up to $5,000, then $10,000.

de:HB 357.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLES 10 AND 13 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE DUTY TO SUPPORT POOR PERSONS.
de:HB 357.summary: Replaces the term "poor person" with "a person unable to financially support oneself" in the duty-to-support law and clarifies that the duty covers support of an adult child with a disability who cannot support themself.

de:HB 359.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 29 AND TITLE 31 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE DISPOSITION OF HUMAN REMAINS.
de:HB 359.summary: Allows the State to bury or cremate an indigent person's unclaimed body or remains without written consent from next of kin or another legally responsible party.

de:HB 363.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 21 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO RESIDENTIAL SPEED LIMITS.
de:HB 363.summary: Changes the statutory speed limit in residence districts from 25 mph to 20 or 25 mph, at the discretion of the agency owning the roadway, and bars enforcing a lower limit until new speed limit signs are posted.

de:HB 365.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE ESTABLISHMENT OF THE DELAWARE INDIGENOUS AFFAIRS COMMISSION.
de:HB 365.summary: Establishes a Commission on Indigenous Affairs in Delaware state government.

de:HB 368.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 11 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO IMMIGRATION ENFORCEMENT AND COOPERATION.
de:HB 368.summary: As amended, bars law enforcement from holding anyone solely on an immigration detainer or civil immigration warrant, except people convicted of a violent felony, registered sex offenders, people with 2 or more DUI convictions and domestic violence perpetrators; limits other civil immigration cooperation; requires annual reports.

de:HB 369.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE ESTABLISHMENT OF THE OFFICE OF GUN VIOLENCE PREVENTION AND COMMUNITY SAFETY.
de:HB 369.summary: Establishes in state law the Office of Gun Violence Prevention and Community Safety within the Department of Safety and Homeland Security, created by a 2025 executive order, to coordinate state, county, and municipal efforts on gun violence and community safety.

de:HB 371.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 3 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE DELAWARE AGRICULTURAL LANDS PRESERVATION ACT.
de:HB 371.summary: Removes the requirement that each county establish a Farmland Preservation Advisory Board.

de:HB 374.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO LARGE PUBLIC WORKS CONTRACTS.
de:HB 374.summary: Requires the Office of Management and Budget to issue an annual report, due each February 1, on workers hired for state public works projects costing $3 million or more, including demographics, home zip code, union status, craft trade, and hours worked.

de:HB 376.title: AN ACT TO AMEND THE CHARTER OF THE TOWN OF MILLVILLE.
de:HB 376.summary: Reorganizes the Town of Millville charter into articles, removes provisions superseded by state law and the town's own assessment process, and adds a tie-breaker for municipal elections: a drawing by lot after three recounts.

de:HB 380.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 6 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO PERSONAL DATA PRIVACY.
de:HB 380.summary: Lowers the Delaware Personal Data Privacy Act's coverage thresholds from 35,000 to 10,000 consumers (10,000 to 5,000 if over 20% of revenue comes from selling data), narrows financial-law exemptions to banks and insurers, and adds contract rules for third-party data sharing.

de:HB 381.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 6 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO COMPUTER SECURITY BREACHES.
de:HB 381.summary: Requires notice of a computer security breach to the Attorney General within 60 days after the breach is determined when affected residents could not be identified in that time, and adds Attorney General notice to substitute notice.

de:HB 383.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO PAY FOR DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION EMPLOYEES.
de:HB 383.summary: Requires Department of Transportation employees in 20 listed job titles, such as Administrative Specialist and Engineering Technician, to be paid time-and-a-half after 37.5 hours a week, starting July 1, 2026.

de:HB 384.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO OPEN-END CONTRACTING FOR HIGHWAY CONSTRUCTION AND RECONSTRUCTION.
de:HB 384.summary: Raises the maximum length of Department of Transportation open-end highway construction contracts from three to five years and allows bid bonds of 10% and performance bonds of 100% of expected maximum work.

de:HB 385.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 16 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO GRANTS FOR NURSE PRECEPTORS.
de:HB 385.summary: Creates a program, run by a nurse workforce nonprofit, that gives hospitals, health centers and other clinical facilities financial and technical support for preceptorship programs, funded by annual General Assembly appropriations. Takes effect six months after enactment.

de:HB 388.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 21 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE LOSS OF DRIVERS' LICENSES DUE TO MEDICAL ISSUES.
de:HB 388.summary: Lets people disqualified from driving for a medical condition keep their physical driver's license for identification by signing an affidavit that they may not drive, instead of surrendering it.

de:HB 390.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE ELECTRONIC SUBMISSION OF BIDS AND BID OPENINGS FOR ELECTRONIC BIDDING.
de:HB 390.summary: Lets state agencies choose electronic-only or combined bid submission on a platform of their choice, but paper bids must be accepted for some purchases under $500,000; requires posting results within two business days; drops newspaper ads when advertised on the electronic procurement system.

de:HB 393.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 26 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO PROTECTIONS FOR PUBLIC UTILITY CONSUMERS.
de:HB 393.summary: Sets rules for third-party residential electric suppliers, including a price cap tied to the standard offer rate and 12-month maximum terms; requires monthly reports and a supplier training program through the Public Service Commission; bars fines or jail under section 218 for licensed sales agents.

de:HB 404.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 14 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND EXTENDED REALITY IN SCHOOLS PILOT PROGRAM.
de:HB 404.summary: As amended, creates a pilot program in which the Department of Education invites 6 to 12 schools to use artificial intelligence and extended reality products recommended by a committee, collects school data, and reports to the Governor and General Assembly by September 30, 2031.

de:HB 406.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 18 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO UNFAIR TRADE PRACTICES IN AUTOMOBILE INSURANCE.
de:HB 406.summary: Extends the existing ban on insurers requiring a particular facility, individual, or business for repair or replacement work as a condition of claim payment from auto glass work to all auto repair and replacement work.

de:HB 407.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLES 7 AND 30 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE DELAWARE HAZARDOUS SUBSTANCES CLEANUP ACT AND THE REALTY TRANSFER TAX.
de:HB 407.summary: Lets DNREC act on emergencies without a court order and authorize removal actions without first seeking public comment, adds the Court of Chancery for cost-recovery suits, raises the civil penalty per fraudulent act from $10,000 to $40,000, and extends fund deposits to 2037.

de:HB 408.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 11 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO TRAFFICKING AN INDIVIDUAL, FORCED LABOR AND SEXUAL SERVITUDE.
de:HB 408.summary: Makes obtaining or purchasing a minor for commercial sexual activity an offense under Delaware's trafficking and sexual servitude statutes even when no third party is involved.

de:HB 409.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 11 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO PROSTITUTION.
de:HB 409.summary: Adds operating, conducting, and advertising a prostitution business to the ways of promoting prostitution in the second degree, expressly covers illicit massage establishments, and defines them as establishments that facilitate prostitution under cover of a massage business.

de:HB 411.title: AN ACT TO AMEND THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO A DIVISION OF ALCOHOL, TOBACCO, AND MARIJUANA ENFORCEMENT.
de:HB 411.summary: Renames the Division of Alcohol and Tobacco Enforcement the Division of Alcohol, Tobacco, and Marijuana Enforcement and changes references to its "agents" to "officers."

de:HB 412.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 7 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO HUNTING, TRAPPING, GAME ANIMALS, GAME BIRDS, DEER, AND PROTECTED WILDLIFE.
de:HB 412.summary: Requires hunters and trappers exempt from licensing to complete an approved education program, adds fishing, crabbing and clamming to licensed activities, allows dogs to track wounded or dead deer, and permits sale of taxidermy and antlers from lawfully taken deer.

de:HB 413.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 21 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO USE OF REVOLVING OR FLASHING GREEN LIGHT.
de:HB 413.summary: Extends the green revolving or flashing light allowance from state and municipal snow removal equipment to vehicles and equipment, including farm tractors and construction equipment, used for road or bridge work, traffic control, or emergency or inclement-weather operations.

de:HB 414.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 11 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO POSSESSING A DESTRUCTIVE WEAPON.
de:HB 414.summary: Specifies that the Superior Court's exclusive jurisdiction over possessing a destructive weapon applies only to adult defendants, with jurisdiction over minors remaining in Family Court.

de:HB 418.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 11 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO FIREARMS.
de:HB 418.summary: Lets people who lawfully possessed unserialized firearms or unfinished frames or receivers before the Act keep them if, within six months, a licensed dealer or manufacturer serializes them or they are made permanently inoperable; defines "permanently inoperable."

de:HB 419.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 31 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO ELIGIBILITY FOR CHILD CARE ASSISTANCE.
de:HB 419.summary: Makes a child automatically eligible for Purchase of Care child care assistance on placement in foster care, or when the Department of Services for Children, Youth and Their Families certifies the child is in a placement requiring it.

de:HB 420.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 24 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO MASSAGE AND BODY WORK.
de:HB 420.summary: Lets massage and bodywork therapists complete pre-licensing education in a hybrid format as set by the Board, and removes references to certified massage technician licenses the Board no longer issues.

de:HB 423.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO DEFERRED COMPENSATION.
de:HB 423.summary: Automatically enrolls newly hired state employees in the state's 457(b) deferred compensation plan at a predetermined percentage of pay, with an opt-out before deductions begin at 90 days and refunds available until 120 days after hire.

de:HB 424.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 16 RELATING TO AUTISM SURVEILLANCE AND REGISTRATION.
de:HB 424.summary: Repeals Delaware's autism surveillance and registration program, which requires health practitioners to report autism cases to the state or face a $100 fine per violation.

de:HB 425.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 14 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO EMPLOYEES AND SALARY SUPPLEMENTS.
de:HB 425.summary: Raises the salary supplement for nationally certified school counselors and nurses from 6% to 12%, adds school social workers, and lets the Department of Education identify additional eligible positions by regulation.

de:HB 426.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 30 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO STATE AID TO MUNICIPALITIES FOR STREETS.
de:HB 426.summary: Removes requirements that reports under the State Aid to Municipalities for Streets program be notarized and printed, allows electronic submission, and requires the annual report to also go to the Department of Transportation.

de:HB 427.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 11 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO OFFENSES INVOLVING DEADLY WEAPONS AND DANGEROUS INSTRUMENTS.
de:HB 427.summary: As amended, lets 16- and 17-year-olds possess BB guns, projectile weapons or firearms without direct adult supervision while target practicing or hunting if a parent permits it and they completed hunter education; hunting also requires a valid Delaware hunting license.

de:HB 429.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 18 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE STEP THERAPY EXCEPTION PROCESS.
de:HB 429.summary: Allows insurers, under the step therapy exception law, to require patients to try an interchangeable biological product or a biosimilar, as well as an AB-rated generic, before covering the brand-name drug.

de:HB 431.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 9 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO COMPOSTING.
de:HB 431.summary: As amended, requires counties to allow commercial composting of yard waste, food residuals and other organic materials on private properties zoned Agricultural Conservation, outside the growth zone, of 4 acres or more; counties may limit the area but must allow at least 5,000 square feet.

de:HB 437.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 4, TITLE 11, TITLE 14, TITLE 16, TITLE 18, TITLE 20, TITLE 21, TITLE 24, TITLE 25, TITLE 29, THE CHARTER OF THE TOWN OF DEWEY BEACH, THE CHARTER OF THE CITY OF HARRINGTON, THE CHARTER OF THE TOWN OF HOUSTON, THE CHARTER OF THE CITY OF MILFORD, AND THE CHARTER OF THE TOWN OF MILLSBORO RELATING TO TECHNICAL CORRECTIONS.
de:HB 437.summary: Makes technical corrections to the Delaware Code across many titles and to municipal charters, including changes identified by the Code Revisors and edits conforming to the Legislative Drafting Manual.

de:HB 439.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 21 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE SALE OF ELECTRIC MOPEDS AND ELECTRIC MOTORCYCLES.
de:HB 439.summary: Bars commercial sellers from advertising electric mopeds and motorcycles as electric bicycles, requires written disclosures about classification, power and registration, treats missing disclosures as unlawful, and bars mopeds from public pathways, bike lanes and sidewalks.

de:HB 444.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 15 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE DELAWARE JOHN LEWIS VOTING RIGHTS ACT.
de:HB 444.summary: As amended, establishes the Delaware John Lewis Voting Rights Act, effective July 1, 2027, which directs that election laws be construed in favor of access to voting and allows challenges to election policies or practices that cause voter suppression or vote dilution affecting protected-class members.

de:HB 445.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 26 AND TITLE 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO LARGE ENERGY USE FACILITIES.
de:HB 445.summary: As amended, bars large energy-use facilities, including data centers, from operating unless they produce or procure 100% of annual energy from clean generation in Delaware or nearby PJM zones; a 10-year plan option allows phased compliance with curtailment and backup-power conditions.

de:HB 446.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 3 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO AGRICULTURE AND STATE FORESTRY.
de:HB 446.summary: Adds definitions of "urban forestry," "urban forest" and "Urban Tree Canopy" to Delaware's forestry law, lists the Department of Agriculture's forestry powers and duties in one section, and makes technical corrections.

de:HB 447.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 14 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO CHILD CARE.
