de:HB 447.summary: Directs the Interagency Resource Management Committee to coordinate planning, programs and funding for child care affordability, including voluntary cost-sharing partnerships among the state, employers, community sponsors and families.

de:HB 448.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 15 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO CAMPAIGN EXPENDITURES.
de:HB 448.summary: Makes security expenses for a candidate's safety, such as home or office security systems and personal security, an authorized campaign expenditure, excluding firearms purchases, and requires the Commissioner to adopt rules within three months.

de:HB 449.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 24 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE DIETITIAN/NUTRITIONIST LICENSURE ACT.
de:HB 449.summary: Splits the dietitian/nutritionist license into licensed dietitian and licensed nutritionist, each with its own scope of practice, education, supervised practice and exam standards; raises required dietitian supervised practice from 900 to 1,000 hours.

de:HB 452.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 14 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE DELAWARE INTERSCHOLASTIC ATHLETIC ASSOCIATION AND BACKGROUND CHECKS FOR CHILD-SERVING ENTITIES.
de:HB 452.summary: Requires Delaware Interscholastic Athletic Association regulations to mandate background checks for sports officials, diversity and anti-discrimination training for officials, annual sportsmanship and anti-harassment training for student athletes, and member-school cooperation with investigations.

de:HB 455.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 21 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO SPECIAL LICENSE PLATES.
de:HB 455.summary: Creates a special license plate for Preservation Delaware, Inc., a statewide nonprofit focused on preserving Delaware's architectural heritage and historic settings.

de:HB 456.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 7 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO SUBAQUEOUS LANDS.
de:HB 456.summary: Changes DNREC's subaqueous lands permitting by exempting common activities already authorized by the Army Corps of Engineers, expanding statewide general permits, setting processing timelines for minor structures, and creating a Marine Contractors and Consultants Licensing Board.

de:HB 457.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 17 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO ACQUISITION AND SALE OF REAL PROPERTY.
de:HB 457.summary: Raises from $10,000 to $25,000 the estimated property value above which the transportation department needs an independent appraisal before selling surplus land, and raises the "minimal utility" no-appraisal sale limit from $3,000 to $25,000.

de:HB 459.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 14 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO ENERGY DRINKS.
de:HB 459.summary: Bans the sale of energy drinks on public middle and high school campuses during regular school hours and the extended school day, including clubs and sporting events, without limiting drinks students bring from off campus.

de:HB 461.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 14 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO SCHOOL TAX.
de:HB 461.summary: Lets New Castle County school districts reset 2026-2027 tax rates using the latest county assessment list, without raising projected operating revenue beyond referendum increases not yet received and the five-year average growth in taxable property. Expires March 31, 2027.

de:HB 462.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 14 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO SCHOOL TAXES.
de:HB 462.summary: Continues authority for non-vocational school districts in New Castle County to set separate residential and non-residential school tax rates, with the non-residential rate between 1 and 1.85 times the residential rate.

de:HB 465.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 11 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO VIRTUAL CURRENCY.
de:HB 465.summary: Adds virtual currency to the criminal code's money laundering definition and gives the state authority to return virtual currency to victims, with Superior Court disposing of funds that cannot be returned.

de:HB 475.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 24 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE DELAWARE NURSING ADVANCEMENT FUND.
de:HB 475.summary: Creates a Delaware Nursing Advancement Fund, financed by a $10 fee on Board of Nursing applications and renewals plus disciplinary fines, to fund a nonprofit studying and promoting the nursing workforce.

de:HB 476.title: AN ACT TO AMEND THE CHARTER OF THE TOWN OF FREDERICA.
de:HB 476.summary: Changes the Town of Frederica's charter to require at least one regular council meeting each month instead of two set meetings, and makes adopted ordinances take effect immediately unless a date is specified.

de:HB 478.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE AUDITOR OF ACCOUNTS AND BACKGROUND CHECKS.
de:HB 478.summary: Makes a technical correction to who may access fingerprint-based background checks under the Auditor of Accounts chapter, to meet federal requirements for access to FBI criminal history records.

de:HB 59.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 11 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO RELEASE AND PUBLICATION OF THE NAME AND PHOTOGRAPH OF INDIVIDUALS CHARGED WITH CRIMES OR DELINQUENCY.
de:HB 59.summary: As amended, bars law enforcement from releasing or publishing the name or photograph of an adult charged with a crime unless the person is charged with a felony and release is necessary for public safety, extending the existing limit for juveniles; takes effect 90 days after enactment.

de:HB 63.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 16 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO FIREWORKS.
de:HB 63.summary: Raises fireworks-law fines, requires retailers to get a State Fire Marshal permit for each sales location and period, requires wholesalers to hold a license, and requires warnings in fireworks ads and written safety notices at sale.

de:HB 84.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 19 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO EMPLOYER-SPONSORED MEETINGS OR COMMUNICATIONS.
de:HB 84.summary: Makes it an unlawful employment practice to penalize employees who decline employer meetings or communications about the employer's political or religious views, including on joining unions; exempts legally required or job-related communications and certain religious and political organizations.

de:HB 89.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLES 19 AND 29 RELATING TO HOME IMPROVEMENT DISPUTE RESOLUTION.
de:HB 89.summary: Directs the Division of Consumer Protection to run a home improvement dispute resolution process requiring contractors to participate in good faith, and allows damages, attorney fees and, if conditions are met, treble damages in later Consumer Fraud Act suits.

de:HB 94.title: AN ACT AMENDING TITLES 10 AND 11 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO LAW ENFORCEMENT COOPERATION IN FEDERAL IMMIGRATION ENFORCEMENT.
de:HB 94.summary: Bars state and local law-enforcement officers from directly participating with federal agencies in civil immigration enforcement at child-serving entities, colleges, places of worship, and health-care facilities unless an exigent circumstance exists, in which case a written report is due within 48 hours.

de:HJR 11.title: DIRECTING THE JUDICIARY TO ESTABLISH A WORKING GROUP TO EXPLORE THE FEASIBILITY OF ESTABLISHING A HOUSING OPPORTUNITY AND POVERTY ELIMINATION (HOPE) COURT PROGRAM IN PARTNERSHIP WITH STATE AGENCIES AND COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS AND TO PROVIDE RECOMMENDATIONS FOR STATEWIDE IMPLEMENTATION.
de:HJR 11.summary: Directs the Judiciary to set up a working group exploring a Housing Opportunity and Poverty Elimination (HOPE) Court Program with state agencies and community organizations, and to recommend statewide implementation.

de:HJR 13.title: DIRECTING THE DEPARTMENT OF LABOR TO STUDY THE CREATION OF A DELAWARE HEALTHCARE APPRENTICESHIP DEGREE PROGRAM AND TO REPORT FINDINGS AND RECOMMENDATIONS TO THE GOVERNOR AND THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY.
de:HJR 13.summary: Directs the Department of Labor, with Education and Health and Social Services, to study a healthcare apprenticeship degree program placing trainees in paid clinical jobs, and to report findings to the Governor and General Assembly.

de:SB 116.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 25 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO RIGHT OF REDEMPTION.
de:SB 116.summary: As amended, lets tenants facing eviction for unpaid rent stop it by paying all past-due rent, costs and fees before the eviction is carried out; not available after two possession judgments for unpaid rent within 18 months.

de:SB 161.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLES 16 AND 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO BEHAVIORAL HEALTH.
de:SB 161.summary: Establishes a statutory framework for licensing, oversight, enforcement, client rights, incident reporting and investigations of behavioral health treatment provider organizations, with licensing authority held by the Division of Substance Abuse and Mental Health.

de:SB 179.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 11 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE DELAWARE SENTENCING GUIDELINES AND ACCOUNTABILITY COMMISSION.
de:SB 179.summary: Repeals the Delaware Sentencing Accountability Commission's current statute and re-establishes it elsewhere in Title 11 with a modernized mission, set membership, defined powers and a required annual data report.

de:SB 189.title: ACT TO AMEND TITLE 18 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO UNFAIR PRACTICES IN THE INSURANCE BUSINESS.
de:SB 189.summary: As amended, lets an injured person without an attorney rescind a motor vehicle accident injury release signed within 30 days of the accident, within 15 days, if they return any payment; requires such releases to carry notice of this right.

de:SB 211.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATED TO AGRICULTURE.
de:SB 211.summary: As amended, increases the Governor's Council on Agriculture from 7 to 9 members, requiring at least one livestock or poultry producer and one farmer aged 40 or younger.

de:SB 219.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 30 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO EXCLUSION OF MILITARY PENSIONS FROM TAXABLE INCOME.
de:SB 219.summary: Phases in a larger state income tax exemption for military pensions, from $12,500 now to $25,000 for all military pensioners by 2029, applied per spouse on joint returns, with 3- or 5-year Delaware residency required for those 60 and older.

de:SB 223.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 14 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE RETENTION OF PERSONNEL RECORDS.
de:SB 223.summary: Requires the Department of Education's regulations on personnel records to cover charter schools, and makes technical corrections to conform to the Legislative Drafting Manual.

de:SB 231.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 14 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO SCHOOL SOCIAL WORKERS.
de:SB 231.summary: Gives school social workers who pass the Association of Social Work Boards clinical exam and hold a Licensed Clinical Social Worker license a salary supplement of 6% of base salary.

de:SB 232.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 11 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO CRIMINAL MISCHIEF.
de:SB 232.summary: As amended, makes criminal mischief a class F felony when someone intentionally damages an authorized emergency vehicle, causing $5,000 or more in losses and leaving the vehicle temporarily unable to respond to emergencies.

de:SB 233.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 21 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE REMOVAL OF ICE AND SNOW FROM VEHICLES.
de:SB 233.summary: Requires drivers to clear accumulated ice and snow from vehicles before operating them ($25 to $75 civil penalty), and sets civil penalties of $200 to $1,500 when ice or snow dislodging from a moving vehicle causes property damage or injury.

de:SB 234.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 20 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO FIRST RESPONDERS.
de:SB 234.summary: Defines "first responder" in Delaware's emergency management law as a law enforcement officer, firefighter, EMS member, hazardous materials team member, 911 dispatcher, emergency manager, or other person responsible for protecting life or property who responds to emergencies.

de:SB 235.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 25 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO RENT INCREASES.
de:SB 235.summary: Removes the sunset date on the manufactured home community rent increase calculations in sections 7052A and 7052B of Title 25, making them permanent in place of the general rent increase grounds in section 7052.

de:SB 249.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 16 AND TITLE 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO SUBSTANCE USE HARM REDUCTION.
de:SB 249.summary: Creates a regulatory framework with legal immunities for substance use harm reduction programs, changes the definition of drug paraphernalia, and decriminalizes paraphernalia possession by people who use drugs while keeping bans tied to manufacturing and distribution.

de:SB 255.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 21 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO TINTING OF MOTOR VEHICLE WINDSHIELD, WINDOWS, OR SIDE WINGS.
de:SB 255.summary: Lowers the minimum visible light transmission for front side window tint from 70% to 50%, states that rear side and rear windows have no minimum, and exempts vehicles operated by law-enforcement officers.

de:SB 26.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 19 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO UNEMPLOYMENT COMPENSATION.
de:SB 26.summary: Lets workers in a non-lockout labor dispute collect unemployment benefits after two weeks, with no wait if the employer breaches a contract or a wage, hours, or working-conditions law, or hires a permanent replacement.

de:SB 27.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE OFFICE OF NEW AMERICANS.
de:SB 27.summary: Establishes the Office of New Americans in the Department of State, led by a director the Secretary appoints, to coordinate information, services and policy recommendations for immigrants, and creates an advisory committee to the office.

de:SB 274.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 16 AND TITLE 21 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO DELAWARE MEDICAL ORDERS FOR SCOPE OF TREATMENT.
de:SB 274.summary: Renames the Delaware Medical Orders for Scope of Treatment as Delaware Portable Orders for Life-Sustaining Treatment (POLST), keeps existing forms valid, and revises rules on completing the orders and patient representatives' authority.

de:SB 278.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 31 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO CHILD CARE ASSISTANCE.
de:SB 278.summary: Requires Purchase of Care child care assistance rules to let DHSS pre-authorize a summer provider for an eligible child at any time after January 1 for enrollment, and bases copayments on household size, income, and full- or half-day care.

de:SB 280.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 11 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THEFT.
de:SB 280.summary: Creates the crime of gift card theft, covering taking or keeping a gift card or its redemption information without consent, tampering with cards or packaging, schemes to obtain them, or using them to obtain value, each with intent to defraud.

de:SB 281.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 31 AND TITLE 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO TECHNICAL UPDATES FOR THE DELAWARE HOSPITAL FOR THE CHRONICALLY ILL.
de:SB 281.summary: Renames the Delaware Hospital for the Chronically Ill the Eleanor Cain Center, removes terms such as "inmates" for residents, and updates the statute to reflect its operation as a skilled nursing facility.

de:SB 283.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 24 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO DENTAL HYGIENE.
de:SB 283.summary: Expands dental hygienists' authority to dispense topical agents and prescribe fluoride under a dentist's standing order, apply sealants without a prior exam if a dentist sees the patient within 12 months, and do assessment and treatment planning.

de:SB 286.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 21 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO COMMERCE AND TRADE.
de:SB 286.summary: Creates a Title 21 chapter on manufacturer-dealer agreements for new motorized vessels, ATVs, off-highway and side-by-side vehicles, and cargo and vessel trailers, requiring written agreements, good cause and notice to end a dealership, inventory repurchase, and paid warranty work.

de:SB 290.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO PUBLIC BODIES.
de:SB 290.summary: Clarifies that quorum does not determine the identity of a public body, which instead depends on the governing document creating the body and the public business being conducted, for purposes of the Freedom of Information Act.

de:SB 292.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 25 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE LANDLORD-TENANT CODE.
de:SB 292.summary: Requires landlords whose tenants' rent is paid from a state reentry fund to help the tenant complete a discharge plan before ending the lease, and narrows exclusions so unlicensed housing operators fall under the Landlord-Tenant Code.

de:SB 293.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 14 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO CHILD CARE LICENSES FOR YOUTH CAMPS.
de:SB 293.summary: Defines "youth camp" in child care law and creates a youth camp license requiring a Division of Public Health permit, Purchase of Care health and safety standards, and, for outdoor camps, access to a weather shelter without a required size.

de:SB 297.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 6 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO CONSUMER PROTECTION.
de:SB 297.summary: Clarifies that the Consumer Fraud Act's "in connection with" language covers unfair or deceptive acts and practices occurring before, during and after the sale, lease, receipt or advertisement of merchandise.

de:SB 300.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 11, TITLE 16, AND TITLE 24 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO DEADLY WEAPONS DEALERS.
de:SB 300.summary: Requires firearm dealers to hold a state license, sets eligibility, security, recordkeeping, background check and training requirements for licensees, and adds State Police inspections, civil penalties and possible license revocation.

de:SB 301.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 16 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO HOSPITAL DISCHARGE PLANS FOR PREGNANT PATIENTS.
de:SB 301.summary: Requires a hospital that discharges a pregnant patient showing signs of labor before delivery to create a discharge plan with aftercare instructions, travel distance and time assessment, verified transportation, and a back-up labor and delivery facility.

de:SB 305.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 21 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO SPECIAL LICENSE PLATES.
de:SB 305.summary: Creates a special license plate for Delaware State University to support student access, academic excellence and university programs.

de:SB 306.title: AN ACT TO AMEND THE CHARTER OF THE CITY OF REHOBOTH BEACH.
de:SB 306.summary: Revises the Rehoboth Beach charter, including removing the Mayor's justice-of-the-peace court powers, ending mileage allowances for non-resident commissioners, and replacing the ordinance-violation penalty cap of $500 or 60 days with a fine of up to $2,500.

de:SB 307.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 26 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO ELIGIBLE TELECOMMUNICATIONS CARRIERS FOR LIFELINE SERVICES.
de:SB 307.summary: Lets Delaware's Public Service Commission designate cellular or wireless providers and resellers as eligible carriers for the federal Lifeline program, a role the FCC now holds. Implementation begins within six months or on notice of final regulations.

de:SB 308.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 26 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE LOAD FORECAST ACCOUNTABILITY ACT.
de:SB 308.summary: As amended, directs the Public Service Commission to investigate and review electric utilities' load forecasts submitted to PJM, coordinate with PJM and other states, access relevant materials, and report to the General Assembly each May 1.

de:SB 309.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 11 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO WORK BY INMATES.
de:SB 309.summary: Ends the Department of Correction's authority to deduct from inmate pay a share of incarceration costs, and discharges all balances owed under that provision.

de:SB 310.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 20 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE DELAWARE DISASTER RECOVERY FUND.
de:SB 310.summary: Creates a Disaster Recovery Fund for assistance to residents and local governments after disasters, activated by the state emergency management director with the concurrence of a Recovery Advisory Council that oversees the fund.

de:SB 311.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 3 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO AGRICULTURE.
de:SB 311.summary: Changes Department of Agriculture licensing rules by requiring certified private pesticide applicators to keep records open to inspection, expanding the definition of landscaper, and removing a character-evidence requirement for grain inspector licenses.

de:SB 312.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 9, TITLE 22, AND TITLE 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO DATA CENTERS.
de:SB 312.summary: Prohibits state agencies, counties and municipalities from signing nondisclosure agreements that restrict public access to information about proposed or actual data centers using 100 megawatts of power or more.

de:SB 315.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE DELAWARE TECHNICAL INNOVATION PROGRAM.
de:SB 315.summary: Lets the Division of Small Business give matching or supplemental grants to Delaware-based small businesses with federal SBIR or STTR awards, with the Council on Development Finance reviewing applications and recommending how funds are allocated.

de:SB 317.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 1 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO VETERANS MONTH.
de:SB 317.summary: Designates May as Veterans Month in Delaware.

de:SB 318.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 21 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO SPECIAL LICENSE PLATES.
de:SB 318.summary: Discontinues the Delaware State Education Association centennial special license plate and replaces it with an updated association plate, while previously issued centennial plates remain valid.

de:SB 319.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 18, TITLE 29, AND TITLE 31 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO COVERAGE FOR DIAGNOSTIC SERVICES AND TREATMENT FOR MENOPAUSE, PERIMENOPAUSE, AND MENOPAUSE AND PERIMENOPAUSE SYMPTOMS.
de:SB 319.summary: Requires individual, group and state employee health plans and Medicaid to cover medically necessary diagnosis and treatment for menopause and perimenopause, including FDA-approved hormone therapy, consultations, testing and non-hormonal treatments.

de:SB 320.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 16 AND TITLE 24 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO PHARMACY AND PHARMACISTS.
de:SB 320.summary: As amended, lets pharmacists prescribe over-the-counter products, opioid antagonists, and FDA-labeled drugs for minor, self-limiting or test-guided conditions, plus opioid use disorder medications under a standing order; bars prescribing other controlled substances.

de:SB 321.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 26 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATED TO UTILITY BILLING.
de:SB 321.summary: Requires electric utilities to offer consolidated billing for community energy subscriptions, netting subscription charges against bill credits and paying them to subscription coordinators; it is the default for new facilities, and older facilities may opt out.

de:SB 322.title: ACT TO AMEND TITLE 14 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO LOCAL SCHOOL TAXES.
de:SB 322.summary: Repeals school districts' ability to raise tax rates up to 10% after a reassessment, instead capping collections based on prior revenue and property growth, and lets districts raise referendum-approved taxes up to 2% a year without a referendum under conditions.

de:SB 324.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 11 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO DEADLY WEAPONS.
de:SB 324.summary: Exempts a constable agency representative buying handguns for the employer's constables from certain firearm background-check and permit requirements, and makes the permit void, or revocable by the State Bureau of Identification director, if the person stops qualifying.

de:SB 325.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 16 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO FIRE PREVENTION.
de:SB 325.summary: Requires fire and ambulance company applicants and members with public contact to get fingerprint criminal background checks, reviewed by the State Fire Prevention Commission, which bars those with listed offenses such as violent felonies; confidential waivers for extraordinary circumstances. Takes effect 180 days after enactment.

de:SB 328.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 14 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO SCHOOL BUILDING SAFETY.
de:SB 328.summary: Requires the Department of Education to set the school facilities evaluation instrument through regulation rather than guidance, and clarifies that the hazardous materials repair standard includes lead.

de:SB 329.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 15 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO ELECTION RESULTS.
de:SB 329.summary: Updates the Superior Court's procedures for certifying general election results, adding early voting and provisional ballots to the materials the Department of Elections must provide, and consolidating requirements for election certificates.

de:SB 330.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE DELAWARE AFRICAN AMERICAN HERITAGE AND CULTURE COMMISSION.
de:SB 330.summary: Establishes the Delaware African American Heritage and Culture Commission as a statewide resource for preserving and sharing the state's African American culture and heritage.

de:SB 332.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 21 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO SPECIAL VANITY LICENSE PLATES.
de:SB 332.summary: Allows special vanity license plates to be transferred between owners without violating the federal court injunction that bars Delaware from issuing new vanity plates or recalling existing ones. Takes effect six months after enactment.

de:SB 334.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLES 18 AND 29 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO HEALTH CARE.
de:SB 334.summary: Creates the Health Care Professional Access Act, requiring carriers from 2028 to use a uniform credentialing application, confirm a clean application within 15 days and decide within 30 more, grant provisional credentials in listed cases, and give notice and a hearing before ending credentials.

de:SB 340.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 16 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO LONG TERM CARE FACILITIES
de:SB 340.summary: As amended, requires nursing facilities, assisted living facilities and group homes for persons with mental illness (not state-run) to carry general and professional liability insurance of at least $1 million per claim and $3 million aggregate each, including abuse coverage, effective 180 days after enactment.

de:SB 341.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 16 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE DELAWARE HEALTH INFORMATION NETWORK.
de:SB 341.summary: Names the Delaware Health Information Network as the state's sanctioned health data utility provider, clarifies its authority to contract with organizations, and aligns its data uses for analytics and research with federal law.

de:SB 345.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 11 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO OFFENSES INVOLVING PUBLIC INDECENCY.
de:SB 345.summary: Replaces references to minors engaging in or being prostituted with "exploited," defined as acts that would be prostitution if the minor were 18 or older. Adds an "illicit massage establishment" definition only if House Bill 409 is enacted.

de:SB 346.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 7 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO APPEALS TO THE ENVIRONMENTAL APPEALS BOARD.
de:SB 346.summary: Changes Environmental Appeals Board procedures to streamline appeals, lets substantially affected persons appeal subaqueous lands permits, and removes appeals of the Secretary's Coastal Zone Management Act consistency findings.

de:SB 347.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 6 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE MEDICAL DEBT PROTECTION ACT
de:SB 347.summary: Adds levying on a patient's tangible personal property to the collection actions medical creditors and debt collectors may not use for health-care debt, and requires parties collecting medical debt to disclose in court pleadings whether they are a medical creditor, debt collector, or neither.

de:SB 53.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 3 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO THE DELAWARE FARM TO COMMUNITY PROGRAM.
de:SB 53.summary: Codifies the Farm to Community Program, run by the Department of Agriculture with the Delaware Farm and Food Council and subject to funding, to help community outlets buy local food products from farmers for free food distribution sites.

de:SB 94.title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 24 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO RESPIRATORY CARE PRACTITIONERS.
de:SB 94.summary: Adds management of extracorporeal life support (ECMO and ECCO2R) and associated integrated therapies to the scope of practice of respiratory care practitioners, and defines "associated integrated therapies."

de:SJR 14.title: DIRECTING THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION TO CONDUCT A STUDY AND REPORT ON WORKFORCE DATA RELATING TO PUBLIC EDUCATION SUPPORT PROFESSIONALS.
de:SJR 14.summary: Directs the Department of Education to report by November 2, 2026 on education support professionals' staffing levels, vacancies, average wages, and the number earning under $40 per hour.

de:SJR 15.title: DIRECTING THE DELAWARE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION TO REEVALUATE THE USE OF THE SAT IN DELAWARE, ENGAGE EDUCATORS IN MODERNIZING THE STATE ACCOUNTABILITY FRAMEWORK, INCLUDING DEVELOPMENT OF A COHERENT HIGH SCHOOL ASSESSMENT SYSTEM, AND DEVELOP ADDITIONAL MEASURES OF STUDENT ACHIEVEMENT AND READINESS.
de:SJR 15.summary: Directs the Department of Education to reevaluate using the SAT in the state accountability system while still offering it during the school day, develop a revised accountability framework with educators, and explore a new high school assessment system.

de:SJR 18.title: DESIGNATING AUGUST 31, 2026, AS "INTERNATIONAL OVERDOSE AWARENESS DAY" IN THE STATE OF DELAWARE AND REQUIRING THE STATE FLAG TO BE FLOWN AT HALF-STAFF IN OBSERVANCE.
de:SJR 18.summary: Designates August 31, 2026 as International Overdose Awareness Day in Delaware and requires the state flag to be flown at half-staff that day.

de:SJR 20.title: DIRECTING THE DIVISION OF MEDICAID AND MEDICAL ASSISTANCE TO EVALUATE ASSESSMENTS FOR INDIVIDUALS RECEIVING HOME AND COMMUNITY-BASED SERVICES.
de:SJR 20.summary: Directs the Department of Health and Social Services to evaluate using independent assessment tools and assessors to determine support needs for people eligible for home and community-based services, reporting by March 1, 2027.

fl:HB 1019.title: Perfluoroalkyl and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances
fl:HB 1019.summary: Bans nonemergency use of PFAS-containing firefighting foam from July 1, 2026, its sale from July 1, 2027 and possession from July 1, 2029, with exceptions; requires inventories and disposal plans filed with DEP and quarterly PFAS sampling by larger public wastewater facilities.

fl:HB 1031.title: Customer Service Callback Queues
fl:HB 1031.summary: Creates a pilot program requiring the Department of Commerce to use a callback queue to return calls from reemployment assistance claimants in the order received, by the end of the next business day.

fl:HB 1069.title: Background Screenings
fl:HB 1069.summary: Deems independent sanctioning authorities qualified entities in the Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse, requires qualified entities to name a user administrator, and bars people screened there from denying or failing to acknowledge expunged or sealed arrests.

fl:HB 1073.title: Public Education
fl:HB 1073.summary: Creates a District School Board Members' Bill of Rights giving members access to district documents (requests unrelated to a noticed meeting filled within 10 business days) and budget information, and bars districts from requiring or incentivizing employees to sign nondisclosure agreements.

fl:HB 1081.title: Cybersecurity Experiential Learning
fl:HB 1081.summary: Requires Cyber Florida, subject to appropriation, to develop a Cybersecurity Experiential Learning Program and report on participation in and improvement of the program.

fl:HB 1085.title: Local Government Cyber Security
fl:HB 1085.summary: Creates a Local Government Cybersecurity Protection Program within the Florida Digital Service awarding cybersecurity products and services to local governments, with preference for fiscally constrained counties, lets local governments buy through its contracts at their own cost, and repeals July 1, 2031 unless renewed.

fl:HB 1087.title: Pub. Rec./Office of Financial Regulation
fl:HB 1087.summary: Reenacts public records exemptions for virtual currency kiosk businesses, qualified stablecoin issuers, and gold and silver coin custodians, with updated public necessity statements.

fl:HB 1115.title: Grants for Genetic Counseling Education
fl:HB 1115.summary: Creates a Genetic Counseling Education Enhancement Grant Program in the State University System, funded subject to appropriation, with awards based on program excellence and annual reporting.

fl:HB 1121.title: Aging and Disability Services
fl:HB 1121.summary: Revises state aging and disability services: sets a pre-enrollment list for long-term care, caps Area Agency on Aging chief executive pay at 150% of the Elderly Affairs secretary's, and changes guardian continuing-education and discipline rules.

fl:HB 1175.title: Safety Design Standards for Office Surgery Suites
fl:HB 1175.summary: Directs the Florida Building Commission and State Fire Marshal to adopt, by January 1, 2027, safety design standards for office surgery suites that let physicians treat up to six patients at once on an outpatient basis.

fl:HB 1201.title: Student Health and Safety
fl:HB 1201.summary: Revises Department of Health duties on epilepsy education, requirements for student seizure action plans, and which school employees must be trained in seizure care, with training valid for five years.

fl:HB 1245.title: Biosolids Management
fl:HB 1245.summary: Bars land application of bulk Class AA biosolids products above the agronomic rate, requires application records kept and available to DEP, and requires UF/IFAS to publish recommended rates; takes effect November 1, 2026.

fl:HB 1285.title: Biosolids Management
fl:HB 1285.summary: Bars the Department of Environmental Protection, from July 1, 2027, from issuing or renewing permits for land application of septage as Class B biosolids if a government-run wastewater plant within 30 miles accepts septage for higher treatment.

fl:HB 1293.title: Fraudulent Entry of Residential Dwellings
fl:HB 1293.summary: Makes it a third-degree felony to take possession of a rental home by knowingly giving false identity information, presenting forged documents, or impersonating someone on a rental application. Lets landlords terminate the lease for such fraud without a chance to cure.

fl:HB 131.title: Curators of Estates
fl:HB 131.summary: Revises when a court may appoint a curator of estates, changes bond requirements, and requires curators to file detailed reports that the court must review.

fl:HB 1329.title: Local Government Finances
fl:HB 1329.summary: Lengthens county and city budget website posting (tentative budgets 5 days before hearings instead of 2, final budgets 5 years instead of 2), requires budget reduction workshops, and sets new requirements for impact fee increases beyond phase-in limits.

fl:HB 1343.title: Insurance Customer Representative Licensing Qualifications
fl:HB 1343.summary: Changes the ways applicants can qualify for the insurance customer representative license and requires the Department of Education to develop an insurance and personal finance course.

fl:HB 1389.title: Affordable Housing
fl:HB 1389.summary: Extends Live Local Act affordable-housing zoning preemptions to land owned by counties, cities, or school districts and to religious-institution property over 3 acres with a worship house for 10 years, and bars setbacks or stepbacks that restrict project height.

fl:HB 1405.title: Statewide Project for Missing Persons with Special Needs
fl:HB 1405.summary: Revives and amends the statewide project for missing persons with special needs, operated through the centers for autism and related disabilities, and appropriates $1,000,000.

fl:HB 145.title: Claims Against the Government
fl:HB 145.summary: Raises limits on state and local government payment of tort claims without further legislative action from $200,000 per person and $300,000 per incident to $350,000 and $500,000, and revises deadlines for some claims.

fl:HB 1451.title: Utility Services
fl:HB 1451.summary: Requires public meetings before municipal utilities approve out-of-city service agreements, ends the 25% surcharge on outside water and sewer customers (phased out by 2029 where bonds require), cuts the allowed rate gap from 50% to 25%, and preempts a 2025 Gainesville utility-authority charter amendment.

fl:HB 1509.title: Veterinarian Licensure by Endorsement
fl:HB 1509.summary: Changes veterinarian licensure by endorsement: drops the requirement of holding an out-of-state license for the prior three years and instead requires a valid, active license in good standing in another state, D.C., or a U.S. territory.

fl:HB 1515.title: Pub. Rec./Uterine Fibroid Research Database
fl:HB 1515.summary: Exempts from public records disclosure certain records and personal identifying information submitted to the Department of Health for the uterine fibroid research database.

fl:HB 1525.title: Lewd or Lascivious Acts
fl:HB 1525.summary: Repeals the "unnatural and lascivious acts" statute and creates a third-degree felony for exposing sexual organs lewdly, or performing certain sexual acts without contact, while observing a child under 16 for sexual arousal or gratification.

fl:HB 175.title: Payment Stablecoin
fl:HB 175.summary: Creates a licensing framework for state-qualified payment stablecoin issuers, modeled on the federal GENIUS Act, requiring a money services business license or a trust company certificate of approval from the Office of Financial Regulation, effective October 1, 2026.

fl:HB 177.title: Offices of Criminal Conflict and Civil Regional Counsel
fl:HB 177.summary: Lets a court appoint a different regional counsel office, before private counsel, to represent an indigent defendant in a death penalty case when the original regional counsel office has a conflict.

fl:HB 199.title: Veterans Affairs
fl:HB 199.summary: Moves eligibility decisions for veterans treatment court from the state attorney to the court and its multidisciplinary team, which considers the state attorney's recommendation. Lets sentencing courts place servicemembers and veterans with nonviolent felony offenses in a postadjudicatory program whose judge hears probation violations.

fl:HB 253.title: Veterans Dental Care Grant Program
fl:HB 253.summary: Sets the purpose of the Veterans Dental Care Grant Program as providing oral health care to Florida veterans with incomes up to 400 percent of the federal poverty level.

fl:HB 271.title: Foreign and Alien Bail Bond Insurers
fl:HB 271.summary: Requires foreign and alien bail bond insurers to report bail bond premiums to the Office of Insurance Regulation as domestic insurers do, with direct written premiums of at least 6.5% of the consideration received.

fl:HB 273.title: Special District Funding
fl:HB 273.summary: As passed by the House, adds certain special districts to state agreements allowing agencies to pay invoices for verified performance as due, and for downtown development districts requires voter approval of added territory, caps administrative costs at 10% of budget, and requires municipal approval of budgets.

fl:HB 277.title: Domestic Violence and Protective Injunctions
fl:HB 277.summary: Raises penalties for domestic violence offenses by people with a prior domestic violence conviction, creates electronic monitoring pilot programs in one county and one judicial circuit, and requires dating and sexual violence injunctions to be entered in a statewide system.

fl:HB 325.title: Education and Workforce Development for Inmates
fl:HB 325.summary: Lets the Department of Transportation fund inmate certification and training, including commercial driver license training, through grants to private educational providers, and lets inmates be transported in or drive state vehicles with a certified correctional officer present.

fl:HB 327.title: Uterine Fibroid Research Database
fl:HB 327.summary: Removes the ban on including personal identifying information of women with uterine fibroids in the Department of Health’s uterine fibroid research database; takes effect only if HB 1515 or similar legislation becomes law.

fl:HB 355.title: Health Care Patient Protection
fl:HB 355.summary: Requires hospital emergency departments to adopt pediatric care policies, train staff annually, record weights in kilograms, and designate a pediatric emergency care coordinator. Directs the state health agency to set minimum pediatric standards and publish hospitals' pediatric readiness assessment scores.

fl:HB 359.title: Search Warrants
fl:HB 359.summary: Allows search warrants to recover deceased bodies and for drones, lets officers apply remotely by audio-video, and sets timing rules for returning warrants and reviewing data from seized devices.

fl:HB 397.title: Violations of Pretrial Release Conditions for Violent Crimes
fl:HB 397.summary: Makes it a first degree misdemeanor to willfully violate a no-contact pretrial release order when the arrest was for violent offenses such as murder, assault, stalking, or sexual battery; repeat violations are third degree felonies.

fl:HB 4001.title: Jefferson County
fl:HB 4001.summary: Caps payments to out-of-contract providers for Jefferson County jail inmates' medical care at 110 percent of the Medicare rate (125 percent for providers with a negative operating margin) and emergency medical transport at 110 percent. Excludes county-run hospitals.

fl:HB 4005.title: City of Naples Airport Authority, Collier County
fl:HB 4005.summary: Changes the City of Naples Airport Authority from appointed to elected members: five seats (three city residents, two county residents outside the city) elected countywide starting in 2026, with candidates needing five years in financial management, small business or aerospace.

fl:HB 4007.title: Martin County
fl:HB 4007.summary: Repeals a 1967 Martin County welfare repayment law and requires the county to set by ordinance how its health care fund is split among licensed hospitals. Defines indigent residents for hospital care and removes the County Health Care Review Board provisions.

fl:HB 4011.title: St. Lucie County Mosquito Control District, St. Lucie County
fl:HB 4011.summary: Revises the boundaries of the St. Lucie County Mosquito Control District and requires a referendum.

fl:HB 4017.title: Nassau County
fl:HB 4017.summary: Repeals the laws creating the Nassau County Recreation and Water Conservation and Control District No. 1, abolishes the district, and transfers its assets and liabilities to the Nassau County Board of County Commissioners.

fl:HB 4019.title: Compensation for Health Care Services for Inmates in Lake County
fl:HB 4019.summary: Limits payments to out-of-contract providers for Lake County jail inmates' care to 110 percent of the Medicare rate (125 percent with a negative operating margin), sets trauma-alert care at trauma centers at 175 percent, and limits emergency transport to 110 percent.

fl:HB 4025.title: Martin and Palm Beach Counties
fl:HB 4025.summary: Directs the state to convey about 41.1 acres known as Tequesta Park to the Village of Tequesta within 60 days. The village must keep it as a public park for recreation, education, and conservation; if sold, ownership reverts to the state.

fl:HB 4027.title: Hillsborough County Public Schools, Hillsborough County
fl:HB 4027.summary: Provides for an elected, rather than appointed, Hillsborough County school superintendent, elected in a partisan election to four-year terms from 2028, subject to approval in a countywide referendum at the 2026 general election.

fl:HB 4035.title: Palm Beach County
fl:HB 4035.summary: Changes Palm Beach County contractor certification: removes the exam-at-least-every-3-months rule, the four-exams-per-year cap, the 60-day wait between attempts, and the Board's notice to appear for an exam.

fl:HB 4037.title: Pasco County Mosquito Control District, Pasco County
fl:HB 4037.summary: Revises term limits for governing board members of the Pasco County Mosquito Control District and requires the county commission to designate geographical districts by specified numerals.

fl:HB 4041.title: Compensation for Health Care Services for Inmates in Indian River County
fl:HB 4041.summary: Caps payments to providers without county contracts for treating Indian River County jail inmates at 110 percent of the Medicare rate (125 percent for some with negative operating margins), sets trauma-center payment for trauma-alert inmates at 175 percent, and caps ambulance payments at 110 percent.

fl:HB 4043.title: Citrus County Hospital Board, Citrus County
fl:HB 4043.summary: Requires the Citrus County Hospital Board to adopt a dissolution plan by September 30, 2026, repeals its governing laws effective October 1, 2026, keeps its community trust or foundation operating, and transfers its assets and liabilities to the county commission.

fl:HB 4045.title: Jacksonville Aviation Authority, Consolidated City of Jacksonville, Duval County
fl:HB 4045.summary: Makes the Jacksonville Aviation Authority responsible for economic development of Cecil Airport as an aerospace hub, requires an annual development plan presentation to the Jacksonville City Council, and revises the authority's purchase threshold amounts.

fl:HB 4051.title: Pace Fire Rescue District, Santa Rosa County
fl:HB 4051.summary: Bars the Pace Fire Rescue District from levying non-ad valorem assessments on tax-exempt churches and religious institutions, bases commercial and industrial assessments on total parcel square footage, and revises the maximum residential, commercial and industrial assessment rates.

fl:HB 4055.title: City of Lake Wales, Polk County
fl:HB 4055.summary: Lets alcohol vendors licensed for on-premises consumption in Lake Wales' Arts, Culture and Entertainment District allow patrons to carry open containers out and drink within the district.

fl:HB 4059.title: Compensation for Health Care Services for Inmates in Polk County
fl:HB 4059.summary: Caps payments to health care providers without county contracts for treating Polk County jail inmates at 110 percent of the Medicare rate (125 percent for some with negative operating margins), and caps ambulance payments at 110 percent.

fl:HB 4061.title: Hillsborough County
fl:HB 4061.summary: Creates the Land Reserve Stewardship District, an independent special district of about 3,707 acres in Hillsborough County with a five-member board that can issue bonds and levy special assessments; the board starts under landowner control.

fl:HB 4063.title: West Palm Beach Police Pension Fund - Special Act Amendment
fl:HB 4063.summary: Amends the West Palm Beach Police Pension Fund's special act, revising membership, retirement age and service, benefit calculation, DROP, death benefits, investments and reemployment rules.

fl:HB 4075.title: Town of Davie, Broward County
fl:HB 4075.summary: Allows a sign on specified agriculturally zoned property in the Town of Davie, as an exception to general law.

fl:HB 4079.title: Marion County
fl:HB 4079.summary: Creates the Uplands Stewardship District in Marion County, an independent special district with set boundaries, a board, budget and financing powers, and notice requirements for home buyers.

fl:HB 4091.title: Sarasota and Manatee Counties
fl:HB 4091.summary: Creates the University Town Center Improvement District, an independent special taxing district in Sarasota and Manatee Counties, with a board of supervisors, defined boundaries, non-ad valorem assessments and bond authority.

fl:HB 4095.title: Headwaters Water Control District, Indian River County
fl:HB 4095.summary: Creates the Headwaters Water Control District in Indian River County as a public corporation, with a charter, boundaries, canal maintenance provisions and rules for charter amendments.

fl:HB 4103.title: Apalachicola Water and Sewer District, Franklin County
fl:HB 4103.summary: Creates the Apalachicola Water and Sewer District in Franklin County, bars the city from incurring certain additional debt, and requires an interlocal agreement transferring water and sewer service, assets, debts and contracts to the district.

fl:HB 4105.title: Port St. Joe Port Authority, Franklin, Gadsden, Gulf, and Liberty Counties
fl:HB 4105.summary: Expands the Port St. Joe Port Authority, now covering Gulf County, to include Franklin, Gadsden and Liberty Counties, with a six-member governor-appointed board (a Port St. Joe chair, two Gulf County members, one from each other county) serving four-year terms.

fl:HB 425.title: Historic Cemeteries Program
fl:HB 425.summary: Requires counties and municipalities to administratively approve rezoning or land-use changes for excess vacant land of a historic African-American cemetery sold to fund its maintenance, for development compatible with adjacent uses.

fl:HB 429.title: Criteria for Determining Criminal Gang Membership
fl:HB 429.summary: Changes the criteria for identifying a criminal gang member, including admission in person or online, being claimed by a gang, being identified by a parent, guardian, or spouse living with the person, and using defined gang-related language online; effective October 1, 2026.

fl:HB 453.title: Requirements for a Standard High School Diploma
fl:HB 453.summary: Makes two years of marching band satisfy both the physical education and performing arts credits for a standard high school diploma, and lets students with disabilities meet the physical education requirement through Special Olympics participation.

fl:HB 461.title: Volunteering at Polling Locations
fl:HB 461.summary: Allows registered or pre-registered high school students to volunteer to assist poll workers for community service hours, as an exception to the ban on election officials accepting donated money or personal services.

fl:HB 47.title: Specific Medical Diagnoses in Child Protective Investigations
fl:HB 47.summary: Creates exceptions and procedures for child protective investigations involving specific medical diagnoses, including consultation with physicians or nurses with relevant experience, medical record requests, and written reports on medical examinations.

fl:HB 477.title: Drug Paraphernalia
fl:HB 477.summary: Excludes certain narcotic drug testing products from the legal definition of drug paraphernalia.

fl:HB 491.title: Faith-based Content in Batterers' Intervention Programs
fl:HB 491.summary: Allows batterers' intervention programs to offer supplemental faith-based activities, while prohibiting programs from requiring participation in them.

fl:HB 5001E.title: General Appropriations Act
fl:HB 5001E.summary: Appropriates money for state agency operations, capital outlay and other purposes for the fiscal year July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027, plus supplemental appropriations for the period ending June 30, 2026.

fl:HB 5003E.title: Implementing the 2026-2027 General Appropriations Act
fl:HB 5003E.summary: Implements the 2026-27 General Appropriations Act by revising education funding calculations, authorizing agencies to submit budget amendments, making many provisions expire July 1, 2027, and requiring the Department of Financial Services to replace the FLAIR state accounting system.

fl:HB 505.title: Virtual Currency Kiosks
fl:HB 505.summary: Requires virtual currency kiosk businesses to register with the state, show an on-screen fraud warning, cap daily transactions at $2,000 for new and $10,000 for existing customers, issue receipts, and fully refund a first transaction reported as fraud within 60 days.

fl:HB 5201E.title: Collective Bargaining
fl:HB 5201E.summary: Provides that 2026-27 collective bargaining issues at impasse between the state and certified representatives of state employee bargaining units are resolved under instructions in the General Appropriations Act and its implementing legislation.

fl:HB 5203E.title: Government Administration
fl:HB 5203E.summary: Creates the Florida Accountability Office within the Legislature, including a division that handles complaints and investigates appropriations projects; revises Auditor General duties, audit procedures, whistle-blower provisions, and budget transfer and amendment rules.

fl:HB 5205E.title: Retirement
fl:HB 5205E.summary: Revises the employer retirement contribution rates for each membership class and subclass of the Florida Retirement System.

fl:HB 5207E.title: Department of Management Services
fl:HB 5207E.summary: Charges state agencies a monthly health insurance assessment for each vacant position, repeals minority business enterprise certification, renames the Office of Supplier Diversity the Office of Supplier Development, changes state employee prescription drug rules, and sets Legislature space rules in the Capitol Complex.

fl:HB 5301E.title: Health Care
fl:HB 5301E.summary: Changes Medicaid provider reimbursement methodology, removes health care innovation provisions, and creates a Department of Children and Families eligibility assistance program run by an independent contractor.

fl:HB 5403E.title: Correctional Facilities Financing and Capital Improvements
fl:HB 5403E.summary: Appropriates funds to the Department of Corrections, directs it to begin planning and design of certain facilities, allows the state to issue bonds for them, and creates a financing oversight committee.

fl:HB 5501E.title: Documentary Stamp Tax Distributions
fl:HB 5501E.summary: Raises the cap on documentary stamp tax proceeds credited to the State Transportation Trust Fund from $360.08 million to $420.08 million, adds a 14 percent Florida Rail Enterprise share, lowers other program shares, and bars South Florida Regional Transportation Authority funding from rail enterprise money.

fl:HB 559.title: Animal Welfare
fl:HB 559.summary: Creates offenses for causing or enticing a minor to commit or witness animal cruelty, fighting or sexual acts with animals, requires an online registry of animal cruelty convicts, and raises civil penalties and severity rankings.

fl:HB 5601E.title: Higher Education
fl:HB 5601E.summary: Transfers University of South Florida Sarasota/Manatee campus property and related liabilities to New College of Florida, lets university boards of trustees set out-of-state fees for nonresident students, and removes the nonresident undergraduate block tuition requirement.

fl:HB 561.title: Educator Preparation and Certification
fl:HB 561.summary: Changes educator certification: lets educator preparation programs enroll participants in introductory coursework, allows temporary certificates for some with expired credentials, and revises reinstatement and inservice rules.

fl:HB 565.title: Agency for Persons with Disabilities
fl:HB 565.summary: Revises the definition of developmental disability, adds Tatton-Brown-Rahman syndrome, requires level 2 screening for employees of residential facilities and adult day training programs, and orders university surveys and a gap analysis of Agency for Persons with Disabilities services.

fl:HB 5701E.title: Petroleum Cleanup Programs
fl:HB 5701E.summary: Removes the 2025-2026 fiscal year limit on barring program deductibles and copayments and enforcing monetary caps in two petroleum cleanup programs, with costs absorbed by the Inland Protection Trust Fund.

fl:HB 625.title: Justice Administrative Commission
fl:HB 625.summary: Expands the Justice Administrative Commission from four to seven members by adding a third state attorney, a criminal defense attorney and a judge, each appointed by a specified official.

fl:HB 6507.title: Relief/L.E./Department of Children and Families
fl:HB 6507.summary: Appropriates $3.8 million to compensate L.E. for injuries and damages the bill attributes to Department of Children and Families negligence, with limits on compensation and attorney fees.

fl:HB 6509.title: Relief/Estate of Mark LaGatta/Department of Transportation
fl:HB 6509.summary: Appropriates $1.2 million to compensate the Estate of Mark LaGatta for injuries and damages the bill attributes to Department of Transportation negligence, with limits on compensation and attorney fees.

fl:HB 6515.title: Relief/Lourdes Latour and Edward Latour/Miami-Dade County
fl:HB 6515.summary: Directs Miami-Dade County to pay $500,000 to Lourdes and Edward Latour under a settlement of a negligence claim, with attorney fees limited to 25% of the award.

fl:HB 6517.title: Relief/Heriberto A. Sanchez-Mayen/City of St. Petersburg
fl:HB 6517.summary: Directs the City of St. Petersburg to pay $2.3 million to Heriberto A. Sanchez-Mayen for injuries from a prisoner-transport van incident, as full compensation for related claims, with attorney fees limited to 25 percent.

fl:HB 7031.title: Internal Revenue Code
fl:HB 7031.summary: As passed by the House, updates corporate income tax to the federal code as of 2026 with listed exceptions, requires vacation rental advertising platforms to collect taxes, adds sales tax exemptions for home hardening products, firearm accessories, and hunting, fishing, and camping goods, and lowers slot machine and cardroom taxes.

fl:HB 7031E.title: Taxation
fl:HB 7031E.summary: Changes Florida taxes, including requiring vacation rental advertising platforms to collect and remit taxes, a refund-based sales tax exemption for home-hardening products, lower slot machine and cardroom tax rates, estimated property taxes on online home listings from February 2027, and new tax credits.

fl:HB 755.title: Areas of Critical State Concern
fl:HB 755.summary: Lets public landowners exempt work on Habitat for Humanity 99-year-lease land in areas of critical state concern from bond requirements, extends at least $5 million a year of Florida Forever Keys land purchases through 2035-36, and revises the oil drilling ban near estuarine reserves.

fl:HB 757.title: School Safety
fl:HB 757.summary: Lets employees and faculty at public postsecondary institutions serve as armed school guardians, requires those institutions to have threat management teams, risk assessments, and active-assailant plans, and makes discharging a firearm within 1,000 feet of a school during school hours a second-degree felony, with exceptions.

fl:HB 797.title: Nonprofit Corporations
fl:HB 797.summary: Renames Florida's not-for-profit corporation law the Florida Nonprofit Corporation Act and revises rules on members, meetings, proxy voting, board elections, director and officer liability, mergers and property held for charitable purposes.

fl:HB 809.title: Temporary Certificates for Practice in Areas of Critical Need
fl:HB 809.summary: Revises when state medical, osteopathic and nursing boards may issue temporary certificates for practice in areas of critical need, and lets holders keep providing primary care after an area loses its critical-need designation under certain conditions.

fl:HB 851.title: Professional Learning for Instructional and School Administrative Personnel
fl:HB 851.summary: Requires certain professional learning systems for instructional and school administrative personnel to offer at least one autism-specific professional learning opportunity.

fl:HB 867.title: Dry Needling by Occupational Therapists
fl:HB 867.summary: Authorizes occupational therapists to perform dry needling and requires the licensing board to set standards, including two years of practice, 50 hours of training, patient consent, and no delegation to others.

fl:HB 883.title: Protected Cell Captive Insurance Companies
fl:HB 883.summary: Allows sponsors to form protected cell captive insurance companies, limits the risks they may insure, revises capital and surplus requirements for captive insurers, and sets filing and approval rules with the Office of Insurance Regulation.

fl:HB 89.title: Veterinary Prescription Disclosure
fl:HB 89.summary: Requires veterinarians, before dispensing medication, to tell clients they may get a written prescription filled at any pharmacy or, if offered, at the vet; get a signed acknowledgment; and post a notice at checkout. Exempts emergencies and controlled substances.

fl:HB 893.title: Trust Fund Interest for Purposes Approved by Supreme Court
fl:HB 893.summary: Lets financial institutions hold lawyer trust accounts whose interest funds free legal services for low-income people through a Supreme Court-established entity, and sets the rate at Wall Street Journal prime minus 3 points, between 0.25 and 1.5 percent.

fl:HB 905.title: Foreign Influence
fl:HB 905.summary: Requires public officers found to have accepted gifts from foreign terrorist organizations or foreign countries of concern to repay double, ends public agreements with such countries, raises penalties for crimes benefiting foreign governments, and bars adoption and surrogacy contracts involving their citizens or residents.

fl:HB 915.title: Medical Assistance Eligibility for Working Individuals with Disabilities
fl:HB 915.summary: Creates the Working People with Disabilities program in the Agency for Health Care Administration, setting eligibility, income and asset rules for Medicaid coverage of adults with disabilities who work.

fl:HB 925.title: Clerks of the Court
fl:HB 925.summary: Lets court clerks keep all revenue collected above the state's projection instead of 50%, keep 10% of school-bus stop-signal civil penalties and more municipal traffic fees, and publish real-property legal notices on a website.

fl:HB 967.title: Electronic Payments Made to Units of Local Governments
fl:HB 967.summary: Requires all local governments, including counties and constitutional officers, to accept credit card, debit card, and electronic fund transfer payments unless another form is required by law, and to offer a way to pay online. Effective July 1, 2026.

fl:HJR 1F.title: Save our Homes from Excessive Property Taxes
fl:HJR 1F.summary: Adds to the proposed constitutional amendment a requirement that the Legislature give local governments any funds needed for public safety services, including law enforcement, fire, emergency medical services, and corrections, if the amendment leaves a local government unable to fully fund them.

fl:SB 1004.title: Domestic Animals
fl:SB 1004.summary: Expands animal cruelty offender data the Department of Law Enforcement posts online, by January 1, 2027; lengthens pet buyers’ refund, exchange and notice periods and adds pet-dealer disclosure duties; has the Department of Business and Professional Regulation develop voluntary dog-breeding best practices.

fl:SB 1022.title: Children’s Initiatives
fl:SB 1022.summary: Establishes the Bay County 32401 Children's Initiative and the Pompano RYZE Children's Initiative, run by nonprofits and subject to public records, meetings and procurement laws.

fl:SB 1028.title: Citizens Property Insurance Corporation
fl:SB 1028.summary: Requires Citizens Property Insurance Corporation to create, by January 1, 2027, two clearinghouses diverting commercial applicants and policyholders to authorized or surplus lines insurers; risks receiving comparable offers become ineligible for Citizens coverage.

fl:SB 1030.title: Recovery Residences
fl:SB 1030.summary: Requires the Department of Children and Families to require only level 2 background screening when 5 percent or more of a licensed entity's controlling ownership transfers, and bars it from requiring certain existing licensed providers to admit individuals during probationary licensing.

fl:SB 1074.title: One-cent Piece
fl:SB 1074.summary: Allows sales tax dealers to round cash transactions to the nearest nickel if the penny is no longer produced, without changing the sales price or tax collected.

fl:SB 1092.title: Podiatric Medicine
fl:SB 1092.summary: Lets podiatric physicians use cellular or tissue-based products not FDA-approved under set conditions, requiring patient consent forms and advertising notices, and narrows which podiatrists must take certain continuing education.

fl:SB 110.title: Homestead Exemptions
fl:SB 110.summary: Treats lessees under a residential or condominium lease of 98 years or more as holding legal or beneficial title for the homestead exemption, even if the lease ends on the lessee's death.

fl:SB 1180.title: Community Development Districts
fl:SB 1180.summary: Allows recall of elected community development district supervisors by petition and referendum, and exempts districts enforcing deed restrictions from synthetic turf rules.

fl:SB 124.title: Florida Virtual School
fl:SB 124.summary: Removes priority course access for certain Florida Virtual School students, lets the school contract with public and private entities, and requires most of its employees to be state employees for retirement-system purposes.

fl:SB 1246.title: Linking Industry to Nursing Education Fund
fl:SB 1246.summary: Lets the Linking Industry to Nursing Education Fund match nonmonetary contributions from health care partners, such as donated instructors, space or equipment, gives monetary contributions priority, and bars proposals made up solely of nonmonetary contributions.

fl:SB 1332.title: Career Offender Registration
fl:SB 1332.summary: Changes the Florida Career Offender Registration Act to align with sexual offender rules, requiring in-person registration within 48 hours of release, more reported information, and reporting address and vehicle changes within 48 hours.

fl:SB 14.title: Relief of Jose Correa by Miami-Dade County
fl:SB 14.summary: Directs Miami-Dade County to pay Jose Correa $4.1 million for injuries from a county bus driver's negligence, with attorney and lobbying fees capped at 25% of the award.

fl:SB 1434.title: Infill Redevelopment
fl:SB 1434.summary: Creates the Infill Redevelopment Act, requiring administrative approval of housing on contaminated or brownfield parcels of at least 5 acres in counties over 1.475 million people, at up to 25 units per acre or the area's average zoning density if lower, with a 20-foot buffer.

fl:SB 1452.title: Department of Financial Services
fl:SB 1452.summary: Changes many Department of Financial Services laws, including My Safe Florida Home eligibility, abandoned-property holder notices and dormancy periods, funeral and insurance licensing, firefighter-relative employment, and state salary payments.

fl:SB 156.title: Criminal Offenses Against Law Enforcement Officers and Other Personnel
fl:SB 156.summary: Extends the bar on using force to resist officers acting in good faith to detention, defines good faith, adds manslaughter of officers to life-without-release sentencing, and raises the offense severity ranking for battery on officers and other specified personnel.

fl:SB 1568.title: Use of Digital Currency by the Department of Financial Services
fl:SB 1568.summary: Creates a voluntary pilot program letting the Department of Financial Services accept designated payment stablecoins for government fees and convert them to U.S. currency, with any yield credited to the state.

fl:SB 1602.title: Housing for Veterans
fl:SB 1602.summary: Creates a pilot program in Broward, Escambia, Hillsborough, and Santa Rosa counties funding landlords who hold vacant units for veterans for up to 45 days.

fl:SB 1668.title: Florida Birth-Related Neurological Injury Compensation Association
fl:SB 1668.summary: Revises the Florida Birth-Related Neurological Injury Compensation Association: puts dental, guardianship legal-cost, and expanded family mental-health benefits into law, requires participants to obtain health coverage, and lets the plan pay premiums and out-of-pocket costs.

fl:SB 168.title: Public Nuisances
fl:SB 168.summary: Adds the site of a gambling house to places that may be declared a public nuisance and removes the cap on total fines imposed on a public nuisance.

fl:SB 1690.title: Child Care and Early Learning Services
fl:SB 1690.summary: Requires certain licensure-exempt child care facilities to meet minimum requirements or lose the exemption, bars insurers from denying or cancelling residential policies because of a large family child care home, and creates the Florida Child Care Fund.

fl:SB 178.title: Athletics in Public K-12 Schools
fl:SB 178.summary: Requires the Florida High School Athletic Association to adopt bylaws letting a head coach use up to $15,000 a year per team in personal funds, with parental written consent, for effects such as a student's food, transportation or recovery services; use must be reported.

fl:SB 192.title: Patient Funds Held in Trust by Chiropractic Physicians
fl:SB 192.summary: Removes the limit on the amount of patient funds a chiropractic physician may hold in trust.

fl:SB 2506E.title: Fuel Taxes
fl:SB 2506E.summary: Replaces percentage-based fuel sales tax transfers to Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission trust funds with fixed amounts, including $6.3 million a year for invasive plant control and $2.5 million a year for boating and freshwater fisheries.

fl:SB 296.title: Victims of Domestic Violence and Dating Violence
fl:SB 296.summary: Lets dating violence victims join the Attorney General's address confidentiality program and orders a feasibility study of an alert system for domestic and dating violence victims.

fl:SB 340.title: Human Trafficking Education for Nurse Licensure
fl:SB 340.summary: Requires applicants for registered nurse or licensed practical nurse licensure to complete a 2-hour human trafficking course, beginning July 1, 2027.

fl:SB 382.title: Micromobility Devices
fl:SB 382.summary: Requires electric bicycle riders on shared paths away from roads to yield to pedestrians, limits e-bike speed to 10 mph on sidewalks when a pedestrian is within 50 feet, creates a Micromobility Device Safety Task Force, and requires police to list micromobility crashes.

fl:SB 394.title: Reinsurance Intermediary Managers
fl:SB 394.summary: Exempts from reinsurance intermediary manager licensing an underwriting manager of facultative risks when that business is under 10% of the reinsurer's assumed annual gross written premium.

fl:SB 432.title: Intoxicating Substances
fl:SB 432.summary: Bans tobacco and nicotine dealers from selling nitrous oxide, exempts certain FDA-approved xylazine animal drug products from Schedule I, and creates a trafficking-in-xylazine offense.

fl:SB 436.title: Felony Battery
fl:SB 436.summary: Adds resisting an officer with violence to the prior offenses that can make a misdemeanor battery a felony, and adds battery on a law enforcement officer causing injury to the prison releasee reoffender offense list.

fl:SB 474.title: Military Affairs
fl:SB 474.summary: Adds the Coast Guard and drops the wartime condition for officials’ military leave, requires 90 days qualifying for paid leave to be on a single order, lets local governments grant extra paid reserve-training leave, and ends the Adjutant General’s About Face and Forward March duties.

fl:SB 484.title: Data Centers
fl:SB 484.summary: Requires electric utilities to file tariffs by October 1, 2026 making customers of 50 megawatts or more bear their own service costs, bars service to those controlled by foreign countries of concern, sets water permit rules for large data centers, and orders a study.

fl:SB 538.title: Extracurricular Activities
fl:SB 538.summary: Lets home-schooled students, and students whose school lacks an activity, join that activity at a school in their district, charging non-enrolled students the greater of the enrolled fee or a cost-based fee up to $400, and changes athletic transfer eligibility.

fl:SB 578.title: Alzheimer’s Disease Awareness Initiative
fl:SB 578.summary: Requires the Department of Elderly Affairs to contract with an entity to develop and run an Alzheimer's Disease Awareness Initiative.

fl:SB 594.title: Local Housing Assistance Plans
fl:SB 594.summary: Lets counties and eligible cities use housing funds for lot rental assistance and for repairs to mobile homes, and requires related strategies in local housing assistance plans.

fl:SB 656.title: Internet Crimes Against Children Programs
fl:SB 656.summary: Renames the Online Sting Operations Grant Program the Internet Crimes Against Children Grant Program, revises its purpose and allowed uses, and creates a task force funding program within the Department of Law Enforcement.

fl:SB 688.title: Naturopathic Medicine
fl:SB 688.summary: Reestablishes licensing of naturopathic doctors, creating a Board of Naturopathic Medicine, licensure by exam or endorsement, and a scope of practice that generally excludes prescribing legend drugs; telehealth is allowed.

fl:SB 7002.title: OGSR/Department of Military Affairs/United States Department of Defense
fl:SB 7002.summary: Delays from October 2, 2026, to October 2, 2031, the repeal of a public records exemption for certain Department of Military Affairs records tied to Department of Defense systems.

fl:SB 7004.title: OGSR/Conviction Integrity Unit Reinvestigation Information
fl:SB 7004.summary: Removes the scheduled repeal of the public records exemption for certain conviction integrity unit reinvestigation information.

fl:SB 7008.title: OGSR/Florida Gaming Control Commission
fl:SB 7008.summary: Extends the Florida Gaming Control Commission's public meeting and records exemptions for closed portions of meetings discussing confidential information, which would otherwise expire October 2, 2026.

fl:SB 7014.title: OGSR/Social Media Platform Investigations
fl:SB 7014.summary: Delays from October 2, 2026, to October 2, 2031, the repeal of two public records exemptions for investigations into social media platforms.

fl:SB 7022.title: Public Records/Examination and Assessment Instruments
fl:SB 7022.summary: Extends the public records exemption for exam and assessment instruments to public schools, school boards, and the education boards, and allows sharing among covered agencies.

fl:SB 7024.title: OGSR/Cybersecurity, Information Technology, and Operational Technology Information
fl:SB 7024.summary: Consolidates agency-specific cybersecurity public records and meeting exemptions into the general agency cybersecurity exemption, covering all state and local agencies.

fl:SB 7040.title: Emergency Preparedness and Response Fund/Executive Office of the Governor
fl:SB 7040.summary: Re-creates the Emergency Preparedness and Response Fund in the Governor's office through July 1, 2028, bars using it to buy aircraft, boats, or motor vehicles, holds federal reimbursements in a separate account, and adds cash-balance and cash-flow reporting.

fl:SB 772.title: Limited Licenses for Portable Electronics or Eyewear Insurance
fl:SB 772.summary: Renames portable electronics insurance as "portable electronics or eyewear insurance," adding eyewear to the limited insurance licenses.

fl:SB 800.title: Engineering
fl:SB 800.summary: Sets escalating fines for repeat unlicensed practice of engineering: $10,000 for a second violation, $15,000 third, $20,000 fourth, and $25,000 for fifth and later.

fl:SB 816.title: Diabetes Research
fl:SB 816.summary: Creates the University of Florida Diabetes Institute, which may run statewide pilot programs, keep a deidentified data repository and convene a research consortium.

fl:SB 820.title: Problem-solving Court Reports
fl:SB 820.summary: Requires the state courts administrator's annual problem-solving court report to include added data such as treatment compliance and program completion.

fl:SB 824.title: School District Unimproved Real Property
fl:SB 824.summary: Requires school districts to annually submit to the Department of Education an inventory of all unimproved real property they own, with details such as location, acreage, acquisition date, and current use.

fl:SB 962.title: Affordable Housing
fl:SB 962.summary: Excludes farms and farm operations, including on-site sale of their products, from the commercial, industrial, or mixed-use zoning definitions that trigger required local approval of affordable housing developments under the Live Local Act.

fl:SB 984.title: Firefighter Cancer Benefits
fl:SB 984.summary: Requires a firefighter's former employer to make cancer-related death benefits available to the firefighter's beneficiary for 1 year after the firefighter leaves employment, if the firefighter met the criteria then and was not employed as a firefighter afterward.

fl:SJR 2F.title: Save our Homes from Excessive Property Taxes
fl:SJR 2F.summary: Amends the proposed property tax constitutional amendment to take effect January 1, 2027 and expire December 31, 2031, after which Article VII, sections 4, 6 and 9 revert to their December 31, 2026 text, preserving other adopted amendments.

hi:HB 1573.title: RELATING TO HEALTH.
hi:HB 1573.summary: Requires e-cigarette and e-liquid manufacturers to certify annually to the Attorney General that they hold a federal FDA Marketing Granted Order. The Attorney General publishes a directory of certified products, and penalties apply to noncompliant manufacturers and to sellers of unlisted products.

hi:HB 1576.title: RELATING TO FILMING.
hi:HB 1576.summary: Requires the business, economic development, and tourism department to give public notice when a production gets a filming permit or agreement, or registers or qualifies for the film tax credit, with email or mail sign-up. Exempts film studio land dispositions from land board prior approval.

hi:HB 1618.title: RELATING TO CESSPOOL CONVERSIONS.
hi:HB 1618.summary: Creates a cesspool conversion revolving loan fund; the Hawaii Green Infrastructure Authority offers low-interest or forgivable loans to eligible households to upgrade cesspools or connect to sewers, with funding the health department may provide from the water pollution control revolving fund.

hi:HB 1682.title: RELATING TO THE DISCLOSURE OF INTIMATE IMAGES.
hi:HB 1682.summary: Creates civil remedies for the unauthorized disclosure of intimate images.

hi:HB 1713.title: RELATING TO SCHOOL IMPACT FEES.
hi:HB 1713.summary: Exempts housing projects under 500 units, units for households at or below 140 percent of area median income, and studios under 400 square feet from school impact fees. Land the State does not accept within five years reverts to the developer. Removes a 2029 sunset.

hi:HB 1721.title: RELATING TO HOUSING.
hi:HB 1721.summary: Lowers required insurance for licensed professionals on expedited building permits from $2 million to $1 million, limits their indemnification to their own negligence, removes their written certification before the county issues a certificate of occupancy, and requires state or county inspection of all such projects.

hi:HB 1728.title: RELATING TO RAINWATER CATCHMENT SYSTEMS.
hi:HB 1728.summary: Requires counties to allow rainwater catchment systems for potable and nonpotable uses on all properties, while allowing counties to require registration, inspection, or notification.

hi:HB 1740.title: RELATING TO THE HAWAII HOUSING FINANCE AND DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION.
hi:HB 1740.summary: Removes the income and ability-to-pay tests for qualified residents of Hawaii Housing Finance and Development Corporation projects, lets them own a majority interest in one dwelling property if disposed of within two years, and revises exemptions for certain corporation-developed projects.

hi:HB 1741.title: RELATING TO HOUSING.
hi:HB 1741.summary: Treats county inclusionary housing mandates as impact fees and, from July 1, 2029, requires an approved needs assessment study before a county adopts or changes one. Mandates above 10% of units also need nexus findings and a financial feasibility determination.

hi:HB 1753.title: RELATING TO SOCIAL MEDIA.
