hi:HB 1753.summary: Requires social media platforms with one million or more monthly users nationwide or $25 million or more in annual revenue to let Hawaii users delete accounts, delete their personal information within 90 days, and not obstruct deletion.

hi:HB 1785.title: RELATING TO STUDENT TRANSPORTATION.
hi:HB 1785.summary: Lets the Department of Education, with the governor's approval, remove a route from a student bus contract after five consecutive school days without service and hire an interim carrier outside procurement law for up to 30 months. The bus fare fund may offset replacement costs.

hi:HB 1801.title: RELATING TO CHILD WELFARE SERVICES.
hi:HB 1801.summary: Appropriates funds for the Department of Human Services to contract with domestic violence organizations to train and consult, virtually or in person, with child welfare services staff in offices statewide.

hi:HB 1853.title: RELATING TO DEMENTIA.
hi:HB 1853.summary: Creates the Hanai Memory Network Program in the Executive Office on Aging to build a network of dementia care specialists and support systems for people with dementia and their caregivers. Appropriates funds.

hi:HB 1854.title: RELATING TO COMMUNITY BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CLINICS.
hi:HB 1854.summary: Creates a state office to certify and decertify community behavioral health clinics and a nine-member oversight board, sets up a prospective payment system, and appropriates $300,000. Requires an office representative on the drug abuse advisory commission.

hi:HB 1864.title: RELATING TO INSURANCE.
hi:HB 1864.summary: Requires insurers, mutual benefit societies, and health maintenance organizations to cover standard fertility preservation services, per 2018 American Society of Clinical Oncology guidelines, for people receiving cancer treatment likely to cause infertility, for policies issued or renewed after December 31, 2026.

hi:HB 1888.title: RELATING TO THE SAFETY OF EDUCATIONAL WORKERS.
hi:HB 1888.summary: Requires the Department of Education and charter schools to report and handle harassment of educational workers. Expands the harassment offense to include interfering with school functions, raises it to a misdemeanor when the target is an educational worker, and appropriates funds.

hi:HB 1891.title: RELATING TO EDUCATION.
hi:HB 1891.summary: Requires the Department of Education to implement universal dyslexia screening and evidence-based interventions, offer teacher training in structured literacy, and support teacher preparation programs in structured literacy instruction. Appropriates funds.

hi:HB 1920.title: RELATING TO THE LOW-INCOME HOUSING TAX CREDIT.
hi:HB 1920.summary: For Low-Income Housing Tax Credits issued after July 1, 2026, lets a partnership or LLC partner that received the credit either allocate it further or sell, transfer, or assign it to any taxpayer. Extends the credit's sunset to December 31, 2032.

hi:HB 1959.title: RELATING TO DOMESTIC VIOLENCE.
hi:HB 1959.summary: Extends for five years the law on abuse of family or household members, including the petty misdemeanor offense, penalties, and deferred acceptance of guilty plea for misdemeanor and petty misdemeanor offenses. Requires Judiciary reports to the Legislature.

hi:HB 1960.title: RELATING TO HUMAN TRAFFICKING.
hi:HB 1960.summary: Requires the Attorney General to develop human trafficking awareness training for hotel and other transient accommodation workers. Employers must train employees periodically, keep records, post signage, and adopt a prevention and reporting policy. Establishes penalties.

hi:HB 1961.title: RELATING TO HEALTH CARE.
hi:HB 1961.summary: Makes it unlawful to obstruct access to a health care facility, make repeated calls to impede its phone lines, or threaten injury to its staff or patients; sets petty misdemeanor penalties (first offense: at least $250 fine and 24 hours jail); allows civil suits.

hi:HB 1969.title: RELATING TO COLORECTAL CANCER.
hi:HB 1969.summary: Requires the Department of Human Services to fund colorectal cancer screenings, as appropriated, for uninsured residents, residents with cost-sharing coverage, and certain noncitizens ineligible for Medicaid; requires insurers to cover follow-up colonoscopies after positive tests without cost sharing.

hi:HB 1973.title: RELATING TO HEALTH.
hi:HB 1973.summary: Creates a one-year KupunAloha pilot program in the Department of Health providing in-home health care and support services to people who do not qualify for other government programs and cannot afford care. Appropriates funds; the program ends June 30, 2027.

hi:HB 1974.title: RELATING TO HEALTH.
hi:HB 1974.summary: Requires the State Health Planning and Development Agency to develop and publish a state plan on hearing loss, and appropriates funds for it.

hi:HB 2021.title: RELATING TO TRANSPORTATION.
hi:HB 2021.summary: Bars exhibition riding such as wheelies and stunts on electric bicycles on public streets, bars high-speed electric devices (motor over 750 watts and capable of over 28 mph) from public roads and areas, and requires e-bike labels, point-of-sale signs and written legality disclosures.

hi:HB 2023.title: RELATING TO TRANSPORTATION.
hi:HB 2023.summary: Directs the transportation director to certify speed-limiting devices (active intelligent speed assistance systems) and select one installer; makes tampering a misdemeanor; requires installation during license suspension or revocation for excessive speeding and repeat high-speed racing, which courts may extend.

hi:HB 2078.title: RELATING TO HABITUAL VIOLENT CRIME.
hi:HB 2078.summary: Requires the Attorney General to report annually on whether the habitual violent crime offense reduces repeat violent crime, requires a one-time Criminal Justice Research Institute report before the 2031 session, and extends the offense's sunset date to June 30, 2031.

hi:HB 2137.title: RELATING TO ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE.
hi:HB 2137.summary: Bans knowingly creating or sharing realistic AI-generated likenesses of identifiable people without written consent when used commercially, for fraud, or likely to cause harm, requires AI disclosure labels, allows civil damages up to $50,000 per violation, and requires disclosure of synthetic performers in advertising.

hi:HB 2218.title: RELATING TO THE DEPARTMENT OF LAND AND NATURAL RESOURCES.
hi:HB 2218.summary: Authorizes the Board of Land and Natural Resources to enter community co-management agreements with qualified community groups, including disposing of public lands through such agreements, and sets qualifications for eligible co-managers.

hi:HB 2270.title: RELATING TO THE DOWNPAYMENT LOAN ASSISTANCE PROGRAM.
hi:HB 2270.summary: Changes the Downpayment Loan Assistance Program by removing the combined loan-to-value ratio limit, letting private lenders originate the loans, reducing the borrower's required contribution, and allowing loan funds to pay closing costs, prepaids, and reserves.

hi:HB 2279.title: RELATING TO EXPUNGEMENT ORDERS.
hi:HB 2279.summary: Makes a person who is arrested for or charged with a crime but convicted only of a violation eligible to have the arrest record for that incident expunged.

hi:HB 2296.title: RELATING TO SCHOOL MEALS.
hi:HB 2296.summary: Limits what the Department of Education may charge students for school meals to no more than one-quarter of the cost of preparing them.

hi:HB 2309.title: RELATING TO THE HAWAIIAN HOMES COMMISSION ACT, 1920.
hi:HB 2309.summary: Adds children of a sibling to the relatives who may receive a Hawaiian homestead lease by transfer or succession, in the same way spouses, children, grandchildren, and siblings can.

hi:HB 2338.title: RELATING TO THE HAWAII COMMUNITY COLLEGE PROMISE PROGRAM.
hi:HB 2338.summary: Changes the Hawaii Community College Promise scholarship to cover 95 percent of unmet direct costs, narrows 'direct cost' to tuition, fees, books, and supplies, and lets the program coordinate with federal student aid programs.

hi:HB 2344.title: RELATING TO SCHOOL FACILITIES.
hi:HB 2344.summary: Creates a temporary nine-member commission to recommend public school consolidations, realignments or closures; the governor, then the legislature in 2028, approves or disapproves the whole report, and approved recommendations are implemented by the education board and department.

hi:HB 2385.title: RELATING TO HOUSING.
hi:HB 2385.summary: Transfers approval of general excise tax exemptions for housing projects under county assistance programs from the counties to the Hawaii housing finance and development corporation starting January 1, 2027; at least half the units must serve households at or below 100% of median income.

hi:HB 2452.title: RELATING TO STATE BONDS.
hi:HB 2452.summary: Authorizes the state to issue general obligation bonds and includes the findings required by the state constitution that the bonds will not push the state past its debt limit.

hi:HB 2498.title: RELATING TO CARE HOMES.
hi:HB 2498.summary: Directs the Hawaii Emergency Management Agency to run a pilot program in central and leeward Oahu helping eligible care homes make structural and operational resilience improvements. Appropriates funds, requires a report, and ends June 30, 2029.

hi:SB 177.title: RELATING TO AQUACULTURE.
hi:SB 177.summary: Lets the state animal industry division write rules for evaluating and authorizing imports of aquatic livestock, including pre-arrival disease testing, inspection, monitoring, and quarantine or depopulation of animals posing risk. Requires a risk-based framework and biocontainment standards.

hi:SB 2001.title: RELATING TO THE BANYAN DRIVE COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DISTRICT.
hi:SB 2001.summary: Creates the Banyan Drive Community Development District in Hilo under the Hawaii Community Development Authority, with a special fund and defined powers. Adds district and lineal descendant representatives to the authority's board and appropriates funds.

hi:SB 2031.title: RELATING TO CONSUMER PROTECTION.
hi:SB 2031.summary: Makes it a deceptive practice to advertise live-event tickets or short-term lodging without clearly disclosing the total price, or to misrepresent fees. Advertising that complies with the federal rule on unfair or deceptive fees is treated as compliant.

hi:SB 2043.title: RELATING TO INSURANCE.
hi:SB 2043.summary: Until 2031, subjects captive insurance companies that are not risk retention captives to examination within five years of licensure and otherwise at the Insurance Commissioner's discretion; from 2032, at least every five years. Requires a report to the Legislature.

hi:SB 2169.title: RELATING TO THE AGRIBUSINESS DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION.
hi:SB 2169.summary: Allows the Agribusiness Development Corporation to acquire real property by condemnation for its immediate or future use if it determines the property is necessary, excluding public lands.

hi:SB 2175.title: RELATING TO DISPOSABLE ELECTRONIC SMOKING DEVICES.
hi:SB 2175.summary: Bans selling, offering for sale, or distributing for sale disposable electronic smoking devices, except those with an FDA marketing granted order, starting January 1, 2027, with fines up to $100 per day.

hi:SB 2247.title: RELATING TO POLITICAL FUNDRAISING BY EXECUTIVE BRANCH EMPLOYEES.
hi:SB 2247.summary: Bars governor-appointed, Senate-confirmed, compensated executive branch employees from organizing, attending, hosting, or soliciting contributions for political fundraisers, or otherwise soliciting campaign contributions.

hi:SB 2259.title: RELATING TO THE DEPARTMENT OF BUSINESS, ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, AND TOURISM.
hi:SB 2259.summary: Creates a dementia-friendly business recognition program in the tourism and economic development department. Businesses whose employees complete a one-hour dementia training receive a website badge and decal, and appear on a state list. Appropriates $90,000.

hi:SB 2271.title: RELATING TO HOSPITAL LICENSING.
hi:SB 2271.summary: Requires the Department of Health to adopt rules letting hospitals show compliance with state licensing inspections through accreditation or certification by an organization approved by the federal Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services.

hi:SB 2338.title: RELATING TO HOUSING.
hi:SB 2338.summary: Exempts Hawaii Housing Finance and Development Corporation and Community Development Authority staff from certain state approval of employment actions, sets executive director pay up to 99% of the governor's salary, and renames the corporation's executive assistant as deputy executive director with a higher pay cap.

hi:SB 2340.title: RELATING TO COMMUNITY CARE FOSTER FAMILY HOMES.
hi:SB 2340.summary: Bars certified community care foster family homes from denying residency to people with intellectual or developmental disabilities who meet a nursing-level or intermediate-care level of care solely because of their disability or Medicaid waiver. Requires Department of Health training and technical assistance.

hi:SB 2401.title: RELATING TO REGIONAL SHORELINE MITIGATION DISTRICTS.
hi:SB 2401.summary: Directs the Office of Planning and Sustainable Development to identify regional shoreline mitigation districts and coordinate communities, property owners and agencies on shoreline adaptation pathways plans, which the Board of Land and Natural Resources may adopt.

hi:SB 2494.title: RELATING TO CORRUPTION.
hi:SB 2494.summary: Sets a nine-year statute of limitations for bribery offenses.

hi:SB 2532.title: RELATING TO THE CAMPAIGN SPENDING COMMISSION'S ELECTRONIC FILING SYSTEM.
hi:SB 2532.summary: Requires designated campaign finance forms to be filed electronically through the Campaign Spending Commission's upgraded electronic filing system. Takes effect November 4, 2026.

hi:SB 2544.title: RELATING TO HOUSING.
hi:SB 2544.summary: Creates a five-year Hawaii Builds pilot program in the housing finance corporation, letting it spend up to $20 million a year from the dwelling unit revolving fund on predevelopment and construction equity for housing projects, with expedited agency review.

hi:SB 2568.title: RELATING TO OFFENSES AGAINST PUBLIC SERVANTS.
hi:SB 2568.summary: Raises harassment from a petty misdemeanor to a misdemeanor when committed against a public servant, defined to include officials, judges and any federal, state or county employee, because of or while the servant performs official duties.

hi:SB 2580.title: RELATING TO THE MOTION PICTURE, DIGITAL MEDIA, AND FILM PRODUCTION INCOME TAX CREDIT.
hi:SB 2580.summary: Changes Hawaii's film production tax credit: adds credit for productions with at least 80 percent local hires, requires third-party certification of costs, raises the per-production cap to $20 million and aggregate cap to $60 million, covers streaming productions, and extends the credit to 2038.

hi:SB 2599.title: RELATING TO DEVELOPMENT.
hi:SB 2599.summary: Redesignates the stadium development district as the Halawa community development district, makes the Hawaii Community Development Authority its zoning and entitlement agency, and creates a special fund for district revenues and assessments.

hi:SB 2600.title: RELATING TO THE GENERAL FUND.
hi:SB 2600.summary: Deposits $50 million of general revenues into the state emergency and budget reserve fund, as the state constitution requires when excess revenue conditions are met.

hi:SB 2721.title: RELATING TO THE ADMINISTRATION OF JUSTICE.
hi:SB 2721.summary: Amends various chapters of the Hawaii Penal Code and related statutes to carry out the recommendations of the Judicial Council's 2025 advisory committee on penal code review; takes effect September 1, 2026.

hi:SB 2851.title: RELATING TO DEAF INDIVIDUALS.
hi:SB 2851.summary: Requires county finance directors to add a deafness designation to a vehicle's registration when a deaf owner applies, with deafness certified by a licensed otolaryngologist or audiologist. The designation shows when law enforcement accesses the vehicle's information. Takes effect January 1, 2027.

hi:SB 2877.title: RELATING TO EDUCATION.
hi:SB 2877.summary: Requires the Department of Education to establish a one-year pilot, which may be conducted at Kalihi public elementary schools, in which fifth graders write and illustrate books within existing curricula. Requires a report to the Legislature and appropriates funds.

hi:SB 2907.title: RELATING TO MARINE AFFAIRS.
hi:SB 2907.summary: Declares Hawaii an ocean cluster and creates an Office of Marine Affairs, governing board, and coordinator position within the Hawaii Technology Development Corporation. Repeals marine affairs duties of the business, economic development, and tourism department and transfers an existing advisory committee's employees and functions.

hi:SB 2921.title: RELATING TO STATE FUNDS.
hi:SB 2921.summary: Authorizes the director of finance to transfer $47,151,001 from 18 listed special, revolving, and trust funds into the general fund for fiscal year 2026-2027.

hi:SB 3001.title: RELATING TO ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE.
hi:SB 3001.summary: Requires AI companion operators to disclose AI status where users could believe it is human, adopt suicide and self-harm response protocols, limit engagement rewards and sexual content for minors, and report annually to the Department of Health from 2028.

hi:SB 3045.title: RELATING TO HEALTH INSURANCE.
hi:SB 3045.summary: Requires health insurers, including Medicaid managed care plans, to cover continuous glucose monitors and related supplies for people diagnosed with diabetes, starting in 2027, when medically necessary and prescribed. Allows copays and deductibles no less favorable than for other equipment.

hi:SB 3076.title: RELATING TO TOBACCO ENFORCEMENT.
hi:SB 3076.summary: Declares untaxed tobacco products forfeitable as contraband without using the state asset forfeiture procedures, as already applies to untaxed cigarettes. Confirms tax and attorney general authority to inspect and seize tobacco products, including e-cigarettes and e-liquids. Effective September 1, 2026.

hi:SB 3132.title: RELATING TO SYNDROMIC SURVEILLANCE.
hi:SB 3132.summary: Requires licensed hospitals with emergency departments to submit syndromic surveillance data (early health-event reporting from patient visits) to the Department of Health, and lets the department set up a state data reporting system.

hi:SB 3204.title: RELATING TO FAMILY RESILIENCE PILOT PROGRAM.
hi:SB 3204.summary: Creates a two-year family resilience pilot program in the Office of Wellness and Resilience, hiring peer support navigators to help up to eighty families with benefits enrollment and parenting classes. Requires a report to the Legislature and uses federal welfare (TANF) funds.

hi:SB 3234.title: RELATING TO TRAFFIC SAFETY.
hi:SB 3234.summary: Appropriates $2,000,000 from the safe routes to school special fund for the Department of Transportation to install pedestrian safety improvements at sites next to school properties, and names the measure in honor of Tehya Mahelona.

hi:SB 3245.title: RELATING TO THE SUPPLEMENTAL NUTRITION ASSISTANCE PROGRAM.
hi:SB 3245.summary: Requires the Department of Human Services to set SNAP minimum certification periods at 12 months (24 for households of all adults 60 or older), join the federal Elderly Simplified Application Project, and report to the Legislature. Takes effect July 1, 2028.

hi:SB 3253.title: RELATING TO CONSERVATION.
hi:SB 3253.summary: Recognizes a nonprofit as the State of Hawaii Conservation Sanctuary to run endangered-species and wildlife sanctuaries, with power to operate for-profit enterprises, hold or lease property, and operate in agricultural districts; exempts state funds it receives from chapter 42F standards.

hi:SB 3320.title: RELATING TO THE FOOD AND PRODUCT INNOVATION NETWORK.
hi:SB 3320.summary: Requires the Food and Product Innovation Network to adopt a food safety framework. Directs the Agribusiness Development Corporation to set performance indicators, a market access strategy, and aligned branding, and the business, economic development, and tourism department to review enterprise zone incentives. Appropriates $2.8 million.

hi:SB 3324.title: RELATING TO MEDICAID.
hi:SB 3324.summary: Appropriates funds to the Department of Human Services to increase payments for Medicaid home- and community-based services, including residential services in community care foster family homes and expanded adult residential care homes. Spending is conditioned on obtaining federal matching funds.

hi:SB 3325.title: RELATING TO PUBLIC SCHOOL MEDICAID REIMBURSEMENTS.
hi:SB 3325.summary: Requires the Department of Education to create an updated plan for maximizing Medicaid reimbursement for administrative and support services provided to students with special needs, and to report annually to the Legislature.

hi:SB 411.title: RELATING TO CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROJECTS AT STATE SMALL BOAT HARBORS AND STATE PARKS.
hi:SB 411.summary: Lets the Department of Land and Natural Resources carry out capital improvement projects on existing small boat harbor and state park facilities without prior legislative and gubernatorial approval. Requires semiannual reports to the Legislature; the authority ends five years after taking effect.

hi:SB 847.title: RELATING TO PSYCHOLOGISTS.
hi:SB 847.summary: Creates a three-year pilot at federally qualified health centers in Kauai and Hawaii counties letting qualified psychologists, supervised by a physician or psychiatrist, prescribe certain psychotropic medications to patients aged 18 to 65. Requires Board of Psychology rules and a report to the Legislature.

hi:SB 888.title: RELATING TO CONSUMER PROTECTION.
hi:SB 888.summary: Bars smart household security device operators from sharing user data with law enforcement unless the user consents in writing, a judicial warrant is provided, or a kidnapping, abduction, or hostage emergency poses imminent death or serious harm. Bars requiring consent to use the device.

ia:HF 1003.title: A bill for an act relating to child placements.
ia:HF 1003.summary: Removes the bill's section requiring HHS to employ dedicated central-office staff for identifying and notifying relatives of a removed child, leaving the court placement-finding rule and updating its Code year to 2026.

ia:HF 1023.title: A bill for an act relating to benefits and contributions for members of the Iowa public employees’ retirement system who are employed in a protection occupation.
ia:HF 1023.summary: Increases the retirement formula for protection-occupation members of Iowa's public employees' retirement system retiring on or after July 1, 2026, adds an annual 1.5% benefit increase for eligible retirees, and changes contributions from 40% member and 60% employer to 50% each.

ia:HF 1028.title: A bill for an act relating to matters under the purview of the department of management, and including effective date and applicability provisions.
ia:HF 1028.summary: Raises from 50 to 100 percent the yearly cap on interdepartmental transfers into a non-entitlement appropriation, directs Technology Reinvestment Fund spending to Department of Management information technology projects, and sets required and prohibited terms in state IT contracts.

ia:HF 1036.title: A bill for an act relating to human trafficking, including screening children, civil statutes of limitations, an annual stakeholder meeting and report, depositions of victims, restitution, restorative facilities and protective services, and investigation and prosecution, and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 1036.summary: Requires juvenile court complaints to be reviewed with a trafficking indicator list and child abuse allegations screened for commercial sexual exploitation, gives child sexual abuse and trafficking victims five years after age 18 to sue, and sets an annual stakeholder meeting and report to 2030.

ia:HF 2185.title: A bill for an act relating to cost sharing for health savings accounts and qualified high-deductible health plans.
ia:HF 2185.summary: Requires health plans to apply copayments, coinsurance or deductibles to a high-deductible plan only after the enrollee meets the minimum deductible, when earlier cost sharing could cost the enrollee health savings account eligibility, except for preventive care.

ia:HF 2199.title: A bill for an act relating to level II law enforcement academy training programs.
ia:HF 2199.summary: Lets applicants to the level II law enforcement academy training program (formerly the short course) qualify with a two- or four-year police science or criminal justice program or the other listed qualifications, instead of needing both.

ia:HF 2200.title: A bill for an act relating to activities in the administration of alcoholic beverage control by the department of revenue, and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2200.summary: As introduced, broadens the alcohol-industry interests that no more than two commission members may hold, bars members from using their office to promote political views or candidates, and bars revenue employees from licensing or enforcing alcohol laws against businesses they have an ownership interest in.

ia:HF 2230.title: A bill for an act relating to teacher education and licensing, including by modifying provisions related to practitioner preparation programs and licenses issued by the board of educational examiners.
ia:HF 2230.summary: Strikes from the bill the requirement that teacher preparation programs give a state-selected end-of-program assessment with a state-set minimum score and published passage rates, keeping the clinical-experience and licensing provisions.

ia:HF 2231.title: A bill for an act establishing a seal of civics excellence program administered by the department of education to recognize student excellence in civics.
ia:HF 2231.summary: Directs the Department of Education to run a voluntary seal of civics excellence program recognizing graduating high school students who show proficiency in civics, with requirements including knowledge of American government and civic or community activities.

ia:HF 2254.title: A bill for an act relating to the prohibition of noncompete clauses in certain employment contracts entered into by the university of Iowa hospitals and clinics, and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2254.summary: Directs the Board of Regents to develop a policy barring University of Iowa Hospitals and Clinics from including noncompete clauses in employment contracts with physicians, advanced nurse practitioners, licensed practical nurses, pharmacists, physician assistants, and registered nurses.

ia:HF 2256.title: A bill for an act exempting a parent’s or legal guardian’s inability to access appropriate behavioral or mental health treatment for their child from the definition of child abuse.
ia:HF 2256.summary: Bars the Department of Health and Human Services from counting as child abuse a parent's failure to provide treatment when, despite reasonable attempts, the parent cannot access appropriate behavioral or mental health care for a child with a diagnosed condition.

ia:HF 2297.title: A bill for an act relating to radon mitigation in residential buildings.
ia:HF 2297.summary: Requires the state building code to require a passive radon mitigation method listed in the 2021 International Residential Code in new single-family and two-family homes built after the requirement is adopted.

ia:HF 2305.title: A bill for an act relating to health care decisions related to palliative care, hospice programs, life-sustaining procedures, out-of-hospital do-not-resuscitate orders, durable power of attorney for health care, and probate court guardianship reports.
ia:HF 2305.summary: Adds adult relatives (by majority decision) and close adult friends to those who may make life-sustaining treatment and resuscitation decisions for patients unable to decide, lets nurse practitioners and physician assistants serve as attending providers, and defines palliative care and serious illness.

ia:HF 2329.title: A bill for an act relating to interest rates and charges on regulated loans, and consumer credit transaction service charges.
ia:HF 2329.summary: Sets the maximum rate on regulated loans at 3 percent per month, ends the banking superintendent's authority to change rates, and changes the consumer credit service charge cap from the lesser of 10 percent or $30 to the lesser of 3 percent or $100.

ia:HF 2337.title: A bill for an act relating to fraudulent practices involving academic credentials or professional or occupational licenses, and making penalties applicable.
ia:HF 2337.summary: Makes falsely claiming an academic degree or credentials to get a job or other personal gain a simple misdemeanor, and falsely claiming a license regulated under Iowa Code chapter 272C an aggravated misdemeanor.

ia:HF 2348.title: A bill for an act relating to animal torture, and providing penalties.
ia:HF 2348.summary: Makes intentionally and maliciously mutilating, burning, poisoning, drowning, starving, or causing intensive or prolonged pain or death to a companion animal a class D felony, and raises the penalty one degree above the underlying offense for people with certain prior animal-cruelty convictions.

ia:HF 2356.title: A bill for an act establishing the state public defender’s pilot project to implement innovative models of child welfare legal representation as the project to preserve families.
ia:HF 2356.summary: Removes the June 2025 end date of the state public defender's pilot program testing new models of legal representation for families in the child welfare system, and continues it as an ongoing project.

ia:HF 2360.title: A bill for an act relating to child endangerment.
ia:HF 2360.summary: Defines a child as anyone under 18 for Iowa's child endangerment law, replacing its separate references to minors with disabilities, so the same offenses and penalties apply to endangering any person under 18.

ia:HF 2490.title: A bill for an act relating to public meetings and records, including public notice requirements for meetings of a governmental body, supervision and fees associated with examining and copying public records, employment separation information for certain government employees, contractors, or appointees, and injunctions to restrain vexatious requesters.
ia:HF 2490.summary: As introduced, requires governmental bodies to give meeting notice by posting it prominently and on any associated website, and to mark amended agendas "AMENDED" and issue a new notice.

ia:HF 2493.title: A bill for an act relating to the statewide preschool program by modifying provisions relating to eligibility, funding, and compulsory attendance and including applicability provisions.
ia:HF 2493.summary: As introduced, extends the state preschool program and its funding to five-year-olds who turn five between March 15 and September 15, starting with school budget years beginning July 1, 2027.

ia:HF 2498.title: A bill for an act enacting the interstate podiatric medical licensure compact.
ia:HF 2498.summary: Enacts the Interstate Podiatric Medical Licensure Compact, creating a streamlined path for podiatrists to be licensed in multiple member states while each state keeps authority to discipline licensees.

ia:HF 2501.title: A bill for an act relating to the conduct of elections.
ia:HF 2501.summary: Requires agencies investigating election misconduct to notify the State Commissioner of Elections, cancels voter registrations left incomplete, pending, or unconfirmed for 90 days without resolution, ends voter attestation of another voter's identity, and changes public measure recount rules.

ia:HF 2514.title: A bill for an act making children of child care workers in this state eligible for the state child care assistance program.
ia:HF 2514.summary: As passed by the House, makes children of child care workers eligible for state child care assistance if the parent works an average of 32 hours weekly providing child care at a participating facility and does not own it; copayments set by rule.

ia:HF 2515.title: A bill for an act relating to deferred or suspended sentences for cases involving sexual exploitation of a minor.
ia:HF 2515.summary: Bars courts from granting deferred sentences or suspended sentences to people convicted of sexual exploitation of a minor under Iowa Code section 728.12.

ia:HF 2523.title: A bill for an act establishing the right of a parent or guardian of a minor child to consent to and authorize certain medical services over the minor child’s objection.
ia:HF 2523.summary: Lets a parent or guardian consent to a minor's evaluation or treatment for a substance use disorder or mental health condition, including inpatient care, even over the minor's objection. A facility is not required to treat if it finds treatment inappropriate.

ia:HF 2526.title: A bill for an act relating to the confidentiality of the residential addresses of foster parents.
ia:HF 2526.summary: Bars the Department of Health and Human Services and its agents from giving a foster child's biological parent a document or oral disclosure of the foster parent's address unless the foster parent consents in writing.

ia:HF 2531.title: A bill for an act relating to interests in minerals owned by counties and cities, and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2531.summary: Requires counties and cities to convey mineral interests they own to the surface owner within five years, except on land they own outright, and requires counties to convey delinquent-tax mineral interests if the owner does not pay within 90 days of notice.

ia:HF 2532.title: A bill for an act relating to probate and trust matters, including time limitations on actions, attorney fees, trust code proceedings and notice requirements, damages for wrongful death, and filing deadlines, and including effective date and applicability provisions.
ia:HF 2532.summary: Changes probate and trust law: sets a two-year limit for claims that nonprobate transfers resulted from undue influence or fraud, lets courts award fees in estate disputes, rewrites how wrongful-death damages are divided, and extends the estate inventory deadline from 90 to 120 days.

ia:HF 2542.title: A bill for an act relating to habitual offenders, and providing penalties.
ia:HF 2542.summary: Raises the minimum prison term for habitual offenders (class C or D felony after two prior felonies) from three to seven years, bars earned time from reducing it, raises the maximum from 15 to 20 years, and bars deferred or suspended sentences.

ia:HF 2543.title: A bill for an act relating to subacute mental health care facilities and services, and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2543.summary: Requires subacute mental health facilities to develop an initial treatment plan within 24 hours, sets 48-hour (urgent) and 5- to 10-day (nonurgent) Medicaid prior authorization deadlines, creates a bed-availability tracking system for children's psychiatric institutions, and orders a review of facility rules.

ia:HF 2562.title: A bill for an act relating to care facility placement decisions for certain adults, and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2562.summary: Lets a physician certify that an adult care-facility patient cannot consent and has no locatable representative, after which a spouse, adult child, parent or sibling, in priority order, may decide the patient's facility placement and help apply for insurance or public benefits.

ia:HF 2585.title: A bill for an act relating to the provision of accessible prescription-related measures for persons who are blind, have a visual impairment, or other print disability.
ia:HF 2585.summary: Requires the pharmacy board to adopt rules so that by January 1, 2027 pharmacies give blind, visually impaired and print-disabled customers accessible prescription labels, bag tags and medical guides at no cost, or refer them elsewhere; institutional pharmacies are exempt.

ia:HF 2591.title: A bill for an act relating to open enrollment, student transfers, and interscholastic athletic eligibility requirements, and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2591.summary: Sets a 140-calendar-day wait for varsity athletic eligibility for grade 9-12 students who open enroll or transfer schools (open enrollment is now 90 school days) and directs rules letting eighth graders join school athletics on the same basis as grades 9-12.

ia:HF 2598.title: A bill for an act relating to a required course of instruction regarding human trafficking prevention for persons applying for the initial issuance of certain commercial driver’s licenses, and including applicability provisions.
ia:HF 2598.summary: Requires applicants for an initial commercial driver's license to certify they completed a human trafficking prevention course of at least 30 minutes, starting March 1, 2027 or when the transportation department's new records system phase takes effect, if earlier.

ia:HF 2602.title: A bill for an act relating to the licensure of massage establishments, and making penalties applicable.
ia:HF 2602.summary: Requires massage therapy establishments, other than sole practitioners and certain exempt locations, to hold a Board of Massage Therapy license starting January 1, 2027, with possible inspections and fingerprint background checks.

ia:HF 2610.title: A bill for an act relating to education programs and systems, including career and technical education expenditures and definitions, statewide lower division general education framework and common course numbering systems, and the implementation of a statewide corequisite model in Iowa community colleges.
ia:HF 2610.summary: Lets the education department allow career academy grant recipients to deposit grant money into a protected investment or endowment account, with only earnings spent, and provides that a regional center may include a physical facility, a career academy program, or both.

ia:HF 2615.title: A bill for an act relating to thoroughbred and quarter horse racing seasons.
ia:HF 2615.summary: As introduced, requires thoroughbred and quarter horse racing seasons to be separate, non-overlapping meets, unless the breed associations and the Polk County track licensee agree in writing to mixed meets.

ia:HF 2617.title: A bill for an act relating to abandoned vehicles.
ia:HF 2617.summary: As passed by the House, rewrites Iowa's abandoned-vehicle law: sets who may tow and impound, requires notice to owners within ten days giving 20 days to reclaim the vehicle or retrieve belongings, and sets rules for selling unclaimed vehicles and distributing proceeds.

ia:HF 2633.title: A bill for an act relating to living organ donors and life insurance, disability insurance, and long-term care insurance.
ia:HF 2633.summary: Bars life, disability and long-term care insurers from declining or limiting coverage, or varying terms and price, based solely on a person being a living organ donor.

ia:HF 2634.title: A bill for an act relating to preneed sellers, sales agents and sales agent applicants, and government cemeteries.
ia:HF 2634.summary: Changes preneed funeral and cemetery rules: repeals the sales agent annual report requirement and creates a "government cemetery" category, for cemeteries run by a city, county or township, excluded from perpetual-care cemetery requirements.

ia:HF 2635.title: A bill for an act relating to health carriers standards of conduct; utilization review organizations, artificial intelligence, audits, and prior authorizations; certificate of need processes; and including applicability provisions.
ia:HF 2635.summary: As passed by the House, sets audit deadlines for health insurers' utilization review, bars carrier penalties for out-of-network referrals, requires qualified reviewers for prior authorization denials, exempts some cancer screenings from prior authorization, and raises certificate-of-need dollar thresholds.

ia:HF 2655.title: A bill for an act relating to the operating privileges of drivers of authorized emergency vehicles and police officers riding police bicycles.
ia:HF 2655.summary: Extends to all authorized emergency vehicle drivers, except designated towing vehicles, the allowances to proceed past red signals and stop signs after slowing and to exceed speed limits without recklessly endangering life or property.

ia:HF 2667.title: A bill for an act relating to project design standards and specifications, including by providing for a statewide urban design and specifications board and requiring certain reports to city councils regarding noncompliant projects.
ia:HF 2667.summary: As passed by the House, creates a statewide urban design and specifications board to publish design and specifications manuals, and requires a cost report to the city council before it approves a city street project that does not match Department of Transportation standards.

ia:HF 2670.title: A bill for an act relating to education, including by modifying provisions related to summative testing in schools and the educational program provided to students enrolled in kindergarten through grade twelve, and including applicability provisions.
ia:HF 2670.summary: Requires a social studies assessment in grades 8 and 11 starting in 2027-2028, moves the grade 10 science assessment to grade 11, has the state board set social studies core indicators, and requires summative tests to align with Iowa standards.

ia:HF 2676.title: A bill for an act relating to health-related matters, including health-related professions, nutrition, medication, and education, and including effective date and applicability provisions.
ia:HF 2676.summary: Requires nutrition continuing education for some physicians and physician assistants and nutrition coursework in medical school, bars certain ingredients in school meals from 2027, limits kindergarten-through-grade-5 digital instruction to 60 minutes daily, and allows over-the-counter ivermectin.

ia:HF 2678.title: A bill for an act providing for certain persons acting under the jurisdiction of the secretary of state, including by providing for information from required filings, and the administrative dissolution of certain entities, and making penalties applicable.
ia:HF 2678.summary: Lets the Secretary of State remove unauthorized personal information from business filings, send interrogatories to entities suspected of fraudulent or unlawful use, and dissolve those that concede violations or fail to respond; also adds out-of-state owners to agricultural landholding reports.

ia:HF 2694.title: A bill for an act relating to the regulation of certain places and activities by the governor.
ia:HF 2694.summary: As passed by the House, bars the governor from closing or regulating places or practices of worship; bars disaster-emergency measures that change election rules without legislative approval, regulate conduct in private residences or require vaccination; and bars requiring private businesses to close in public health disasters.

ia:HF 2695.title: A bill for an act relating to the application of foreign law and limiting changes in venue of civil actions, and including applicability provisions.
ia:HF 2695.summary: Bars courts and tribunals from transferring a civil case if that would apply foreign law violating a constitutional right, and voids rulings and contract provisions based on foreign law that deny a party a right guaranteed by the U.S. or Iowa constitutions.

ia:HF 2706.title: A bill for an act relating to judicial officers, including magistrate appointments in judicial election districts, senior magistrates, and judicial officer compensation, and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2706.summary: Changes judicial officer rules, including appointing magistrates by judicial election district instead of by county, and addressing senior magistrates and judicial officer compensation.

ia:HF 2707.title: A bill for an act relating to alignment of delivery of health and human services programs and services, aging and disability services, and volunteer services, and including applicability and effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2707.summary: Directs the Department of Health and Human Services to divide the state into districts, initially matching the existing behavioral health districts, and changes behavioral health, aging and disability, and volunteer guardian and conservator services.

ia:HF 2711.title: A bill for an act relating to state policies and programs with race or gender requirements.
ia:HF 2711.summary: Adds to the bill a ban on state funding of programs that give preference based on legacy status, industry or geographic location, a bar on tax expenditures for such preferential programs, and strikes a subsection of section 15A.1.

ia:HF 2724.title: A bill for an act requiring the board of educational examiners to establish additional endorsements and authorizations.
ia:HF 2724.summary: As passed by the House, requires the board of educational examiners to adopt fine arts, math and science teaching endorsements requiring a bachelor's degree, an instructional strategist II endorsement without a master's requirement, and an activities administration authorization.

ia:HF 2749.title: A bill for an act relating to real estate transfer tax, including declarations of value.
ia:HF 2749.summary: Exempts deeds that transfer trust assets to beneficiaries without payment from the requirement to file a declaration of value with the county recorder.

ia:HF 2754.title: A bill for an act relating to education, including by modifying provisions related to charter school approval, contracts, funding, and operations, services provided to charter schools by area education agencies, charter school student participation in extracurricular activities provided by public schools, the Iowa public employees’ retirement system, education savings accounts, independent accreditation, teacher training and licensure, the statewide voluntary preschool program, the district-to-community college sharing or concurrent enrollment program, open enrollment, school tuition organizations, private instruction, and innovation zone schools; making appropriations; and including effective date and applicability provisions.
ia:HF 2754.summary: Redefines "nonpublic school" in section 257.11B as an accredited nonpublic school, or an institution meeting special education standards, that accepts all applicants for admission in the same manner as a school district.

ia:HF 2756.title: A bill for an act relating to licensing of service companies, motor vehicle service contracts, and residential service contracts, and providing civil penalties and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2756.summary: Revises Iowa's motor vehicle and residential service contract law effective January 1, 2027: lowers the license renewal fee from $500 to $200, requires licensees to report ownership, officer and out-of-state enforcement changes within 30 days, and requires keeping a license while contracts remain in force.

ia:HF 2757.title: A bill for an act relating to nuclear electric generation facilities by creating sales and use tax exemptions and refunds, making appropriations to the state board of regents for establishing and maintaining a nuclear energy workforce, making penalties applicable, and including applicability and retroactive applicability provisions.
ia:HF 2757.summary: Exempts property and services used to build, expand, repair, or restart nuclear power plants from sales and use tax until commercial operation, if the facility pays $2,200 per megawatt of capacity annually, up to four years, into a Board of Regents nuclear workforce fund.

ia:HF 2761.title: A bill for an act relating to driver’s licenses and nonoperator’s identification cards marked to reflect gold star status.
ia:HF 2761.summary: As introduced, lets surviving spouses, parents, children and siblings of service members who died on active duty during a time of military conflict, or as a result of that service, request that their driver's license or ID card be marked "GOLD STAR FAMILY."

ia:HF 2765.title: A bill for an act providing for the regulation of mining, making penalties applicable, and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2765.summary: Requires the state soil conservation division to adopt rules, including emergency rules, for land subsidence above underground mines on public land or public rights-of-way, covering reporting, repair-plan engineer qualifications, and repair timeliness. Takes effect on enactment.

ia:HF 2766.title: A bill for an act relating to captive insurance companies and life captive reinsurance companies, and including civil penalties.
ia:HF 2766.summary: Makes gross premiums tax returns of insurance and captive insurance companies confidential, with a serious misdemeanor for state employees who publish them, and changes rules for captive insurance and life captive reinsurance companies.

ia:HF 2768.title: A bill for an act relating to and making appropriations for state government administration and regulation, including the department of administrative services, auditor of state, ethics and campaign disclosure board, offices of governor and lieutenant governor, department of inspections, appeals, and licensing, department of insurance and financial services, department of management, Iowa public employees’ retirement system, public information board, department of revenue, secretary of state, treasurer of state, and utilities commission.
ia:HF 2768.summary: Appropriates state money for fiscal year 2026-2027 to general government agencies, including the auditor, governor's office, revenue, insurance, secretary of state, treasurer, and utilities commission, and redirects some fee deposits to the Licensing and Regulation Fund.

ia:HF 2769.title: A bill for an act relating to and making appropriations to the judicial branch.
ia:HF 2769.summary: Replaces the bill with judicial branch appropriations for the fiscal year starting July 1, 2026, including about $202.7 million for judicial salaries and court operations, $3.6 million for jury and witness fees, and $3.29 million for court-ordered juvenile services.

ia:HF 2770.title: A bill for an act relating to and making appropriations to the justice system, providing fees, and including applicability provisions.
ia:HF 2770.summary: Appropriates money for fiscal year 2026-2027 to the departments of justice, corrections, public safety and public defense and other justice agencies, raises state-paid appointed counsel pay by $4 per hour from July 1, 2026, and creates an attorney loan repayment program.

ia:HF 2771.title: A bill for an act relating to and making appropriations involving state government entities associated with agriculture, natural resources, and environmental protection, and including contingent effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2771.summary: Appropriates state money for fiscal year 2026-2027 to the departments of agriculture and natural resources, the Iowa Finance Authority, and Iowa State University and the University of Iowa, and makes Iowa Code changes.

ia:HF 2772.title: A bill for an act relating to and making appropriations for the economic development of the state, including to the economic development authority, Iowa finance authority, department of workforce development, and state board of regents and certain regents institutions, and codifying the housing renewal program.
ia:HF 2772.summary: Replaces the bill with fiscal 2026-27 appropriations for the Economic Development Authority, Iowa Finance Authority, Workforce Development and certain Regents institutions, with Economic Development Authority goals and reporting requirements, and creates a housing renewal program and fund.

ia:HF 2778.title: A bill for an act modifying the individual income tax credit for emergency medical services personnel to include volunteer ambulance drivers, and including retroactive applicability provisions.
ia:HF 2778.summary: As introduced, extends the $250 individual income tax credit for emergency medical services personnel to volunteer ambulance drivers, applying to tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2026.

ia:HF 2779.title: A bill for an act relating to authorizations to conduct advance deposit wagering.
ia:HF 2779.summary: Requires the racing and gaming commission to authorize entities meeting simulcasting licensure rules, instead of the Polk County racetrack licensee, to run advance deposit wagering, and bars phone or electronic wagers within five miles of a racetrack without the track's agreement.

ia:HF 2780.title: A bill for an act relating to alcoholic beverage control by providing for certificates of compliance and the issuance of class “A” wine permits to nonnative wine manufacturers, permitting cities to create social districts for the consumption of alcoholic beverages, and providing fees.
ia:HF 2780.summary: Changes alcohol permit rules by removing the distiller's certificate requirement for some brand resellers, allowing class A wine permits for nonnative wine makers, and letting cities create social districts for drinking alcohol in certain public places.

ia:HF 2781.title: A bill for an act relating to allocations of moneys from the juvenile detention home fund.
ia:HF 2781.summary: Changes how the juvenile detention home fund is divided, giving each home $150,000 first and sharing the rest based on each home's share of the prior year's costs.

ia:HF 2782.title: A bill for an act relating to and making appropriations to the department of veterans affairs and the department of health and human services, including aging and disability services, behavioral health, public health, and community access and eligibility; the medical assistance program, state supplementary assistance, Hawki, and other health-related programs; family well-being and protection; state-operated specialty care; administration and compliance; transfers, cash flow, and nonreversions; report on nonreversion of moneys; more options for maternal support program; reimbursement rates review; mental diseases exclusion waiver; full-time equivalent dashboard; comprehensive family support program; federal community mental health services block grant; behavioral health expenditure report; opioid settlement fund; emergency rules; graduate medical education; and special population nursing facilities; and including effective date and retroactive applicability provisions.
ia:HF 2782.summary: Adds to a pending amendment $225,000, distributed July 1, 2026, to the oldest continuously operating medical society in the state's most populous county, for safety net patients' access to specialty care.

ia:HF 2783.title: A bill for an act relating to and making appropriations to the education system, including the funding and operation of the department for the blind, department of education, state board of regents, department of workforce development, and Iowa special education council.
ia:HF 2783.summary: Adds to a pending amendment a work group, appointed by the education director with education, school and legislative members, to review special education weightings, unchanged since 2004, and recommend changes that meet student needs while minimizing property tax increases.

ia:HF 2785.title: A bill for an act extending the biodiesel blended fuel tax credit.
ia:HF 2785.summary: Extends the repeal date of the biodiesel blended fuel promotion tax credit for retail dealers, for individual and corporate income taxes, from January 1, 2028, to January 1, 2033.

ia:HF 2786.title: A bill for an act modifying the sales or use tax refund for biodiesel production.
ia:HF 2786.summary: Raises the sales or use tax refund for biodiesel producers from 4 to 5 cents per gallon produced in Iowa and moves the refund's repeal date from January 1, 2028, to January 1, 2031.

ia:HF 2787.title: A bill for an act prohibiting warrant resolution clinics, including enforcement mechanisms, providing penalties, and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2787.summary: Bans warrant resolution clinics, advertised events letting people with outstanding arrest warrants resolve them without immediate arrest, and bars public funds or facilities for them; knowing violations are simple misdemeanors, with civil penalties up to $10,000 for private organizers.

ia:HF 2788.title: A bill for an act relating to abortions including definitions, informed consent, dispensing of abortion-inducing drugs, and other abortion-related provisions.
ia:HF 2788.summary: Requires a pre-abortion in-person physician exam including screening for coercion or abuse. Sets informed-consent steps for drug-induced abortions, requires abortion-inducing drugs be dispensed to the patient in a health care setting, and lets the woman or her representative sue those who dispense otherwise.

ia:HF 2791.title: A bill for an act permitting an exchange of the cash reserve levy for another local levy within the school budget for certain school districts to correct for an extreme circumstance and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2791.summary: As introduced, lets school districts whose taxable value fell by $100 million or more from a single-property correction exceed the cash reserve levy limit for 2026-27, if they cut other levies by at least as much. Takes effect on enactment.

ia:HF 2793.title: A bill for an act relating to a railway tracks overpass and underpass fund, and making appropriations.
ia:HF 2793.summary: As introduced, creates a railway tracks overpass and underpass fund under the Department of Transportation to give grants to cities and counties for building highway overpasses and underpasses across railway tracks.

ia:HF 2794.title: A bill for an act establishing a sexual assault forensic examination center grant program and trust fund.
ia:HF 2794.summary: Creates a grant program in the Department of Justice under which, if funded, the attorney general contracts with a nonprofit not affiliated with a hospital to run sexual assault forensic examination centers, with annual reports to the attorney general and legislature.

ia:HF 2797.title: A bill for an act relating to the peace officer, public safety, and emergency personnel bill of rights, and providing fees.
ia:HF 2797.summary: Requires courts to award attorney fees, expenses and costs to a peace officer who wins a challenge to placement on a prosecutor's Brady-Giglio list, paid by the state or local government responsible for the prosecuting agency; applies to placements since July 1, 2021.

ia:HF 2799.title: A bill for an act relating to matters under the purview of the economic development authority, the utilities commission, and the department of education, including creation of the headquarters expansion and development for growth and employment program, and the business incentives for growth program training fund; repeal of the new jobs tax credit program; the major economic growth attraction program; load forecasting and analysis of electric transmission system expansion plans; creation of the electric transmission system expansion planning and analysis and load forecasting fund; the industrial new jobs training program; and establishing the new jobs training program interim study committee; and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2799.summary: Creates the EDGE headquarters tax incentive program and a training fund, repeals the New Jobs Tax Credit, has the economic development authority commission an Iowa State University electricity load forecast every two years, and changes industrial new jobs training.

ia:HF 2800.title: A bill for an act relating to state and local government and finances, including by making, modifying, limiting, or reducing appropriations, distributions, or transfers, authorizing expenditure of unappropriated moneys in special funds, making corrections, and providing for properly related matters including the national electrical code, local civil rights laws, political party state central committees, noxious weeds, nonresident deer hunting licenses, proprietary treatment systems, poultry associations, tax credits, alternative nicotine and vapor products, public assistance programs, judicial branch and county attorney salaries, civil litigation abuse, human trafficking, federal grants and loans notifications, quarterly payments to area education agencies, civic proficiency in higher education, charter schools under the Iowa public employees’ retirement system, school district incentives, extracurricular interscholastic eligibility, and levy increases, and including effective date, applicability, and retroactive applicability provisions.
ia:HF 2800.summary: Makes appropriation changes and many related government provisions, including the National Electrical Code, local civil rights laws, a health care access tax credit, judicial and county attorney salaries, a civil litigation abuse cause of action, and school district levy increases.

ia:HF 2801.title: A bill for an act modifying the major economic growth attraction program, and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2801.summary: Lets the economic development authority award either a tax credit of up to 5 percent of qualifying investment to up to two businesses, or up to 10 percent, paid over 10 years, to one business in a rural county.

ia:HF 523.title: A bill for an act relating to the ability of peace officers to file a petition for emergency protective orders on behalf of persons seeking relief from domestic abuse.
ia:HF 523.summary: As introduced, lets a peace officer file a petition for a 72-hour emergency protective order for a person who says they are in present danger of domestic abuse and asks the officer to file it.

ia:HF 571.title: A bill for an act relating to protections for medical practitioners and health care institutions, including those related to the exercise of conscience, whistleblower activities, and free speech, and providing penalties.
ia:HF 571.summary: Allows medical practitioners and health care institutions to refuse to participate in or pay for health care services that violate their conscience, bars discrimination for refusing, bars retaliation for whistleblowing, and limits licensing penalties for protected speech.

ia:HF 640.title: A bill for an act concerning self-storage facilities, including acceptances and defaults of rental agreements.
ia:HF 640.summary: Changes self-storage rules: a renter who keeps a unit without signing a written agreement within 30 days is treated as accepting it, operators give 15 days' notice to remove property after non-rent defaults, and residential use is an immediate default.

ia:HF 648.title: A bill for an act relating to a licensed sedation provider host permit for a dentist.
ia:HF 648.summary: Creates a sedation provider host permit letting a dentist who completes a board-approved course and meets equipment and life-support training requirements employ a sedation provider to give moderate sedation to patients 13 and older and monitor them.

ia:HF 703.title: A bill for an act concerning information regarding certain state and federal student loan programs.
ia:HF 703.summary: Requires the Iowa College Aid Bureau to compare estimated rates on federal Direct PLUS loans with state college family and partnership loans, publish a statement if the state loans may be lower, and notify Iowa colleges, which must include it in aid offers.

ia:HF 766.title: A bill for an act relating to motor vehicle window tint, and making penalties applicable.
ia:HF 766.summary: As introduced, bars driving with front windshields under 70 percent light transmittance or side windows beside or ahead of the driver under 50 percent, replacing the state transportation department's rulemaking authority over window tint.

ia:HF 777.title: A bill for an act relating to applications for a motor vehicle salvage certificate of title by an insurer without surrendering the certificate of title or manufacturer’s or importer’s statement of origin, making penalties applicable, and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 777.summary: Lets supporting documents for an insurer's salvage-title application, such as a power of attorney, be signed under penalty of perjury, including electronically, instead of notarized; relieves the department and county treasurers of liability for relying on them after reasonable verification. Takes effect January 1, 2027.

ia:HF 864.title: A bill for an act requiring persons who operate certain internet sites, applications, or a segment of an internet site or application that contains material pornographic for minors to perform reasonable age verification.
ia:HF 864.summary: Requires operators of sites or apps with a substantial portion of content pornographic for minors to use reasonable age verification, limits retention of users' identifying data, exempts news organizations and internet access providers, and lets the attorney general enforce.

ia:HF 907.title: A bill for an act requiring the department of transportation to provide for the registration of noncommercial fleet vehicles and issue special noncommercial fleet vehicle registration plates.
ia:HF 907.summary: Requires the Department of Transportation, by December 1, 2028, to create a registration program and special reassignable plates, exempt from annual validation stickers, for noncommercial fleet vehicles: groups of two or more commonly owned or controlled vehicles used for business.

ia:HF 917.title: A bill for an act relating to civil liability actions against motocross facilities.
ia:HF 917.summary: Shields motocross facility operators from liability for injuries or deaths from the inherent risks of motocross, except for intentional injury, negligence, unsafe equipment, or failure to use reasonable care, and requires posted warning signs.

ia:HF 960.title: A bill for an act relating to the sales tax exemption for the purchase of central office equipment or transmission equipment used by certain entities primarily in the furnishing of telecommunications services on a commercial basis.
ia:HF 960.summary: Expands the sales tax exemption for telecommunications central office and transmission equipment by dropping "primarily" and adding internet access services, for carriers, cable operators, utilities, cooperatives, and mobile radio providers.

ia:HF 990.title: A bill for an act relating to the issuance of medical cannabidiol registration cards and licensure of medical cannabidiol dispensaries.
ia:HF 990.summary: Removes the Iowa residency requirement for a medical cannabidiol registration card and lets the Department of Health and Human Services license up to 10 medical cannabidiol dispensaries instead of 5.

ia:HF 992.title: A bill for an act relating to the fee for duplicates or other evidence of interstate fuel use tax permits or licenses.
ia:HF 992.summary: As introduced, raises the fee for a duplicate or other evidence of an interstate fuel permit or license from 50 cents to $1.

ia:SF 176.title: A bill for an act relating to participation in cocurricular and extracurricular activities offered by school districts by pupils who open enroll for purposes of receiving educational instruction and course content primarily over the internet.
ia:SF 176.summary: As introduced, lets students who open enroll in online instruction take part in their home district's extracurricular activities only if the online school's own attendance center does not sponsor those activities.

ia:SF 2039.title: A bill for an act providing for intervention by members of the general assembly in proceedings for judicial review of agency action under the Iowa administrative procedure Act. Effective date: 07/01/2026.
ia:SF 2039.summary: Allows the majority and minority leaders of the Senate and the speaker and minority leader of the House to each intervene in court reviews of state agency actions, and lets other legislators join a motion to intervene.

ia:SF 2086.title: A bill for an act authorizing schools to offer an elective junior fire fighter program to students enrolled in grades eleven and twelve.
ia:SF 2086.summary: Lets schools offer an elective junior fire fighter program to grade 11 and 12 students under an agreement with a local fire department; participants may take Firefighter I certification tests, but certification is issued only at age 18.

ia:SF 2088.title: A bill for an act relating to transportation, including the administration and regulation of matters associated with the operation, registration, and titling of motor vehicles and the Mississippi river parkway commission, making penalties applicable, and including applicability provisions.
ia:SF 2088.summary: Raises the property damage level that requires a driver crash report from $1,500 to $5,000, requires reports from uninsured drivers, allows online renewal of nonoperator IDs and replacement of licenses, and has the state transportation department run one vehicle records system counties must use.

ia:SF 2114.title: A bill for an act relating to intimidation with a dangerous weapon, and making penalties applicable.
ia:SF 2114.summary: Extends intimidation with a dangerous weapon (class C with intent to injure or provoke fear or anger, class D without) to shooting or discharging at another person, and removes the assembly-of-people and reasonable-fear-of-serious-injury elements.

ia:SF 2139.title: A bill for an act enacting the athletic trainer compact.
ia:SF 2139.summary: Enacts the athletic trainer licensure compact, letting a trainer licensed in one participating state practice in another through a compact privilege without a separate license; the compact takes effect when seven states adopt it.

ia:SF 2168.title: A bill for an act relating to workforce matters including apprenticeships and other career training, unemployment insurance, and membership of the state workforce development board, making appropriations, and including effective date provisions.
ia:SF 2168.summary: Changes workforce laws: adds intermediary sponsors to apprenticeship programs, raises the annual apprenticeship training appropriation to $4.5 million, creates a reemployment case management program for unemployment claimants, repeals the summer youth intern pilot, and adds four workforce board members.

ia:SF 2187.title: A bill for an act relating to the verification of citizenship and immigration status of persons who apply for or renew a driver’s license or nonoperator’s identification card, and including applicability provisions.
ia:SF 2187.summary: Requires the Department of Transportation to use the federal SAVE system to verify citizenship or immigration status of driver's license and ID card applicants and renewers who do not prove citizenship, and bars issuing or renewing if lawful presence cannot be verified.

ia:SF 2189.title: A bill for an act relating to information required for nonresidents who apply for vehicle registration and issuance of a certificate of title.
ia:SF 2189.summary: Lets a nonresident who owns Iowa real property and uses the vehicle mainly there register or title it by showing reasonable proof of owning the property, and list an out-of-state license number instead of the vehicle's primary user's Iowa details.

ia:SF 2201.title: A bill for an act relating to school funding by establishing the state percent of growth and the categorical state percent of growth for the budget year beginning July 1, 2026, modifying provisions relating to property tax replacement payments, transportation equity aid funding, funding for school district budget adjustments, and school district enrollment, establishing an education support personnel salary supplement, making appropriations, and including effective date and applicability provisions.
ia:SF 2201.summary: As amended by the House, sets the state percent of growth for school funding at 2.0 percent for the budget year beginning July 1, 2026, caps transportation equity payments at $1 million per district, appropriates $7 million for education support staff pay, and changes enrollment counts and payment timing.

ia:SF 2207.title: A bill for an act relating to the submission of proposed legislation by the governor and state departments and agencies.
ia:SF 2207.summary: Moves the deadline for state departments and agencies to submit proposed bills and resolutions to the Legislative Services Agency from 45 to 60 days before a session, and applies it to the governor except in the year of initial inauguration.

ia:SF 2218.title: A bill for an act relating to state regulatory compliance and eligibility requirements, including by modifying provisions related to the verification of the identity and employment eligibility of individuals by the board of educational examiners, school districts, accredited nonpublic schools, charter schools, and innovation zone schools; the provision of a false social security number to an employer, prospective employer, or a potential employee; qualifications for employment, professional licensure, voter registration, and bail; making penalties applicable; and including applicability provisions.
ia:SF 2218.summary: Requires work authorization proof for teacher licenses, E-Verify by public employers, and SAVE checks for professional licenses and voter rolls; bars unauthorized aliens from registering to vote; fines employers knowingly employing workers using another's Social Security number; sets pretrial detention presumptions.

ia:SF 2219.title: A bill for an act requiring boards of directors of school districts, governing boards of charter schools, and authorities in charge of accredited nonpublic schools to adopt policies related to exempting student absences for school-sponsored activities, programs, competitions, and projects.
ia:SF 2219.summary: Requires school districts, charter schools, and accredited nonpublic schools to adopt policies granting exempt absences, with make-up of missed classwork, for students involved in school-sponsored activities, programs, competitions, or projects.

ia:SF 2220.title: A bill for an act relating to education, including by modifying provisions related to the Iowa statewide assessment of student progress and programs for gifted and talented children, and by requiring school districts to develop an advanced mathematics pathway and implement procedures for subject acceleration and whole-grade acceleration, and including applicability provisions.
ia:SF 2220.summary: Moves the statewide science assessment from grade 10 to grade 11, requires school districts to set uniform procedures for identifying and serving gifted and talented students, and requires advanced math pathways and procedures for subject and whole-grade acceleration.

ia:SF 2263.title: A bill for an act relating to the carrying, transportation, and possession of weapons, and including effective date provisions.
ia:SF 2263.summary: Allows dangerous weapons in locked, out-of-sight private vehicles in public nonsecure parking lots, bars foster care rules from prohibiting lawful firearms in vehicles carrying foster children, and bars state and local enforcement of "red flag" firearm seizure laws, with $50,000 civil penalties per occurrence.

ia:SF 2280.title: A bill for an act relating to the safety of persons in certain professions involved with the judicial system, including authorizing a member of the general assembly, judicial officer, attorney general, deputy attorney general, or assistant attorney general to be issued a professional permit to carry weapons, establishing the criminal offenses of threatening and the malicious sharing of personal information of a general assembly member or a judicial officer or a general assembly member’s or a judicial officer’s immediate family, and considering true threats to public officials as harassment, and providing penalties.
ia:SF 2280.summary: Allows legislators, judicial officers, and attorneys in the attorney general's office to get professional permits to carry weapons, makes threatening them or immediate family with specified intent a class C felony, and makes malicious sharing of their personal information a serious misdemeanor.

ia:SF 2284.title: A bill for an act relating to the use of automated systems that detect traffic violations or registration plate information, and making penalties applicable.
ia:SF 2284.summary: Sets rules for automatic license plate readers, including a local ordinance requirement, Department of Public Safety approved models, a facial recognition ban, search logs, deletion of images after 30 days, and limits on sharing images, with simple misdemeanor penalties.

ia:SF 2289.title: A bill for an act relating to matters under the purview of the department of inspections, appeals, and licensing, and including effective date provisions.
ia:SF 2289.summary: Lets the gaming commission issue cease-and-desist orders to unlicensed gambling operators, adds sports wagering to lifetime gambling bans, raises the commission members' expense cap from $30,000 to $45,000, conditions state withholding on certain winnings on federal reporting, and lets pediatric palliative facilities serve zero residents.

ia:SF 2296.title: A bill for an act relating to digital financial kiosks, modifying civil penalties, and including effective date and applicability provisions.
ia:SF 2296.summary: Changes Iowa's digital-asset kiosk law: requires kiosk operators to hold a money transmission license, redefines digital financial asset, measures charges against prevailing market value, and treats violations as unlawful practices enforced under the attorney general's consumer fraud authority.

ia:SF 2299.title: A bill for an act relating to the district-to-community college sharing or concurrent enrollment program.
ia:SF 2299.summary: Requires a parent, guardian, or adult student, if the school requests it, to repay the school what it paid a community college when the student fails or withdraws from a concurrent enrollment class.

ia:SF 2304.title: A bill for an act relating to certain public utilities, including the development of ratemaking principles permitted for recovery costs of certain investments in infrastructure by water and wastewater utilities and cost considerations for acquisitions of water, sanitary sewer, or storm water utilities.
ia:SF 2304.summary: Lets investor-owned water and wastewater utilities recover costs of certain required infrastructure projects through a monthly customer charge after the Utilities Commission approves a multiyear plan, capping charge revenue at 10 percent of authorized revenue requirement.

ia:SF 2318.title: A bill for an act relating to nonresident deer hunting licenses.
ia:SF 2318.summary: Requires nonresident deer hunters who buy an antlered or any-sex license to also buy an antlerless-only license unless the state commission designates the hunting zone as exempt; current law requires the second license in every zone.

ia:SF 2320.title: A bill for an act modifying provisions related to the district-to-community college sharing or concurrent enrollment program.
ia:SF 2320.summary: Requires students to take the in-person version of a community college course offered both in person and online through concurrent enrollment, unless the school superintendent or designee authorizes the online version.

ia:SF 2365.title: A bill for an act relating to public improvement contracts, including notice requirements.
ia:SF 2365.summary: Requires a public body to send the principal contractor, surety and claimants written notice of the date it finally accepted a public improvement within 14 days, and shields the body from liability for failing to send it.

ia:SF 2378.title: A bill for an act relating to the ability of property owners to protest proposed changes in zoning districts.
