ia:SF 2378.summary: Repeals the rule requiring a three-fourths city council vote on a zoning change when owners of 20 percent of affected or nearby property file a written protest, and lets people affected by a variance appeal to the council within 60 days.

ia:SF 2379.title: A bill for an act relating to victim protections including victim counselors, protective orders, sex offender registration, rights of sexual abuse victims, mental competency and civil commitment, restitution, and victim rights, and including effective date provisions.
ia:SF 2379.summary: Changes crime victim laws, including confidentiality of victim counselor communications, protective orders, sex offender registration, sexual abuse evidence, victim rights, restoration of mental competency, and restitution.

ia:SF 2399.title: A bill for an act relating to bail and bond amounts and conditions.
ia:SF 2399.summary: Bars magistrates from setting bail below the uniform bond schedule without written justification, limits release on own recognizance to nonviolent, nondrug simple or serious misdemeanors, and directs the Judicial Council to update the bond schedule by July 1, 2027.

ia:SF 2417.title: A bill for an act establishing requirements and guidelines for conversational AI services, and providing civil penalties, and including applicability provisions.
ia:SF 2417.summary: Requires operators of public conversational AI services to disclose AI status to minors, avoid unpredictable engagement rewards for minors, limit sexual content, and adopt suicide and self-harm referral protocols; attorney general enforces, with $1,000-per-violation penalties up to $500,000 per operator, from July 1, 2027.

ia:SF 2422.title: A bill for an act relating to public assistance programs under the purview of the department of health and human services, including the supplemental nutrition assistance program, Medicaid, and the Iowa health and wellness plan, and including effective date provisions.
ia:SF 2422.summary: Adds the SAVE immigration database to public assistance eligibility checks, writes SNAP immigration-status limits into state law, sets Medicaid retroactive coverage at two months for pregnant women, children and nursing home residents and none for other adults, and requires legislative approval for some Medicaid changes.

ia:SF 2426.title: A bill for an act relating to sufficient English language proficiency requirements for commercial drivers, providing penalties, and including applicability provisions.
ia:SF 2426.summary: Requires the Department of Transportation to test English proficiency of commercial driver's license and learner's permit applicants and renewals and deny those who fail, makes driving a commercial vehicle without proficiency a serious misdemeanor, and bars carriers from employing such drivers ($10,000 fine).

ia:SF 2428.title: A bill for an act relating to education, including by modifying provisions related to the duties of the department of education; the discipline of students enrolled in school districts, charter schools, and innovation zone schools who cause violent or nonviolent disruptions; the responsibilities and powers of the department of education, school district teachers, and other educational staff related to students who have individualized education programs or plans under section 504 of the federal Rehabilitation Act; school district professional development plans; and authorizing teachers to request a meeting of a student’s individualized education program team.
ia:SF 2428.summary: Authorizes teachers to remove students for nonviolent classroom disruptions and requires removal for violent ones, creates oversight committees on readmission, sets individualized education program team duties and training, and creates an attendance center pilot program.

ia:SF 2429.title: A bill for an act relating to fluid milk products annual permits, and including effective date provisions.
ia:SF 2429.summary: Raises the maximum gross weight for annual permits for vehicles hauling fluid milk products to or from milk plants on primary roads from 96,000 to 136,000 pounds, effective January 1, 2027.

ia:SF 2430.title: A bill for an act relating to the display of flags at half-staff on public buildings.
ia:SF 2430.summary: Requires custodians of public buildings to follow governor's proclamations on flying the U.S. and Iowa flags at half-staff, and lets the attorney general take legal action over violations.

ia:SF 2453.title: A bill for an act providing for investment by regents institutions in certified innovation funds and including effective date provisions.
ia:SF 2453.summary: Requires the foundations of the University of Iowa, Iowa State, and Northern Iowa to invest at least 1 percent of their endowment assets by July 1, 2027, in innovation funds certified by the economic development authority.

ia:SF 2465.title: A bill for an act relating to agriculture, including by providing for the powers and duties of the department of agriculture and land stewardship, including the promotion and regulation of commodities and products, the regulation of the transportation of agricultural items, the use of agricultural land, sales and use taxes, and veterinary practice and income taxes, making penalties applicable, and including effective date and applicability provisions.
ia:SF 2465.summary: Makes many agriculture changes, including Choose Iowa program membership and school purchasing provisions, grain dealer and weights and measures rules, agricultural tourism and land use provisions, a honeybee sales tax exemption, and rural veterinarian loan repayment changes.

ia:SF 2467.title: A bill for an act concerning reimbursement of the attorney general for services relating to the second injury fund for workers’ compensation.
ia:SF 2467.summary: Raises the annual cap on reimbursement to the attorney general from the workers' compensation Second Injury Fund for legal services from $450,000 to $900,000.

ia:SF 2468.title: A bill for an act providing for the conversion of partnerships into other forms of domestic or foreign organizations, and providing for fees.
ia:SF 2468.summary: Lets Iowa general partnerships convert into other business forms, such as limited partnerships, LLCs, corporations, nonprofits or business trusts, or into out-of-state organizations, with partner approval, a filed plan and articles of conversion, and a $50 filing fee.

ia:SF 2471.title: A bill for an act relating to fees for lifetime fur harvester licenses.
ia:SF 2471.summary: Sets the fee for a lifetime fur harvester license for Iowa residents disabled in military service at $5 plus any processing fee, instead of a fee set by Department of Natural Resources rules.

ia:SF 2472.title: A bill for an act relating to state and local government taxes, fees, financial authority, and budgets, by modifying property assessment provisions, divisions of revenue, and funding from the secure an advanced vision for education fund, establishing a program for first-time homebuyers, modifying and making appropriations, and including effective date, applicability, and retroactive applicability provisions.
ia:SF 2472.summary: Limits county and city general property tax levy rates for fiscal years 2027-28 through 2029-30 to yield about 102 percent of the prior year's dollars excluding new valuation, creates the FirstHome Iowa program, and changes urban renewal rules.

ia:SF 2474.title: A bill for an act relating to education, including by modifying provisions related to the Iowa dyslexia board and requiring the department of education to prepare a report related to cardiac emergency response plans and automated external defibrillators.
ia:SF 2474.summary: Requires the Department of Education to report to the legislature by January 15, 2027 how many schools have cardiac emergency response plans and where each school's defibrillators are located, and extends the Iowa dyslexia board's repeal date from 2027 to 2032.

ia:SF 2478.title: A bill for an act relating to transportation and other infrastructure-related appropriations to the department of transportation, including allocation and use of moneys from the road use tax fund and the primary road fund.
ia:SF 2478.summary: Appropriates money for fiscal year 2026-2027 from the road use tax fund and primary road fund to the Department of Transportation for operations, motor vehicle services, and facility maintenance.

ia:SF 2484.title: A bill for an act relating to and making appropriations from the rebuild Iowa infrastructure fund, technology reinvestment fund, and renewable fuel infrastructure fund, providing for related matters including financial assistance eligibility for regional sports authority districts, department of health and human services information technology systems, the railway tracks overpass and underpass fund, and eligibility for entities to receive financial assistance from both the Iowa major events and tourism fund and the sports tourism infrastructure program, and including effective date provisions.
ia:SF 2484.summary: Appropriates money for fiscal year 2026-2027 from the Rebuild Iowa Infrastructure Fund and Technology Reinvestment Fund for state infrastructure and technology projects, changes some earlier appropriations, and raises the Capitol maintenance fund deposit from $500,000 to $750,000.

ia:SF 2488.title: A bill for an act relating to early childhood and family services, including the creation of an early childhood and family services system, making appropriations, convening an early childhood Iowa interim study committee, and including applicability, retroactive applicability, and effective date provisions.
ia:SF 2488.summary: Creates an early childhood and family services system under the Department of Health and Human Services, with districts and advisory councils delivering prevention and early intervention services for children under 19 and their families.

ia:SF 2490.title: A bill for an act relating to oil and gas production, including filing requirements, the authority of the department of natural resources, confidential information, pooling orders, negotiation of surface damage, imposition and distribution of a tax, and jurisdiction, and providing civil penalties.
ia:SF 2490.summary: Changes oil and gas production law: yearly filings with the Department of Natural Resources, variances from its rules, five-year confidentiality, pooling orders, surface-owner permission and damage agreements, a severance tax on production, and a bar on most local limits on oil and gas operations.

ia:SF 2492.title: A bill for an act creating a state corporate income tax deduction for net controlled foreign corporation tested income, and including retroactive applicability provisions.
ia:SF 2492.summary: Removes the reference to global intangible low-taxed income from Iowa's corporate deduction for income under federal section 951A, so it covers net controlled foreign corporation tested income, which replaced it. Applies to tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2026.

ia:SF 2493.title: A bill for an act relating to the excise tax on certain ethanol blended gasoline purchased exclusively for use in an implement of husbandry used in agricultural production.
ia:SF 2493.summary: Exempts ethanol-blended gasoline with more than 85 percent ethanol from the motor fuel excise tax when bought at a terminal or refinery rack for farm implements, with buyers documenting purchases using a Department of Revenue exemption certificate.

ia:SF 2496.title: A bill for an act relating to Iowa’s urban renewal law by modifying the division of revenue for certain emergency medical services property tax levies, and including effective date and applicability provisions.
ia:SF 2496.summary: Excludes property taxes for emergency medical services levies from the tax increment financing revenue division in urban renewal areas, for taxes due in fiscal years beginning on or after July 1, 2026.

ia:SF 2497.title: A bill for an act providing for an assignment of assets for the benefit of creditors, exempting the related tax on the transfer of real estate, and including effective date provisions.
ia:SF 2497.summary: Replaces Iowa's current assignment-for-creditors law with the Uniform Assignment for Benefit of Creditors Act, setting rules for a debtor's transfer of all assets to an assignee who pays creditors, with creditor notice. Exempts the transfer from real estate transfer tax. Effective January 1, 2027.

ia:SF 273.title: A bill for an act relating to mandatory reporting to the board of educational examiners of licensed school employees who engage in grooming behavior toward students.
ia:SF 273.summary: As introduced, redefines "grooming behavior" that schools must report to the board of educational examiners as a pattern of behavior to entice or entrap a student in order to take advantage of the student, including through a sex act.

ia:SF 274.title: A bill for an act relating to forms of payment for entry into an extracurricular interscholastic athletic contest or competition.
ia:SF 274.summary: Requires public schools, and organizations registering with the Department of Education, to accept legal tender as payment for entry to interscholastic athletic events they sponsor, with some exceptions.

ia:SF 304.title: A bill for an act providing an exception to a minor’s legal capacity to consent to the provision of medical care or services for a sexually transmitted disease or infection.
ia:SF 304.summary: Removes a minor's legal ability to consent to vaccinations for sexually transmitted diseases or infections, while leaving consent to prevention, diagnosis and treatment otherwise unchanged.

ia:SF 378.title: A bill for an act relating to speed limits, including the speed limit range for which certain excessive speed violations cannot be considered for certain purposes and the default speed limit for all vehicular traffic, and making penalties applicable.
ia:SF 378.summary: Raises the default speed limit from 55 to 60 miles per hour, and extends the rule that the Department of Transportation and insurers disregard a driver's first two violations of 10 mph or less over to zones with limits up to 60.

ia:SF 469.title: A bill for an act creating an emeritus license to practice medicine and surgery or osteopathic medicine and surgery.
ia:SF 469.summary: Requires the Board of Medicine to issue three-year, once-renewable emeritus licenses to physicians aged 60 or older primarily supervising and training residents, with the same scope of practice, no continuing education requirement, and half-price fees.

ia:SF 472.title: A bill for an act relating to retention and recertification elections for public employee collective bargaining units and including effective date and applicability provisions.
ia:SF 472.summary: Exempts from the bill's retention and recertification elections any public employee bargaining unit in which at least 30 percent of members are public safety employees.

ia:SF 473.title: A bill for an act relating to certain sincerely held religious or moral beliefs of certain entities for purposes of child foster care and adoption.
ia:SF 473.summary: Adds a requirement that the Department of Health and Human Services convene the Sabrina Ray Child Welfare Task Force within 30 days after session ends and report to government oversight committees by February 10, 2027.

ia:SF 492.title: A bill for an act relating to the acquisition of certain vehicles by a vehicle recycler, and making penalties applicable.
ia:SF 492.summary: Bars licensed vehicle recyclers from buying a titleless vehicle at least 12 model years old for under $1,000 unless they check state records for lienholders, except when buying from a scrap metal dealer.

ia:SF 512.title: A bill for an act relating to statutes of limitations in civil actions.
ia:SF 512.summary: Adds language to Iowa's civil statute of limitations law stating that it does not change when a claim accrues, including the discovery rule, and that limitation periods may be changed only by an act of the General Assembly.

ia:SF 542.title: A bill for an act relating to the suspension of child support and medical support in certain circumstances.
ia:SF 542.summary: Lets a court suspend a child or medical support order, without advance notice, on application of the paying person when juvenile court places the child with them; parties may object within 21 days, and the obligation generally ends 60 days after the juvenile case ends.

ia:SF 563.title: A bill for an act relating to the licensure of crematory operators and funeral establishments, and making penalties applicable.
ia:SF 563.summary: Requires the Board of Mortuary Science to adopt rules licensing crematory operators, including a specialized cremation course, to license funeral directors who apply, and lets either operate a cremation establishment.

ia:SF 629.title: A bill for an act providing for an expedited filing service for filers of business documents administered by the secretary of state, and providing fees.
ia:SF 629.summary: Adds two faster expedited-filing options for business documents at the Secretary of State: a one-hour service for a $200 surcharge and same-day service for $125, alongside the existing two-day ($50) and five-day ($15) options.

ia:SF 639.title: A bill for an act creating a specialty business court, and including effective date provisions.
ia:SF 639.summary: Adds that an action may be transferred to the new specialty business court if all parties consent in writing to the assignment or transfer.

ia:SF 654.title: A bill for an act relating to wildlife, including the treatment of beaver dams, identification for traps, snares, and tree stands, maximum fur dealer license fees, and deer depredation, and making penalties applicable.
ia:SF 654.summary: Requires metal ID plates on deer tree stands on public land ($30 fine), lets owners' agents and drainage districts breach beaver dams, lets trap and snare tags show a department-issued ID number, and caps fur dealer license fees at $50 a year.

ia:SF 93.title: A bill for an act relating to qualifications to serve as a commissioner or an executive director for a county commission of veteran affairs. Effective date: 07/01/2026.
ia:SF 93.summary: Allows Iowa residents who are current or former Iowa National Guard or Iowa-based reserve members, with satisfactory service or an honorable discharge, not only veterans, to serve on county veterans affairs commissions; executive directors must still be veterans.

ia:SJR 11.title: A joint resolution proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the State of Iowa relating to requirements for certain state tax law changes.
ia:SJR 11.summary: Replaces the resolution with a proposed constitutional amendment requiring a two-thirds vote of each house of the General Assembly to pass any bill that increases corporate income tax credits or creates a new corporate tax credit.

id:H 508.title: TRANSPORTATION – Amends and adds to existing law to revise provisions regarding bicycle and pedestrian projects.
id:H 508.summary: As introduced, revises a definition in Idaho transportation code, allows federal funds and grants to be used to improve bicycle and pedestrian facilities, and amends a provision on violations.

id:H 516.title: EDUCATION – Amends and adds to existing law to establish provisions regarding the prohibition of taxpayer funding of teachers unions.
id:H 516.summary: Bars school districts from deducting teachers union dues, distributing union communications, or paying leave for union activities, with exceptions; paid representational time requires the union to reimburse the district. Sets civil penalties of up to $250, $1,500 or $2,500 by violation type.

id:H 522.title: UNMANNED AIRCRAFT SYSTEMS – Adds to existing law to establish provisions regarding unmanned aircraft systems near Department of Correction facilities.
id:H 522.summary: As amended in the Senate, makes it a misdemeanor, with a fine up to $1,000 or six months in jail, to fly a drone within 400 feet above a state prison's perimeter, and lets officials take reasonable measures against drones used harmfully there.

id:H 542.title: SOCIAL MEDIA – Adds to existing law to establish the Stop Harms from Addictive Social Media Act.
id:H 542.summary: As amended in the Senate, requires social media platforms with $1 billion or more in advertising revenue to get verifiable parental consent for accounts of users 16 and under and bars addictive interface features and profile-based ads in those users' feeds.

id:H 561.title: STATE GOVERNMENT AND STATE AFFAIRS – Amends existing law to revise and remove provisions regarding flags flown by a governmental entity, to provide a penalty, and to establish provisions regarding enforcement by the Attorney General.
id:H 561.summary: As amended in the Senate, revises the list of flags governments may display and sets a $2,000-per-flag, per-day civil penalty for violations; the Attorney General sues after giving 10 days' written notice to cure.

id:H 575.title: STATE CONTROLLER – Amends existing law to provide that the State Controller shall publish a list of asset forfeitures and to provide that law enforcement shall report asset forfeiture information to the State Controller.
id:H 575.summary: Requires the state controller to store and publish a current list of asset forfeitures, and requires state, county and local law enforcement agencies to share forfeiture information with the controller.

id:H 585.title: ELECTRICAL, PLUMBING, AND HVAC INSPECTIONS – Adds to existing law to provide for timely electrical, plumbing, and HVAC inspections and the option for third-party inspections in certain situations.
id:H 585.summary: Lets permit holders hire a third-party inspector, with a fee refund, when an electrical, plumbing or HVAC inspection is not done within 48 business hours, and requires a 10 percent refund when no reason for a failed inspection is given within three business days.

id:H 602.title: FOREIGN LAWS – Adds to existing law to establish provisions prohibiting the use of foreign laws in Idaho courts.
id:H 602.summary: As introduced, bars the use of foreign laws and foreign legal doctrines in Idaho courts.

id:H 629.title: TRANSPORTATION – Amends existing law to provide for a printed copy of a registration card for vehicles.
id:H 629.summary: As amended in the Senate, requires a person issued a vehicle registration card electronically to print it, and lets the printed copy satisfy the requirement to carry the card in the vehicle.

id:H 637.title: GOLD AND SILVER – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding gold and silver coin and specie.
id:H 637.summary: Expands Idaho's gold and silver coin and specie legal-tender provision, enacted in 2025, from coin minted domestically to foreign or domestic coin, and moves the section to a new code number.

id:H 648.title: INSURANCE – Adds to existing law to establish provisions regarding coverage of anticancer medications under health benefit plans.
id:H 648.summary: Requires health benefit plans issued or renewed from January 2027 that cover anticancer drugs to apply the same copayment, coinsurance and deductible to oral anticancer drugs as to injected or intravenous ones.

id:H 650.title: STATE GOVERNMENT AND STATE AFFAIRS – Adds to existing law to provide for state sovereignty, jurisdictional presumption, and a limitation on federal power.
id:H 650.summary: As introduced, declares a strong presumption that Idaho has jurisdiction over matters within the state unless the U.S. Constitution clearly and specifically grants authority to the federal government.

id:H 665.title: MOTOR VEHICLES – Amending existing law to revise provisions regarding Appaloosa license plates.
id:H 665.summary: Changes the recipient of Appaloosa license plate fees to the Appaloosa Museum and Heritage Center Foundation, broadens the fee purpose to horse education and programming, and raises the plate's vehicle weight limit from 16,000 to 26,000 pounds.

id:H 667.title: MOTOR VEHICLES – Amends existing law to eliminate the nondomiciled CDL program in Idaho.
id:H 667.summary: As introduced, bars Idaho from honoring learner's permits from other states or countries for commercial driver's licenses, which will be issued only to those who complete the entire process in Idaho.

id:H 674.title: TELECOMMUNICATION SERVICE – Amends and adds to existing law to revise provisions regarding the discontinuation of telecommunication service.
id:H 674.summary: As introduced, lets a telephone company discontinue local service if the Federal Communications Commission permits it, and requires the Public Utilities Commission to adopt the FCC's discontinuance findings.

id:H 678.title: TRAPPING – Adds to existing law to provide for the checking of wolf traps.
id:H 678.summary: Requires anyone setting a trap or snare for gray wolves to inspect it every 72 hours and promptly remove any catch; inspection may be in person or by a remote camera with an unobstructed view.

id:H 681.title: CRIMINAL PROCEDURE – Amends existing law to provide that there shall be no statute of limitations for certain felonies.
id:H 681.summary: Removes the statute of limitations for prosecuting aggravated lewd conduct with a child and producing sexually exploitative material, adding them to crimes such as murder and certain rapes that can be prosecuted at any time.

id:H 683.title: SEX OFFENDERS – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding where a sex offender resides.
id:H 683.summary: Redefines a registered sex offender's residence as where the offender habitually lives, including homeless locations and places visited over five hours more than five times in 30 days, and revises the facility exception to the 500-foot school and daycare residence ban.

id:H 684.title: COUNTY SHERIFFS – Adds to existing law to authorize a sheriff’s office to seek reimbursement for costs of recapture.
id:H 684.summary: Allows a county sheriff's office that travels out of state to retrieve an absconded prisoner, probationer or parolee to seek invoiced reimbursement; requires the Department of Correction to budget for it and ensure payment within 30 days.

id:H 689.title: ADMINISTRATIVE SUBPOENAS – Amends existing law to revise a provision regarding an administrative subpoena.
id:H 689.summary: Adds the crime of visual representations of the sexual abuse of children, which includes AI-generated images, to the offenses for which prosecutors or the attorney general may subpoena electronic service providers for subscriber identifying records.

id:H 696.title: PRISONERS – Amends existing law to revise the definition of “sexual contact.”
id:H 696.summary: Broadens the definition of sexual contact in Idaho's law on sexual contact with prisoners and supervised offenders to include contact between the mouth and any body part, and any willful touching over or under clothing intended to arouse or gratify.

id:H 706.title: IDAHO BUILDING CODES – Adds to existing law to establish provisions regarding single stairway building exceptions.
id:H 706.summary: Lets local governments allow apartment buildings up to six stories to be served by a single interior exit stair if they meet fire-safety standards, such as sprinklers throughout, a two-hour fire-rated stairway and elevator shaft, and no more than four units per floor.

id:H 711.title: EDUCATION – Amends and adds to existing law to provide for alternative authorization for administrators and to authorize the use of funds for related mentoring.
id:H 711.summary: Creates a three-year interim certificate for school principals and superintendents without an administrator certificate, requiring a bachelor's degree, five years of relevant experience, coursework and mentoring by a certified administrator, and lets districts use mentoring funds for it.

id:H 721.title: IDAHO BUILDING CODE ACT – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding public school building plan reviews.
id:H 721.summary: Requires permitting authorities to complete initial plan review for public works within 30 calendar days and removes the requirement that school districts get plan approval before advertising for bids on school construction.

id:H 728.title: EDUCATION – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding educational staff, teachers, and certificates.
id:H 728.summary: Revises school staff definitions, adding classified staff and instructional support staff; extends the State Board of Education's lifetime-certificate rulemaking authority to pupil service and other certificated staff; corrects education code references.

id:H 730.title: SUPPLEMENTAL NUTRITION ASSISTANCE PROGRAM – Amends and adds to existing law to establish provisions regarding Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program integrity measures and verification.
id:H 730.summary: Requires Health and Welfare to match SNAP households against lottery winnings of $3,000 or more and other databases, verify applicants' citizenship or immigration status, and disenroll those not lawfully present; bars income and asset limits above federal standards.

id:H 750.title: TRANSACTIONS – Amends and adds to existing law to establish provisions regarding programmable money.
id:H 750.summary: As amended, excludes "programmable money" from the Uniform Commercial Code definition of money, bars issuers from denying transactions based on listed lawful characteristics, activities or social credit scores, and sets civil remedies and misdemeanor penalties.

id:H 752.title: INDECENCY AND OBSCENITY – Adds to existing law to prohibit a person from entering a restroom or changing room of the opposite sex, to provide a penalty, and to provide exceptions.
id:H 752.summary: As introduced, makes it a misdemeanor to knowingly enter a restroom, changing room, locker room or shower room in a government building or public accommodation designated for the opposite biological sex; a repeat conviction within five years is a felony, with exceptions.

id:H 758.title: DAYCARE LICENSING – Amends existing law to provide for supervision requirements while a child is sleeping and to establish an exception regarding children to be counted in attendance at a daycare.
id:H 758.summary: As amended in the Senate, lets daycare providers meet the supervision rule for sleeping children by using live video and audio while staying nearby, and stops counting a home provider's own children aged five or older toward child-to-staff ratios.

id:H 766.title: DEVELOPMENT IMPACT FEES – Amends existing law to revise a definition regarding which governmental entities are authorized to adopt development impact fees.
id:H 766.summary: As introduced, adds fire and ambulance service districts to the entities that may adopt development impact fee ordinances, alongside cities, counties and single county-wide highway districts.

id:H 772.title: INDUSTRIAL HEMP – Amends existing law to provide for negligent violations.
id:H 772.summary: Provides that industrial hemp producers do not commit a negligent violation if the hemp is grown only for grain or fiber, the producer made reasonable efforts to follow THC and state-plan rules, and total THC is 1 percent or less by dry weight.

id:H 773.title: DEPARTMENT OF FINANCE – Amends and repeals existing law to remove obsolete provisions.
id:H 773.summary: Repeals 19 sections of Idaho law, 17 on the Idaho Corporate Credit Union and two on cemeteries, and removes a credit union liquidity-reserve provision that refers to it, under the Idaho Code Cleanup Act.

id:H 776.title: CHILD PROTECTION – Adds to existing law to provide for safety checks for children under one year of age.
id:H 776.summary: Requires Health and Welfare to verify within 12 hours a reported risk factor, such as prior termination of parental rights, for a caregiver of a child under age 1, then give verified cases a priority response and a written safety assessment.

id:H 788.title: MEDICAID – Adds to existing law to establish provisions regarding Medicaid prior authorization exemptions for certain preceptorships.
id:H 788.summary: As amended in the Senate, gives physicians, physician assistants and advanced practice nurses in family medicine, psychiatry or obstetrics who provide 360 preceptorship hours a year, 60 percent in rural or underserved areas, a 12-month Medicaid prior authorization exemption, capped at 100 per specialty yearly.

id:H 797.title: FIRE PROTECTION DISTRICTS – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding the residence qualifications for fire protection district commissioners.
id:H 797.summary: Requires fire protection district commissioners to live in the subdistrict they represent for at least 90 consecutive days before appointment or election, in addition to living in the district for a year.

id:H 798.title: STATE TREASURER – Repeals existing law to remove obsolete provisions relating to securities lending agreements.
id:H 798.summary: Repeals Section 67-1210B of Idaho Code on state securities lending agreements, which the bill's intent section calls obsolete, outdated or unnecessary; the statement of purpose says securities lending ended in December 2015.

id:H 799.title: ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES – Repeals existing law to remove obsolete provisions regarding the prohibition and sale of liquors and wines.
id:H 799.summary: Repeals three alcohol statutes: a provision on convictions before the 1939 Liquor Act, a requirement that sellers furnish price lists, and a requirement to file attorney contact information with the State Liquor Division.

id:H 800.title: MANUFACTURED HOMES – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding siting of manufactured homes in residential areas.
id:H 800.summary: Lowers the minimum size cities and counties may require for manufactured homes outside mobile home parks from 1,000 to 400 square feet (single-section) or 800 (multisectional), and limits multi-unit manufactured homes to areas where multifamily housing is allowed.

id:H 803.title: EXECUTION – Amends existing law to provide that procedures used in an execution shall not be subject to certain provisions of law.
id:H 803.summary: Exempts execution procedures set by the corrections director from the state administrative procedure act, and expands the list of execution personnel whose identities are confidential and not discoverable to include firing squad members and technical-assistance providers.

id:H 810.title: ELECTIONS – Amends existing law to provide certain physical presence requirements for state representatives and senators.
id:H 810.summary: As amended in the Senate, adds a requirement that legislative candidates maintain a residence in their district with at least 120 nights' presence in the year before filing, with an exemption for active military service.

id:H 815.title: EDUCATION – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding the transportation support program.
id:H 815.summary: Changes the baseline year used to calculate state transportation support for certain public charter schools (those that began transportation before July 1, 2009 and received under $3,000 in fiscal 2010) to their first fiscal year of full operations after 2010.

id:H 817.title: TOBACCO PRODUCTS – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding the sale of cigars.
id:H 817.summary: Creates an annual tobacco permit for mobile cigar retailers, valid at temporary locations statewide, and exempts them and 21-and-over cigar gardens from vendor-assisted-sale rules, and, at 21-and-over events, from sealed-package and free-sample rules for cigars bought at retail.

id:H 822.title: PEDIATRIC SECRETIVE TRANSITIONS PARENTAL RIGHTS ACT – Adds to existing law to establish the Pediatric Secretive Transitions Parental Rights Act.
id:H 822.summary: As amended in the Senate, bars schools, child care and health care providers from aiding a minor's social transition without written parental consent, requires parent notice within 72 hours of certain student requests, and allows parent lawsuits and Attorney General penalties.

id:H 826.title: HONEY INDUSTRY – Amends, repeals, and adds to existing law to revise provisions regarding the Idaho Honey Commission.
id:H 826.summary: Transfers regulatory duties for the honey industry from the Idaho Honey Commission to the Idaho Department of Agriculture and removes outdated code language.

id:H 832.title: EDUCATION – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding career technical education certificates.
id:H 832.summary: Removes the minimum hours of professional experience from state law for career technical education teaching certificates, leaving the State Board of Career Technical Education to set requirements by subject area through rules.

id:H 843.title: TAXATION – Amends existing law to eliminate proration of the homestead property tax exemption.
id:H 843.summary: Ends proration of the homestead property tax exemption; the full exemption applies as of January 1 of the tax year in which a complete application is approved.

id:H 846.title: EDUCATION – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding student enrollment counts.
id:H 846.summary: Changes from "may" to "shall" the bar on counting as enrolled a student with 11 or more consecutive unexcused absences before an official count, and adds the same bar for unexcused absences on the first 10 consecutive days of school.

id:H 849.title: EDUCATION – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding certain placement and movement on the career ladder.
id:H 849.summary: As introduced, lets career and technical education teachers and qualified school service professionals, such as counselors and nurses, who enter K-12 from private industry advance a Career Ladder rung after one proficient evaluation year instead of four.

id:H 855.title: FISH AND GAME – Amends existing law regarding lifetime hunting and fishing licenses.
id:H 855.summary: As introduced, requires five years of Idaho residency, instead of six months, to buy a lifetime hunting or fishing license.

id:H 856.title: PROTECTION OF GRAVES – Amends existing law to prohibit certain acts regarding graves and to provide exemptions.
id:H 856.summary: Expands Idaho's ban on possessing, selling, buying, leasing or displaying grave artifacts and human remains, adds exemptions for law enforcement, medical, research, museum and funeral uses, makes violations a felony, and allows seizure and forfeiture of evidence and remains.

id:H 860.title: PARENT AND CHILD – Amends existing law to provide for parental rights in medical decisions.
id:H 860.summary: As amended in the Senate, revises the Idaho Parental Rights Act's medical consent rules: sets optional, revocable blanket-consent forms, lists consent exceptions (emergencies, first aid, crime-related care, 988 calls, pregnancy diagnosis and prenatal care), and repeals the minor-consent-to-treatment chapter.

id:H 863.title: MEDICAID – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding provider payment.
id:H 863.summary: As introduced, reduces Medicaid payment rates for residential habilitation providers, cutting General Fund Medicaid spending by $21.8 million in fiscal 2027, and requires the department to report to the Legislature how those funds are used.

id:H 872.title: ELECTIONS – Amends existing law to remove a provision regarding the preparation of ballots for general elections.
id:H 872.summary: Removes the requirement that constitutional amendments and other ballot issues be printed on a separate general election ballot form, so they may share a page with the rest of the ballot.

id:H 879.title: INDUSTRIAL HEMP – Amends existing law to provide for the sale of hemp products intended for human ingestion or inhalation.
id:H 879.summary: As introduced, makes establishments that sell certain hemp products at retail subject to the existing Industrial Hemp Research and Development Act.

id:H 883.title: EDUCATION – Adds to existing law to provide for school district and public charter school earned autonomy regarding spending.
id:H 883.summary: Lets school districts and non-virtual charter schools that meet academic, graduation and financial-stability benchmarks spend state funding, including salary and categorical funds, as they choose, with fewer state reporting requirements.

id:H 887.title: WATER SKIING – Amends existing law to provide an exception for water skiing.
id:H 887.summary: Lets a boat tow a water skier without a second person as observer if it has a large mounted mirror showing the skier and is in a permitted slalom course or operating during specified hours and seasons.

id:H 889.title: STATE PROCUREMENT – Amends, repeals, and adds to existing law regarding the procurement of property by the State of Idaho.
id:H 889.summary: As introduced, revises state procurement rules by defining new terms, setting best-and-final offer procedures, allowing multiple-award contracts, requiring bid scoring to be published with solicitations, and letting prior state contract performance count toward bid qualification.

id:H 893.title: CODIFIER’S CORRECTIONS – Amends existing law to make codifier’s corrections.
id:H 893.summary: Makes the annual non-substantive codifier corrections to Idaho Code, such as fixing grammar, punctuation, code references and statute numbering.

id:H 895.title: DATA CENTERS – Adds to existing law to establish limitations on consumptive use of water for cooling certain data centers.
id:H 895.summary: As introduced, requires new data centers to cool without consuming water, or to use water from a municipal, water district, or water and sewer district system.

id:H 897.title: TAXATION – Amends existing law to revise a sales tax exemption for data center equipment and to revise a certain property tax exemption for certain capital investments.
id:H 897.summary: As amended in the Senate, limits the data center sales tax exemption to server equipment for projects starting on or after July 1, 2026, ends it after 20 years, and requires exempt entities to keep receipts 10 years and report annually on tax exempted, jobs, investment, and power and water use.

id:H 898.title: STATE HISTORIC PRESERVATION OFFICER – Amends, repeals, and adds to existing law to provide for the State Historic Preservation Officer.
id:H 898.summary: As introduced, moves the State Historic Preservation Office from the Idaho State Historical Society to the new Office of Species, Minerals, and Energy Coordination in the Governor's office.

id:H 911.title: PUBLIC UTILITIES – Adds to existing law to provide for new large loads.
id:H 911.summary: As introduced, requires utilities to serve new electrical loads of 50 megawatts or more only under a Public Utilities Commission-approved contract, filed before service begins and supported by a "no harm test" for existing ratepayers.

id:H 913.title: MEDICAID – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding Medicaid eligibility expansion.
id:H 913.summary: As introduced, requires the Department of Health and Welfare to implement Medicaid work and community engagement requirements by December 31, 2026, verifying compliance for the three months before enrollment or redetermination.

id:H 919.title: APPROPRIATIONS – DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATION – PERMANENT BUILDING FUND – Relates to the appropriation to the Department of Administration for the Division of Public Works for fiscal year 2027.
id:H 919.summary: As introduced, appropriates $72.5 million from the Permanent Building Fund for fiscal 2027 state building maintenance, alteration and repair, ADA projects and Capitol Mall and Chinden Campus facilities, plus design of a Bonneville County readiness center.

id:H 920.title: APPROPRIATIONS – HEALTH EDUCATION PROGRAMS – Relates to the appropriation to the State Board of Education and the Board of Regents of the University of Idaho for Health Education Programs for fiscal year 2027.
id:H 920.summary: Appropriates $900,000 more for fiscal year 2027 for health education programs, funding additional psychiatry, family medicine and child psychiatry residents and fellowships, for a total of $30.2 million.

id:H 921.title: APPROPRIATIONS – DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION – Relates to the appropriation to the State Department of Education for fiscal year 2027.
id:H 921.summary: Appropriates fiscal year 2027 funds for the State Department of Education, adding $517,800 to the baseline, including spending for school bus stop-arm cameras, a one-time farm-to-school grant and child nutrition program costs.

id:H 923.title: APPROPRIATIONS – DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATION – Relates to the appropriation to the Department of Administration for fiscal year 2027.
id:H 923.summary: As introduced, appropriates an additional $782,000 for fiscal 2027 to the Department of Administration, shifting utilities costs to dedicated funds and funding a Medicaid procurement bureau chief, utilities increases and IT hardware.

id:H 924.title: APPROPRIATIONS – STATE LIQUOR DIVISION – Relates to the appropriation to the State Liquor Division for fiscal year 2027.
id:H 924.summary: As introduced, appropriates fiscal 2027 funding increases to the State Liquor Division for utilities and supplies inflation, replacing store security systems, shelving and equipment, and IT and security equipment.

id:H 925.title: APPROPRIATIONS – JUDICIAL BRANCH – Relates to the appropriation to the Judicial Branch for fiscal year 2027.
id:H 925.summary: Appropriates $4.07 million more to the Judicial Branch for fiscal 2027: $3.1 million from dedicated court funds, $800,700 for senior magistrate judge retirement costs, and $165,300 from the General Fund for the Guardian ad Litem program.

id:H 928.title: MERIT-BASED HEALTH CARE – Adds to existing law to establish the Merit-Based Health Care Act.
id:H 928.summary: As amended in the Senate, bars Medicaid-participating health care providers from discriminatory hiring and specified diversity, equity and inclusion practices, makes compliance a Medicaid contract condition, and lets the Attorney General seek civil penalties up to $100,000 for repeat violations.

id:H 929.title: HEALTH CARE – Adds to existing law to establish provisions regarding certain out-of-pocket payments for health care services.
id:H 929.summary: As introduced, bars health insurers from preventing providers from offering discounted cash prices, lets patients' cash payments count toward deductibles and out-of-pocket maximums with documentation, and requires providers to accept cash payments as full settlement. Effective July 1, 2026.

id:H 930.title: CAMPAIGN FINANCE – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding the duties of political treasurers.
id:H 930.summary: As introduced, requires candidates and political committees to keep campaign money in a separate checking account, requires reporting personal loans over $1,000, and limits investing campaign funds to cash-equivalent accounts, not stocks.

id:H 931.title: PORTABLE BENEFIT PLAN ACT – Amends language added by House Bill 645 regarding the Portable Benefit Plan Act.
id:H 931.summary: Removes the definition of the Idaho Department of Insurance from the new Portable Benefit Plan Act (House Bill 645), which lets independent contractors use portable accounts to fund benefit plans.

id:H 932.title: STATE GUN – States findings of the Legislature and provides for an advisory question regarding the state gun of Idaho to be placed on the ballot before the voters.
id:H 932.summary: Places a non-binding advisory question on the 2026 general election ballot asking voters to pick a state gun from six listed firearms, including the Winchester Model 1894, M1 Garand and Colt M1911.

id:H 933.title: APPROPRIATIONS – COMMISSION ON AGING – Relates to the appropriation to the Commission on Aging for fiscal year 2027.
id:H 933.summary: Appropriates an added $129,900 for fiscal year 2027 to the Commission on Aging for senior nutrition, for a total budget of $16.8 million.

id:H 934.title: TAXATION – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding the Idaho Parental Choice Tax Credit.
id:H 934.summary: As introduced, makes technical corrections to the Idaho Parental Choice Tax Credit: eligible students are ages 5 to 18 at any time in the tax year, tutoring must be academic, and advance payments may be claimed only initially.

id:H 939.title: HUNTING – Amends existing law regarding the use of certain technologies.
id:H 939.summary: As introduced, regulates the use of thermal imaging, night vision, transmitting trail cameras and drones for hunting, with exemptions including for predators and for agricultural purposes.

id:H 940.title: EDUCATION – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding the Idaho Digital Learning Academy.
id:H 940.summary: As introduced, limits the Idaho Digital Learning Alliance to supplemental online courses focused on grades 6-12, ends offerings such as virtual school participation and K-5 programs, sets minimum course fees, and caps state funding at $445 per course.

id:H 942.title: APPROPRIATIONS – MILLENNIUM INCOME FUND – Relates to the appropriation from the Idaho Millennium Income Fund for fiscal year 2027.
id:H 942.summary: As introduced, appropriates the Idaho Millennium Income Fund tobacco settlement money for fiscal 2027 to behavioral health and youth programs, including Kamiah Recovery Center and the Idaho Children's Trust Fund.

id:H 949.title: APPROPRIATIONS – WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT COUNCIL AND STEM ACTION CENTER – Relates to the appropriation to the Workforce Development Council and the STEM Action Center for fiscal years 2026 and 2027.
id:H 949.summary: Adds $3.08 million in net general funds and six positions to the Workforce Development Council for fiscal 2027, cuts $5.99 million and seven positions from the STEM Action Center, and cuts $76,400 from its fiscal 2026 budget.

id:H 950.title: APPROPRIATIONS – LEGISLATURE – Appropriates $200,000 to the Legislature for fiscal year 2026 for the Medicaid Review Panel.
id:H 950.summary: Appropriates $200,000 from the General Fund to the Legislature for fiscal 2026 operating costs; its fiscal note says the money may fund consultants overseeing the transition to Medicaid managed care.

id:H 957.title: DEPARTMENT OF WATER RESOURCES – Repeals existing law to remove outdated or unnecessary provisions.
id:H 957.summary: Repeals nine sections of Idaho Code on water resources that the sponsors describe as outdated, including provisions on a never-adopted Salmon Falls Creek compact and an inactive water conservation trust account.

id:H 959.title: TAXATION – Amends and adds to existing law to provide for an initiative petition to raise or lower the property tax budgets for fire protection districts and ambulance service districts and to revise provisions regarding certain property tax budget limits.
id:H 959.summary: Raises the property tax budget growth cap for fire protection and ambulance districts from 8 to 15 percent where new construction and annexation cover it, limits forgone-increase recovery to years before 2026, and lets voters raise or cut district budgets by initiative.

id:H 964.title: APPROPRIATIONS – DEPARTMENT OF FISH AND GAME – Relates to the appropriation to the Department of Fish and Game for fiscal year 2027.
id:H 964.summary: As introduced, appropriates an additional $14.2 million for fiscal 2027 to the Department of Fish and Game for fisheries habitat, wolf depredation response and other items, and directs use of funds for wolf trapping.

id:H 966.title: APPROPRIATIONS – DEPARTMENT OF CORRECTION – Relates to the appropriation to the Department of Correction for fiscal year 2027.
id:H 966.summary: As introduced, appropriates $200,000 a year from the General Fund to the Department of Correction to cover House Bill 684, which lets sheriffs seek reimbursement for retrieving absconders from out of state.

id:H 968.title: APPROPRIATIONS – Relates to the appropriation and transfer of moneys in the state treasury for fiscal years 2026 and 2027.
id:H 968.summary: Moves money and interest earnings from several state funds to the General Fund in fiscal 2026 and 2027, lets the Board of Examiners transfer from the twenty-seventh payroll fund if revenues fall short, and directs federal relief interest to two other funds.

id:H 971.title: APPROPRIATIONS – OFFICE OF THE ATTORNEY GENERAL – Relates to the appropriation to the Office of the Attorney General for fiscal years 2026 and 2027.
id:H 971.summary: As introduced, appropriates an additional $880,000 from the Consumer Protection Fund to the Attorney General's office in each of fiscal 2026 and 2027, and allows the money to be used for any of the Attorney General's duties, not only consumer protection.

id:H 972.title: APPROPRIATIONS – HEALTH AND WELFARE – DIVISION OF WELFARE – Relates to the appropriation to the Department of Health and Welfare for fiscal year 2027.
id:H 972.summary: As introduced, appropriates $351,000 from the General Fund and $163,000 in federal funds for fiscal 2027 to the Division of Welfare for system changes needed to carry out House Bill 730 on SNAP eligibility.

id:H 973.title: APPROPRIATIONS – MILITARY DIVISION – Relates to the appropriation to the Military Division for fiscal year 2026.
id:H 973.summary: As introduced, appropriates $6.5 million in federal funds for fiscal 2026 to the Military Division to replace climate control systems in Idaho Air National Guard buildings at Gowen Field.

id:H 974.title: APPROPRIATIONS – IDAHO STATE POLICE – Relates to the appropriation to the Idaho State Police for fiscal year 2027.
id:H 974.summary: Appropriates an additional $6,695,000 to the Idaho State Police for fiscal 2027 personnel costs, mostly from the Law Enforcement (Project Choice) Fund, to fund a new pay plan for commissioned officers.

id:H 975.title: APPROPRIATIONS – Relates to the appropriation and transfer of moneys in the state treasury for fiscal year 2027.
id:H 975.summary: As introduced, directs that no Budget Stabilization Fund transfer occur even if the fund balance exceeds 15 percent of General Fund revenues, leaving the $880.2 million balance unchanged in fiscal 2027.

id:H 976.title: APPROPRIATIONS – Relates to the appropriation and transfer of funds for strategic initiatives and local highway districts.
id:H 976.summary: Amends House Bill 968 to send 40 percent of a transfer of $32,877,300 or half of certain interest earnings, whichever is greater, through the Local Highway Distribution Fund and 60 percent to the Strategic Initiatives Program Fund.

id:H 978.title: APPROPRIATIONS – HEALTH AND WELFARE – PUBLIC HEALTH SERVICES – Relates to the appropriation to the Department of Health and Welfare for fiscal year 2027.
id:H 978.summary: As introduced, adds $35.1 million to the Health and Welfare Department's Public Health Services budget for fiscal 2027, including restoring the Immunization Assessment Fund, and moves the Idaho Home Visiting Program to another division.

id:HJM 19.title: EDUCATION – States findings of the Legislature, supports federal efforts to eliminate the U.S. Department of Education, and urges Congress to fully cooperate with these efforts.
id:HJM 19.summary: As introduced, states the Idaho Legislature's support for eliminating the U.S. Department of Education and returning primary authority over education policy to the states. It does not change funding.

id:S 1236.title: IDAHO WOMEN’S COMMISSION – Repeals existing law relating to the Idaho Women’s Commission.
id:S 1236.summary: Repeals the Idaho Women's Commission chapter of Idaho Code, eliminating the commission.

id:S 1247.title: MEMORANDUM OF AGREEMENT – Adds to existing law to establish provisions regarding law enforcement entering into a memorandum of agreement.
id:S 1247.summary: As passed by the Senate, requires public agencies, and employers with over 150 employees and certain public contracts, to use E-Verify for new hires from January 1, 2027, bars knowingly hiring unverified workers, and lets the labor director sue to enforce.

id:S 1254.title: CHIROPRACTIC PRACTICE ACT – Amends existing law to clarify the existing right of persons licensed to practice chiropractic to prescribe certain prescription drug products.
id:S 1254.summary: Lets chiropractors certified in clinical nutrition prescribe, not only obtain and administer, a limited list of prescription vitamins, minerals, fluids, epinephrine and oxygen; the intent section calls this a clarification of existing law.

id:S 1262.title: INSURER INVESTMENTS – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding miscellaneous insurer investments.
id:S 1262.summary: Removes the alternative limit of 75% of capital and surplus on insurers' miscellaneous investments, leaving the cap at 10% of the insurer's assets.

id:S 1270.title: CELL-CULTIVATED ANIMAL PROTEINS – Adds to existing law to establish provisions regarding cell-cultivated animal protein labeling, oversight, and penalties.
id:S 1270.summary: Requires cell-cultivated animal protein products and restaurant menu listings to carry the label "lab-grown," "cell-cultivated" or "cell-cultured," bars meat-cut terms like "steak" on them unless USDA authorizes, and sets civil penalties up to $500 per violation.

id:S 1288.title: EDUCATION – Adds to existing law to provide for the establishment of the Idaho High-Needs Student Fund.
id:S 1288.summary: As introduced, creates the Idaho High Needs Student Fund to reimburse school districts and charter schools, through an application to the Department of Education, for extraordinary costs of serving students with disabilities. The governor recommended $5 million.

id:S 1294.title: INFANTS AND NEWBORNS – Adds to existing law to establish provisions regarding hearing loss screening.
id:S 1294.summary: As amended, requires newborns to be screened for hearing loss before hospital discharge, or within 21 days for births elsewhere, and makes the requirement unenforceable if losing federal funding would raise state costs.

id:S 1297.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE – Adds to existing law to establish the Conversational AI Safety Act.
id:S 1297.summary: As amended, requires conversational AI operators to adopt a suicidal-ideation response protocol and, for minors, show an AI disclosure, block sexually explicit output and avoid unpredictable rewards; the Attorney General may seek $1,000 per violation, up to $500,000 per operator.

id:S 1299.title: DIGITAL IDENTIFICATION – Adds to existing law to establish provisions regarding limitations on digital identification.
id:S 1299.summary: Bars state and local public entities from requiring digital identification, denying services for refusing it, or demanding access to a person's device, and limits retention of identity data. The attorney general and aggrieved persons may sue to enforce.

id:S 1300.title: STATE GOVERNMENT – Amends current law to revise provisions regarding director appointments to certain executive agencies.
id:S 1300.summary: As introduced, makes the directors of the Transportation, Fish and Game, and Parks and Recreation departments gubernatorial appointees subject to Senate confirmation.

id:S 1313.title: NATUROPATHIC DOCTOR LICENSING AND NATUROPATH REGISTRATION – Amends existing law to provide for the voluntary licensure of pharmacists as naturopathic doctors.
id:S 1313.summary: Allows licensed pharmacists to voluntarily seek a naturopathic doctor license from the state board, if they hold a naturopathic doctoral degree and meet experience or exam requirements.

id:S 1320.title: STATE CONTROLLER – Amends existing law to remove obsolete provisions.
id:S 1320.summary: Repeals the Business Information Infrastructure Fund and removes expired language on transferring indirect cost recovery money into it for the state controller's business systems modernization project.

id:S 1322.title: ELECTIONS – Amends existing law to add certain requirements for an affidavit in lieu of personal identification.
id:S 1322.summary: Adds a required date of birth or Idaho driver's license/ID number to the affidavit voters may sign in lieu of personal identification, and requires election judges to verify its information against voter registration records before issuing a ballot.

id:S 1330.title: SMALL CLAIMS DEPARTMENT OF THE MAGISTRATE DIVISION – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding the scope of a claim and attorney’s fees.
id:S 1330.summary: Raises the maximum claim in small claims court from $5,000 to $15,000, for both money and personal property cases.

id:S 1335.title: EDUCATION – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding contract requirements for state-supported medical and veterinary students.
id:S 1335.summary: Extends to Idaho veterinary students supported by state funds, beginning fall 2027, the contract rule requiring four years of Idaho practice, including at least 600 hours a year with agricultural animals, or repayment of the state's costs.

id:S 1336.title: EDUCATION – Amends and adds to existing law to revise and establish provisions regarding civics education.
id:S 1336.summary: As amended, requires grades 9-12 students to complete two credits each in American history and American government, adds instruction on the American founding and on totalitarian ideologies such as communism and fascism, and sets criteria for history and civics materials.

id:S 1348.title: PUBLIC OUTDOOR TARGET RANGES – Amends and adds to existing law to establish provisions for the opening of the shotgun sporting complex adjacent to Farragut State Park.
id:S 1348.summary: Directs the Fish and Game Commission to plan a public shotgun sporting complex on Fish and Game lands next to Farragut State Park and open it by December 31, 2040, with at least six trap and skeet fields and 15 sporting clay stations.

id:S 1352.title: HOUSING – Adds to existing law to establish provisions regarding starter home subdivisions.
id:S 1352.summary: As amended, bars cities of more than 10,000 people from banning starter home subdivisions (4+ acres, lots up to 1,500 square feet) and requires them by February 1, 2027 to cap minimum lot size, setbacks and lot width.

id:S 1354.title: ACCESSORY DWELLING UNITS – Amends and adds to existing law to revise provisions regarding prohibitions against restrictive covenants banning accessory dwelling units and to establish provisions regarding accessory dwelling units in the Local Land Use Planning Act.
id:S 1354.summary: As amended, bars cities of more than 10,000 people from banning accessory dwelling units, requires approval of compliant units administratively as a matter of right under objective standards, and bars homeowner associations from limiting them without owner consent.

id:S 1356.title: SINGLE COUNTYWIDE HIGHWAY DISTRICTS – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding the election of commissioners in certain single countywide highway districts.
id:S 1356.summary: Starting with 2028 elections, has commissioners of countywide highway districts in counties over 200,000 people nominated in the May primary and elected in the even-year general election, with all district voters voting on each seat.

id:S 1369.title: PLACE OF TRIAL OF CIVIL ACTIONS – Adds to and repeals existing law to establish provisions regarding place of trial for certain civil actions.
id:S 1369.summary: Rewrites the civil-action venue statute, adding the county where the cause of action arose as a place to sue, alongside the county where a defendant lives; restates existing rules for non-resident defendants, insurers and Idaho corporations.

id:S 1376.title: ELECTIONS – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding the filing of declarations of candidacy.
id:S 1376.summary: Moves filing of local candidates' nominating petitions from the political subdivision's clerk to the county clerk, and requires subdivision clerks to give the county clerk subdistrict maps by January 1 of each year an election may be held.

id:S 1389.title: POLLING PLACES – Amends existing law to limit liability for owners of property used as a polling place.
id:S 1389.summary: Limits the liability of property owners who let their property be used as a polling place free of charge, and provides that using property with certain tax exemptions as a polling place does not affect the exemption.

id:S 1391.title: PROPERTY – Amends Senate Bill No. 1326 to provide for scope and applicability.
id:S 1391.summary: Adds to the scope section in Senate Bill 1326, if enacted, a statement that it does not limit lawful entry authorized under Idaho Code sections 7-705, 40-1310, 40-2301 and 54-1230.

id:S 1396.title: PACIFIC FISHERIES LEGISLATIVE TASK FORCE – Repeals existing law to remove obsolete provisions relating to membership on the Pacific Fisheries Legislative Task Force.
id:S 1396.summary: Repeals the Idaho law on legislators' membership in the Pacific Fisheries Legislative Task Force, under the Idaho Code Cleanup Act.

id:S 1397.title: WASTEWATER CORPORATIONS – Amends and adds to existing law to provide when wastewater corporations may be a public utility.
id:S 1397.summary: Treats operators of wastewater systems for compensation with 100 or more service connections as public utilities regulated by the Idaho Public Utilities Commission, which may charge them fees up to its oversight costs; smaller systems are exempt.

id:S 1401.title: APPROPRIATIONS – HEALTH AND WELFARE – PUBLIC HEALTH SERVICES – Relates to the appropriation to the Department of Health and Welfare for fiscal year 2027.
id:S 1401.summary: As introduced, appropriates an additional $35.6 million for fiscal 2027 to Public Health Services, including restoring the Immunization Assessment Fund, and moves the Idaho Home Visiting Program to the early learning division.

id:S 1402.title: APPROPRIATIONS – DEPARTMENT OF JUVENILE CORRECTIONS – Relates to the appropriation to the Department of Juvenile Corrections for fiscal year 2027.
id:S 1402.summary: Appropriates an added $2.57 million for fiscal year 2027 to the Department of Juvenile Corrections, covering direct care staff, county support, vehicles, facility upkeep and IT hardware, for a total of $61.8 million.

id:S 1404.title: APPROPRIATIONS – DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE – Relates to the appropriation to the Department of Agriculture for fiscal years 2026 and 2027.
id:S 1404.summary: As introduced, appropriates an additional $829,900 for fiscal 2027 to the Department of Agriculture for IT hardware, vehicles, lab and field equipment and boat inspection signs, plus fiscal 2026 funds for exotic pest control and quagga mussel treatment.

id:S 1405.title: APPROPRIATIONS – SOIL AND WATER CONSERVATION COMMISSION – Relates to the appropriation to the Soil and Water Conservation Commission for fiscal years 2026 and 2027.
id:S 1405.summary: As introduced, appropriates fiscal 2027 funding for the Soil and Water Conservation Commission, including Conservation Reserve Enhancement Program payments, and moves the commission from the Department of Agriculture to the Department of Water Resources.

id:S 1406.title: APPROPRIATIONS – OFFICE OF THE STATE PUBLIC DEFENDER – Relates to the appropriation to the Office of the State Public Defender for fiscal year 2027.
id:S 1406.summary: Appropriates an added $505,100 for fiscal year 2027 to the State Public Defender, including six trial attorneys, data migration and storage, and health benefit costs, for a total of $82.2 million.

id:S 1407.title: APPROPRIATIONS – DIVISION OF OCCUPATIONAL AND PROFESSIONAL LICENSES – Relates to the appropriation to the Division of Occupational and Professional Licenses for fiscal year 2027.
id:S 1407.summary: Appropriates an added $472,700 for fiscal year 2027 to the Division of Occupational and Professional Licenses to replace nine inspector vehicles and buy network equipment and laptops, for a total of $37.3 million.

id:S 1408.title: APPROPRIATIONS – PUBLIC SCHOOLS – EDUCATIONAL SERVICES FOR THE DEAF AND THE BLIND – Relates to the appropriation to the Public Schools Educational Support Program’s Division of Educational Services for the Deaf and the Blind for fiscal year 2027.
id:S 1408.summary: As introduced, appropriates an additional $356,300 for fiscal 2027 to the Idaho Educational Services for the Deaf and the Blind, including pay parity with the career ladder and replacement of a bus and van.

id:S 1409.title: APPROPRIATIONS – IDAHO STATE POLICE – Relates to the appropriation to the Idaho State Police for fiscal year 2027.
id:S 1409.summary: As introduced, appropriates an additional $4.9 million for fiscal 2027 to the Idaho State Police for a commercial vehicle safety grant, a mobile Livescan program and replacement patrol vehicles and equipment.

id:S 1410.title: MEDICAID – Adds to existing law to provide legislative approval for the Department of Health and Welfare to submit a state plan amendment regarding change in encounter rate due to change in scope of services.
id:S 1410.summary: Sets a state process for adjusting Medicaid payment rates for federally qualified health centers and rural health clinics when their services change, requiring a 4.5 percent minimum cost change per visit and an application after six months of full implementation.

id:S 1412.title: EDUCATION – Adds to existing law to provide for the Idaho Student Safety and Educator Disclosure Act.
id:S 1412.summary: Creates the Idaho Student Safety and Educator Disclosure Act: requires job applicants to disclose or authorize disclosure of educator-student misconduct investigations, bars schools from internal child abuse investigations instead of reporting to law enforcement, and refers related resignations or terminations to the Professional Standards Commission.

id:S 1416.title: APPROPRIATIONS – SMEC – Relates to the appropriation to the Office of Species, Minerals, and Energy Coordination for fiscal year 2027.
id:S 1416.summary: As introduced, appropriates $46.1 million for fiscal 2027 to the new Office of Species, Minerals, and Energy Coordination, which merges the energy and mineral resources and species conservation offices, plus added funding for nuclear projects, fish habitat and energy resiliency grants.

id:S 1417.title: APPROPRIATIONS – DEPARTMENT OF PARKS AND RECREATION – Relates to the appropriation to the Department of Parks and Recreation for fiscal years 2027 and 2026.
id:S 1417.summary: As introduced, appropriates fiscal 2027 funding increases to the Department of Parks and Recreation, including staff and operations for a new park near Salmon, trail maintenance, RV campsites and a roundabout at Farragut State Park.

id:S 1418.title: KRATOM – Adds to existing law to establish the Idaho Kratom Consumer Protection and Safety Act.
id:S 1418.summary: As amended, bars selling adulterated kratom products, including those with added 7-hydroxymitragynine or over 1 milligram per serving, bars sales to anyone under 21, requires labels, and sets civil penalties up to $1,000 for a first violation.

id:S 1424.title: MOTOR VEHICLES – Amends existing law to provide for an exception for licensed dealers in Idaho for a manufacturer or distributor with a manufacturer-owned or distributor-owned dealership.
id:S 1424.summary: As introduced, prohibits vehicle manufacturers that had not begun doing so before January 1, 2026 from selling vehicles directly to consumers without using franchised dealers, and updates Idaho's dealer franchise laws.

id:S 1426.title: IDAHO TRANSPORTATION DEPARTMENT – FUNDING – Relates to the funding of the Idaho Transportation Department for fiscal year 2027.
id:S 1426.summary: As introduced, appropriates an additional $98.9 million for fiscal 2027 to the Idaho Transportation Department for deferred maintenance, equipment, airfields and construction and right-of-way acquisition.

id:S 1427.title: APPROPRIATIONS – DEPARTMENT OF LANDS – Relates to the appropriation to the Department of Lands for fiscal years 2026 and 2027.
id:S 1427.summary: As introduced, appropriates fiscal 2027 enhancements to the Department of Lands, including fire radio equipment, a vehicle storage structure, vehicles, computer hardware, and partial restoration of fire preparedness funding.

id:S 1430.title: FIREARMS – Amends existing law to revise a provision regarding preemption of firearms regulation, to provide a penalty, and to provide for a cause of action.
id:S 1430.summary: As introduced, sets a $10,000-per-violation civil penalty for local governments that knowingly violate the state firearms-preemption law and allows suits for damages or injunctions, after the Attorney General gives the government 30 days to cure.

id:S 1431.title: APPROPRIATIONS – DEPARTMENT OF WATER RESOURCES – Relates to the appropriation to the Department of Water Resources for fiscal year 2027.
id:S 1431.summary: As introduced, appropriates an additional $390,000 onetime for fiscal 2027 to the Department of Water Resources for aquifer monitoring, stream gaging and adjudication staff.

id:S 1432.title: APPROPRIATIONS – HEALTH AND WELFARE – OTHER PROGRAMS – Relates to the appropriation to the Department of Health and Welfare for fiscal year 2027.
id:S 1432.summary: Appropriates fiscal year 2027 funds for the Department of Health and Welfare's support, licensing and independent councils programs, adding about $864,900 to the baseline budget, for a total of $72.5 million.

id:S 1433.title: APPROPRIATIONS – HEALTH AND WELFARE – MEDICAID – Relates to the appropriation to the Department of Health and Welfare for fiscal years 2026 and 2027.
id:S 1433.summary: As introduced, appropriates an additional $493.4 million for fiscal 2027 to the Division of Medicaid, including funding for the claims system procurement, estate recovery, program integrity and Hospital Assessment Fund adjustments.

id:S 1435.title: APPROPRIATIONS – HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES – Relates to the maintenance appropriations to the Department of Health and Welfare and the State Independent Living Council for fiscal year 2027.
id:S 1435.summary: As introduced, sets the fiscal 2027 maintenance budget for the Department of Health and Welfare and State Independent Living Council, with standard cost adjustments, a base reduction of up to 5 percent, and the cost of House Bill 863.

id:S 1436.title: STATE PROCUREMENT – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding cooperative and group discount purchasing.
id:S 1436.summary: As introduced, clarifies that shared, group discount and cooperative purchasing contracts may include state-specific modifications to the underlying contract.

id:S 1437.title: APPROPRIATIONS – IDAHO STATE POLICE – Relates to the appropriation to the Idaho State Police for fiscal year 2027.
id:S 1437.summary: Appropriates an additional $63,000 from the General Fund to the Idaho State Police Forensic Services Program for fiscal 2027 operating costs, tied to DNA sample collection for added misdemeanor offenses.

id:S 1438.title: APPROPRIATIONS – PUBLIC SCHOOLS – IDAHO DIGITAL LEARNING ACADEMY DIVISION – Relates to the appropriation to the Public Schools Educational Support Program’s Division of the Idaho Digital Learning Academy for fiscal year 2027.
id:S 1438.summary: Cuts the Idaho Digital Learning Academy's fiscal 2027 appropriation by $13.5 million, to $12.31 million, bars it from drawing on the Public Education Stabilization Fund, and requires reports on course compliance and costs.

id:S 1439.title: EDUCATION – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding the Model School Facility Council.
id:S 1439.summary: Delays from 2026 to 2027 the deadline for the model school facility council's plan governing use of school modernization facilities fund money.

id:S 1442.title: IDAHO REFUGEE AND ILLEGAL ALIEN ACCOUNTABILITY ACT – Adds to existing law to establish provisions regarding an audit of the resettlement of refugees and to establish provisions regarding the immigration status and nationality of arrested individuals.
id:S 1442.summary: Requires Idaho-incorporated refugee resettlement entities to give the Legislature annual audits; requires resettlement entities to catalog unlawfully present people they serve; requires law enforcement to verify and record arrestees' immigration status and nationality, with biannual reports to the state controller.

id:S 1444.title: APPROPRIATIONS – PUBLIC SCHOOLS – DIVISION OF STUDENT SUPPORT – Relates to the appropriation to the Public Schools Educational Support Program’s Division of Student Support for fiscal years 2026 and 2027.
id:S 1444.summary: As introduced, appropriates an additional $2.2 million ongoing for public school student support, adds federal grant spending authority, and reduces discretionary funding for virtual-only schools.

id:S 1445.title: INVASIVE SPECIES – Adds to existing law to provide that certain rats are invasive species.
id:S 1445.summary: Declares Norway rats, roof rats and any wild, uncontrolled rat invasive species, and empowers local governments to control and remove them on public property, and on private property with the owner's written permission.

id:S 1446.title: APPROPRIATIONS – Relates to the appropriation to the Department of Health and Welfare and the Judicial Branch for fiscal year 2027.
id:S 1446.summary: As introduced, restores Assertive Community Treatment and peer support services using internal savings, Millennium Income Fund and opioid settlement money, appropriating about $30.7 million for fiscal 2027.

id:S 1447.title: APPROPRIATIONS – PUBLIC SCHOOLS – STUDENT SUPPORT DIVISION – Relates to the appropriation to the Public Schools Educational Support Program’s Division of Student Support for fiscal year 2027.
id:S 1447.summary: As introduced, appropriates $5 million for fiscal 2027 from the Idaho High Needs Student Fund for school districts and charter schools, and transfers $5 million into that fund from other accounts.

id:S 1448.title: MINORS – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding material harmful to minors.
id:S 1448.summary: As introduced, adds definitions and clarifying language to Idaho's 2024 Children's and Library Protection Act, responding to a Ninth Circuit opinion and a U.S. Supreme Court decision on Texas's age-verification law.

id:S 1452.title: APPROPRIATIONS – PUBLIC SCHOOLS – IDAHO DIGITAL LEARNING ACADEMY – Relates to the appropriation to the Public Schools Educational Support Program’s Division of the Idaho Digital Learning Academy for fiscal year 2027.
id:S 1452.summary: As introduced, changes the public school budget bill so Idaho Digital Learning Academy course fees are not all capped at $40, allowing a $100 minimum fee for non-graduation courses as House Bill 940 provides.

id:S 1454.title: APPROPRIATIONS – HEALTH AND WELFARE – EARLY LEARNING AND DEVELOPMENT, YOUTH SAFETY AND PERMANENCY, AND FAMILY AND COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS – Relates to the appropriation to the Department of Health and Welfare for fiscal years 2026 and 2027.
id:S 1454.summary: As introduced, appropriates an additional $5.7 million for fiscal 2027 to Health and Welfare divisions for early learning, family partnerships and youth safety, and adds the Idaho Home Visiting Program to the early learning division.

il:HB 2790.title: MUNI CD-COMMERCIAL OPERATIONS
il:HB 2790.summary: Lets Illinois municipalities license and regulate all commercial operations within their boundaries, for-profit or not, but impose no tax on them except as otherwise authorized by law. Excludes agritourism, agricultural property, agribusinesses, agricultural experiences and pollution control facilities.

il:HB 2955.title: EPA-PFAS WASTEWATER
il:HB 2955.summary: As introduced, creates a PFAS Wastewater Citizen Protection Committee to deliver a PFAS Action Plan within a year, update it annually and report, with technical help from the Illinois Sustainable Technology Center. The Act is repealed December 31, 2044.
