il:HB 3275.title: SCH-CARDIAC EMERGENCY RESPONSE
il:HB 3275.summary: As amended, requires interscholastic athletic associations to require paid school head coaches or chief sponsors to hold CPR, first aid and AED certification, and requires school cardiac emergency response plans to include a trained response team and annual drills.

il:HB 3393.title: CRIM PRO--SPEEDY TRIAL TOLL
il:HB 3393.summary: Creates a rebuttable presumption that a child victim under 13 testifies outside the courtroom by closed-circuit television in certain sexual offense and aggravated battery prosecutions; the defendant can overcome it by clear and convincing evidence that the child will not suffer severe emotional distress.

il:HB 3711.title: PROFESSIONAL MISCONDUCT
il:HB 3711.summary: Requires health professionals and institutions to report specified sexual and violent misconduct to the state professional regulation department, requires law enforcement to report investigations, arrests and charges and prosecutors convictions of licensees, and creates a Sexual Assault Survivors Fund.

il:HB 3751.title: DCEO-EMPLOY SOCIAL ENTERPRISE
il:HB 3751.summary: Adds employment social enterprises to the businesses and groups the Department of Commerce's Office of Economic Equity and Empowerment assists through targeted programs, resources and outreach.

il:HB 4949.title: FAMILY JUSTICE CENTERS ACT
il:HB 4949.summary: Authorizes cities, counties, the state or nonprofits to set up Family Justice Centers where agencies provide services to domestic violence, sexual violence, stalking and trafficking survivors in one place, with consent, confidentiality and 16-hour annual staff training rules.

il:SB 3107.title: QUICK-TAKE OAK PARK
il:SB 3107.summary: As introduced, allows the Village of Oak Park to use quick-take eminent domain for two years to acquire specified properties on Madison Street and Humphrey Avenue in Cook County for a public building and facility.

in:HB 1001.title: Housing matters.
in:HB 1001.summary: Changes housing rules by limiting fees units of government may charge for building permits after 2026, requiring annual housing status reports from local governments, and revising loan allocations from the residential housing infrastructure fund.

in:HB 1002.title: Electric utility affordability.
in:HB 1002.summary: Requires electric utilities to put households applying for energy assistance on levelized billing with opt-outs, bars residential shutoffs when the forecast heat index is 95 or higher, and requires investor-owned utilities to seek rate changes through three-year rate plans.

in:HB 1003.title: Boards and commissions.
in:HB 1003.summary: Creates an agricultural promotion and regulation task force, repeals the fire prevention and building safety commission and moves its duties to the homeland security department, and repeals, merges or changes various other state boards and commissions.

in:HB 1004.title: Various education matters.
in:HB 1004.summary: Changes many state education laws, including removing spending restrictions for remediation programs, allowing temporary contracts for teachers on emergency permits, and moving firearm safety educational materials duties from the Department of Education to the Department of Homeland Security.

in:HB 1018.title: School age child care.
in:HB 1018.summary: Removes certain transportation requirements from approval criteria for the school age child care project fund and requires the Division of Family Resources to set rules on cost standards for transporting a child to a facility other than their school.

in:HB 1031.title: County coroners.
in:HB 1031.summary: Changes coroner training and death investigation rules, including hospital blood and tissue retention protocols. Makes it a Class B misdemeanor for a coroner or deputy to investigate a death or sign a death certificate without required training.

in:HB 1036.title: Children in need of services.
in:HB 1036.summary: Requires the Department of Child Services, subject to procedural safeguards, to have in-person contact with an alleged child abuse or neglect victim before concluding an assessment or dismissing or ending a pending child in need of services case.

in:HB 1038.title: Gaming matters.
in:HB 1038.summary: Requires Allen, DeKalb and Steuben counties to put an inland casino question on the 2026 ballot, lets the gaming commission award a casino license if voters approve, and sets horse racing satellite licenses at three instead of four per permit holder.

in:HB 1042.title: Regulation and investment of cryptocurrency.
in:HB 1042.summary: Requires specified state retirement and savings plans to offer a self-directed brokerage account with a cryptocurrency option, and bars most public agencies and local governments from restricting digital-asset payments or taxing them differently than comparable transactions.

in:HB 1048.title: VFD clothing and automobile allowances.
in:HB 1048.summary: Raises the clothing and automobile allowance for active volunteer fire department members from $100 to $250 and requires the unit served to pay it directly to each active, participating member.

in:HB 1052.title: Various administrative law matters.
in:HB 1052.summary: Adds grounds for the horse racing commission to revoke licenses, sets civil penalties for sweepstakes games, adds sports wagering to the voluntary exclusion program, and changes beer wholesaler and wine retailer permit rules.

in:HB 1056.title: Resisting law enforcement conflict resolution.
in:HB 1056.summary: Resolves a conflict between two 2025 laws, HEA 1014 and HEA 1637, concerning resisting law enforcement.

in:HB 1058.title: Annexation.
in:HB 1058.summary: Treats annexation territory divided by railroad tracks as contiguous to the municipality if the territory on at least one side of the tracks touches the municipality.

in:HB 1062.title: Wake boarding and wake surfing.
in:HB 1062.summary: Sets restrictions, with a penalty, on wake boarding and wake surfing on public freshwater lakes, and separate restrictions on small lakes.

in:HB 1065.title: Ban on gratuities for public officials.
in:HB 1065.summary: Makes it a Class A misdemeanor to commingle campaign committee funds with the personal funds of a committee officer, member or associate, and a Level 6 felony if $50,000 or more is commingled.

in:HB 1088.title: Technical corrections.
in:HB 1088.summary: Fixes spelling, formatting, grammar and cross-reference issues in the Indiana Code and resolves technical conflicts from the 2025 session.

in:HB 1092.title: Child services matters.
in:HB 1092.summary: Requires sports wagering operators to withhold certain withdrawals from users delinquent on child support, requires background checks for some child caring institution volunteers, and requires caseworkers to show their department credential to interview a child alone at school.

in:HB 1098.title: Work based learning liability.
in:HB 1098.summary: Requires intermediaries and employers in work based learning programs to sign a duties agreement, and makes participating students eligible for workers' compensation benefits, subject to limits.

in:HB 1114.title: Coverage for certain cancer prescriptions.
in:HB 1114.summary: Bars state employee plans, insurers and HMOs that cover advanced metastatic cancer from requiring patients to fail on, or have a history of failing, a different drug before covering a prescription.

in:HB 1115.title: Homeowners association governance.
in:HB 1115.summary: Requires homeowners association boards to give members four days' written notice of board meetings with an agenda, counts remote attendees as present at member meetings, requires a fine schedule before fines, and limits consent needed to amend governing documents to two-thirds of owners.

in:HB 1116.title: Virtual currency kiosks.
in:HB 1116.summary: Bans the operation of virtual currency kiosks in Indiana, makes violations actionable by the attorney general as deceptive consumer sales, and allows forfeiture of kiosk charges and the kiosks themselves for knowing violations.

in:HB 1122.title: License plates for former state legislators.
in:HB 1122.summary: Allows special license plates for former legislators who served at least five House terms, at least three Senate terms, or 12 combined years in both chambers.

in:HB 1131.title: Licensed estheticians and electrologists.
in:HB 1131.summary: Expands the definition of esthetician to cover microneedling with proof of advanced training on request, and lets electrologist applicants skip cosmetology or esthetician licensure while meeting a combined 600 hours of education and experience.

in:HB 1145.title: Thirteenth check.
in:HB 1145.summary: Lets members of the excise police and conservation officers' retirement plan choose a joint and survivor payout, and provides a thirteenth retirement check in 2026 to certain members of several state retirement funds.

in:HB 1147.title: Licensure of certified public accountants.
in:HB 1147.summary: Makes a bachelor's degree with an accounting concentration, or equivalent as the board decides, enough to be eligible to take the CPA licensure exam.

in:HB 1150.title: Local regulation.
in:HB 1150.summary: Bars homeowners association rules that restrict vehicles or outdoor equipment by fuel type or prohibit displaying an American flag, and bars associations from installing or allowing automated license plate readers unless installed by law enforcement.

in:HB 1152.title: Homeowners association matters.
in:HB 1152.summary: Lets homeowners associations raise budgets without a quorum (up to 110% within five years of first sale; otherwise the lesser of 105% or the Midwest housing consumer price index increase), bars fees tied to association services, and bars banning amateur radio antennas.

in:HB 1153.title: Auto dealer matters.
in:HB 1153.summary: Requires auto dealers to collect and keep identifying information from potential purchasers, requires transport operators from July 1, 2026 to have an Indiana business address or federal registration to apply for a registration number, and makes operating without a dealer license a Class A infraction.

in:HB 1155.title: Traffic enforcement.
in:HB 1155.summary: Creates a pilot project letting large homeowners association subdivisions (1,500+ lots, 15+ miles of private road) set speed limits and stop signs that police can enforce on their private roads.

in:HB 1161.title: Local government matters.
in:HB 1161.summary: Makes certain county board appointees serve at the pleasure of the appointing authority, staggers terms on nine-member local health boards, and changes oath-of-office procedures for town police commissioners in reorganized subdivisions.

in:HB 1165.title: Various animal related matters.
in:HB 1165.summary: Increases penalties for certain animal offenses, changes animal offense definitions, applies animal cruelty law to rodents that are not nuisances, and removes partial liability for people who remove an animal from a vehicle.

in:HB 1177.title: Child care assistance.
in:HB 1177.summary: Raises the maximum employer size eligible for the employer child care expenditure income tax credit, and counts child care facility operating costs and contracted child care services for employees as qualified expenses.

in:HB 1192.title: Seed laws.
in:HB 1192.summary: Writes various administrative rules into the Indiana seed law, repeals certain administrative rules, and makes conforming and technical changes.

in:HB 1193.title: Civil rights commission.
in:HB 1193.summary: Bars the civil rights commission from representing private individuals in court, requires it to refer complaints first to other agencies with jurisdiction, and limits it to representing the state in civil actions.

in:HB 1200.title: Bureau of motor vehicles.
in:HB 1200.summary: Changes motor vehicle and driver licensing law, including barring INDOT from using variable speed limits, setting the driver's license age at 16 instead of 16 years 90 days, and requiring English proficiency for commercial motor vehicle operators.

in:HB 1202.title: Various public safety matters.
in:HB 1202.summary: Requires ignition interlock vendors to register devices with the toxicology department, and requires homeland security department inspections before child care centers, child care ministries and child caring institutions are licensed.

in:HB 1210.title: Department of local government finance.
in:HB 1210.summary: Makes many local government finance changes: requires municipalities to post municipal advisor contracts online, changes Gary riverboat wagering tax payments, allows alternative refunding bond procedures for some school corporations, and requires mobile home buyers to retitle within 90 days.

in:HB 1242.title: Education reports.
in:HB 1242.summary: Requires the Department of Education to compile a report of statewide school corporation and charter school data for legislative committees, and the Department of Local Government Finance to study differences in per-student operating funding among school corporations.

in:HB 1248.title: Advanced DNA testing for cold cases.
in:HB 1248.summary: Sets a process for qualified nonprofits to fund advanced DNA testing, including genetic genealogy, on cold cases for homicide, sex offenses and high-risk missing persons. Victims, family members, coroners or police with a nonprofit agreement may request eligibility, at no state cost.

in:HB 1249.title: Various criminal law matters.
in:HB 1249.summary: As passed by the House, lets a child charged with dangerous possession of a firearm be tried in juvenile court in some cases, and makes it a Level 5 felony if the child has a prior handgun carrying conviction or possesses the firearm at or near a school.

in:HB 1252.title: Broker companies.
in:HB 1252.summary: Requires a broker company that refers a client or customer to another broker company to disclose if it may be compensated for the referral.

in:HB 1254.title: Various dental matters; respiratory care.
in:HB 1254.summary: Changes education requirements for dental hygienists, nitrous oxide rules for hygienists, requirements for applicants who failed the licensure exam three times, and licensing rules for respiratory care practitioners.

in:HB 1257.title: Child services matters.
in:HB 1257.summary: Adds four legislative appointees to the child fatality review committee, lets courts grant postadoption contact when a child is at least one year old, and requires the Department of Child Services to disclose more information on child deaths and abuse reports.

in:HB 1258.title: Crimes of violence.
in:HB 1258.summary: Rewrites and consolidates the definition of crime of violence, adds dangerous firearm possession and unlawful handgun carrying with two priors to the list, and removes the repeat violent arrestee provisions.

in:HB 1260.title: Various insurance matters.
in:HB 1260.summary: Requires reporting of suspected insurance fraud to the insurance department or the National Insurance Crime Bureau, limits liability for those reports, sets fees for claims data access, and changes property and casualty insurance guaranty rules.

in:HB 1266.title: Department of education and education matters.
in:HB 1266.summary: Makes many changes to education law, including a math teaching framework, a data science math pathway, curriculum material timelines, and salary differences for teachers with a literacy endorsement.

in:HB 1268.title: Indiana defense matters.
in:HB 1268.summary: Adds two voting members and a nonvoting National Guard adjutant general to the Indiana defense task force, and requires annual reports from the task force and the defense development office on spending priorities.

in:HB 1273.title: Requirements for proxy advisors.
in:HB 1273.summary: Requires proxy advisors that recommend against company management to disclose to clients whether a written financial analysis supports it, post a website statement when none exists, and provide the analysis on request when one exists.

in:HB 1274.title: Insurance mandated gun free zone notices.
in:HB 1274.summary: Bars insurers from requiring an insured or prospective insured to post or display a gun free zone notice.

in:HB 1277.title: Health and human services matters.
in:HB 1277.summary: Requires waiver service providers to give recipients documentation to check for errors, requires certain Medicaid recipients to choose an integrated health care coordination provider, and makes other health and human services changes.

in:HB 1278.title: Nursing matters; education programs.
in:HB 1278.summary: Requires the Indiana State Nurses Association to recommend nurses to the governor for every nursing board vacancy or expired term, and lets institutions with a nursing program running five years raise enrollment at any rate they choose.

in:HB 1286.title: Military protective order.
in:HB 1286.summary: Requires parties in protective order cases to tell the court about military protective orders between them, lets the court consider such orders as evidence, and adds certain Canadian court protection orders to the foreign orders treated as facially valid.

in:HB 1296.title: Mental health services.
in:HB 1296.summary: Requires the state social services secretary to certify integrated reentry and correctional support programs, and requires recovery residence owners to register with the mental health and addiction division, which must post a public list.

in:HB 1307.title: Department of child services ombudsman.
in:HB 1307.summary: Requires, rather than permits, the child services ombudsman office to hire experts and staff, investigate complaints that the department failed to protect a child or follow rules, and issue recommendations when complaints have merit.

in:HB 1325.title: Special education.
in:HB 1325.summary: Requires the Department of Education, with health, child services and social services agencies, to report and make recommendations on data about residential placement, developmental preschool and special education.

in:HB 1336.title: Securities and investment adviser representatives.
in:HB 1336.summary: Exempts merger and acquisition brokers from broker-dealer registration in some cases, requires broker-dealer agents and investment adviser representatives to pass FINRA exams unless exceptions apply, and requires investment adviser representatives to complete continuing education.

in:HB 1342.title: County commissioner districts.
in:HB 1342.summary: Urges the legislative council to assign an interim study committee to study whether county executives should adopt certain processes for establishing or revising county commissioner districts.

in:HB 1343.title: Public safety matters.
in:HB 1343.summary: Lets the law enforcement training board hire an executive director, allows waiving some training for officers experienced in other states, raises the county jail copayment cap from $15 to $30, and requires engine cut-off switches on certain boats.

in:HB 1348.title: Regulation of grease control equipment.
in:HB 1348.summary: As passed by the House, sets a statewide regulatory scheme for grease control equipment and requires units that have issued onsite sewage permits since 2023 to keep allowing septage disposal at their wastewater plants, which must accept septage from bordering units.

in:HB 1355.title: Confined feeding operations.
in:HB 1355.summary: Creates a preapplication process for approving confined feeding operations, requires refunds of application fees in some cases, exempts some operations from solid manure equipment rules, and sets requirements for earthen berms at manure storage facilities.

in:HB 1357.title: Child services provider background checks.
in:HB 1357.summary: Requires employees of child welfare programs, home-based family preservation providers, child caring institutions, group homes and child placing agencies to undergo a background check every four years, without a separate federal check for added services with the same employer.

in:HB 1360.title: Access to public records.
in:HB 1360.summary: Lets public agencies run public records request portals with CAPTCHA and address checks, decline suspected scraping or phishing requests, charge extra fees to non-Indiana requesters, prioritize Indiana residents, and deny requests duplicating a requester's litigation discovery.

in:HB 1361.title: Fertilizer.
in:HB 1361.summary: Writes commercial fertilizer administrative rules into law, covering labels, registration, sampling, and containment and storage requirements for fluid and dry bulk fertilizer.

in:HB 1368.title: Carbon.
in:HB 1368.summary: Requires utilities to accept certain payment methods from the Department of Natural Resources, directs the natural resources commission to seek federal authority over Class VI wells, and sets a regulatory scheme for underground carbon dioxide storage.

in:HB 1389.title: Adoption and foster care matters.
in:HB 1389.summary: Bars governments from discriminating against people in adoption and foster care matters based on sincerely held religious belief unless required by a compelling interest, lets them consider whether a person shares a child's or parent's religion in placement, and allows lawsuits.

in:HB 1406.title: Tax and fiscal matters.
in:HB 1406.summary: Makes tax changes including property tax statements comparing 2027 and 2026 liability, limits on property tax exemption for some nonprofit hospital property, $35,000,000 yearly in redevelopment-site awards, and venture capital tax credit adjustments.

in:HB 1408.title: Education matters.
in:HB 1408.summary: Requires Ivy Tech campuses to review building use data before capital requests and prepare strategic plans, and gives the legislature access to state workforce and education data.

in:HB 1423.title: Indianapolis public education corporation.
in:HB 1423.summary: Creates the Indianapolis public education corporation and board with powers over property tax referendums and charter authorizers, and exempts Indianapolis Public Schools from building closure and transfer laws.

in:HB 1424.title: Farm and homestead food sales.
in:HB 1424.summary: Exempts homestead and small farm vendors from certain food-establishment health rules, and bars state and local health agencies from imposing rules on them beyond federal law, though agencies may investigate foodborne illness complaints.

in:SB 1.title: Human services matters.
in:SB 1.summary: Creates a rural health transformation fund, bars buying candy and soft drinks with SNAP benefits, ends expanded categorical SNAP eligibility, adds SNAP and Medicaid immigration-status checks, and changes Healthy Indiana Plan work requirements and copayments.

in:SB 112.title: Candidacy documents.
in:SB 112.summary: Treats the address on a candidate's notice of withdrawal as a request to update the address on the candidate's voter registration record.

in:SB 113.title: Elections matters.
in:SB 113.summary: Requires county election boards to report precinct-level results for each candidate and public question within 14 days after an election, requires the state to publish them online, and lengthens election material retention from 22 to 34 months.

in:SB 119.title: Grooming.
in:SB 119.summary: Bars sexually violent predators and offenders against children from working or volunteering at facilities or events aimed at children, and renames inappropriate communication with a child as sexual grooming, adding repeated contact with someone believed under 14 meant to lower resistance to sexual conduct.

in:SB 12.title: Prohibition of ranked choice voting.
in:SB 12.summary: Prohibits the use of ranked choice voting.

in:SB 139.title: Jury duty exemption for women breastfeeding.
in:SB 139.summary: Lets a woman who gave birth in the past 365 days and is breastfeeding be exempted from jury service by notifying the jury administrator that she wishes to be exempt.

in:SB 14.title: Pension matters.
in:SB 14.summary: Excludes pay received in anticipation of retirement from pension averages, lets certain public employees buy service credit, matches state employee deferred-compensation contributions up to $28 per paycheck after 2026, ends the retirement medical benefits account by default, and raises the 1977 fund death benefit.

in:SB 140.title: Public safety.
in:SB 140.summary: Adds posting a person's personal information on social media with intent to cause injury, property damage or a crime against that person to the definition of threat in the intimidation law, and raises the penalty for intimidating a legislator.

in:SB 144.title: Tobacco, e-liquid, and vapor devices.
in:SB 144.summary: Raises penalties for selling tobacco or delivering e-liquid to people under 21 from Class C to Class B, sets Class B for vapor device sales to them and Class C for under-21 possession, and bans e-liquid and vapor advertising within 1,000 feet of schools.

in:SB 15.title: Foster youth.
in:SB 15.summary: Requires the Department of Child Services to create, update, distribute and publish online a "foster youth bill of rights" summarizing foster youths' rights and responsibilities.

in:SB 160.title: Public safety.
in:SB 160.summary: Makes wearing a mask while committing a crime a sentencing aggravator, and makes it a Class A misdemeanor to put refuse on another's property intending to make the occupant reasonably fear for their physical safety.

in:SB 162.title: Department of workforce development.
in:SB 162.summary: Changes unemployment insurance rules: removes vacation and sick pay from deductible income, narrows the "suitable work" definition to extended benefit claims, codifies certain administrative rules, and allows added benefits for some disaster unemployment claimants.

in:SB 163.title: Various property tax matters.
in:SB 163.summary: Bars assessors from entering property for a physical inspection without the taxpayer's permission, allows tax representatives for taxpayers in specified circumstances, changes the expiration date of the county option circuit breaker tax credit, and sets contents of a report on automated valuation systems.

in:SB 164.title: Study of community or urban microfarming.
in:SB 164.summary: Requires the department of agriculture to study whether to create community or urban microfarm zones statewide and report findings to the general assembly by December 1, 2027.

in:SB 171.title: Family and children matters.
in:SB 171.summary: Requires notice of adoption petitions to open child in need of services courts, allows adoption consent by video, lets courts grant postadoption contact for children at least 12 months old, and sets rules for changing the placement of a child in foster care.

in:SB 176.title: Shooting ranges.
in:SB 176.summary: Bars local governments from treating shooting range upgrades as a nonconforming-use expansion or a basis to deny, delay or condition permits; allows retail sporting goods stores in commercial zones and indoor ranges in commercial, industrial or agricultural zones if conditions are met.

in:SB 179.title: Indiana department of transportation.
in:SB 179.summary: Lets INDOT assume federal transportation duties under certain environmental laws, changes local road and bridge grant eligibility, limits single-trip overweight truck permits, and allows the Indiana Plane Coordinate System to describe real property.

in:SB 180.title: Various health care matters.
in:SB 180.summary: Removes the 75-hour minimum and 16 classroom hours from home health aide training, changes dental hygienist education and nitrous oxide rules, and changes respiratory care practitioner licensing.

in:SB 185.title: Alcohol and tobacco matters.
in:SB 185.summary: Adds rules for tobacco sales certificates, including wholesale sales, sets e-liquid and vapor device requirements, restricts foreign-adversary vapor products, and lowers habitual illegal tobacco sale and minor entrance infractions from six violations a year to three.

in:SB 189.title: Nonparticipating providers.
in:SB 189.summary: Requires a party requesting independent dispute resolution over out-of-network bills to notify the facility within three business days, and lets health carriers give notice and negotiate when 25 or more disputes are filed in 90 days.

in:SB 191.title: Electronic record of confidential address.
in:SB 191.summary: Exempts county recorders from having to accept electronically submitted documents that contain identifying information of a person in the address confidentiality program.

in:SB 199.title: Various education matters.
in:SB 199.summary: Makes various education changes, including reports due December 1, 2026 on civic literacy and paid leave, added requirements for schools with low reading-test pass rates, and a review of accrediting agencies by the higher education commission.

in:SB 2.title: Bail procedures.
in:SB 2.summary: Makes non-murder offenses non-bailable when the state proves the evidence is strong and, by clear and convincing evidence, that the arrestee is dangerous and no release conditions would protect the public, and sets bail hearing procedures.

in:SB 200.title: Public school matters.
in:SB 200.summary: Voids certain indemnity, choice-of-law and automatic-renewal clauses in school vendor contracts made or renewed after June 30, 2026, lets youth organizations file grievances if schools deny them access to students, and requires schools that allow colleges to present to students to allow military personnel too.

in:SB 204.title: Various education matters.
in:SB 204.summary: Lets teachers licensed at charter schools seek an initial practitioner license, bars uniform academic-needs salary increases across a bargaining unit, repeals the student athlete cardiac arrest provisions, and bars requiring immunization for health-program clinical training when a parent or student objects on religious grounds.

in:SB 222.title: Family and social services administration matters.
in:SB 222.summary: Counts 9-8-8 crisis response centers and mobile crisis teams as first responders, requires certified peers to be trained by the state or an accredited body, and limits Medicaid presumptive eligibility determinations to qualified providers.

in:SB 225.title: Health matters.
in:SB 225.summary: Bars hospitals and debt collectors from collecting medical debt when the hospital is out of compliance with specified statutes, requires 60 days' notice to the health department before a hospital closes or ends a service line, and changes surgical center rules.

in:SB 226.title: Indiana department of administration.
in:SB 226.summary: Lets the Indiana department of administration use category management for state purchasing, requires an independent verification and validation program for state contracts, and requires agencies to submit annual procurement plans.

in:SB 227.title: Counter action against unmanned aircraft systems (UAS).
in:SB 227.summary: Makes the state police the statewide coordinator of counter-drone activities, taking effect only if federal law authorizes state or local police to detect or neutralize drones and the governor publishes notice; lets it designate local participating agencies and Indianapolis as a pilot site.

in:SB 228.title: Midwest continental divide commission.
in:SB 228.summary: Changes the Midwest continental divide commission's law so its land use and zoning plan is a plan rather than an overlay district, and addresses zoning changes or variances within half a mile of an approved trail project.

in:SB 23.title: Alcoholic beverage permits for county fairs.
in:SB 23.summary: Lets the alcohol and tobacco commission issue permits to sell alcohol on county fairgrounds run by a local board, and adds local-board events to activities allowed under existing winery, brewer, distiller and retailer permits.

in:SB 230.title: Department of agriculture.
in:SB 230.summary: Changes the role of supervisors on soil and conservation boards, drops the requirement that landfill inspectors send reports to the soil conservation division, withholds funding from districts missing the March 31 financial statement deadline, and repeals the Indiana land resource council.

in:SB 232.title: Real property appraisals.
in:SB 232.summary: Allows the city of Gary to hire an appraiser to appraise city-owned property it plans to sell, and bars city employees and officials from buying property the appraiser appraised.

in:SB 233.title: Powers and duties of the election commission.
in:SB 233.summary: Creates a separate Election Commission process to disband inactive state-level campaign committees, and requires rather than allows the commission to assess civil penalties of up to $1,000 or $500 for certain violations, plus a $500 penalty for electronic filing violations.

in:SB 239.title: Various education matters.
in:SB 239.summary: Allows converting existing public schools to charter schools under added conditions, lets innovation network charter schools contract with several school corporations, revises closed school building transfers, and requires notice to parents of students at risk of missing grade-level math proficiency.

in:SB 241.title: Utility service enhancement improvement costs.
in:SB 241.summary: Raises from 2,000 to 3,000 the customer count below which a water-service conservancy district may leave state utility commission jurisdiction, limits tap and capacity fees for nonprofit workforce housing, and lets water utilities adjust rates for chemical and power cost changes over 3%.

in:SB 243.title: Various tax matters.
in:SB 243.summary: Updates Indiana income tax law to match federal changes in the 2025 federal budget act, allows electronic delivery of tax department documents, extends the deadline for federal audit adjustments from 180 days to one year, and changes cigarette, petroleum severance and alcohol tax rules.

in:SB 246.title: Redaction of court records.
in:SB 246.summary: Requires redaction of names and other identifying information of child victims and child witnesses in criminal cases, using anonymous labels like "Child Witness No. 1" rather than initials or family relationships.

in:SB 249.title: State chemist.
in:SB 249.summary: Writes state animal food rules into law, covering commercial feed and pet food labels, ingredients, additives, manufacturing practices, inspection fees and feed licenses.

in:SB 25.title: School board candidates.
in:SB 25.summary: Sets the order in which school board candidates appear on the ballot within designated groups, listing candidates alphabetically by surname.

in:SB 254.title: Ivy Tech Community College.
in:SB 254.summary: Consolidates Ivy Tech's duties and board responsibilities, adds logistics, information technology and life sciences as trustee expertise, sets campus board roles, and requires the Indiana Economic Development Corporation to create an education-to-employment research program and data framework by December 1, 2026.

in:SB 259.title: Partnership composite returns.
in:SB 259.summary: Removes penalties for pass-through entities that leave nonresident partners, shareholders or beneficiaries with no positive distributive share income off a composite return.

in:SB 261.title: Criminal vandalism.
in:SB 261.summary: Renames criminal mischief as criminal vandalism, folds institutional, cemetery, railroad and critical infrastructure mischief into it with the same penalties and defenses, and moves cave damage and refuse provisions.

in:SB 262.title: INSPECT program.
in:SB 262.summary: Sets when pharmacies and other dispensers need not report to the INSPECT prescription monitoring program, requires opioid treatment programs to follow federal consent rules before reporting, and lets the pharmacy board share program data with health and social services officials.

in:SB 27.title: Stadium authority.
in:SB 27.summary: Creates the northwest Indiana stadium authority and board with power to finance and build a stadium using bonds, and changes Lake and Porter County food, beverage and innkeeper taxes and lets Hammond impose an admissions tax.

in:SB 270.title: Township mergers.
in:SB 270.summary: Requires the state to score township governments by performance by the end of 2026, and generally requires townships scoring four or more points to merge with another township or reorganize with a municipality, with mergers effective by January 1, 2029.

in:SB 271.title: Telecommunications wire and valuable metal dealers.
in:SB 271.summary: Adds telecommunications network wire to the definition of valuable metal for metal dealer laws, bars selling or buying it unless conditions are met, and lets people who suffer losses from violations sue for damages.

in:SB 275.title: FSSA fiscal matters.
in:SB 275.summary: Requires waiver service providers to give recipients documentation to review for errors, sets a time frame for the disability services bureau to decide requests for more service units, and creates some Medicaid reimbursement exemptions under value-based arrangements.

in:SB 277.title: Indiana department of environmental management.
in:SB 277.summary: Changes the structure and powers of the environmental management department and rules board, bars decisions based solely on unpromulgated federal risk values, and revises permitting, hearing, reporting, water pollution and waste statutes.

in:SB 285.title: Housing matters.
in:SB 285.summary: Bars camping or long-term sheltering on public land unless authorized, directs officers to assess whether emergency detention is warranted, defines gravely disabled for involuntary commitment, and sets criteria for homeless-services funding applicants.

in:SB 291.title: Court security.
in:SB 291.summary: Lets judges and household family members ask public agencies to stop publishing or remove their personal information, with a civil action against agencies that fail to; lets the supreme court and court of appeals each appoint a court marshal with limited police powers.

in:SB 293.title: Pharmacist licensure.
in:SB 293.summary: Requires passing the North American Pharmacist Licensure Examination to be licensed as a pharmacist, removes an exam requirement for certain pharmacists seeking license reciprocity, and voids conflicting rules.

in:SB 3.title: Constitutional amendment ballot language.
in:SB 3.summary: Sets the ballot language for the proposed constitutional amendment concerning bail.

in:SB 4.title: Various fiscal matters.
in:SB 4.summary: Requires a fiscal impact analysis of all gubernatorial executive orders within seven days, lowers the proposed-rule cost threshold for budget committee review to $500,000, and changes community mental health center funding and reporting rules.

in:SB 56.title: Veterinary licensing.
in:SB 56.summary: Lets the board of veterinary medicine license veterinarians and registered veterinary technicians without an examination if they meet health care professional reciprocity requirements.

in:SB 6.title: Extension of water or wastewater mains.
in:SB 6.summary: Requires municipal utilities to mail written notice to affected landowners and the county plan commission, and post information online, before condemning land for water or wastewater main extensions outside city limits or the utility's service territory.

in:SB 71.title: Various probate matters.
in:SB 71.summary: Creates a guardianship code revision task force and changes rules on paying property or debts owed to minors, up to $25,000 without a court order, court approval of minors' claim settlements, and transfers under the Uniform Transfers to Minors Act.

in:SB 76.title: Immigration matters.
in:SB 76.summary: Lets the attorney general defend officers, governments or colleges sued over certain immigration matters; requires governments holding a person under an immigration detainer request to comply and notify the judge; and bars employers from knowingly hiring unauthorized aliens, enforced by the attorney general.

in:SB 80.title: Code publication.
in:SB 80.summary: Resolves amend-repeal conflicts from the 2025 session, relocates definitions chapters in alphabetical order, and updates cross-references, with no substantive change to law.

in:SB 88.title: Education matters.
in:SB 88.summary: Changes good citizenship instruction requirements, requires state colleges to accept the Classic Learning Test like the ACT or SAT for admission, and has the education department list schools offering exams to students enrolled elsewhere.

in:SB 89.title: Three-way permits.
in:SB 89.summary: Lets the alcohol and tobacco commission issue new three-way alcohol permits: three each to Schererville and Lafayette, two each to West Lafayette, Delphi and Bloomington, and eight to restaurants in a Michigan City transit district.

in:SB 9.title: Victim impact statements.
in:SB 9.summary: Requires a defendant to be present in the courtroom when a victim speaks about the crime and sentence, unless safety risk or disruption, and lets a court hold a later hearing for the victim if the defendant skipped sentencing.

in:SB 91.title: Syringe exchange program.
in:SB 91.summary: Bars syringe exchange programs from operating fixed sites within 1,000 feet of specified facilities, bars providing chemical reagents or precursors, sets participation requirements, and lets the health department deny, suspend or revoke registrations for violations.

in:SB 92.title: Community corrections trust funds.
in:SB 92.summary: Lets counties running community corrections programs set up a county community corrections trust fund, with set funding sources, permitted uses, and reporting and audit requirements.

in:SJR 1.title: Constitutional amendment concerning bail.
in:SJR 1.summary: Proposes a state constitutional amendment making offenses other than murder or treason not bailable if the proof is evident or the presumption strong and the state shows by clear and convincing evidence that no release conditions will reasonably protect others or the community.

ky:HB 139.title: AN ACT relating to elections and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 139.summary: Lets the State Board of Elections share data with other agencies to remove ineligible voters, bars buying voting systems that tabulate from barcodes or QR codes, and changes several election deadlines and procedures.

ky:HB 142.title: AN ACT relating to depredating wildlife and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 142.summary: Sets rules for landowners, tenants and designees to take or trap wildlife damaging property, including destruction tags and 24-hour reporting, and lets the Fish and Wildlife Commission set an extra 7 to 10 day antlerless deer season in overpopulated areas.

ky:HB 311.title: AN ACT relating to railroad crossings.
ky:HB 311.summary: Requires railroads to remove obstructive vegetation 250 feet each way at public grade crossings by January 1, 2029; railroads may petition the Transportation Cabinet for waivers. After 30 days' notice, the cabinet or local government removes it and bills the railroad.

ky:HB 504.title: AN ACT making appropriations for the operations, maintenance, support, and functioning of the Judicial Branch of the government of the Commonwealth of Kentucky and its various officers, boards, commissions, subdivisions, and other state-supported activities.
ky:HB 504.summary: Overrides the Governor's line-item vetoes of the Judicial Branch budget, which appropriates money for the Judicial Branch's operating and capital projects and sets general provisions and a budget reduction or surplus expenditure plan.

ky:HB 519.title: AN ACT relating to identity documents.
ky:HB 519.summary: Lets license and ID card applicants choose a communication disorder notation, removable on request, with no proof or fee required. A Senate amendment also ends the four-year license option and lets renewal occur any time within a year of expiration.

ky:HB 567.title: AN ACT relating to open records.
ky:HB 567.summary: As passed by the Senate, lets records custodians require a government photo ID showing an address, or other proof, of Kentucky residency; counts requests from licensed attorneys for certain clients as resident requests; and lets planning commissions add a nonvoting military installation representative.

ky:HB 6.title: AN ACT relating to child care and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 6.summary: Licenses child-care microcenters, requires a private third-party administrator for the Employee Child Care Assistance Partnership Program, changes the Certified Child Care Community Designation Program, and requires a child care modernization plan from the health cabinet by October 1, 2026.

ky:HB 652.title: AN ACT relating to critical facility mapping and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 652.summary: Moves administration of the school mapping data program to the Kentucky 911 Services Board and assigns responsibility for mapping data accuracy walk-throughs.

ky:HB 658.title: AN ACT relating to limited commercial driver's licenses and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 658.summary: Directs the Transportation Cabinet to extend limited farm-related commercial driver's license terms to the federal maximum; from July 1, 2027, lets county officials in counties without a regional licensing office issue renewal and duplicate licenses and IDs by agreement, with a $25 convenience fee.

ky:HB 669.title: AN ACT relating to child welfare.
ky:HB 669.summary: Requires the Cabinet for Health and Family Services to check whether each child in its custody gets or qualifies for Social Security or veterans benefits, and creates the Success Sequence Savings and Disbursement Plan, requiring financial training before a child accesses part of saved benefits.

ky:HB 676.title: AN ACT relating to the Kentucky statewide health data utility.
ky:HB 676.summary: Directs Legislative Research Commission staff to study creating a Kentucky statewide health data utility and report to a legislative health committee by December 1, 2026.

ky:HB 727.title: AN ACT relating to education and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 727.summary: Changes many education statutes, including class-size and caseload rules for exceptional children and school board training topics; lets a legislative subcommittee temporarily authorize new state education reports; repeals the summer learning camp and teacher computer purchase laws.

ky:HB 78.title: AN ACT relating to firearms liability protections and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 78.summary: Limits civil lawsuits against firearm and ammunition makers, sellers and trade associations over criminal misuse of their products, preempts local laws imposing such liability, and gives the Attorney General enforcement authority.

ky:HB 826.title: AN ACT relating to education.
ky:HB 826.summary: Requires at least 85% of Office of Adult Education general funds to go to adult education programs, requires a paper-test option for the high school equivalency exam, and removes the McConnell Center from developing a required American civics course.

ky:HB 869.title: AN ACT relating to fiscal matters and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 869.summary: As passed by the Senate, creates a refundable economic development credit for approved incentive projects based on a four-tier county ranking, raises skills training credit caps to $5,000 or $4,000 per trainee, and creates a heritage community revolving fund.

ky:HJR 24.title: A JOINT RESOLUTION directing the Cabinet for Health and Family Services to withdraw all waiver applications that have been submitted to the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services to establish a community engagement program, and declaring an emergency.
ky:HJR 24.summary: Directs the Cabinet for Health and Family Services to withdraw, within five days, its Medicaid waiver applications for a community engagement program, including the one filed June 25, 2025.

ky:HJR 81.title: A JOINT RESOLUTION authorizing the release of funds and declaring an emergency.
ky:HJR 81.summary: Authorizes the state budget director to release $52,502,260 in General Fund money to the Kentucky Infrastructure Authority for 17 listed water and wastewater projects under the Kentucky WWATERS program.

ky:SB 124.title: AN ACT relating to sick leave for school district personnel.
ky:SB 124.summary: Lets school district employees use sick leave for religious holidays not on the school calendar, and lets districts pay employees before retirement for accrued sick leave above 15 days at up to 30% of the daily wage.

ky:SB 127.title: AN ACT relating to actuarial costs of annual leave payments in the Teachers' Retirement System.
ky:SB 127.summary: As amended, makes the state pay Teachers’ Retirement System actuarial costs of annual leave accrued through July 31, 2026, plus up to 5 days yearly for school districts and some state schools; last employers pay rest. Credits leave for retirement only if accrued before August 1, 2026 with employers already paying it.

ky:SB 129.title: AN ACT relating to unemployment insurance.
ky:SB 129.summary: Ends the 0.075% employer unemployment insurance rate reduction after 2026 and sets a 0.0115% reduction from 2027, adjustable yearly up to 0.025%, suspended if the upgrade fund reaches $15 million or the trust fund does not exceed its 2022 balance.

ky:SB 133.title: AN ACT relating to the fiscal reporting of local entities.
ky:SB 133.summary: Raises the receipts or spending thresholds that set audit requirements for special purpose governmental entities, lets entities with two straight unqualified audit opinions move to an audit every four years, and allows agreed-upon-procedures engagements for some, starting July 2027.

ky:SB 147.title: AN ACT relating to vital records.
ky:SB 147.summary: Raises the maximum fee for certifying vital records from $5 to $10 and for a certified birth record from $10 to $15, adds fee waivers for line-of-duty death certificates and declared disasters, and changes how certified copies are requested.

ky:SB 156.title: AN ACT relating to child marriage.
ky:SB 156.summary: Removes the exception letting 17-year-olds marry with court permission, so marriage and marriage licenses are barred under age 18. Lawful marriages entered into before the effective date remain valid.

ky:SB 160.title: AN ACT relating to child-care centers and declaring an emergency.
ky:SB 160.summary: Lists factors the Cabinet for Health and Family Services must consider before issuing a plan of correction or suspending or revoking a child-care center license, and requires two weekly support contacts, one in person, for centers on a six-month preliminary license.

ky:SB 197.title: AN ACT providing funding and establishing conditions for state government agencies and institutions, making an appropriation therefor, and declaring an emergency.
ky:SB 197.summary: Amends the state budget bills to add supplemental appropriations for various programs and projects, with conditions attached.

ky:SB 214.title: AN ACT relating to agriculture and declaring an emergency.
ky:SB 214.summary: Allows the Department of Agriculture to accept nonfederal grants and funds from any public or private source, and creates a Kentucky Urban Youth Agriculture Initiative run jointly by the Kentucky State University and University of Kentucky extension services.

ky:SB 261.title: AN ACT relating to pedestrian swinging bridges.
ky:SB 261.summary: Allows fiscal courts and cities to spend public funds to care for and maintain pedestrian swinging bridges open for recreation, and limits liability for owners of land leased to a local government that maintains such a bridge.

ky:SB 281.title: AN ACT relating to grandparent visitation.
ky:SB 281.summary: Requires clear and convincing evidence of compelling factors before granting grandparent visitation over a fit parent (a lower standard applies if a non-parent has custody), lists best-interest factors, and removes the presumption favoring visitation when the child's parent has died.

ky:SB 312.title: AN ACT relating to court-ordered transports.
ky:SB 312.summary: Allows certified court security officers to transport people detained or in custody as ordered by a court, including outside the court facility, to arrest while transporting or supervising them, and to transport people ordered into involuntary hospitalization.

ky:SB 324.title: AN ACT relating to the entertainment industry.
ky:SB 324.summary: Lets unused portions of the $75 million annual film tax credit cap carry into the next year, adds video games, music videos and commercials to eligible productions, and raises minimum qualifying spending for some productions.

ky:SB 37.title: AN ACT relating to state symbols.
ky:SB 37.summary: Names the Treeing Walker Coonhound state dog, cats and dogs adopted from or living in Kentucky shelters or rescues official state pets, the eastern spotted skunk state nongame mammal, and the eastern hellbender state amphibian.

ky:SB 59.title: AN ACT relating to prohibited uses of tax dollars and resources.
ky:SB 59.summary: Extends the ban on using public money to advocate on ballot questions to public resources such as staff, facilities and websites. Sets fines of $500, then $1,000, then a Class A misdemeanor; exempts educational television and employees acting on personal time.

ky:SB 65.title: AN ACT relating to deficient administrative regulations and declaring an emergency.
ky:SB 65.summary: Declares six proposed administrative regulations (Medicaid outpatient pharmacy, tobacco and vapor licensing, online insurance verification, controlled substance monitoring, relative caregiver services) null and void and bars agencies from reissuing similar ones through June 1, 2027. Takes effect immediately as an emergency.

ky:SB 66.title: AN ACT relating to the operation of a motor vehicle.
ky:SB 66.summary: Bars driving with clonazepam, cyclobenzaprine or fentanyl detected in the blood, removes blood-test refusal as an aggravating circumstance, and says refusing a preliminary breath test cannot be used in court or cause a license suspension.

ky:SB 70.title: AN ACT relating to the Public Pension Oversight Board.
ky:SB 70.summary: Adds the State Treasurer and a House and Senate state-government committee chair or vice chair to the Public Pension Oversight Board from January 2027, drops one gubernatorial appointee, and extends an annual pension report to line-of-duty death benefits.

ky:SB 9.title: AN ACT relating to housing districts.
ky:SB 9.summary: Lets local governments create residential infrastructure districts financed by bonds and special property assessments, and housing development districts where projects can be exempted from planning review and receive annual incentive payments based on property taxes. Caps agricultural land at 20% of a housing district.

ky:SB 94.title: AN ACT relating to motor vehicle dealers.
ky:SB 94.summary: Sets rules for how motor vehicle manufacturers must compensate dealers for warranty work, including time allowances, labor rates, parts markups, and payment procedures and deadlines.

ky:SB 98.title: AN ACT relating to welding safety.
ky:SB 98.summary: As passed by the Senate, requires structural steel welding on projects whose specifications cite AWS D1.1 or D1.5 to use welders certified by an accredited testing facility and meet those standards, effective January 1, 2027. Exempts homeowner or farmer welding on their own premises.

ky:SCR 66.title: A CONCURRENT RESOLUTION urging the University of Kentucky and the University of Louisville to explore opportunities to participate in federal nuclear-related programs and to expand their curricula to offer courses and degree paths to train the workforce that will construct and operate the next generation of nuclear energy facilities.
ky:SCR 66.summary: Urges the University of Kentucky and University of Louisville to explore participating in the U.S. Department of Energy's Nuclear Energy University Program and to expand courses and degree paths training the nuclear energy workforce.

ky:SJR 116.title: A JOINT RESOLUTION directing the University of Kentucky, the University of Louisville, and Eastern Kentucky University to coordinate a search for actionable solutions to physician shortages and to explore and expand health care opportunities in medically underserved areas in collaboration with community, state agency, professional associations, and other stakeholders.
ky:SJR 116.summary: Directs the University of Kentucky, University of Louisville and Eastern Kentucky University to coordinate a search for solutions to physician shortages and report to the General Assembly by January 1, 2027.

ky:SJR 54.title: A JOINT RESOLUTION directing the Department for Libraries and Archives and the Cabinet for Health and Family Services to cooperate in exploring ways to increase enrollment in Dolly Partonâs Imagination Library Program.
ky:SJR 54.summary: Directs the Department for Libraries and Archives and the Cabinet for Health and Family Services to explore ways to increase enrollment in Dolly Parton's Imagination Library and report by November 1, 2026.

ky:SJR 62.title: A JOINT RESOLUTION directing the Division of Water to provide recommendations and clear guidance on how local governments can more easily access jurisdictional streams and waterways for cleanup after a flood.
ky:SJR 62.summary: Directs the Division of Water to report to the Legislative Research Commission by December 15, 2026 on how state and local governments can more easily access public waterways after flooding for debris removal and cleanup.

ky:SJR 74.title: A JOINT RESOLUTION directing the Legislative Research Commission and state agencies to collaborate to create a statewide fiscal map of substance use disorder programs and funding sources.
ky:SJR 74.summary: Directs the Legislative Research Commission and state agencies to create a statewide fiscal map of substance use disorder programs and funding sources, post it online, and report to the General Assembly by October 30, 2026.

ky:SJR 75.title: A JOINT RESOLUTION directing the Public Service Commission to explore measures that would address affordability and the provision of essential utility services and declaring an emergency.
ky:SJR 75.summary: Directs the Public Service Commission to open administrative cases to identify ways to make utility service more affordable for low- and fixed-income customers and to report to the Legislative Research Commission by September 1, 2027.

la:HB 1.title: APPROPRIATIONS: Provides for the ordinary operating expenses of state government for Fiscal Year 2026-2027
la:HB 1.summary: Appropriates $46.2 billion for state government operating expenses in fiscal year 2026-27, including $11.7 billion in state general fund money, and transfers $850 million from the Revenue Stabilization Fund to several funds.

la:HB 1005.title: INDIGENT DEFENSE: Provides relative to the office of the state public defender (EN NO IMPACT   See Note)
la:HB 1005.summary: Replaces references to the Louisiana Public Defender Board with the office of the state public defender, whom the governor appoints with Senate confirmation to a two-year term. District public defenders who contract with the office are independent contractors.

la:HB 1007.title: DISTRICTS/SPECIAL: Creates the Faubourg Nouveau Marigny Improvement District in Orleans Parish
la:HB 1007.summary: Creates the Faubourg Nouveau Marigny Improvement District in Orleans Parish, run by a five-member board, to fund beautification and streetscape projects. Allows a voter-approved parcel fee, such as up to $100 a year for improved residential parcels.

la:HB 1017.title: RETIREMENT/FIREFIGHTERS: Prohibits certain post-divorce earnable compensation in the Firefighters' Retirement System from being included in a former spouse's portion of community property (EN NO IMPACT APV)
la:HB 1017.summary: Excludes from a former spouse's share of community property any raise in a full-time firefighter's earnable compensation, made after the community ends, that was conditional on passing a written exam and working test.

la:HB 1018.title: ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGE PERMT: Provides relative to limitations on the issuance of certain alcoholic beverage permits
la:HB 1018.summary: Bars new high and low alcohol permits for small premises under 5,000 square feet in Louisiana House District 2 from August 1, 2026 through 2027. Exempts downtown Shreveport, Bossier City and purchases of existing licensed premises.

la:HB 1028.title: MEDICAID: Requires the Louisiana Department of Health to increase the reimbursement rates for nonemergency medical transportation providers (EN +$2,601,174 GF EX See Note)
la:HB 1028.summary: Requires the Department of Health to set Medicaid non-emergency medical transportation rates of at least $14.50 per trip and $2.10 per mile, with a multi-passenger rate method. Limits rides outside the home or neighboring parishes unless medically necessary.

la:HB 1029.title: ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGE PERMT: Provides relative to limitations on the issuance of certain alcoholic beverage permits
la:HB 1029.summary: As passed by the House, extends the ban on new Class B and C high- and low-alcohol permits in Louisiana House District 3 from the end of 2026 to the end of 2032. Exempts national chains, defined as companies operating in 10 or more states.

la:HB 1043.title: COURTS: Provides relative to the civil jurisdictional amounts for the First and Second Parish Courts
la:HB 1043.summary: Raises the civil jurisdictional limit of the First and Second Parish Courts of Jefferson Parish from $20,000 to $50,000.

la:HB 1049.title: PUBLIC MEETINGS: Provides relative to public meetings (EN NO IMPACT   See Note)
la:HB 1049.summary: Lets school boards set reasonable rules on public comment, requires public meeting notices to be posted so the public can read them, and requires draft minutes to go to members five business days before approval.

la:HB 1050.title: MTR VEHICLE/DRIVER LIC: Modifies provisions relative to certain requirements for commercial driver's licenses
la:HB 1050.summary: Revises commercial driver's license rules: removes the tractor-trailer restriction on Class A licenses earned in other vehicles, removes the "straight vehicle" definition, and repeals vision standards for intrastate driver waivers.

la:HB 1051.title: PROPERTY/VACANT SUBSTAND: Provides relative to the demolition of certain dilapidated property in the city of Shreveport
la:HB 1051.summary: Requires Shreveport commercial property owners who received an insurance payment for fire damage to demolish the structure if the city finds it dilapidated and dangerous, applying retroactively to Jan. 1, 2023.

la:HB 1052.title: CHILDRENS CODE: Provides relative to confidentiality policies and procedures pertaining to work product created, received, or maintained by child advocacy centers and multidisciplinary investigative teams
la:HB 1052.summary: Requires each multidisciplinary child abuse investigative team and child advocacy center to adopt a written confidentiality policy limiting shared information to authorized participants for investigation, assessment, prosecution and treatment, and covers team work product.

la:HB 1056.title: PROPERTY/PUBLIC: Authorizes the transfer of certain state property in Natchitoches Parish
la:HB 1056.summary: Authorizes the president of the Board of Elementary and Secondary Education and the commissioner of administration to transfer about 1.16 acres of state property in Natchitoches Parish, excluding mineral rights, which the state keeps.

la:HB 1062.title: SCHOOLS: Provides relative to the membership, powers, and duties of the board of directors of the Special School District
la:HB 1062.summary: Changes the Special School District board: ends the one-member-per-health-region appointment rule, requires annual nominee lists by Aug. 1, has the board authorize the superintendent to select textbooks, and requires annual superintendent evaluations.

la:HB 1076.title: HEALTH/BEHAVIORAL: Repeals the termination of the Louisiana Behavior Analyst Board
la:HB 1076.summary: Repeals the July 1, 2028 termination date of the Louisiana Behavior Analyst Board, keeping the board and behavior analyst licensing in place.

la:HB 1081.title: PORTS/HARBORS/TERMINALS: Provides for the Louisiana Ports and Waterways Investment Commission (EN NO IMPACT   See Note)
la:HB 1081.summary: Moves the Louisiana Ports and Waterways Investment Commission from the governor's office to the Office of Multimodal Commerce within the Department of Transportation and Development.

la:HB 1082.title: CIVIL/VENUE: Provides for venue with respect to the Municipal Police Employees' Retirement System
la:HB 1082.summary: As passed by the House, requires lawsuits involving the Municipal Police Employees' Retirement System to be filed in the district court of the judicial district where the employer is located, instead of East Baton Rouge or the system's domicile parish.

la:HB 1084.title: STUDENT/TUITION: Provides relative to tuition and mandatory fees for public postsecondary education institutions
la:HB 1084.summary: Authorizes each public college and university to set and adjust tuition and fees for all programs, with increases capped at 10% per year and no cap on reductions, starting January 1, 2027.

la:HB 1095.title: NURSING HOMES: Provides for alternative power sources at nursing facilities
la:HB 1095.summary: Creates a rebate program, capped at $2 million total, for certain nursing facilities that install solar energy systems, and clarifies that nursing facilities must keep fuel or an alternative power source stored on site.

la:HB 1098.title: LIABILITY/CIVIL: Provides with respect to a limitation of liability for aerospace entities
la:HB 1098.summary: As passed by the House, bars nuisance, trespass and similar claims against aerospace flight entities over noise, vibration, light, exhaust and other flight-related disturbances. Exceptions include gross negligence, violating federal license conditions and falling debris beyond normal risk.

la:HB 1100.title: SMALL BUSINESS: Repeals requirements for enriching bread and flour sold in this state
la:HB 1100.summary: Repeals the state requirement that bread and flour sold in Louisiana be enriched with vitamins, along with the related labeling, exemption and Department of Health inspection provisions.

la:HB 1117.title: INSURANCE: Provides relative to certain insurer contractual payments and prescriptive period
la:HB 1117.summary: As passed by the House, provides that an insurer's payment under its contract is not an acknowledgment of debt and does not interrupt the time limit for suing on the policy.

la:HB 1126.title: LEGISLATIVE EXPENSES: Makes appropriations for the expenses of the legislature for Fiscal Year 2026-2027
la:HB 1126.summary: Appropriates $94.5 million in state general funds for the expenses of the Legislature and legislative agencies for fiscal year 2026-2027, including $33.0 million for the House and $28.1 million for the Senate.

la:HB 1129.title: PROPERTY/PUBLIC: Provides relative to the selling of state-owned surplus movable property (EN SEE FISC NOTE SG EX)
la:HB 1129.summary: Gives preference to in-state auctioneers over out-of-state ones when the commissioner of administration sells surplus state movable property, if service quality is equal and cost is within 10 percent.

la:HB 1139.title: MENTAL HEALTH: Requires certain behavioral health services for patients receiving treatment pursuant to an emergency certificate
la:HB 1139.summary: Requires a health care facility that admits a patient on an emergency certificate to have a licensed professional conduct a behavioral health evaluation and contact the patient's behavioral health provider for treatment history within 72 hours.

la:HB 1153.title: ENVIRONMENT/ENFORCEMENT: Authorizes parishes and municipalities to declare bans on burning
la:HB 1153.summary: Lets parish and municipal governments issue burn bans during elevated fire risk, requires lifting them when risk ends, requires parishes to publish notice in the official journal, and sets fines of $500 to $2,500 for violations.

la:HB 1161.title: PROPERTY/PUBLIC: Authorizes the transfer of certain state property in Lafourche Parish
la:HB 1161.summary: Authorizes the transportation and development secretary to transfer certain Lafourche Parish property to the city of Thibodaux and certain Jefferson Parish property to the city of Gretna, reserving mineral rights to the state.

la:HB 1162.title: INSURANCE CLAIMS: Provides relative to the verification of contractors
la:HB 1162.summary: Requires insurers to verify a contractor's license with the state licensing board before paying a property-repair claim that names the contractor as payee, and shields insurers from bad-faith penalties for delays caused by failed verification if they notify the insured within five business days.

la:HB 1182.title: OCCUPATIONAL THERAPISTS: Provides relative to the rules governing Occupational Therapists and Occupational Therapy Assistants
la:HB 1182.summary: Requires occupational therapy license applicants to pass the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy exam, replaces references to the American Occupational Therapy Association with that board, removes a license waiver for certain state employees, and raises most license fees.

la:HB 1186.title: BUILDING CODES: Provides relative to the Uniform Construction Code and inspector licensing
la:HB 1186.summary: Replaces the Uniform Construction Code Council with a Uniform Construction Code Commission that adopts the state building code and licenses inspectors.

la:HB 1189.title: WILDLIFE & FISHERIES: Provides for charter boat fishing guide licenses
la:HB 1189.summary: Requires freshwater charter boat fishing guides operating on U.S. waters in Louisiana to hold a U.S. Coast Guard captain's license, and renames the nonresident saltwater guide license a nonresident charter boat fishing guide license.

la:HB 119.title: CRIME: Provides relative to unlawful conduct involving images of another person created by artificial intelligence (EN SEE FISC NOTE GF EX)
la:HB 119.summary: Raises penalties for disseminating or selling AI-created images of a person (up to five years if under 17), creates a crime of possessing such images of people under 17, and adds up to two consecutive years when an educator's victim is a student.

la:HB 1193.title: CONTRACTS/BIDS: Provides for Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity construction phase contracts (EN SEE FISC NOTE SD EX See Note)
la:HB 1193.summary: Lets the Coastal Protection and Restoration Authority award indefinite delivery, indefinite quantity construction contracts for coastal protection projects, using single or multiple awards and low bid, best value or qualification-based selection.

la:HB 1194.title: AGRICULTURAL COMMODITIES: Provides with respect to the Healthy Food Retail Act (EN NO IMPACT   See Note)
la:HB 1194.summary: Expands the Healthy Food Retail Act to cover food deserts, defined as low-income census tracts with many residents far from a supermarket, and other food access projects, with priority for projects showing demand and long-term sustainability.

la:HB 1195.title: AMUSEMENTS/SPORTS: Provides relative to the Louisiana State Athletic Commission
la:HB 1195.summary: Changes State Athletic Commission rules: cuts the maximum rounds in a boxing contest from 20 to 12, raises the maximum fine on licensees from $1,000 to $5,000 and on unauthorized events from $500 to $5,000, and adds cease and desist authority.

la:HB 1199.title: INSURANCE/HEALTH: Provides relative to health insurance coverage for genetic testing and the treatment of SCN2A-associated medical conditions (EN NO IMPACT   See Note)
la:HB 1199.summary: Requires health plans, starting Jan. 1, 2027, to cover genetic testing and medically necessary treatment for SCN2A-associated conditions when ordered by a treating provider, while allowing nondiscriminatory prior authorization.

la:HB 1201.title: ELECTED OFFICIALS/COMP: Provides with respect to the compensation of statewide elected officials and legislators (EN INCREASE GF EX See Note)
la:HB 1201.summary: Lets legislators claim per diem and mileage for up to 10 days a month of official business, extends the $1,000 monthly housing allowance to all legislators, and adds inflation adjustments and allowances for statewide elected officials other than the governor.

la:HB 1203.title: EDUCATION: Provides relative to parent-driven learning microschools
la:HB 1203.summary: Defines parent-driven learning microschools as parent groups teaching mixed-age children in homes or community spaces. Provides that using a building for one does not change its zoning, building code or fire safety status, and exempts microschools from state registration and early learning center licensing.

la:HB 1228.title: HEARING AID DEALERS: Relative to the Louisiana Board of Hearing Aid Dealers
la:HB 1228.summary: Changes hearing aid dealer rules: ends their role collecting taxes, requires a seller email on sales contracts, lets buyers cancel by notifying the seller in person, by mail or by email, and revises licensing requirements.

la:HB 1230.title: COMMERCIAL REGULATIONS: Provides relative to the Louisiana Money Transmission Act
la:HB 1230.summary: Repeals the Sale of Checks and Money Transmission Act and enacts the Louisiana Money Transmission Act, setting licensing, exemption, supervision and examination rules for money transmitters under the financial institutions commissioner, including multistate examinations.

la:HB 1231.title: MEDICAID MANAGED CARE: Provides relative to Medicaid coverage for continuous glucose monitoring devices for individuals with certain conditions (EN NO IMPACT   See Note)
la:HB 1231.summary: Changes Medicaid coverage of continuous glucose monitoring to cover diabetes, including gestational diabetes, for people who require insulin or have level 2 or 3 hypoglycemia, rather than only those needing insulin more than twice daily.

la:HB 1234.title: CRIMINAL/PENALTIES: Provides relative to penalties for hit-and-run driving (EN SEE FISC NOTE GF EX)
la:HB 1234.summary: Requires at least two or five years of a hit-and-run sentence, depending on the offense level, to be served without parole, probation or suspension when the victim is a pedestrian or bicyclist.

la:HB 1236.title: INSURANCE: Provides relative to pharmacy benefit managers reimbursements (EN +$2,265,844 SG EX See Note)
la:HB 1236.summary: Changes how pharmacy benefit managers reimburse pharmacies, requiring a formula with a professional dispensing fee of at least $9 applied retroactively to January 1, 2026, and barring managers from recovering that fee from pharmacies.

la:HB 1237.title: RETIREMENT/STATEWIDE SYS: Provides relative to the Municipal Police Employees Retirement System and the Firefighters' Retirement System (EN SEE ACTUARIAL NOTE FC)
la:HB 1237.summary: Requires a police chief or mayor to sign and notarize a police officer's affidavit opting out of the municipal police retirement system, repeals partial-dissolution payments for police departments, and changes the payment formula and triggers for fire departments.

la:HB 1243.title: SEWERAGE/N O WATER BD: Provides relative to the Sewerage and Water Board of New Orleans
la:HB 1243.summary: Removes the state-law makeup of the New Orleans Sewerage and Water Board, including its selection committee and quorum rule, and lets the board's composition follow the city charter, with the city council setting appointment and term rules by ordinance.

la:HB 1249.title: HEALTH/SCHOOL CLINICS: Provides relative to school-based health center services provided to students (EN SEE FISC NOTE LF EX)
la:HB 1249.summary: Bars school employees from preventing a student from using medically necessary school-based health center services when a parent, guardian or adult student consents, and requires school policies that avoid delays or extra barriers for licensed providers.

la:HB 1252.title: COURTS: Provides relative to the city court system in Avoyelles Parish (EN SEE FISC NOTE LF EX)
la:HB 1252.summary: Assigns Avoyelles Parish wards to the Marksville and Bunkie city courts, which share concurrent jurisdiction with the 12th Judicial District Court over misdemeanors, civil disputes under $50,000 and juvenile matters, for cases filed from January 1, 2027.

la:HB 1256.title: PROPERTY/UNCLAIMED: Provides with respect to abandoned digital assets
la:HB 1256.summary: Adds digital assets to the unclaimed property law, presuming them abandoned three years after the owner's last sign of interest. Holder notices must warn that the asset may be liquidated without a response; the state generally waits three years after receiving it to liquidate.

la:HB 129.title: HIGHWAYS: Designates certain portions of Louisiana highways
la:HB 129.summary: Designates a stretch of Louisiana Highway 1 in Shreveport as the "Virginia Green Evans Memorial Highway" and directs signage if local or private money covers its cost, up to $750 per sign.

la:HB 153.title: COURTS/CRIMINAL: Provides with respect to the collection of criminal court fines and fees
la:HB 153.summary: Bars reporting criminal fines and fees debt to credit bureaus or consumer reporting agencies. Does not apply to traffic law violations under Title 32 or municipal law violations. Takes effect August 1, 2026.

la:HB 159.title: CRIMINAL/SENTENCING: Creates a pretrial incarceration alternative pilot program in Caddo Parish (EN SEE FISC NOTE LF EX See Note)
la:HB 159.summary: Lets the Caddo Parish Sheriff run a pretrial pilot program, starting by January 1, 2027, using electronic monitoring instead of jail for eligible defendants, with court and district attorney approval.

la:HB 166.title: JUVENILES: Removes Vermilion Parish as a member of the Acadiana Regional Juvenile Justice District
la:HB 166.summary: Removes Vermilion Parish from the Acadiana Regional Juvenile Justice District and cuts the district commission from 11 to 10 members.

la:HB 167.title: PUBLIC SFTY/CORRECTIONS: Provides for the issuance of certain documentation to inmates before their release from incarceration (EN SEE FISC NOTE GF EX)
la:HB 167.summary: Requires the corrections department to give felony inmates released to a Louisiana residence documentation for job searches and, with the Office of Motor Vehicles, to start ID paperwork nine months before release and issue those without current ID a six-year special ID card.

la:HB 180.title: PROPERTY/EXPROPRIATION: Provides relative to expropriation by private entities
la:HB 180.summary: Defines "foreign adversary" and "agent of a foreign adversary" for the law on expropriation by private entities, presuming control when a person holds at least 50% of an entity's voting interests or profits.

la:HB 2.title: CAPITAL OUTLAY: Provides for the comprehensive Capital Outlay budget
la:HB 2.summary: Sets the capital outlay budget for fiscal year 2026-27, with about $3.17 billion in cash and authority for about $11.5 billion in general obligation bonds for listed projects.

la:HB 210.title: ETHICS/CODE: Provides for restrictions on payments from nonpublic sources
la:HB 210.summary: Bars statewide elected officials from being paid for lobbying, consulting or advising. Applies retroactively an existing exception letting school board and local governing authority members work for employers doing business with their government, except where an ethics body has issued a final decision.

la:HB 211.title: COURTS: Provides relative to the creation, administration, and eligibility requirements of the Homelessness Court program (EN SEE FISC NOTE GF EX)
la:HB 211.summary: Lets district courts create Homelessness Court programs with probation conditions, and creates the crime of unauthorized camping on public property, punishable by up to $500, six months in jail, or both. Offenders may qualify for court programs.
