la:HB 226.title: CIVIL/PROCEDURE: Provides relative to requests for admissions
la:HB 226.summary: Replaces the rule that a request for admission is deemed admitted after 30 days without a written answer with a requirement for a Rule 10.1 conference first, except for default judgments.

la:HB 227.title: CIVIL/PROCEDURE: Provides that filings may be made on letter size rather than legal size paper
la:HB 227.summary: Allows court filings, electronic or paper, on letter size or legal size paper, and removes full dates of birth from the personal information barred from civil and criminal court filings.

la:HB 258.title: ETHICS/DUAL OFFICEHOLDG: Provides for exceptions to the dual officeholding laws for volunteer firefighters and judicial branch employees
la:HB 258.summary: As passed by the Senate, adds dual officeholding exceptions for volunteer firefighters, unpaid advisory committee members and judicial branch employees serving on boards, and bars full-time appointed officers and employees from serving on boards not required by law for their duties.

la:HB 291.title: INSURANCE/HEALTH: Prohibits health insurers from taking adverse payment or contracting actions against participating facilities based solely on another provider's network status (EN INCREASE  EX See Note)
la:HB 291.summary: Bars health insurers from reducing payments to, or suspending or ending contracts with, a participating licensed health care facility solely because a nonparticipating provider was involved in a patient's care; the Office of Group Benefits is exempt.

la:HB 3.title: CAPITAL OUTLAY: Provides for the Omnibus Bond Act
la:HB 3.summary: Authorizes a five-year capital improvement program, repealing certain prior bond authorizations, creating new ones, and providing for bond authorization and sale by the State Bond Commission.

la:HB 302.title: TOBACCO/TOBACCO PRODUCTS: Prohibits the sale of vapor products near schools
la:HB 302.summary: Bars the sale or storage of vapor products within 300 feet of a school where a municipal or parish ordinance provides, measured along sidewalks unless the local government chooses straight-line measurement for new permits.

la:HB 312.title: APPROPRIATIONS/SUPPLEML: Makes supplemental appropriations for Fiscal Year 2025-2026
la:HB 312.summary: Makes supplemental appropriations for fiscal year 2025-26, adding about $301.8 million in state general fund money, including $144.3 million from surplus toward the state employees' retirement system's unfunded liability.

la:HB 314.title: REVENUE SHARING: Provides for the Revenue Sharing Distribution for Fiscal Year 2026-2027
la:HB 314.summary: Distributes $90 million in state revenue sharing to parishes in fiscal year 2026-27, with 80% allocated by population and 20% by number of homesteads, paid in three installments.

la:HB 316.title: EDUCATION: Provides relative to student literacy (EN SEE FISC NOTE GF EX)
la:HB 316.summary: Adds adolescent literacy instruction to special and secondary education teacher programs, and requires schools to assess grade 4-8 students who scored below mastery in English, notify parents of reading deficiencies, and provide interventions and reading improvement plans.

la:HB 324.title: JUDGES: Provides relative to judicial salaries (EN +$6,690,757 GF EX See Note)
la:HB 324.summary: Raises salaries of Louisiana Supreme Court, appeals court and district court judges by $10,723 to $12,129 from July 1, 2026, and by 2.7% from July 1, 2027, with the 2026-27 increase paid from judiciary reserves.

la:HB 325.title: TOPS: Provides relative to TOPS-Tech (EN INCREASE GF EX See Note)
la:HB 325.summary: Lets part-time students receive TOPS awards in some cases. For TOPS-Tech, adds a third eligibility criterion of nine early college credit hours, and students qualify by meeting two of three criteria, for 2026-2027 graduates onward.

la:HB 337.title: GAMING: Provides relative to charitable bingo and the issuance of special licenses
la:HB 337.summary: Increases the number of special bingo sessions a licensed charitable organization may hold each year under a special license from two to four.

la:HB 342.title: EDUCATION/SPECIAL: Provides that a local education agency shall have the burden of proof in any special education due process hearing relative to the appropriateness of a student's current or proposed program or placement (EN SEE FISC NOTE LF EX)
la:HB 342.summary: Requires the local education agency to carry the burden of proof, by a preponderance of the evidence, in special education due process hearings on whether a student's program or placement is appropriate.

la:HB 352.title: STUDENTS: Provides relative to behavioral health services for public school students (EN SEE FISC NOTE LF EX)
la:HB 352.summary: Requires school boards to post behavioral health service policies online and in handbooks, requires in-classroom services where medically necessary, sets a service-delivery review meeting within 21 days of a parent's treatment plan, and bars recording other students during virtual supervision.

la:HB 36.title: JUVENILES: Removes Evangeline Parish as a member of the Acadiana Regional Juvenile Justice District
la:HB 36.summary: Adds parish presidents in certain parishes as joint appointing authorities for the Acadiana Regional Juvenile Justice District commission, and requires approval by every board member and each member parish's governing authority before a tax measure goes on the ballot.

la:HB 368.title: DISTRICTS/HISTORIC: Provides relative to historic preservation districts and landmarks commissions in the city of New Orleans
la:HB 368.summary: Raises the maximum fine for demolishing a New Orleans historic structure without approval from the greater of $25,000 or 15% of assessed value to the greater of $50,000 or 15%, and creates a lien on the property for fines.

la:HB 386.title: SCHOOLS/CHARTER: Provides relative to charter school funding (EN NO IMPACT   See Note)
la:HB 386.summary: Lets Type 1, 3 and 3B charter schools, with local school board approval, act as their own local education agency for federal funding, under state board rules letting the state superintendent rescind that authority if obligations are not met.

la:HB 387.title: BUILDING CODES: Provides relative to plans submitted to the fire marshal
la:HB 387.summary: Adds plans submitted in violation of R.S. 37:701(I)(3) to the cases where the state fire marshal need not send a letter listing unmet code requirements.

la:HB 398.title: PUBLIC OFFLS/EMPS: Prohibits payment for meals and incidental expenses for state public officials and employees from exceeding amounts for such expenses established by the U.S. General Services Administration
la:HB 398.summary: Caps reimbursement for meals and incidental expenses of judicial, legislative and executive branch officers and employees at the U.S. General Services Administration daily maximum rates, with an allowance for agency-hosted conferences and working meals.

la:HB 399.title: CRIMINAL/PROCEDURE: Provides relative to temporary release of inmates for limited purposes (EN SEE FISC NOTE GF EX)
la:HB 399.summary: Extends from 60 to 120 days the expected time of death that lets the corrections secretary grant temporary release to an inmate with a terminal illness for palliative or medical care. Takes effect August 1, 2026.

la:HB 401.title: BRIDGES/FERRIES: Designates the elevated portion of United States Highway 190 as the "Lance Corporal Justin D. McLeese Memorial Bridge"
la:HB 401.summary: Names the U.S. Highway 190 bridge over the Bogue Falaya River in Covington the "Lance Corporal Justin D. McLeese Memorial Bridge" and directs signage once local or private funds cover costs of up to $2,250 per sign.

la:HB 403.title: SMALL BUSINESS: Provides for the production of homemade food for sale to the public
la:HB 403.summary: Raises from $30,000 to $100,000 the yearly sales limit for producers of low-risk homemade foods who are exempt from food safety and sanitary requirements.

la:HB 410.title: CIVIL/PROCEDURE: Requires notification of all parties to record in-person communication
la:HB 410.summary: Bars using wearable video-recording eyeglasses to record or transcribe a conversation unless all participants are notified. Exempts public meetings, law enforcement and emergencies, recording evidence for legal proceedings, and recordings made by a participant in their own home or business.

la:HB 414.title: HEALTH: Provides for prohibitions on hiring individuals with certain criminal convictions
la:HB 414.summary: Requires background checks on anyone owning or managing a therapeutic group home, removes licensed ambulance personnel from hiring bans for criminal offenses, and lets hospitals run criminal history checks through accredited consumer reporting agencies.

la:HB 42.title: RETIREMENT/TEACHERS: Provides relative to a phased retirement program within the Teachers' Retirement System of Louisiana (EN INCREASE FC GF EX See Note)
la:HB 42.summary: Creates a phased retirement program in the Teachers' Retirement System that public postsecondary boards may adopt: employees work at least half time for 12-36 months at a reduced benefit with no contributions, then receive the full benefit.

la:HB 420.title: CHILDREN/DCFS: Requires the Department of Children and Family Services to obtain background checks on all employees (EN INCREASE GF EX See Note)
la:HB 420.summary: Requires the Department of Children and Family Services to run criminal background checks and state central registry searches on all current and prospective employees, not only those in child-facing roles, and extends the termination rule for registry matches.

la:HB 429.title: CRIME/THEFT: Adds theft or unauthorized entry of a critical infrastructure as a predicate crime for terrorism (EN SEE FISC NOTE GF EX)
la:HB 429.summary: Adds unauthorized entry and theft of critical infrastructure to crimes that count as terrorism when done to intimidate or coerce, with five to 20 years at hard labor, and adds oil and natural gas drilling operations and public drinking water systems to critical infrastructure.

la:HB 431.title: MUNICIPAL: Requires certain training for certain local officials (EN NO IMPACT   See Note)
la:HB 431.summary: Requires all mayors to earn at least 16 hours of training credit each year starting Jan. 1, 2027, directs the Louisiana Municipal Association to offer courses in at least 14 governance categories, and requires mayors to attest compliance.

la:HB 441.title: SEWERAGE/N O WATER BD: Provides relative to employees of the New Orleans Sewerage and Water Board
la:HB 441.summary: Repeals the 2024 requirement that the state and New Orleans civil service commissions plan the transfer of Sewerage and Water Board employees into the state civil service system.

la:HB 457.title: HOMELESS: Establishes minimum housing standards for individuals experiencing homelessness (EN SEE FISC NOTE GF EX See Note)
la:HB 457.summary: Allows the Department of Health, consulting the fire marshal, to set minimum safety, sanitation, privacy and habitability standards for emergency shelters, unlicensed group homes and halfway houses receiving public funds, and authorizes annual fire marshal inspections.

la:HB 459.title: ELECTIONS/CANDIDATES: Provides relative to the use of artificial intelligence in political campaigns
la:HB 459.summary: Bars electioneering communications that use AI to portray a candidate or recall-subject official in a falsely authentic way unless labeled as AI-created. Penalties apply only with intent to injure reputation or deceive voters; exempts broadcasters with no control over content.

la:HB 463.title: DISTRICTS/COMMUNICATIONS: Provides relative to emergency communications service charges
la:HB 463.summary: Raises the maximum monthly wireless emergency telephone service charge a communications district may levy from $1.25 to $2 per connection, and requires a board vote and public hearing before Terrebonne Parish's district exceeds $1.25.

la:HB 468.title: REAL ESTATE: Provides with respect to the wholesale of residential real properties
la:HB 468.summary: Regulates wholesaling of residential real estate: requires written disclosures, a deposit of at least 1 percent of the price held in escrow, and a seller cancellation right for a set period; violations face civil penalties up to $5,000 each.

la:HB 481.title: PUBLIC PRINTING: Provides for the cost of publishing official proceedings and public notices
la:HB 481.summary: Sets the maximum contract rate parishes, municipalities and school boards pay to publish proceedings and notices at three cents per character, up from 1.5 or 2 cents, and caps costs at the lesser of that or the rate in effect January 1, 2026.

la:HB 487.title: MTR VEHICLE/VIOLATIONS: Provides relative to running red lights (EN SEE FISC NOTE LF RV)
la:HB 487.summary: Adds a $250 penalty for passing vehicles using the shoulder or turning lane at a red light without injury, and bars booting vehicles over unpaid red-light camera tickets before an administrative hearing, except in Orleans Parish.

la:HB 511.title: HIGHWAYS/OFFICE: Authorizes the Louisiana Commission on Law Enforcement and the Administration of Criminal Justice to establish a grant program for pursuit intervention technologies (EN NO IMPACT   See Note)
la:HB 511.summary: Creates a grant program to fund law enforcement agencies' purchase and training of technology to safely end high-speed pursuits, such as GPS tracking projectiles, vehicle-stopping nets and remote-controlled tire deflation devices.

la:HB 513.title: ATHLETICS: Provides relative to the name, image, and likeness of intercollegiate and interscholastic athletes (EN NO IMPACT GF EX See Note)
la:HB 513.summary: Extends name, image and likeness compensation rules to high school athletes, with parental consent for those under 18, and revises required college and university NIL policies on compensation, representation and compliance.

la:HB 538.title: COURTS/JUVENILE: Provides relative to the judicial expense fund for the Juvenile Court for the parish of East Baton Rouge
la:HB 538.summary: Raises the maximum additional civil filing fee for the East Baton Rouge Juvenile Court judicial expense fund from $15 to $45 and gives the judges sitting together, rather than the chief judge, control of the fee and fund.

la:HB 549.title: WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT: Creates the Bayou Growth Opportunity Workforce Program (EN SEE FISC NOTE GF RV See Note)
la:HB 549.summary: Creates the Bayou Growth Opportunity Program and a special fund to give competitive awards to qualified employers for worker training, run by Louisiana Works with workforce development boards.

la:HB 552.title: DWI: Provides relative to driving while intoxicated (EN NO IMPACT   See Note)
la:HB 552.summary: Changes the responsive verdicts for vehicular negligent injuring and first degree vehicular negligent injuring from guilty of operating a vehicle while intoxicated to guilty of operating a vehicle while intoxicated or impaired.

la:HB 559.title: COURTS/COURT COSTS: Increases court costs for the Fourth Judicial District (EN +$313,179 LF RV See Note)
la:HB 559.summary: Raises the maximum court cost collected for the Fourth Judicial District's judicial expense fund from $15 to $35 in civil filings and criminal convictions, effective August 1, 2026.

la:HB 571.title: COURTS/COURT COSTS: Provides relative to creating the Complex Litigation Section Program in the Nineteenth Judicial District Court (EN NO IMPACT   See Note)
la:HB 571.summary: Extends the 19th Judicial District Court's Complex Litigation Section Pilot Program, which allows added filing fees in complex cases, until July 31, 2028.

la:HB 590.title: TRAFFIC/VIOLATIONS: Provides with respect to training law enforcement officers regarding certain traffic stops
la:HB 590.summary: Allows the Office of Motor Vehicles to create envelopes for drivers with mental, physical or developmental disabilities or autism to provide proof of disability, which may include guidelines helping officers communicate with them during traffic stops.

la:HB 591.title: INSURANCE: Creates the Paid Family Leave Insurance Act
la:HB 591.summary: Creates the Paid Family Leave Insurance Act, letting life and disability insurers offer optional paid family leave coverage, as a policy or rider, with benefits lasting at least two weeks in a 52-week period.

la:HB 593.title: MTR VEHICLE/OFFICE: Increases the maximum service and transaction fee a governing authority may assess to fund an office of motor vehicles field office not fully funded by the state (EN +$1,540,000 LF RV See Note)
la:HB 593.summary: Raises the maximum local fee per transaction at Office of Motor Vehicles field offices to $8 statewide, up from $4.50 and higher caps in a few places, with Shreveport field offices exempt. Takes effect August 1, 2026.

la:HB 608.title: ATHLETICS: Provides relative to the confidentiality of documents related to an intercollegiate athletics revenue sharing program
la:HB 608.summary: Makes the total revenue a college spends on athlete revenue sharing public, but keeps confidential each athlete's payment, each sport's allocation, and negotiation records. Applies to past and pending records requests.

la:HB 616.title: MENTAL HEALTH: Provides for oversight of publicly funded homeless service providers
la:HB 616.summary: Allows the legislative auditor to review publicly funded homeless service providers, requires providers to submit to audits on request of funders, and requires suspending or ending public funding for providers that do not comply.

la:HB 624.title: SCHOOLS: Provides relative to emergency operations plans at public schools
la:HB 624.summary: Renames school crisis plans "emergency operations plans," requires schools and districts to submit safety questionnaires to the state, and requires classrooms occupied by students to be locked and secured except between class periods.

la:HB 638.title: CONTRACTORS: Provides relative to payments to contractors and subcontractors
la:HB 638.summary: Requires owners to pay contractors within 35 days of a written payment request, with a late penalty of 1.5% of the amount due per day, and raises the daily late-payment penalty owed to subcontractors and suppliers from 0.5% to 1.5%.

la:HB 682.title: VETERANS: Provides for certain veterans to work as school guardians at public schools
la:HB 682.summary: Lets schools or law enforcement agencies engage honorably discharged veterans with background checks and school incident training as school guardians, who may temporarily detain people reasonably believed to have committed or be about to commit a felony, but are not peace officers unless separately commissioned.

la:HB 688.title: FISHING: Adds Atlantic tarpon to the definition of saltwater game fish
la:HB 688.summary: Adds Atlantic tarpon to the definition of saltwater game fish and updates the names of listed saltwater game fish.

la:HB 690.title: EDUCATION: Provides relative to education service providers and vendors of educational products (EN NO IMPACT   See Note)
la:HB 690.summary: Amends the bill to let a vendor or service provider tied to a foreign adversary or foreign terrorist organization cure the violation by divesting, removing such agents or ending support, and to let charter school boards fix or replace affected management companies.

la:HB 707.title: PETROLEUM/OIL-GAS: Provides relative to the Liquefied Petroleum Gas Commission
la:HB 707.summary: Lets the Liquefied Petroleum Gas Commission contract with the Department of Agriculture and Forestry for market promotion funded by its assessment, and changes advisory board appointments, permit-class representation, and meeting and quorum rules.

la:HB 708.title: COURTS/JUSTICE OF PEACE: Authorizes concurrent jurisdiction for justice of the peace and city courts in East Baton Rouge Parish
la:HB 708.summary: Gives East Baton Rouge Parish justices of the peace concurrent jurisdiction with city courts over evictions from residential, commercial or farm leases with monthly rent of $5,000 or less, and redraws the six justice of the peace and constable districts.

la:HB 718.title: LIABILITY/CIVIL: Provides a limitation of liability to a landowner who authorizes the free use of his private property for aeronautical activities at nonpublic use airports
la:HB 718.summary: Shields owners of nonpublic-use airports from liability for loss or damage tied to an aircraft's emergency landing on their property, except for willful or malicious failure to warn of a danger.

la:HB 719.title: DISTRICT ATTORNEYS/ASST: Provides relative to the number of assistant district attorneys in each judicial district (EN +$3,411,000 GF EX See Note)
la:HB 719.summary: Raises the number of assistant district attorneys in 30 judicial districts, for example from 55 to 71 in the 19th, and cuts Orleans Parish from 83 to 73. Increases take effect only when funded, and some also need a state commission's recommendation.

la:HB 723.title: MTR VEHICLE/MOTORCYCLES: Authorizes drivers of certain two-wheeled vehicles to proceed through a red light under certain circumstances
la:HB 723.summary: Lets drivers of motorcycles, mopeds and bicycles proceed through a red light at a vehicle-actuated signal after stopping for two full cycles or two minutes, treating it as a stop sign, and yielding to pedestrians and cross traffic.

la:HB 730.title: AIRCRAFT/AVIATION: Provides relative to the use of automatic dependent surveillance-broadcast systems (EN SEE FISC NOTE LF RV)
la:HB 730.summary: Bars using aircraft tracking data from ADS-B systems as a basis for charging fees or taxes to owners of aircraft of 12,499 pounds or less operating in the state.

la:HB 732.title: MTR VEHICLE/OFFICE: Provides for a temporary waiver of fees for final delinquent debt based on special circumstances (EN DECREASE SG RV See Note)
la:HB 732.summary: Lets the motor vehicles commissioner pause fines, fees and license suspensions for up to 30 days so a person can get life-sustaining medicine or treatment. Suspends the road usage fee on non-plug-in hybrids until August 1, 2027.

la:HB 748.title: HIGHWAYS: Provides that any Louisiana school board-owned vehicles be exempt from paying tolls on any bridges and highways in the state (EN DECREASE GF RV See Note)
la:HB 748.summary: Gives school board-owned or leased vehicles free passage over state-operated tolled ferries, bridges and roads, with the Greater New Orleans Expressway excluded.

la:HB 75.title: GAMING: Creates an enhanced promotional play pilot program relative to net slot machine proceeds (EN -$574,627 GF RV See Note)
la:HB 75.summary: Creates a pilot program, July 2026 through June 2027, raising the promotional play wagers racing-facility slot licensees may offer from $5 million to $7 million. Requires licensees to report the effect on proceeds, fees and taxes by March 1, 2027.

la:HB 750.title: CONSUMERS/PROTECTION: Provides for cancellation of automatic renewal subscriptions
la:HB 750.summary: As passed by the House, requires businesses offering automatic-renewal contracts to disclose terms and cancellation instructions clearly before charging, keep consent records for a year, and provide an easy cancellation method. Allows 30 days to cure violations and requires notice before certain renewals.

la:HB 755.title: PUBLIC CONTRACTS: Establishes indefinite delivery and indefinite quantity professional services contracting for design services for certain projects (EN NO IMPACT   See Note)
la:HB 755.summary: Sets selection rules for state indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity design contracts: the Division of Administration refers agency requests to a selection board, contracts exclude new buildings, last up to two years with a $1 million maximum fee, and agencies must keep two in effect.

la:HB 761.title: HEALTH/CANCER: Provides with respect to the advisory board created to recommend new treatments for rare cancers (EN NO IMPACT   See Note)
la:HB 761.summary: Expands the rare cancer treatment advisory board from 15 to 17 members, raises the number of rare-cancer oncologists on it from two to four, and extends the report deadline after each meeting from 30 to 45 days.

la:HB 762.title: MTR VEHICLE/OFFICE: Prohibits the Office of Motor Vehicles from referring certain cases to the Office of Debt Recovery
la:HB 762.summary: Bars the Office of Motor Vehicles from sending debt from unpaid reinstatement fees tied to lapsed or missing insurance to the state debt recovery office, while allowing it to refer such debts to the attorney general.

la:HB 769.title: DOMESTIC ABUSE: Provides relative to the removal authority process with respect to domestic offenders
la:HB 769.summary: As passed by the House, lets a court hold a person charged with domestic abuse battery, protective order violations, stalking or force offenses against a family member without bail for 48 to 72 hours. The hold runs within the existing 72-hour limit for first appearance.

la:HB 775.title: HEALTH/CHILDREN: Provides relative to minor's consent for medical procedures and treatments
la:HB 775.summary: Requires consent from a parent, guardian or temporary caregiver before health care providers treat a person under the age of majority, replacing prior law letting minors consent. Lists exceptions, including military service, emancipation, pregnancy care, substance misuse treatment and sexually transmitted disease treatment.

la:HB 783.title: HEALTH/LDH: Provides relative to the regulation of food and food safety
la:HB 783.summary: Requires products made from dairy-identical proteins produced by microbial fermentation to carry a label saying so in at least 30-point type, and bars their sale if House Bill 512 of 2026 takes effect.

la:HB 784.title: SEX OFFENSE/REGISTRY: Provides relative to sex offender registration and notification requirements
la:HB 784.summary: Adds unlawful sexual deepfakes of minors to offenses requiring sex offender registration, sets three business days to register after release from confinement, and replaces the restriction code on registrants' driver's licenses with a QR code.

la:HB 789.title: CRIMINAL/PROCEDURE: Provides with respect to the seizure of off-road vehicles (EN SEE FISC NOTE LF EX)
la:HB 789.summary: Limits reckless off-road vehicle offenses to public roads in municipalities or incorporated areas, lets law enforcement seize vehicles on probable cause with a warrant sought in 72 hours, and sets a forfeiture process requiring notice to the district attorney within 10 days.

la:HB 796.title: CHIROPRACTORS: Provides relative to the Louisiana Board of Chiropractic Examiners
la:HB 796.summary: Allows chiropractors licensed five years with a clean three-year record to delegate adjustments to chiropractic college students (preceptees) with the preceptor onsite; bars delegating diagnosis or treatment plans; requires both to register with the board and notify patients.

la:HB 797.title: BANKS/BANKING: Creates the Bayou Gold Program (EN INCREASE SG EX See Note)
la:HB 797.summary: Creates the Bayou Gold Program, a voluntary Treasury certification for electronic payment platforms offering gold- and silver-backed transactions, with two-year certifications and a public registry of certified platforms.

la:HB 799.title: FIRE PROTECT/FIRE MARSHAL: Provides relative to boilers (EN INCREASE SG RV See Note)
la:HB 799.summary: Repeals the State Board of Boiler Examiners and has the state fire marshal license boiler inspectors and installers, issue $150 operating certificates, and fine owners up to $250 a day for ignoring a warning; inspectors can order unsafe boilers shut down.

la:HB 804.title: ENERGY: Creates the Louisiana Energy Protection Act (EN NO IMPACT   See Note)
la:HB 804.summary: Bars lawsuits in Louisiana courts seeking damages for climate change from greenhouse gas emissions, except claims over violations of emission laws, permit terms or certain federal workplace safety standards.

la:HB 807.title: FUNDS/FUNDING: Establishes the Workforce Instructor Capacity Investment Program to enhance workforce training programs to meet employer demand in certain industry sectors (EN INCREASE SD EX See Note)
la:HB 807.summary: Creates the Workforce Instructor Capacity Investment Program and a state fund to help two-year colleges expand instructor capacity in high-demand fields, including shared instructor arrangements with private employers.

la:HB 812.title: ASSESSORS: Authorizes limited increases in annual compensation for assessors in each parish (EN +$847,031 LF EX See Note)
la:HB 812.summary: Raises the top population bracket for the middle tier of parish assessor pay to 250,000 and adds 5% annual pay increases through 2029 if the assessor first publishes notice, except for assessors who violate an aircraft exemption.

la:HB 821.title: LAW ENFORCEMENT: Provides for the establishment of the Louisiana Center for Safe Schools within the Louisiana Commission on Law Enforcement and Administration of Criminal Justice (EN +$250,000 GF EX See Note)
la:HB 821.summary: Moves the Louisiana Center for Safe Schools from the Governor's homeland security office to the Commission on Law Enforcement and Administration of Criminal Justice, with duties including school safety training, threat assessment systems and emergency planning help.

la:HB 823.title: COURTS: Establishes a homeless diversion pilot program in Orleans Parish (EN SEE FISC NOTE LF EX See Note)
la:HB 823.summary: Creates a Homeless Diversion Pilot Program in Orleans Parish, under which the district attorney dismisses proceedings against participants who complete program terms, with annual evaluations sent to the Louisiana Supreme Court.

la:HB 848.title: MTR VEHICLE/DEALERS: Provides with respect to all terrain vehicle dealerships
la:HB 848.summary: As passed by the House, adds golf carts to the all-terrain vehicle dealer law, covers any retailer selling them, and requires those dealers to have repair facilities and parts, on-site or within 1,000 feet, via a third-party repair agreement, or through a manufacturer-authorized provider.

la:HB 850.title: INSURANCE: Provides relative to cancellation notice requirements in the Standard Fire Policy
la:HB 850.summary: Lengthens the cancellation notice for standard fire insurance policies from 30 to 60 days for the insured and mortgagee, keeps 10 days for nonpayment, and requires insurers to give cancellation reasons on written request.

la:HB 864.title: HIGHWAYS: Authorizes municipalities to establish fire limits and to prohibit the storage, placement, accumulation, abandonment, or use of certain materials within the right-of-way of certain public structures
la:HB 864.summary: As passed by the House, lets municipalities set fire limits and bar storing, placing or using flammable, explosive or combustible material in the right-of-way of public bridges, overpasses and tunnels. Penalty is up to $1,000, six months in jail, or both; permitted events and regulated utilities are excepted.

la:HB 870.title: INSURANCE/HEALTH: Provides relative to formulary placement and cost-sharing requirements for certain generic drugs and biosimilars (EN NO IMPACT   See Note)
la:HB 870.summary: Requires health insurers covering a reference drug to list a newly marketed lower-priced generic or biosimilar on the formulary at a more favorable cost-sharing tier without added prior authorization or step therapy; insurers using net cost instead must notify the insurance commissioner.

la:HB 874.title: TRANSPORTATION DEPT: Provides with respect to electronic credentials (EN SEE FISC NOTE GF EX)
la:HB 874.summary: Lets the commissioner of administration work with bar, athletic, university and motor vehicle agencies to add more credentials to digital wallets, and reinstates 250 yearly transactions, rather than 25, as the threshold for lenders to designate a public tag agent.

la:HB 895.title: HEALTH/MEDICAL TREATMENT: Provides relative to the treatment of sexual assault survivors by hospitals and healthcare providers (EN NO IMPACT   See Note)
la:HB 895.summary: Changes the law on care for sexual assault survivors so HIV and STI post-exposure prophylaxis given during the forensic medical exam is administered according to the Drug Information Handbook; emergency contraception remains available.

la:HB 908.title: SECRETARY OF STATE: Provides with respect to certain fees charged  by the secretary of state (EN +$3,790,515 SG RV See Note)
la:HB 908.summary: Raises many Secretary of State business filing fees, such as corporation filings from $75 to $95 and LLC filings from $100 to $125, with other filing and certificate fees rising $5 to $35, effective Oct. 1, 2026.

la:HB 909.title: INSURANCE: Required coverage for behavioral health crisis services (EN INCREASE  EX See Note)
la:HB 909.summary: Requires health insurers to cover mobile crisis response and behavioral health crisis care by licensed providers, bars prior authorization for them, and lets insurers require documentation of the crisis, medical necessity and a follow-up plan.

la:HB 933.title: RECORDS/RECORDATION: Provides for commemorative birth certificates (EN +$125,000 SG RV See Note)
la:HB 933.summary: Creates commemorative birth certificates bearing the state seal and the governor's signature, with the same evidentiary status as a certified copy, and sets fees divided between the state registrar and the office on women's health.

la:HB 940.title: CRIME: Provides relative to the unlawful use of an unmanned aircraft system (EN SEE FISC NOTE GF EX)
la:HB 940.summary: Allows law enforcement to take reasonable mitigation measures against drones suspected of illegal or threatening conduct, and creates a Counter-Unmanned Aircraft Systems Joint Task Force under the state police.

la:HB 949.title: HEALTH CARE/PROVIDERS: Provides relative to the Louisiana State Radiologic Technology Board of Examiners (EN INCREASE SG RV See Note)
la:HB 949.summary: Expands the Radiologic Technology Board's licensing role to cover nuclear medicine, radiation therapy and fusion technologists, radiologist assistants and limited purpose permit holders, adding definitions and permit requirements.

la:HB 950.title: CONSUMERS/PROTECTION: Provides for consumer protection for the elderly (EN SEE FISC NOTE GF EX See Note)
la:HB 950.summary: Allows the Office of Elderly Affairs to create a Pension Protection and Retirement Income Support and Guidance program that provides educational materials for seniors on retirement accounts, financial products, and warning signs of financial exploitation.

la:HB 951.title: LABOR: Creates the office of business workforce solutions within Louisiana Works (EN INCREASE GF EX See Note)
la:HB 951.summary: As passed by the House, creates the Office of the Louisiana Talent Accelerator within Louisiana Works, adds Workforce Investment Council duties, and creates a Business Workforce Committee, mostly business representatives, to advise the office. Exempts the office from the state procurement code.

la:HB 953.title: PLUMBERS: Provides relative to plumbing licenses
la:HB 953.summary: Abolishes the State Plumbing Board and moves plumber and gas fitter licensing to a new Plumbing Contractors Subcommittee of the State Licensing Board for Contractors, adding two board members from plumbing industry groups.

la:HB 956.title: FIRE PROTECT/FIRE MARSHAL: Provides relative to fireworks
la:HB 956.summary: Changes fireworks rules: limits retail sales to 1.4G-class fireworks, starts sale hours at 7 a.m., adds Memorial Day and Labor Day sale windows, repeals Class C public displays, and raises pyrotechnic operator license fees to $200 new and $100 renewal.

la:HB 968.title: CRIMINAL/JUSTICE: Provides relative to electronic monitoring and associated costs (EN SEE FISC NOTE LF EX)
la:HB 968.summary: Requires adults on electronic monitoring to give the monitoring provider a payment method, and sets notice, hearing and device-removal procedures when a monitored person fails to pay supervision fees.

la:HB 971.title: MEDICAID: Provides relative to Medicaid reimbursement for rural health clinics (EN +$2,655,159 GF EX See Note)
la:HB 971.summary: As passed by the House, requires the Department of Health to equalize Medicaid reimbursement rates between independent and provider-based rural health clinics within 90 days, by state plan amendment or rules. Takes effect only if the legislature appropriates funds.

la:HB 975.title: SUNSET LAW: Re-creates the Department of Public Service
la:HB 975.summary: Re-creates the Department of Public Service and its statutory entities, effective June 30, 2026, and sets a new termination date of July 1, 2031 unless re-created again.

la:HB 979.title: LAW ENFORCE/OFFICERS: Increases the benefit paid to survivors of law enforcement officers and firemen (EN +$800,000 GF EX See Note)
la:HB 979.summary: Raises the state-paid survivor benefit for qualifying deaths of firefighters and law enforcement officers from $250,000 to $300,000, applying to deaths on or after July 1, 2025.

la:HB 983.title: APPROPRIATIONS: Appropriates funds for the expenses of the judiciary for Fiscal Year 2026-2027
la:HB 983.summary: Appropriates $233.3 million for the judicial branch's operating expenses in fiscal year 2026-27, including $206.1 million from the state general fund, with funding for judicial pay increases and the criminal justice information system.

la:HB 989.title: MOTOR VEHICLES: Modifies charges collected by public license tag agents
la:HB 989.summary: Raises the maximum convenience charge and the registration reinstatement fee that public license tag agents may collect from $23 to $27.

la:HB 999.title: MTR VEHICLE/COMPULS INS: Permits the impoundment of out-of-state vehicles not covered by compulsory liability insurance
la:HB 999.summary: Clarifies that proof-of-insurance enforcement, plate confiscation and impoundment apply to out-of-state vehicles operated in Louisiana, and allows first-class mail for notices of noncompliance, with copies to towing companies and the Office of Motor Vehicles within three days.

la:SB 163.title: COMMERCIAL REGULATIONS: Provides relative to the licensing and regulation of virtual currency businesses. (8/1/26)
la:SB 163.summary: Repeals the termination dates in the Virtual Currency Business Act, and voids state authorization of virtual currency activities to the extent conflicting with a federal licensing law once it takes effect.

la:SB 237.title: CHILDREN: Provides relative to child welfare. (8/1/26) (EN NO IMPACT   See Note)
la:SB 237.summary: Changes child welfare notification and oversight: requires notice of child abuse deaths to legislative leaders and committee chairs, requires reporting of deaths and near-fatalities to the child ombudsman, and gives the ombudsman remote access to state child-services systems.

la:SB 25.title: REGISTRARS OF VOTERS: Adjusts compensation schedule for Registrar of Voters. (7/1/26) (EN +$496,168 GF EX See Note)
la:SB 25.summary: Revises the pay schedule for parish registrars of voters and their staff, with fewer population levels and higher pay at each step, and changes the boundaries of Senate Districts 33, 34 and 35.

la:SB 268.title: LOCAL FINANCE: Provides for lead service line replacement. (8/1/26)
la:SB 268.summary: Lets municipalities adopt ordinances allowing city water systems to enter private property to replace lead service lines after at least seven days' notice, except in emergencies. Entry is limited to the replacement work.

la:SB 274.title: ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY: Provides for lead hazard risk assessments for certain child care facilities and prekindergarten programs. (8/1/26) (EN INCREASE SG EX See Note)
la:SB 274.summary: Requires a risk assessor, rather than an inspector, to check early learning, daycare and prekindergarten facilities first operating on or after August 1, 2026 for lead hazards, with results submitted with license applications and no opening until any hazards are controlled.

la:SB 283.title: SPECIAL DISTRICTS: Creates the BLVD at Harding Area Special District in the city of Baton Rouge. (gov sig)
la:SB 283.summary: Creates two special districts in Baton Rouge, the BLVD at Harding Area district and a Baton Rouge Community College economic development district, each run by a board with power to issue bonds. Extends tax increment financing authority to the Harding district.

la:SB 348.title: MOTOR VEHICLES: Provides for third party service providers and enforcement of motor vehicle liability security. (8/1/26)
la:SB 348.summary: Allows local law enforcement in municipalities incorporated after Oct. 1, 2019 to contract with private providers for plate processing and notices once an officer starts a vehicle enforcement action, and lets a motorist voluntarily surrender a plate; ends July 31, 2028.

la:SB 384.title: TECHNOLOGY: Authorizes creation of the Pilot Innovation Hub. (8/1/26) (EN SEE FISC NOTE LF EX See Note)
la:SB 384.summary: Lets parishes designate themselves Pilot Innovation Hubs, where local governments may contract with a pilot innovation contractor to test new technologies, using public property and aligned permitting and zoning.

la:SB 387.title: HEALTH/ACC INSURANCE: Provides relative to pharmacy benefit managers. (1/1/27) (EN INCREASE SG EX See Note)
la:SB 387.summary: Regulates pharmacy benefit managers: limits their pay to flat fees, bars keeping rebates and spread pricing, and allows annual audits. Sets a $25,000 civil penalty per violation, with license suspension or revocation if not corrected within 30 days.

la:SB 389.title: AMUSEMENTS/SPORTS: Provides for agents and athletes. (gov sig) (EN +$62,400 GF EX See Note)
la:SB 389.summary: Expands athlete agent registration to cover agents for college and high school athletes and those handling name, image and likeness deals, with two-year registration, background checks and required disclosures.

la:SB 405.title: NURSING HOMES: Provides for a statewide quality oversight initiative for nursing facilities. (8/1/26) (EN  GF EX See Note)
la:SB 405.summary: Requires the Department of Health to develop a statewide quality oversight initiative for nursing facilities with stakeholders, and to report to legislative health committees starting January 1, 2028.

la:SB 406.title: TAX/LOCAL: Authorizes the city of Slidell to levy a hotel occupancy tax. (gov sig) (EN +$590,000 LF RV See Note)
la:SB 406.summary: Lets the city of Slidell, with voter approval, levy a hotel occupancy tax of up to 2% of room charges, with proceeds funding recreational facilities or tourism initiatives named in the tax proposition.

la:SB 414.title: CONSUMERS: Provides for the Louisiana Medical Debt Protection Act. (gov sig)
la:SB 414.summary: Creates the Louisiana Medical Debt Protection Act, capping interest on medical debt from medically necessary care at 3% a year, voiding higher contract rates, and letting the attorney general seek civil penalties.

la:SB 42.title: CRIME/PUNISHMENT: Prohibits using artificial intelligence to create child sexual abuse materials. (8/1/26)
la:SB 42.summary: Expands the definition of child sexual abuse materials to include computer or AI-generated images virtually indistinguishable from a child under 17, and includes causing artificial intelligence to generate such materials in the definition of producing.

la:SB 43.title: HEALTH SERVICES: Provides relative to psychedelic-assisted therapy. (8/1/26) (EN INCREASE GF EX See Note)
la:SB 43.summary: Creates a Psychedelic-Assisted Therapy Initiative in the Department of Health to connect eligible patients with academic health center clinical trials, and lets those centers form consortia with drug developers for ibogaine trials.

la:SB 433.title: MEDICAID: Provides for Medicaid coverage of certain medications. (1/1/27) (EN +$3,000,000 GF EX See Note)
la:SB 433.summary: Requires Medicaid to cover medically necessary, FDA-approved weight loss medications for recipients who meet Department of Health criteria. Allows prior authorization, bars step therapy, and takes effect upon legislative appropriation.

la:SB 444.title: EXPROPRIATION: Provides relative to expropriation by the city of St. George. (gov sig)
la:SB 444.summary: Lets the city of St. George take property by expropriation for public projects such as streets, drainage, utilities and flood protection, using the same procedures as the Department of Transportation and Development, including taking before judgment.

la:SB 449.title: PUBLIC CONTRACTS: Provides for the procurement of materials and goods. (8/1/26)
la:SB 449.summary: Exempts political subdivisions that own or operate a railroad from public bid requirements when buying used locomotives, rolling stock, track maintenance equipment and their parts. Takes effect August 1, 2026.

la:SB 450.title: SCHOOLS: Requires mandatory reporting of school threats and provides for physical security school assessments for K-12 schools.  (8/1/26) (EN SEE FISC NOTE GF EX)
la:SB 450.summary: Requires local law enforcement to report school threats of violence or terrorism to the state fusion center within seven days, and lets public and nonpublic schools request state physical security assessments, which are confidential and carry liability immunity.

la:SB 469.title: UTILITIES: Provides relative to the Louisiana Underground Utilities and Facilities Damage Prevention Law. (8/1/26)
la:SB 469.summary: Changes underground utility damage-prevention rules: adds 30-day notice and a good-faith coordination agreement for BEAD-funded broadband projects, requires signage at broadband excavations in public rights-of-way, and requires operators to give a positive response before marking deadlines.

la:SB 479.title: JUDGES: Provides for legislative address to the governor for the removal of certain judges for malfeasance, gross misconduct, or incompetence committed while in office. (See Act)
la:SB 479.summary: Sets procedures for impeachment investigations: defines "gross misconduct" and, on a three-fifths request of both chambers, creates a joint committee with subpoena power to examine sworn citizen complaints. Authorizes the House to impeach by majority vote.

la:SB 480.title: FISH/FISHING: Provides for anchorage in certain waterways with fishing gear restriction. (8/1/26)
la:SB 480.summary: Allows boats fishing with nets in Oyster Bayou to anchor, if they are not in an oyster lease and at least one person stays aboard.

la:SB 485.title: TAX/LOCAL: Provides for the levy of premium tax in the city of St. George. (7/1/26)
la:SB 485.summary: Gives the city of St. George exclusive authority, starting Jan. 1, 2027, to levy insurance premium taxes on risks within its limits, bars Baton Rouge and East Baton Rouge Parish from collecting them there, and prohibits duplicate taxation.

la:SB 487.title: CHARITABLE GAMING: Provides for the Charitable Raffles, Bingo and Keno Licensing Law. (8/1/26)
la:SB 487.summary: Requires charitable gaming premises and equipment leases to be written and mutually agreed, bars rentals for sessions under two hours, and repeals the ban on combining financial interests among game operators, manufacturers, distributors and premises lessors.

la:SB 513.title: PUBLIC CONTRACTS: Provides for public works project delivery methods. (8/1/26)
la:SB 513.summary: Lets public airports use design-build contracting for vertical facilities such as workforce training buildings, control towers, parking garages and hangars, excluding commercial airport passenger terminals and equipment. Takes effect August 1, 2026.

md:HB 107.title: Motor Vehicles - Intelligent Speed Assistance System Pilot Program - Establishment
md:HB 107.summary: Requires the Motor Vehicle Administration to start a pilot program by October 1, 2027, requiring drivers with enough points for license suspension or revocation to use a vehicle device that prevents exceeding the speed limit.

md:HB 1075.title: Higher Education - Maryland Graduate and Professional Scholarship Program - Eligible Institutions
md:HB 1075.summary: Expands eligibility for the Maryland Graduate and Professional Scholarship Program to include certain students attending the University of Maryland Eastern Shore.

md:HB 1087.title: Health Care Facilities - Surgical Smoke - Smoke Evacuation Systems
md:HB 1087.summary: Requires health care facilities that perform surgery to adopt and carry out, by January 1, 2028, policies requiring a smoke evacuation system during procedures that may generate surgical smoke.

md:HB 1091.title: Health Insurance and Dental Plan Organizations - Dentists - Assignment of Benefits and Reimbursement of Nonpreferred Providers
md:HB 1091.summary: Bars insurers and dental plans from blocking assignment of benefits to dentists or refusing to pay out-of-network dentists directly under an assignment. Those dentists must give cost disclosures first and submit a form; insurers may refuse in listed cases.

md:HB 1101.title: Worcester County - Alcoholic Beverages - Temporary To-Go Event Permit and Class C Per Diem Municipal To-Go Beer, Wine, and Liquor License
md:HB 1101.summary: Creates, in Worcester County, a Class C per diem municipal to-go beer, wine and liquor license for Pocomoke City, Berlin and Snow Hill, and a temporary to-go event permit, letting drinks be carried within a special event area for up to seven days.

md:HB 1110.title: Judicial In Rem Tax Foreclosure - Notice Requirements
md:HB 1110.summary: Replaces the requirement to mail notice and a copy of an in rem tax foreclosure complaint to interested parties within 5 days with service of the complaint under the Maryland Rules.

md:HB 1118.title: Health, Health Insurance, and Health Occupations - Perinatal Behavioral Health Conditions
md:HB 1118.summary: Requires Medicaid and insurers, from January 1, 2027, to cover screening for perinatal behavioral health conditions such as postpartum depression. Requires providers to screen at well visits in a child's first year and the health department to identify screening tools.

md:HB 1137.title: Residential-in-Commercial-Zone Laws - Study (Bring Back Main Street Act)
md:HB 1137.summary: Requires the Department of Housing and Community Development to study laws requiring local governments to allow residential or mixed-use development on commercially zoned lots, and report by December 1, 2026.

md:HB 1151.title: Maryland Department of Health - Study on Maryland Medical Assistance Program Reimbursement of Hospice Room and Board Services
md:HB 1151.summary: Requires the Health Care Commission and Medicaid to study the effects of Medicaid paying for hospice house room and board, including costs, savings and hospital use, with a report to legislative committees by December 1, 2026.

md:HB 1203.title: Garrett County - Alcoholic Beverages Act of 2026
md:HB 1203.summary: Adds a substitute member to Garrett County's alcohol license board, creates a private-event permit for wineries, requires staffing at catered events, and requires county license applicants to state citizenship or, if not citizens, give evidence their immigration status complies with federal law.

md:HB 121.title: Baltimore County - Alcoholic Beverages - Sale for Off-Premises Consumption
md:HB 121.summary: Lets Baltimore County Class B and D restaurant and bar licensees get a permit to sell sealed mixed drinks with food for off-premises use to buyers 21 or older until 11 p.m., if the county board adopts regulations. No extra fee may be charged.

md:HB 1216.title: Insurance – Certificates of Guarantee for County Bond Requirements – All Counties
md:HB 1216.summary: Lets any county, instead of only specified counties, accept certificates of guarantee issued by a nonprofit contractors' association or its subsidiary to meet county bond requirements.

md:HB 1218.title: Safe and Healthy Homes for All Act
md:HB 1218.summary: Requires the Office of Tenant and Landlord Affairs to develop a plan to identify and address rental properties with 50 or more units that pose severe health and safety risks, and requires DHCD to publish a list of them.

md:HB 1219.title: Climate Change, Homeowner's Insurance, and Emergency Management - Study
md:HB 1219.summary: Requires the University System of Maryland to study how climate change relates to homeowner's insurance availability and cost and to disaster preparedness, reporting by July 1, 2027, with up to $100,000 from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund.

md:HB 1243.title: Prince George's County - Personal Property Tax Exemption for Small Manufacturers PG 423-26
md:HB 1243.summary: Exempts personal property of small manufacturers holding an alcoholic beverages manufacturer's license, with 50 or fewer employees, from municipal personal property tax in Prince George's County, for tax years beginning after June 30, 2026.

md:HB 1286.title: Anne Arundel County - Alcoholic Beverages - Barbershop and Beauty Salon License
md:HB 1286.summary: Lets Anne Arundel County barbershop and beauty salon license holders serve each customer up to 1.7 ounces of liquor per visit for on-premises consumption, in addition to beer and wine.

md:HB 1300.title: African American Heritage Preservation Program and Maryland Commission for Women - Renaming and Alterations
md:HB 1300.summary: Renames the African American Heritage Preservation Program for Speaker Adrienne A. Jones, makes the Maryland Commission for Women's executive director a skilled service state employee rather than a Secretary appointee, and changes the commission's duties.

md:HB 1305.title: State Child Welfare System - Reporting
md:HB 1305.summary: Requires the State Department of Education to report annually on foster youth who enroll in and graduate from college within six years, include comparison data for other students, and by December 1, 2026 submit a report on improving outcomes for students in child welfare.

md:HB 1321.title: Child Care Scholarship Program - Application Process and Copays - Alterations
md:HB 1321.summary: Requires the State Department of Education to help Child Care Scholarship applicants who qualify for public prekindergarten or Head Start enroll in them during an enrollment freeze, bars copays at or below the poverty line, and allows sliding-fee copays capped at 7% of income.

md:HB 1326.title: Child Abuse and Neglect - Disclosure of Reports and Records
md:HB 1326.summary: Lets the Department of Human Services disclose child abuse and neglect records, after a finalized indicated finding, to administrators of government-run child care centers, youth sports coaches and managers, and child-supervising organizations assessing suitability for work or volunteering.

md:HB 1330.title: Homeowners’ Property Tax Credit – Year–Round Application
md:HB 1330.summary: Moves the homeowners' property tax credit application deadline from October 1 to February 14 of the taxable year and removes the October late-application window. Applies to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2027.

md:HB 1335.title: Department of Information Technology - Information Technology Staffing and Capability Assessment - Independent Study
md:HB 1335.summary: Requires the Department of Information Technology to hire an outside party to study IT and cybersecurity staffing and workforce alignment in the State, and submit the study by November 1, 2027.

md:HB 1364.title: Public Health - Mammograms - Arterial Calcification Notice
md:HB 1364.summary: Requires mammography centers to add a set notice about breast arterial calcification to the screening results letter sent to patients under federal law.

md:HB 1365.title: Health Occupations, Public Health, and Insurance - Menopause - Provider Training Coverage Requirements, Policy Initiatives, and Access to Care
md:HB 1365.summary: Adds the Maryland Commission for Women's director to the State Advisory Council on Health and Wellness, gives continuing-education credit for menopause training, and requires insurers to cover evaluation and management of menopause symptoms.

md:HB 141.title: State Personnel - Collective Bargaining - Graduate Assistants
md:HB 141.summary: Lets graduate assistants, fellows and postdoctoral interns at the University of Maryland, College Park and UMBC bargain collectively, starting July 1, 2028.

md:HB 1425.title: Baltimore City - Alcoholic Beverages Licenses - Revisions
md:HB 1425.summary: Repeals the deadline for Baltimore City Class A license holders to pay the fee for Sunday sales, and changes the deadline for showing proof that personal property taxes owed to the city and State are paid.

md:HB 1430.title: Maryland Public Charter School Program - School Facilities - Funding
md:HB 1430.summary: Requires the Governor, from fiscal 2028, to budget capital improvement funds for public charter school facilities equal to prior-year charter enrollment times $200, distributed directly to schools by the Interagency Commission on School Construction.

md:HB 1434.title: Maryland Department of Health - Caregiver Resource Webpage - Establishment
md:HB 1434.summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to create and maintain a webpage of information and resources for caregivers.

md:HB 1466.title: Department of Housing and Community Development - Appraisal Gap From Historic Redlining Financial Assistance Program - Qualified Properties
md:HB 1466.summary: Expands qualified properties under the Appraisal Gap From Historic Redlining Financial Assistance Program to include residential property in areas the Department of Housing and Community Development identifies as historically redlined or having undergone urban renewal.

md:HB 1470.title: Medical Assistance Programs - Drug Dispensing - Cost-of-Dispensing Survey
md:HB 1470.summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to conduct its in-State drug cost-of-dispensing survey for Medicaid at least every 3 years, starting in 2026, and report results to the General Assembly by December 1 of survey years.

md:HB 1474.title: Baltimore County - Alcoholic Beverages Licenses - Transfers and Conversions
md:HB 1474.summary: Repeals certain limits on transferring Baltimore County alcohol licenses to other premises or converting them to another class, repeals several special Class B license categories, and converts those licenses existing July 1, 2026 to Class B hotel and restaurant licenses.

md:HB 1490.title: Family Investment Program - Temporary Cash Assistance - Good Cause and Adequate Reason Exceptions
md:HB 1490.summary: Bars the Family Investment Program from denying, reducing or ending cash assistance when a person has good cause for not cooperating with child support, which includes cases where cooperation may be against the child's best interest.

md:HB 1526.title: Carroll County - Alcoholic Beverages - Class 1 Distillery On-Premises Consumption Permit
md:HB 1526.summary: Creates a Class 1 distillery on-site consumption permit in Carroll County, letting a licensed distillery sell, prepare and serve food, nonalcoholic drinks and its own spirits for on-premises and off-premises consumption, with a diagram of the consumption area required.

md:HB 1540.title: University of Maryland Capital Region Medical Center - Funding - Repeal of Termination Date
md:HB 1540.summary: Removes the termination date on the requirement that the Governor include annual budget funding for the University of Maryland Capital Region Medical Center, and updates the General Assembly's findings about that funding.

md:HB 1587.title: Gaming - Operation of Electronic Instant Bingo Machines and Report by State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency
md:HB 1587.summary: Raises from 54 to 100 the bingo cards a device may let a user play at once under the slot machine definition, lets electronic instant bingo machines skip paper tickets unless the player asks, and requires a report on possible expansion by December 1, 2026.

md:HB 161.title: Property Tax Credit - Retail Service Station Conversions
md:HB 161.summary: Lets local governments grant a property tax credit on real property converted from a retail gas station to certain retail, residential or mixed uses, only if underground storage tanks have been permanently closed.

md:HB 1616.title: Mutual Insurance Holding Companies - Conversion to Mutual Insurers
md:HB 1616.summary: Allows a mutual insurance holding company to convert to a mutual insurer after adopting and getting approval of a plan of conversion, and sets requirements for that plan and its submission to the Maryland Insurance Commissioner.

md:HB 191.title: Consumer Protection - Retail Transactions for Essential Consumer Goods - Cash Payments
md:HB 191.summary: Bars merchants from refusing cash, requiring cards, or charging cash payers more for essential goods such as food, medicine and fuel in in-person sales under $300 between 6 a.m. and 10 p.m. Violations count as unfair or deceptive trade practices.

md:HB 200.title: Sale of Residential Real Property - Required Flood Risk Disclosure
md:HB 200.summary: Requires the Department of the Environment to create a flood risk disclosure form, and from July 1, 2027 requires sellers of certain homes to give buyers a completed form before signing a sale contract.

md:HB 2100.title: Election Districts - General Assembly and Representatives in Congress
md:HB 2100.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment, for the November 2026 ballot, stating that the state constitution provides no criteria for congressional district boundaries, limits legislative district requirements to state House and Senate districts, and lets the legislature give the Supreme Court original jurisdiction over congressional maps.

md:HB 2101.title: Arbitration Reform for State Employees Act of 2026 - Withdraw and Repeal of Duplicate Proposed Constitutional Amendment
md:HB 2101.summary: Repeals a duplicate proposed constitutional amendment on collective bargaining for State employees, so only one copy appears on the November 2026 ballot. An identical amendment in another act stays on the ballot. Takes effect immediately as an emergency.

md:HB 211.title: Baltimore County – Property Tax Credit – Fraternal Order of Police Lodge 34
md:HB 211.summary: Lets Baltimore County grant a 100% property tax credit on real property owned by Fraternal Order of Police Lodge 34 in Middle River, for tax years beginning after June 30, 2026.

md:HB 216.title: Criminal Law - Benefits Exploitation
md:HB 216.summary: Bars knowingly recruiting, harboring, transporting or obtaining a person to take their government benefits (such as Medicaid, SNAP or Social Security) through deception, coercion or other means, and bars profiting from or aiding that conduct. Penalties scale with the benefits' value.

md:HB 282.title: Adult Protective Services – Modifications
md:HB 282.summary: Changes adult protective services law by adding an online reporting portal, requiring investigators to assess risk of harm and find abuse indicated, not indicated or undetermined, repealing the 10-day deadline for emergency investigations, and revising definitions.

md:HB 288.title: State Superintendent of Schools - Prolonged State of Emergency - Authority to Declare
md:HB 288.summary: Lets the State Superintendent of Schools declare a prolonged state of emergency, lasting at least 14 consecutive school days, for a natural or civil disaster, public health emergency, or identified security threat, after consulting the Governor.

md:HB 3.title: Higher Education - Student Financial Assistance - Dependents of State or Local Public Safety Employees (Maryland Fallen Heroes Tuition Benefits Act)
md:HB 3.summary: Makes two public-safety memorial scholarships subject to budget funding with renewals prioritized, and exempts spouses and dependent children of State or local public safety employees who die in the line of duty from out-of-state or out-of-county tuition at public colleges.

md:HB 306.title: Vehicle Laws - Manufacturers and Dealers - Prices Listed on Dealer Websites (Jack Fitzgerald Price Transparency Act)
md:HB 306.summary: Bars vehicle manufacturers from penalizing a dealer for stating on its website that an advertised price is the manufacturer's minimum advertised price and that the dealer may offer a lower price.

md:HB 315.title: Landlord and Tenant - Discrimination in Housing for Income-Based Housing Subsidies and Positive Rental History Reporting
md:HB 315.summary: Bars landlords that screen credit from refusing applicants with income-based housing subsidies because of income, credit score, or adverse credit history from before the subsidy, with exceptions. Landlords with six or more units must offer positive rent-payment reporting to tenants.

md:HB 319.title: County Boards of Education - Student Transportation - Sunset Repeal and Study
md:HB 319.summary: Repeals the sunset on a 2021 law letting county school boards transport students in vehicles other than Type I or II school vehicles when none can reasonably be provided, and requires a State Department of Education regulation review and report by January 1, 2027.

md:HB 320.title: Anne Arundel County - Property Tax Credit - Rural Legacy Program
md:HB 320.summary: Authorizes Anne Arundel County to give a property tax credit for property in the county's Rural Legacy Area whose owner has sold development rights under the Rural Legacy Program.

md:HB 325.title: Education - Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board - Composition
md:HB 325.summary: Removes the Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board seat for a nonpublic school classroom teacher, and replaces the one nonpublic special education facilities seat with two: a licensed special education teacher and an administrator.

md:HB 326.title: Education - Maryland Center for School Safety - Anonymous Reporting System
md:HB 326.summary: Requires the Maryland Center for School Safety to administer an anonymous system for reporting school safety concerns, requires local school systems to participate by July 1, 2027 unless they run a substantially similar public system, and withholds related records from public inspection.

md:HB 330.title: Maryland Legal Services Corporation - Board of Directors - Membership
md:HB 330.summary: Increases the Maryland Legal Services Corporation Board of Directors from 9 to 12 members.

md:HB 340.title: School Psychologist Interstate Licensure Compact
md:HB 340.summary: Enters Maryland into the School Psychologist Interstate Licensure Compact, letting school psychologists with multistate licenses practice in member states, setting licensure requirements, creating a compact commission and allowing withdrawal.

md:HB 359.title: Property Tax Credit - Urban Agricultural Property - Alterations
md:HB 359.summary: Changes the local urban agricultural property tax credit: drops the acreage and priority-funding-area limits but excludes land assessed as agricultural, adds activities like beekeeping, livestock and agritourism, and requires one year's public notice before a locality ends the credit.

md:HB 372.title: Hospitals - Emergency Pregnancy-Related Medical Conditions - Procedures
md:HB 372.summary: Requires hospitals with emergency departments to provide stabilizing treatment or transfer for patients with emergency pregnancy-related conditions and to allow pregnancy termination when the treating practitioner finds it medically necessary to stabilize the patient; sets civil penalties for negligent violations.

md:HB 388.title: Baltimore County Public Library - Collective Bargaining - Supervisory Employees
md:HB 388.summary: Lets supervisory employees of the Baltimore County Public Library join and bargain through an employee organization, allows at most two bargaining units (one for supervisors, one for others), and leaves existing units and contracts in place.

md:HB 396.title: Residential Child Care Programs - Education of Children and Training of Child and Youth Care Practitioners
md:HB 396.summary: Requires residential child care programs to keep children age 5 and older enrolled in their prior school unless a social services department decides otherwise, and sets requirements for approved training programs for residential child and youth care practitioners. Takes effect January 1, 2027.

md:HB 406.title: Prince George's County - Alcoholic Beverages - Multiple Licenses Prohibition - Exceptions PG 313-26
md:HB 406.summary: Removes the ban on the Prince George's County license board issuing multiple Class B on-sale beer and wine, or beer, wine and liquor, licenses to the same person or premises.

md:HB 439.title: Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing and Maryland Advisory Council on Deaf and Hard of Hearing - Renaming
md:HB 439.summary: Renames the Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing and its advisory council to include "Deafblind," and adds the Department of Disabilities Secretary or designee to the council.

md:HB 443.title: Prince George's County - Alcoholic Beverages - Class B-SEC (Small Event Center) License PG 312-26
md:HB 443.summary: Creates a Class B-SEC small event center beer, wine and liquor license in Prince George's County for on-premises sales at events, capped at 24 licenses per year or three per legislative district, with a $3,500 annual fee.

md:HB 456.title: Howard County - Alcoholic Beverages - Gift Basket Permit Ho. Co. 2-26
md:HB 456.summary: Creates a Howard County gift basket permit letting flower businesses sell and deliver baskets with limited amounts of beer, wine or liquor to adults in the county, and exempts the permit from school-distance limits.

md:HB 457.title: Institutions of Higher Education - Provision of Menstrual Hygiene Products - Requirement
md:HB 457.summary: Requires colleges that offer on-campus housing to provide free menstrual hygiene products in all student health centers by August 1, 2028.

md:HB 474.title: Vehicle Laws - Dangerous Accumulations of Snow and Ice - Removal From Exposed Vehicle Surfaces (Clear Before You Drive Act)
md:HB 474.summary: Bars driving or towing a vehicle without reasonable efforts to remove snow and ice that threatens people or property from exposed surfaces, with exceptions; police may enforce it only when stopping a driver for another violation. Sets fines, higher if it contributes to a crash.

md:HB 497.title: Family Law - Temporary and Final Protective Orders - Duration
md:HB 497.summary: Lengthens temporary protective orders from up to 7 days after service to up to 14 days after issuance, and requires the final protective order hearing within 14 days after the temporary order is issued.

md:HB 519.title: Anne Arundel County - Alcoholic Beverages - Entertainment Permits
md:HB 519.summary: Renames Anne Arundel County alcohol-license entertainment permits: music becomes background entertainment, entertainment becomes general entertainment, dancing becomes full entertainment. Removes the dancing prohibition for license holders without an entertainment permit.

md:HB 522.title: Anne Arundel County - Alcoholic Beverages Licenses - Class C Per Diem License Fees
md:HB 522.summary: Sets Anne Arundel County Class C per diem alcohol license fees for events of 500 or more attendees at $25 per point of sale per day for beer or beer and wine, and $50 for beer, wine and liquor.

md:HB 529.title: Code Revision - Health - Maryland Medical Assistance Program
md:HB 529.summary: Revises and recodifies the State's Medicaid laws as a nonsubstantive revision, with technical and stylistic changes and updated terminology.

md:HB 546.title: Primary and Secondary Education - Educator Professional Development - Course on Well-Being and Flourishing
md:HB 546.summary: Requires the State Department of Education to make available by July 1, 2027 a professional development course for school staff on educator well-being, if it can do so at no cost or at comparable cost to similar courses.

md:HB 548.title: Land Use - Permitting - Development Rights (Maryland Housing Certainty Act)
md:HB 548.summary: Requires local governments to judge housing development applications under the laws in effect when a complete application is submitted, decide completeness within 30 days, and gives approved projects vested development rights for the longer of five years or a locally set period.

md:HB 552.title: Commission on the House of Reformation and Instruction for Colored Children - Establishment
md:HB 552.summary: Creates the Commission on the House of Reformation and Instruction for Colored Children to direct an investigation of the historic site, including locating graves, identifying people buried there, notifying descendants, and a final report by December 31, 2029.

md:HB 558.title: Prince George's County - Alcoholic Beverages - Wine Festival Licenses PG 316-26
md:HB 558.summary: Removes the limit of one Prince George's County wine festival license per year and lets the licensing board choose multiple weekends for wine festivals each year.

md:HB 561.title: Maryland Child Care Credential Program - Extension of Funding
md:HB 561.summary: Requires the Governor to appropriate $5,687,000 to the Maryland Child Care Credential Program in each of fiscal years 2028 through 2030.

md:HB 57.title: Public Schools - Maryland Civic Excellence Program - Established
md:HB 57.summary: Creates a Maryland Civic Excellence Program in the State Department of Education to recognize public high school students for civic readiness, with criteria set by the State Board, including a capstone project. Local school systems may take part.

md:HB 571.title: Nonprofit Housing Corporations - Taxes and Special Assessments Exemptions - Alterations
md:HB 571.summary: Broadens the definition of nonprofit housing corporation (501(c)(3), primarily affordable housing) for State and local tax and special assessment exemptions and extends them to subsidiaries. Excludes Baltimore City property and projects that received local government funding before July 1, 2026.

md:HB 573.title: Fair Housing and Housing Discrimination - Regulations, Intent, and Discriminatory Effect
md:HB 573.summary: Bars housing acts with a discriminatory effect (disparate impact on protected groups or reinforcing segregated housing) regardless of intent, unless there was no discriminatory intent, the act was necessary for a legitimate interest, and no less discriminatory option existed. Authorizes housing department regulations.

md:HB 575.title: Public Schools - Student Attendance - Excused or Discretionary Absences for Civic Engagement
md:HB 575.summary: Requires local school boards' attendance policies to allow an excused or discretionary absence for students doing civic engagement, such as testifying at or meeting with a legislative body, or serving in the General Assembly Page Program.

md:HB 583.title: Prince George’s County – Alcoholic Beverages – Notice of Issuance of Class C Per Diem Beer, Wine, and Liquor License PG 319–26
md:HB 583.summary: Updates the name of the office that the Prince George's County license board must notify when issuing a Class C per diem beer, wine and liquor license.

md:HB 586.title: County Boards of Library Trustees - Membership - Student Member
md:HB 586.summary: Lets a county library board of trustees select a high school junior or senior as a student member, with a one-year term; the student member may vote on policy matters.

md:HB 591.title: Wicomico County - Highway Pedestrian Safety Act
md:HB 591.summary: Bars standing in a Wicomico County roadway, shoulder, median or intersection that the county or a municipality deems inherently dangerous, and bars police from citing anyone unless compliant warning signs are installed.

md:HB 6.title: Public Institutions of Higher Education - Pregnant and Parenting Students - Plan and Reporting
md:HB 6.summary: Requires the Higher Education Commission to collect data on students' parental status from public colleges and universities (except UMGC), requires community colleges to adopt a plan for pregnant and parenting students, and requires a report to the legislature by September 1, 2027.

md:HB 606.title: Anne Arundel County - Residential Property Tax Payment Deferrals - Eligibility
md:HB 606.summary: Changes a disability-benefit qualification for Anne Arundel County residential property tax deferrals from federal benefits for armed forces members to those for 'service members,' described as adding certain reserve components, NOAA and Public Health Service members.

md:HB 623.title: Education - Purple Star Schools Program and Purple Star Colleges Program
md:HB 623.summary: Changes the definition of "military-connected student" in the Purple Star Schools Program and creates a Purple Star Colleges Program to recognize colleges that support military-connected students.

md:HB 664.title: Cecil County - Alcoholic Beverages - Alteration of License Quota
md:HB 664.summary: Limits Cecil County's alcohol license quota to Class A licenses, capped at one per 2,000 registered voters with at least two in each election district, and stops other license classes from counting toward it.

md:HB 671.title: Office of the Long-Term Care Ombudsman - Mandatory Appropriation
md:HB 671.summary: Requires the Governor, starting in fiscal 2027, to budget at least $2,000,000 a year for the Office of the Long-Term Care Ombudsman from money managed care organizations remit under state regulation, with general funds covering any shortfall.

md:HB 677.title: Reduction Facilities and Veterans Service Organizations - Hydrolyzed and Soil Remains - Immunity
md:HB 677.summary: Extends good-faith civil immunity to registered reduction operators who transfer, and veterans service organizations that receive, unclaimed hydrolyzed or soil remains of a veteran or eligible dependent for disposition.

md:HB 680.title: Children's Cabinet Fund - Renaming and Funding for Grants to Local Management Boards
md:HB 680.summary: Renames the Children's Cabinet Fund the Children's Cabinet Interagency Fund and requires the Governor to include budget appropriations to it, at least equal to fiscal 2027's for fiscal 2028-2030 and $500,000 above fiscal 2030's for fiscal 2031, for grants to local management boards.

md:HB 682.title: Anne Arundel County – Alcoholic Beverages – Golf Course License and Sports Activity Venue Licenses
md:HB 682.summary: Creates an Anne Arundel County Class C GC license for selling beer, wine and liquor at golf courses, and sports activity venue licenses for selling beer and wine, or beer, wine and liquor, at commercial recreation facilities.

md:HB 684.title: Health Insurance - Material Changes to Provider Networks - Notification and Special Enrollment Period
md:HB 684.summary: Extends enrollee notice and 90-day continued-care rights from primary care providers to behavioral health providers leaving a network, requires notice of intent to terminate a contract, and gives individual-market enrollees a special enrollment period when their provider is terminated.

md:HB 711.title: Data Privacy - Consumer Data, Public Records, and Message Switching System (Data Privacy Act)
md:HB 711.summary: Bars data controllers from knowingly selling consumer data to government units that engaged in or supported civil immigration enforcement in the prior six months; widens limits on immigration-enforcement access to public records and law enforcement databases.

md:HB 727.title: Anne Arundel County - Alcoholic Beverages - Class C (Veterans' Organization) Licenses - Membership
md:HB 727.summary: Changes the membership requirement for an Anne Arundel County Class C veterans' organization license from service in a war to service in the uniformed services, which the bill's purpose says includes certain NOAA and Public Health Service members.

md:HB 738.title: Real Property - Transfer-on-Death Deed - Establishment
