md:HB 738.summary: Establishes the Maryland Transfer-on-Death Deed Act, setting rules for creating, recording and revoking deeds that pass real property to a named beneficiary at the owner's death, and exempting those deeds from recordation and transfer taxes.

md:HB 742.title: Growing Family Child Care Opportunities Program - Funding
md:HB 742.summary: Requires the Governor to include $450,000 in the annual budget for the Growing Family Child Care Opportunities Program in fiscal years 2028 through 2030.

md:HB 748.title: Publicly Funded Prekindergarten - Early Childhood Educator Career Ladder for Private Providers - New Pathways
md:HB 748.summary: Replaces fixed deadlines in the private prekindergarten educator career ladder with ongoing ones, including a three-month window after hire for assistants to earn credentials and set deadlines for lead teachers qualifying by experience to earn an associate degree.

md:HB 753.title: Tax Sales - Homeowner Protections - Revisions
md:HB 753.summary: Requires homes of owners with documented terminal illness or medical hardship to be withheld from tax sale, lets homeowners designate a representative to work with the Tax Sale Ombudsman, and raises the Homeowner Protection Program value cap from $300,000 to $450,000.

md:HB 776.title: Juvenile Law - Child in Need of Supervision - Mandatory Petition (NyKayla Strawder Memorial Act)
md:HB 776.summary: Requires an intake officer to file a child-in-need-of-supervision petition when a child under 13 is alleged to have committed an act resulting in a death, and requires law enforcement to forward such complaints to the Department of Juvenile Services.

md:HB 783.title: Washington County - Property Tax Credit - Platoon 22, Incorporated
md:HB 783.summary: Requires Washington County and its municipalities to grant a 100% property tax credit on real property owned by Platoon 22, Incorporated and used to provide housing to veterans.

md:HB 805.title: Building Homes Act
md:HB 805.summary: Lets counties and municipalities grant a property tax credit on homes with a nonprofit-provided mortgage and a covenant of at least 20 years restricting income and resale price, for tax years after June 30, 2026.

md:HB 810.title: Study to Evaluate Blockchain-Based Real Property Lease and Title Recordation and Verification
md:HB 810.summary: Requires the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to study using blockchain to record and verify property ownership and leases, and how it could help resolve disputes involving squatting, reporting by December 31, 2026.

md:HB 811.title: Aging-in-Place Programs - Grants - Multigenerational Third Places ( Village Multigenerational Third Places Act)
md:HB 811.summary: Lets the Department of Aging give grants to nonprofits and area agencies on aging to support social connection for aging-in-place participants through events at multigenerational third places, meaning community spaces used by people of different ages.

md:HB 816.title: Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund - Affordability Program and Industry Automobile Insurance Association Assessments
md:HB 816.summary: Lowers from 3% to 1% the cap on the private passenger auto assessment allocation percentage that supports the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund, and lets the fund, with Insurance Commissioner approval, run a premium-limiting affordability program for low-income policyholders; effective July 2027, ends June 30, 2029.

md:HB 828.title: State Board of Education - Membership - Employee of a County Board of Education
md:HB 828.summary: Allows up to two State Board of Education members, including the teacher member, to be local school board employees, and lets them join executive sessions but not vote on certain teacher or personnel dismissal and discipline appeals.

md:HB 845.title: Higher Education - Student Financial Assistance - Alterations to Scholarship Programs
md:HB 845.summary: Extends Community College Promise Scholarship eligibility to Delmar, Maryland residents who graduated from Delmar High School in Delaware, and renames and widens the transportation workers scholarship to include surviving workers and relatives, usable for total cost of attendance.

md:HB 846.title: Property Tax - City of Hagerstown and the Hagerstown Multi-Use Sports and Events Facility, Inc. - Exemption
md:HB 846.summary: Exempts property owned by the City of Hagerstown and used mainly for public social, recreational and entertainment purposes from state, county and municipal property taxes, retroactive to fiscal 2024 with refunds, including for the Hagerstown Multi-Use Sports and Events Facility.

md:HB 849.title: Child Care Scholarship Program - Freeze in Enrollment - Exceptions and Waitlist
md:HB 849.summary: Bars Child Care Scholarship enrollment freezes from covering certain groups such as children with enrolled siblings and homeless children, and requires a waitlist with priority enrollment for certain applicants.

md:HB 862.title: Railroads - Required Crew for Movement of Freight
md:HB 862.summary: Bars freight trains sharing a corridor with high-speed passenger or commuter trains from running with fewer than two crew; fines up to $10,000 for a willful violation, $25,000 within 3 years of a prior one; needs similar laws in New York, Pennsylvania and Virginia.

md:HB 866.title: Workgroup for the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing - Extension
md:HB 866.summary: Extends the Workgroup for the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing to December 31, 2028, and moves its report deadline to December 1, 2028.

md:HB 882.title: Consumer Health Information - Termination Date and Mandatory Funding for the State's Consumer Health Information Hub - Repeal
md:HB 882.summary: Makes the Consumer Health Information Hub's duties apply only to the extent funding is available, ends the required budget appropriation for the Hub, and removes the termination date on consumer health information provisions.

md:HB 889.title: Wicomico County - Property Tax Credit - Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services, Inc.
md:HB 889.summary: Authorizes Wicomico County and its towns to grant property tax credits for property owned by Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services, Inc. that is used for development, rehabilitation and transfer to private owners.

md:HB 894.title: Land Use - Transit-Oriented Development - Alterations (Maryland Transit and Housing Opportunity Act)
md:HB 894.summary: Makes transit-oriented developments designated on or after October 1, 2026 at stations with hourly rail service automatic enterprise zones unless the locality opts out, generally bars minimum parking requirements within 0.25 mile of such stations, and prioritizes State-owned land near stations for infrastructure loans.

md:HB 914.title: Worcester County - Board of License Commissioners - Membership
md:HB 914.summary: Increases the Worcester County Board of License Commissioners from three to five members appointed by the Governor, with terms staggered; takes effect June 1, 2026.

md:HB 919.title: Maryland Higher Education Commission - Practical Applications of Real Estate Appraisal (PAREA) Grant Program - Established
md:HB 919.summary: Creates a Maryland Higher Education Commission grant program for minorities living in historically redlined neighborhoods and underrepresented communities to pursue Practical Applications of Real Estate Appraisal training.

md:HB 936.title: Montgomery County Public Schools - Jane E. Lawton Local Food Procurement MC 7-26
md:HB 936.summary: Requires Montgomery County public schools to publish the dollar amount of school-meal food bought from certified local farms and invasive-species providers in 2026-27, then set target increases for later school years and a plan to meet them.

md:HB 951.title: Real Property - Recordation and Land Records - Revisions
md:HB 951.summary: Repeals the margin requirement for printed deeds and other instruments offered for recording, and requires circuit court clerks to date each change or correction made to the general alphabetical index.

md:HB 991.title: Harford County - Alcoholic Beverages - Class HC (Health Club) License - Hours of Sale
md:HB 991.summary: Extends the closing time for beer and wine sales by Harford County Class HC (health club) licensees from 9 p.m. to 11 p.m.

md:SB 101.title: Higher Education - Loan Repayment and Scholarships for Correctional Officers
md:SB 101.summary: Expands the state police officer and probation agent scholarship and loan repayment programs to include correctional officers, with the same eligibility and service requirements, and renames the programs.

md:SB 12.title: Residential Rental Apartments - Air-Conditioning Requirement
md:SB 12.summary: Requires landlords of apartment buildings with 10 or more units to provide air conditioning from June 1 to September 30, capable of keeping habitable spaces at 80 degrees or below, in new units, units that had or required it since 2025, and some renovated units.

md:SB 13.title: Alcoholic Beverages - License Fee Refund Requirements - Alterations
md:SB 13.summary: Extends alcoholic beverages license fee refunds for license holders called into the armed forces to those called into the uniformed services, including the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration Corps and Public Health Service.

md:SB 140.title: Criminal Law - Benefits Exploitation
md:SB 140.summary: Bars knowingly recruiting, harboring, transporting or obtaining a person to take their government benefits (such as Medicaid, SNAP or Social Security) through deception, coercion or other means, and bars profiting from or aiding that conduct. Penalties scale with the value involved.

md:SB 148.title: Income Tax - Credit for 9-1-1 Specialist Retirement Income (Supporting Our 9-1-1 Specialists Act)
md:SB 148.summary: Creates a nonrefundable income tax credit for tax years 2026 through 2028 equal to 4.75% of the first $15,000 of retirement income from 9-1-1 specialist service, capped at $700, with $250,000 in total credits certifiable per year.

md:SB 16.title: Child Support - Earnings Withholdings Limits
md:SB 16.summary: Caps child support earnings withholding at 35% of disposable earnings for obligors whose income is at or below 250% of the federal poverty level for one person, and lets employees contest withholding amounts.

md:SB 168.title: Study to Evaluate Blockchain-Based Real Property Lease and Title Recordation and Verification
md:SB 168.summary: Requires the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to study using blockchain to record and verify property ownership and leases, including for squatting disputes, and report by December 31, 2026.

md:SB 169.title: Hospitals - Emergency Pregnancy-Related Medical Conditions - Procedures
md:SB 169.summary: Requires hospitals that find a patient has an emergency pregnancy-related condition to stabilize the patient, including by terminating the pregnancy when the treating practitioner finds it medically necessary, or transfer them; bars retaliation against certain staff; sets civil penalties up to $25,000-$50,000 per violation.

md:SB 182.title: Adult Protective Services - Modifications
md:SB 182.summary: Changes adult protective services law by adding an online reporting portal, requiring investigators to assess risk of harm and find abuse indicated, not indicated or undetermined, repealing the 10-day deadline for emergency investigations, and revising definitions.

md:SB 187.title: Correctional Services - Comprehensive Rehabilitative Prerelease Services - Female Incarcerated Individuals (Monica Cooper Prerelease Act)
md:SB 187.summary: Requires the women's prerelease unit to become a facility in Baltimore City for incarcerated women within 36 months of release, resets deadlines (opening by September 2031), adds public-benefits screening to services, and requires annual Correctional Ombudsman progress reports.

md:SB 194.title: Income and Property Tax Incentives - Members and Veterans of the Space Force - Application
md:SB 194.summary: Creates one definition of "active military, naval, air, or space service" and applies it to property tax benefits for disabled veterans, disabled service members and surviving spouses, and to the job creation tax credit's definition of qualified veteran employee.

md:SB 198.title: Prince George's Community College - Aerospace and Aviation Systems Technology Programs - Feasibility Study
md:SB 198.summary: Requires Prince George's Community College to study aerospace and aviation systems technology training programs and report to the General Assembly by December 1, 2027, with $100,000 in the fiscal 2028 budget for the study.

md:SB 204.title: Public Schools - Maryland Civic Excellence Program - Established
md:SB 204.summary: Creates the Maryland Civic Excellence Program in the State Department of Education to recognize public high school students' civic readiness and engagement, with the State Board of Education setting criteria by regulation and local school systems opting in.

md:SB 242.title: Modernizing Civil Relief for Service Members Act
md:SB 242.summary: Lets active service members and spouses who relocate to Maryland on service orders practice under another state's license for the orders' duration after applying, and removes the 1-year post-discharge limit from the "eligible veteran" definition in licensing laws.

md:SB 244.title: Code Revision - Health - Maryland Medical Assistance Program
md:SB 244.summary: Revises and recodifies the State's Medicaid laws as a nonsubstantive revision, with technical and stylistic changes and updated terminology.

md:SB 252.title: Maryland Legal Services Corporation - Board of Directors - Membership
md:SB 252.summary: Increases the Maryland Legal Services Corporation Board of Directors from 9 to 12 members.

md:SB 253.title: Baltimore County Public Library - Collective Bargaining - Supervisory Employees
md:SB 253.summary: Lets supervisory employees of the Baltimore County Public Library form or join employee organizations and bargain collectively, and authorizes bargaining units for library employees.

md:SB 263.title: Education - Dependent Children of Active Service Members - Advance Enrollment Procedures
md:SB 263.summary: Requires county superintendents to let a dependent child of an active service member advance enroll, including by fee-free remote registration, and requires boards to avoid delays in services for children with disabilities. Directs the Secretary of Veterans and Military Families to publish enrollment information.

md:SB 276.title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program and Health Insurance - Coverage for Orthoses and Prostheses (So Every Body Can Move Act)
md:SB 276.summary: Requires Medicaid and certain insurers to cover orthoses starting January 1, 2027, and clarifies that required prosthesis coverage includes all prostheses a provider finds medically necessary for daily living, work or physical activities.

md:SB 285.title: Higher Education - Scholarships for Correctional Officers
md:SB 285.summary: Expands the Maryland Police Officers and Probation Agents Scholarship Program to include correctional officers and students in certificate programs, and renames the program.

md:SB 292.title: County Boards of Education - Student Transportation - Sunset Repeal and Study
md:SB 292.summary: Repeals the sunset on a 2021 law letting county school boards transport students in vehicles other than Type I or II school vehicles when none can reasonably be provided, and requires a State Department of Education regulation review and report by January 1, 2027.

md:SB 30.title: Baltimore County - Property Tax Credit - Fraternal Order of Police Lodge 34
md:SB 30.summary: Lets Baltimore County grant a 100% property tax credit on real property owned by Fraternal Order of Police Lodge 34 in Middle River, for tax years beginning after June 30, 2026.

md:SB 309.title: Sales and Use Tax - Precious Metal Bullion or Coins - Exemption
md:SB 309.summary: Expands the sales and use tax exemption for precious metal bullion and coins by repealing the minimum sale price and Baltimore Convention Center sale requirements, and revises the definition so value depends primarily on metal content.

md:SB 311.title: Education - The Blueprint for Maryland's Future - Revisions
md:SB 311.summary: Extends the current low-income student count method for compensatory education and concentration of poverty grants through fiscal 2028, adds teacher certification options, and delays the National Board Certification requirement for licensed principals from 2029 to 2034.

md:SB 322.title: Courts - Jury Service - Disqualification
md:SB 322.summary: Changes jury disqualification: a person convicted of a crime punishable by over a year is disqualified while serving the sentence, including parole or probation. Also disqualifies those convicted of perjury, witness or jury intimidation, or fraud crimes. Repeals the pardon provision.

md:SB 324.title: Higher Education - Public Senior Higher Education Institutions - Direct Admission Program and Study
md:SB 324.summary: Creates a direct admission program at participating public senior colleges starting 2028-2029, offering conditional admission with a waived application fee to high school students who meet set requirements, including college and career ready standards and a minimum GPA.

md:SB 325.title: Land Use - Permitting - Development Rights (Maryland Housing Certainty Act)
md:SB 325.summary: Requires housing development applications to be judged only under laws in effect when a complete application is submitted, and gives approved projects vested development rights for 5 years or a locally set period, whichever is longer.

md:SB 339.title: Maryland School for the Deaf - Membership of Board of Trustees - Alterations
md:SB 339.summary: Reduces the Maryland School for the Deaf Board of Trustees from 19 to 13 members, raises the minimum number of deaf members from 6 to 7, and sets a phase-out of six members.

md:SB 366.title: Motor Vehicles - Intelligent Speed Assistance System Pilot Program - Establishment
md:SB 366.summary: Requires the Motor Vehicle Administration to create, by October 1, 2027, a pilot program requiring drivers whose accumulated points would trigger license suspension or revocation to use an aftermarket intelligent speed assistance device that prevents exceeding the speed limit, under a restricted license.

md:SB 378.title: Public Libraries - Young Readers Matching Grant Program, Funding, and Services
md:SB 378.summary: Increases state per-capita aid to public library systems and regional resource centers starting in fiscal 2028, changes the services libraries must offer, and raises the Young Readers Grant Program's mandated funding from $350,000 to $450,000.

md:SB 379.title: Recovery Residence Grant Program - Funding
md:SB 379.summary: Extends through fiscal year 2030 the requirement to include $500,000 in the state budget for the Recovery Residence Grant Program.

md:SB 398.title: Anne Arundel County - Board of License Commissioners - Alterations
md:SB 398.summary: Increases the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners from three to five members, requires the Governor to appoint them from lists recommended by county legislators, limits two per legislative district, and requires a conflict-of-interest policy.

md:SB 400.title: Anne Arundel County - Alcoholic Beverages - Entertainment Permits
md:SB 400.summary: Renames Anne Arundel County music, entertainment and dancing permits as background, general and full entertainment permits, changes what each allows, and requires outdoor entertainment under the general and full permits to be at least 100 feet from residentially zoned property.

md:SB 401.title: Anne Arundel County - Board of License Commissioners and Part-Time Inspectors - Compensation
md:SB 401.summary: Raises annual salaries for the chair, part-time inspectors and other members of the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners and includes cost-of-living increases given to nonrepresented county employees.

md:SB 410.title: Public Libraries - State Library Resource Center - Funding
md:SB 410.summary: Raises per capita State aid for the State Library Resource Center starting in fiscal 2028, by 10 cents per capita that year, rising to 57 cents in fiscal 2032.

md:SB 414.title: Anne Arundel County - Alcoholic Beverages - Consumption-Only Nonprofit Swim Club License
md:SB 414.summary: Creates a $100 annual consumption-only license for nonprofit swim clubs in Anne Arundel County, letting members and guests bring their own alcohol to designated events, up to five days a year between 2 p.m. and 10 p.m.

md:SB 42.title: Reduction Facilities and Veterans Service Organizations - Hydrolyzed and Soil Remains - Immunity
md:SB 42.summary: Extends civil-liability protection for good-faith transfers or receipt of unclaimed veterans' remains to hydrolyzed and soil remains, covering funeral establishments, reduction operators, crematories and veterans service organizations.

md:SB 420.title: Public Institutions of Higher Education - Pregnant and Parenting Students - Plan and Reporting
md:SB 420.summary: Requires the Maryland Higher Education Commission to collect data on students' parental status from every public college, and extends pregnant and parenting student support plan requirements to community colleges.

md:SB 426.title: Public Information Act - Divorce Records
md:SB 426.summary: Requires custodians to deny public inspection of divorce records, including applications, financial records, settlements and custody orders, except to people in interest, their lawyers, or by court order; final divorce decrees remain open.

md:SB 428.title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program and Health Insurance - Collaborative Care Model - Cost Sharing Prohibition
md:SB 428.summary: Bars the Maryland Department of Health from charging copayments, coinsurance or deductibles for collaborative care model services, requires insurers to cover them, and orders a study on ending cost sharing.

md:SB 441.title: Anne Arundel County - Alcoholic Beverages - Golf Course License and Sports Activity Venue Licenses
md:SB 441.summary: Creates in Anne Arundel County a Class C GC golf course license for beer, wine and liquor and two sports activity venue licenses (beer and wine, or beer, wine and liquor), all for on-premises consumption.

md:SB 442.title: Anne Arundel County - Population Ratio Quota for Class A (Off-Sale) and Class D (Off-Sale) Licenses - Exemption
md:SB 442.summary: Exempts an Anne Arundel County license application filed on or after January 1, 2023 and approved by June 30, 2025 from the limit of one off-sale (Class A or D) license per 3,500 residents in an assessment district; terminates December 31, 2028.

md:SB 448.title: Carroll County - Public Facilities Bond
md:SB 448.summary: Authorizes the Carroll County Commissioners to borrow up to $27 million through general obligation bonds for public facilities, including water and sewer projects and loans to volunteer fire departments.

md:SB 450.title: Carroll County - Office of Permits and Inspections - Denial of Commercial Permit or License for Unpaid Personal Property Taxes
md:SB 450.summary: Lets the Carroll County Office of Permits and Inspections deny or refuse to renew a commercial license or permit for unpaid personal property taxes, unless the applicant shows evidence of disputing the amount, and allows issuance once the taxes are shown to be paid.

md:SB 459.title: Procurement - Advertising - Maryland News Organizations (Local News for Maryland Communities Act of 2026)
md:SB 459.summary: Requires state procurement units to direct 50% of advertising contract dollars to Maryland news organizations, except advertising aimed outside Maryland for tourism, recruitment or investment, and to prioritize outlets serving underserved communities.

md:SB 461.title: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program - Heat and Eat Program - Study
md:SB 461.summary: Requires the Department of Human Services to study how many households lose automatic utility allowance eligibility in the SNAP Heat and Eat program under the 2025 federal budget law, and report findings and recommendations by December 1, 2026.

md:SB 467.title: Maryland Child Care Credential Program - Extension of Funding
md:SB 467.summary: Requires the Governor to include $5,687,000 a year in the budget for the Maryland Child Care Credential Program in fiscal years 2028 through 2030.

md:SB 469.title: Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund - Affordability Program and Industry Automobile Insurance Association Assessments
md:SB 469.summary: Lowers from 3% to 1% the cap on the private passenger auto assessment allocation percentage that supports the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund, and lets the fund, with Insurance Commissioner approval, run a premium-limiting affordability program for low-income policyholders; effective July 2027, ends June 30, 2029.

md:SB 48.title: Education - Public School Construction - Alterations
md:SB 48.summary: Revises public school construction rules, requiring county boards to get State Superintendent approval for certain actions, letting the Interagency Commission set funding eligibility rules, creating an appeal process, and changing report due dates and debt service reimbursement provisions.

md:SB 486.title: Higher Education - Maryland Graduate and Professional Scholarship Program - Eligible Institutions
md:SB 486.summary: Expands eligibility for the Maryland Graduate and Professional Scholarship Program to include certain students attending the University of Maryland Eastern Shore.

md:SB 496.title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program - Coverage for the Treatment of Obesity - Authorization
md:SB 496.summary: Allows Medicaid, starting January 1, 2027, to cover obesity treatment, including behavioral therapy, bariatric surgery and FDA-approved weight-management medication, and lets the Health Department seek federal approval for that coverage.

md:SB 497.title: Property Tax - City of Hagerstown and the Hagerstown Multi-Use Sports and Events Facility, Inc. - Exemption
md:SB 497.summary: Exempts City of Hagerstown-owned property used mainly for public social, recreational or entertainment purposes from State, county and municipal property tax, and makes that exemption and the Hagerstown Multi-Use Sports and Events Facility's exemption retroactive to fiscal 2024, with refunds.

md:SB 501.title: Washington County - Property Tax Credit - Platoon 22, Incorporated
md:SB 501.summary: Requires Washington County and its municipalities to grant a 100% property tax credit on real property owned by Platoon 22, Incorporated and used to provide housing to veterans.

md:SB 503.title: Growing Family Child Care Opportunities Program - Funding
md:SB 503.summary: Requires the Governor to include $450,000 in the budget for the Growing Family Child Care Opportunities Program in each of fiscal years 2028 through 2030.

md:SB 507.title: Public Schools - Individuals With Disabilities - Accessibility and Emergency Planning
md:SB 507.summary: Requires each school system's safety evaluation to identify disability-accessibility issues, and its annual report to list times a school facility became inaccessible to a student with a disability in a way that could impede evacuation. The report is confidential, except to legislators on request.

md:SB 509.title: Higher Education - Workforce Pell Grant Program - Implementation
md:SB 509.summary: Sets up Maryland's Workforce Pell Grant process: the Governor, consulting the Workforce Development Board, may approve short-term career programs for federal Pell Grants; the board and MHEC may charge application fees, and the board must collect institution data.

md:SB 521.title: Health Insurance - Material Changes to Provider Networks - Notification and Special Enrollment Period
md:SB 521.summary: Extends enrollee notice and 90-day continued-care rights from primary care providers to behavioral health providers leaving a network, requires notice of intent to terminate a contract, and gives individual-market enrollees a special enrollment period when their provider is terminated.

md:SB 530.title: Aging-in-Place Programs - Grants - Multigenerational Third Places (Village Multigenerational Third Places Act)
md:SB 530.summary: Lets the Department of Aging give grants to nonprofits and area agencies on aging for events at multigenerational third places that support social connection among people in aging-in-place programs.

md:SB 532.title: Higher Education Institutions - Over-the-Counter Contraception - Access and Reporting
md:SB 532.summary: Requires public four-year colleges to report annually on over-the-counter contraception access, adds reporting items for community colleges, and requires community colleges to give students access to all over-the-counter contraception methods.

md:SB 535.title: County Boards of Library Trustees - Membership - Student Member
md:SB 535.summary: Lets a county library board of trustees select a high school junior or senior as a student member, with a one-year term; the student member may vote on policy matters.

md:SB 58.title: Property Tax Credit - Retail Service Station Conversions
md:SB 58.summary: Lets local governments grant a property tax credit on real property converted from a retail gas station to certain retail, residential or mixed uses, only if underground storage tanks have been permanently closed.

md:SB 597.title: Higher Education - Maryland Artificial Intelligence Partnership
md:SB 597.summary: Creates the Maryland Artificial Intelligence Partnership within the University System of Maryland to coordinate AI workforce, business and research efforts, with a strategic plan due December 1, 2026. Also creates an AI public services fellowship and, conditionally, an AI incubation lab.

md:SB 6.title: State Personnel - Collective Bargaining - Nontenure Track Faculty
md:SB 6.summary: Gives collective bargaining rights to nontenure-track faculty at University System of Maryland institutions, Morgan State University and St. Mary's College, and creates a separate bargaining unit for them.

md:SB 607.title: Income Tax - Subtraction Modification for Public Safety Retirement Income - Amount
md:SB 607.summary: Phases in an increase in the Maryland income tax subtraction for public safety retirement income from $15,000 to $20,000 by 2030, rising $1,000 each year starting in 2026.

md:SB 636.title: Baltimore City - Alcoholic Beverages Licenses - Revisions
md:SB 636.summary: Repeals the deadline for Baltimore City Class A license holders to pay the fee for Sunday sales, and changes the deadline for showing proof that personal property taxes owed to the city and State are paid.

md:SB 637.title: Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund - Fund Producer Commission Rate
md:SB 637.summary: Lowers the minimum commission the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund pays producers on private passenger auto policies from 10% to 5% of premium, and bars commissions on policies the Fund writes directly.

md:SB 646.title: Public School System Contracts - Prohibited Provisions
md:SB 646.summary: Bars public school system contracts from including specified terms, such as unfunded indemnification, binding arbitration, out-of-state venue, liability caps, or terms the other party can change unilaterally; such terms are void. Excludes collective bargaining agreements and existing contracts.

md:SB 657.title: Maryland Higher Education Commission - Practical Applications of Real Estate Appraisal (PAREA) Grant Program - Established
md:SB 657.summary: Creates a Higher Education Commission grant program for minority residents of historically redlined and underrepresented communities to complete Practical Applications of Real Estate Appraisal (PAREA) training, aimed at closing appraisal gaps and diversifying the appraisal field.

md:SB 668.title: Children's Cabinet Fund - Renaming and Funding for Grants to Local Management Boards
md:SB 668.summary: Renames the Children's Cabinet Fund the Children's Cabinet Interagency Fund and requires the Governor to include budget appropriations to it, at least equal to fiscal 2027's for fiscal 2028-2030 and $500,000 above fiscal 2030's for fiscal 2031, for grants to local management boards.

md:SB 681.title: Worcester County - Board of License Commissioners - Membership
md:SB 681.summary: Increases the Worcester County Board of License Commissioners from three to five members appointed by the Governor, with terms staggered; takes effect June 1, 2026.

md:SB 700.title: Wicomico County - Alcoholic Beverages - Class B (Golf Course) License - Hours of Sale
md:SB 700.summary: Lets Wicomico County Class B golf course license holders begin selling beer, wine and liquor at 7 a.m. instead of 10 a.m., Monday through Sunday.

md:SB 72.title: Baltimore County - Alcoholic Beverages - Sale for Off-Premises Consumption
md:SB 72.summary: Lets Baltimore County restaurants and bars with certain licenses sell mixed drinks in sealed containers for off-premises consumption with food, to buyers 21 or older, until 11 p.m., if the licensing board adopts regulations; bars an added fee.

md:SB 728.title: Higher Education - Student Financial Assistance - Alterations to Scholarship Programs
md:SB 728.summary: Extends Maryland Community College Promise Scholarship eligibility to Delmar, Maryland residents who graduate from Delmar High School in Delaware, and widens the Fallen Transportation Workers Scholarship to cover surviving transportation workers and more relatives, for total cost of attendance.

md:SB 729.title: Real Property - Access to Counsel in Evictions Program - Expansion
md:SB 729.summary: Extends the Access to Counsel in Evictions Program to residents of mobile home parks, giving them legal representation in repossession actions and requiring outreach, an informational pamphlet and annual reporting that cover them.

md:SB 739.title: Climate Change, Homeowner's Insurance, and Emergency Management - Study
md:SB 739.summary: Requires the University System of Maryland to study how climate change affects homeowner's insurance availability and cost and emergency preparedness, and report recommendations to the General Assembly by July 1, 2027, including on flood insurance programs.

md:SB 747.title: Condominiums - Unit Owner Responsibility for Damage or Destruction and Mandatory Insurance Coverage
md:SB 747.summary: Changes a condo owner's liability for damage originating in their unit from up to $10,000 of the council's insurance deductible to the least of repair cost, deductible or $25,000, and requires residential condominium unit owners to carry insurance and show proof annually.

md:SB 76.title: Anne Arundel County - Alcoholic Beverages - Class C (Veterans' Organization) Licenses - Membership
md:SB 76.summary: Changes the Anne Arundel County Class C (veterans' organization) alcohol license to cover clubs composed of members who served in the uniformed services, not just the armed forces, adding veterans who served in NOAA and the Public Health Service.

md:SB 760.title: Real Property - Recordation and Land Records - Revisions
md:SB 760.summary: Repeals the margin requirement for printed deeds offered for recordation and requires circuit court clerks to date each change or correction made to the general alphabetical index.

md:SB 765.title: Property Taxes - Tax Sales, Legacy Protection Program, and Tax Credits
md:SB 765.summary: Extends State Tax Sale Ombudsman services to estates and heirs of deceased homeowners, creates a Legacy Protection Program with $250,000 a year from the state and $500,000 from counties, and gives eligible heirs homeowners' and homestead tax credits for up to three years.

md:SB 769.title: University System of Maryland - Academic Facilities Bonding Authority
md:SB 769.summary: Approves $26 million of University System of Maryland academic facility projects and $24 million of facility renewal projects, authorizing $50 million in bonds, which are not State debt.

md:SB 791.title: Correctional Services and Criminal Procedure - Immigration Enforcement - Prohibitions (Community Trust Act)
md:SB 791.summary: Adds a provision stating that the bill's section on law enforcement agents may not be construed to bar an agent from participating in a joint task force that includes the Department of Homeland Security.

md:SB 794.title: Health Insurance - Special Enrollment Period for Pregnancy - Coverage Effective Date
md:SB 794.summary: Lets a person who enrolls in health coverage during a pregnancy special enrollment period choose coverage starting the month pregnancy is confirmed or the month after plan selection, for plans issued or renewed on or after January 1, 2027.

md:SB 802.title: Garrett County - Alcoholic Beverages Act of 2026
md:SB 802.summary: Creates a Garrett County Special Event Permit for winery licensees, adds a substitute board member, lets catering-option licensees sell alcohol at events on unlicensed or temporarily licensed premises, and requires license applicants to state citizenship or, for noncitizens, show immigration status complies with federal law.

md:SB 803.title: Alcoholic Beverages - Class 3 Wineries and Class 4 Limited Wineries - Alterations
md:SB 803.summary: Expands the definition of pomace brandy that Class 4 limited wineries may make and sell, and lets Class 3 wineries buy bulk wine from Class 4 limited wineries, which may sell and deliver it.

md:SB 807.title: Alcoholic Beverages - Class 8 Farm Brewery Licenses
md:SB 807.summary: Creates a Class 10 farm distillery license, open to Class 8 farm brewery holders, to distill and sell spirits made on the licensed farm, requires farm brewery and distillery holders to engage in agritourism, and changes brewery food service and zoning exceptions.

md:SB 808.title: Health Insurance - Provider Panels - Requirements
md:SB 808.summary: Changes how health insurers handle provider panel applications, adding a $500-per-day penalty paid to the provider for missed notices, shortening decision deadlines, repealing the application fee, and requiring more frequent provider directory updates.

md:SB 809.title: Supporting Our Caregiver Infrastructure Program - Feasibility Study
md:SB 809.summary: Requires the University of Maryland, College Park to study the feasibility of a program giving caregivers universal monthly payments for each dependent they care for, with a final report by July 1, 2028.

md:SB 839.title: Medical Assistance Programs - Drug Dispensing - Cost-of-Dispensing Survey
md:SB 839.summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to conduct the in-State Medicaid cost-of-dispensing survey for pharmacies at least once every three years, beginning in 2026, and report results to the General Assembly.

md:SB 851.title: Anne Arundel County - Property Tax Credit - Rural Legacy Program
md:SB 851.summary: Authorizes Anne Arundel County to grant, by local law, a property tax credit for real property in a Rural Legacy Area whose owner has sold development rights under the Rural Legacy Program.

md:SB 852.title: Anne Arundel County – Alcoholic Beverages – Barbershop and Beauty Salon License
md:SB 852.summary: Lets Anne Arundel County barbershop and beauty salon license holders serve each customer up to 1.7 ounces of liquor per visit for on-premises consumption, in addition to beer and wine.

md:SB 864.title: Higher Education - Tuition Exemption for Foster Care Recipients - Eligibility
md:SB 864.summary: Lowers from 13 to 8 the age on or after which a person must have lived in an out-of-home placement to qualify for the foster care tuition and mandatory fee exemption at public colleges. Takes effect July 1, 2026.

md:SB 865.title: Workgroup on the Affordability of Private Passenger Automobile Insurance – Extension and Alteration of Membership and Duties
md:SB 865.summary: Extends the auto insurance affordability workgroup to June 30, 2027, changes its membership, and adds duties to develop specific recommendations to reduce premiums, including on territorial rating. Requires an updated report by January 1, 2027.

md:SB 890.title: Insurance - Captive Insurers - Premium Receipts Tax Study
md:SB 890.summary: Requires the Maryland Insurance Administration to study the use, regulation and taxation of captive insurance companies by entities in the State and report findings and recommendations by January 1, 2027.

md:SB 892.title: Health Occupations, Public Health, and Insurance - Menopause - Provider Training Coverage Requirements, Policy Initiatives, and Access to Care
md:SB 892.summary: Requires health insurers to cover evaluation and management of menopause symptoms, directs the Department of Health to identify provider training programs for which health boards grant continuing education credit, and changes the Advisory Council on Health and Wellness.

md:SB 897.title: Cecil County - Alcoholic Beverages - Alteration of License Quota
md:SB 897.summary: Changes the Cecil County license quota to count only Class A licenses, at 1 per 2,000 registered voters, and allows the board to issue at least two Class A licenses in each election district.

md:SB 898.title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program - Behavior Technicians - Reimbursement
md:SB 898.summary: Requires Maryland Medicaid to reimburse registered behavior technicians for applied behavior analysis services to recipients with autism spectrum disorder, and bars requiring certification as a condition of reimbursement, except that certification may be required within 150 days of starting.

md:SB 941.title: Safe and Healthy Homes for All Act
md:SB 941.summary: Requires the housing department's landlord and tenant office to develop a plan, due August 31, 2027, to identify rental properties with 50 or more units that pose severe health and safety risks and propose interventions, and to publish a list of those properties online.

md:SB 974.title: Caroline County - Alcoholic Beverages - Inspector
md:SB 974.summary: Requires the Caroline County alcoholic beverage license board's inspector to be either someone the board appoints or the county codes administrator, who currently fills the role.

md:SB 982.title: Mutual Insurance Holding Companies - Conversion to Mutual Insurers
md:SB 982.summary: Lets a mutual insurance holding company that owns all of a reorganized stock insurer convert to a mutual insurer under a plan approved by a board majority and at least 75% of members voting, then by the Insurance Commissioner.

mi:HB 4011.title: Property: conveyance of state property; transfer of certain state-owned property in Arenac County; provide for. Creates land transfer act.
mi:HB 4011.summary: As introduced, authorizes the State Administrative Board to convey about 118 acres of state land in Arenac County, site of the closed Standish Maximum Correctional Facility, by competitive sale, sale to local government, or transfer.

mi:HB 4135.title: Property: conveyance of state property; conveyance of certain state-owned property in Jackson County; provide for. Creates land transfer act.
mi:HB 4135.summary: As introduced, authorizes the State Administrative Board to convey about 81 acres of state land in Jackson County, with Jackson County given first right to buy it for $1.00 within two years of enactment.

mi:HB 4301.title: Vehicles: emergency vehicles; definition of authorized emergency vehicle; expand. Amends secs. 2 & 698 of 1949 PA 300 (MCL 257.2 & 257.698).   TIE BAR WITH: HB 4302'25
mi:HB 4301.summary: Adds vehicles owned by the Michigan Mutual Aid Box Alarm System and operated during an interlocal emergency to the definition of authorized emergency vehicle, and lets them use red, white, amber or green flashing lights.

mi:HB 4302.title: Vehicles: emergency vehicles; exception to commercial driver license for authorized emergency vehicles of Michigan Mutual Aid Box Alarm System; create. Amends sec. 312e of 1949 PA 300 (MCL 257.312e).   TIE BAR WITH: HB 4301'25
mi:HB 4302.summary: Exempts Michigan Mutual Aid Box Alarm System employees and members who drive authorized emergency vehicles and meet firefighter driver-training standards from the commercial driver license vehicle group designation requirement.

mi:HB 4598.title: Crimes: organized; gift card fraud; provide for. Amends sec. 4 of 2012 PA 455 (MCL 752.1084).
mi:HB 4598.summary: Adds gift card fraud to Michigan's organized retail crime law: knowingly acquiring, tampering with, or using gift cards or redemption information with intent to defraud is a felony punishable by up to 5 years in prison or a $5,000 fine.

mi:HB 4599.title: Crimes: organized; certain definitions related to gift card fraud; provide for. Amends 2012 PA 455 (MCL 752.1081 - 752.1087) by adding sec. 3a.   TIE BAR WITH: HB 4598'25
mi:HB 4599.summary: Defines "gift card," "gift card redemption information," "issuer," and "seller" for the organized retail crime law's gift card fraud provisions; takes effect only if House Bill 4598 is enacted.

mi:HB 4678.title: Agriculture: weights and measures; certain definitions; provide for. Amends 1964 PA 283 (MCL 290.601 - 290.635) by adding sec. 28g.   TIE BAR WITH: HB 4679'25
mi:HB 4678.summary: As introduced, lets qualified equipment rental businesses sell motor fuel to refill rented equipment at a flat rate or per-gallon fee, if stated in the rental contract.

mi:HB 4679.title: Agriculture: weights and measures; certain definitions; provide for. Amends secs. 10 & 28c of 1964 PA 283 (MCL 290.610 & 290.628c).   TIE BAR WITH: HB 4678'25
mi:HB 4679.summary: As introduced, says the Department of Agriculture and Rural Development need not inspect and test each qualified fuel dispenser, and treats testing requirements as met if the dispenser complies with HB 4678 and federal transportation rules.

mi:HB 4703.title: Insurance: health insurers; coverage for group prenatal care services; require. Amends 1956 PA 218 (MCL 500.100 - 500.8302) by adding sec. 3406ss.
mi:HB 4703.summary: As introduced, requires health insurance policies issued or renewed in Michigan on or after January 1, 2026 to cover group prenatal care services.

mi:HB 4793.title: Elections: school; requirement for school board members to file an acceptance of office; eliminate. Amends secs. 309 & 310 of 1954 PA 116 (MCL 168.309 & 168.310).   TIE BAR WITH: HB 4794'25,  HB 4795'25
mi:HB 4793.summary: Eliminates the requirement that school board members file a written acceptance of office. Takes effect only if House Bills 4794 and 4795 are also enacted.

mi:HB 4794.title: Elections: school; requirement for community college board of trustee members to file an acceptance of office; eliminate. Amends secs. 156 & 157 of 1966 PA 331 (MCL 389.156 & 389.157).   TIE BAR WITH: HB 4793'25
mi:HB 4794.summary: Eliminates the requirement that community college trustees file an acceptance of office, while keeping the oath of office. Takes effect only if House Bill 4793 is also enacted.

mi:HB 4795.title: Elections: school; requirement for intermediate school board members to file an acceptance of office; eliminate. Amends sec. 861 of 1976 PA 451 (MCL 380.861).   TIE BAR WITH: HB 4793'25
mi:HB 4795.summary: Eliminates the requirement that appointed members of a consolidating school district's board file an acceptance of office with the intermediate superintendent. Takes effect only if House Bill 4793 is also enacted.

mi:HB 5109.title: Vehicles: other; allocation to transportation administration collection fund; modify. Amends sec. 810b of 1949 PA 300 (MCL 257.810b).
mi:HB 5109.summary: Reduces by $1.7 million a year, for fiscal years 2027 through 2029, the amount the state treasurer may receive into the transportation administration collection fund, and deposits that $1.7 million in the general fund instead.

mi:HB 5120.title: Civil procedure: service of process; cost for service of process for personal protection orders; eliminate. Amends secs. 2559 & 2950 of 1961 PA 236 (MCL 600.2559 & 600.2950).   TIE BAR WITH: HB 5121'25,  HB 6033'26
mi:HB 5120.summary: As passed by the House, requires courts issuing domestic-relationship personal protection orders to designate the law enforcement agency that serves them and give petitioners two or more copies free; service within 72 hours is at no cost while the Personal Protection Order Service Fund has money.

mi:HB 5121.title: Civil procedure: service of process; cost for service of process for personal protection orders; eliminate. Amends sec. 2950a of 1961 PA 236 (MCL 600.2950a) & adds secs. 2950d & 2950p.   TIE BAR WITH: HB 5120'25,  HB 6033'26
mi:HB 5121.summary: As passed by the House, creates the Personal Protection Order Service Fund, administered by State Police, to pay law enforcement for serving personal protection order documents, and sets service rules, including service within 72 hours and further attempts within 10 days if the first fails.

mi:HB 5317.title: Counties: boards and commissions; county parks and recreation commission membership; modify. Amends sec. 1 of 1965 PA 261 (MCL 46.351).
mi:HB 5317.summary: Lets counties under 100,000 population, beginning January 1, 2027, reduce the appointed members of a county parks and recreation commission from seven to four, and makes wording updates to the commission's membership rules.

mi:HB 5356.title: Vehicles: title; requirements for transfer of title by a dealer; provide for. Amends 14, 41a, 78, 217, 217c, 233, 233a, 233b, 234, 238, 239, 240, 248, 248a, 248j, 249, 250, 258, 801b, 806 & 810a of 1949 PA 300 (MCL 257.14 et seq.) & adds sec. 9b.
mi:HB 5356.summary: As passed by the House, revises Vehicle Code title, registration and salvage rules, including raising the police salvage-vehicle inspection fee cap from $100 to $125 and setting a $5,000 value threshold for ownership-bond rules for licensed new vehicle dealers.

mi:HB 5482.title: State agencies (existing): generally; plans to correct audit recommendations; require notification to the legislature if the executive branch fails to prepare. Amends sec. 242 of 1984 PA 431 (MCL 18.1242).
mi:HB 5482.summary: Removes the requirement that appropriation acts for capital outlay projects include State Building Authority rental payments for the authorized projects.

mi:HB 5485.summary: As passed by the House, requires dam owners to register dams in 5 staggered rounds with asset management and compliance documents, creates a dam safety emergency fund, and creates a dam risk reduction grant program requiring owners to match at least 10%.

mi:HB 5514.title: Children: other; prohibition of use of certain restraint while transporting youths to certain youth residential treatment programs; provide for. Creates new act.
mi:HB 5514.summary: Bars youth transportation companies from using blindfolds, hoods, or mechanical restraints on youths headed to residential treatment programs, limits physical restraint to imminent serious harm, bars pickups from 9 p.m. to 6 a.m., and sets civil fines up to $1,000.

mi:HB 6007.title: Food: service establishments; delegation of certain duties and exemption of certain persons from licensure; modify. Amends secs. 3105, 3113, 3129, 3139, 4101, 4105, 5101 & 6103 of 2000 PA 92 (MCL 289.3105 et seq.).
mi:HB 6007.summary: Lets the state take back wholesale food-processing oversight from local health departments in some cases, adds licensing exemptions (such as minor-run lemonade stands), and requires 120 days' written notice before revoking a local health department's certification.

mi:HB 6033.title: Civil procedure: costs and fees; fees for service of process; revise. Amends sec. 2559 of 1961 PA 236 (MCL 600.2559).
mi:HB 6033.summary: As passed by the House, bars courts and police from charging personal protection order petitioners service fees while the Personal Protection Order Service Fund has money, lets police collect at least $50 per completed service from the fund, and raises other service-of-process fees.

mi:HB 6080.title: Education: teachers and administrators; certain professional development courses; prohibit. Amends sec. 1248 of 1976 PA 451 (MCL 380.1248).
mi:HB 6080.summary: Requires coursework counted as 'relevant special training' in teacher layoff, placement and promotion decisions to be degree-eligible credit from an accredited institution, shown on a transcript and letter-graded; pass/fail coursework is ineligible unless converted to a letter grade.

mi:HB 6127.title: Gaming: other; expenditures in the internet gaming fund; modify. Amends secs. 14 & 16 of 2019 PA 152 (MCL 432.314 & 432.316).
mi:HB 6127.summary: Raises the annual Internet Gaming Fund allocation to the first responder presumed coverage fund from $2.0 million to up to $7.0 million (half its claim and administrative costs), and allocates $1.0 million a year for tribal governments.

mi:HB 6130.title: Education: financing; Michigan trust fund act; modify. Amends sec. 12 of 2000 PA 489 (MCL 12.262).
mi:HB 6130.summary: Bars appropriations or spending from the community district education trust fund after September 30, 2026, and transfers any remaining balance to the state school aid fund on October 1, 2026.

mi:HB 6259.title: Criminal procedure: sentencing guidelines; sentencing guidelines for criminal sexual conduct; modify. Amends sec. 16y, ch. XVII of 1927 PA 175 (MCL 777.16y).   TIE BAR WITH: HB 6261'26,  HB 6262'26
mi:HB 6259.summary: As introduced, reclassifies second- and third-degree criminal sexual conduct in the sentencing guidelines as Class A felonies with a statutory maximum of life; takes effect only if HB 6261 and 6262 are enacted.

mi:HB 6260.title: Crimes: criminal sexual conduct; penalties for criminal sexual conduct in the first degree; modify. Amends sec. 520b of 1931 PA 328 (MCL 750.520b).
mi:HB 6260.summary: As introduced, sets a 15-year mandatory minimum sentence for first-degree criminal sexual conduct, which already carries a maximum of life.

mi:HB 6261.title: Crimes: criminal sexual conduct; penalties for criminal sexual conduct in the second degree; modify. Amends sec. 520c of 1931 PA 328 (MCL 750.520c).
mi:HB 6261.summary: As introduced, sets a 10-year mandatory minimum and raises the maximum from 15 years to life for second-degree criminal sexual conduct.

mi:HB 6262.title: Crimes: criminal sexual conduct; penalties for criminal sexual conduct in the third degree; modify. Amends sec. 520d of 1931 PA 328 (MCL 750.520d).
mi:HB 6262.summary: As introduced, sets a 5-year mandatory minimum and raises the maximum from 15 years to life for third-degree criminal sexual conduct.

mi:HB 6263.title: Crimes: criminal sexual conduct; penalties for criminal sexual conduct in the fourth degree; modify. Amends sec. 520e of 1931 PA 328 (MCL 750.520e).
mi:HB 6263.summary: As introduced, changes fourth-degree criminal sexual conduct from a misdemeanor to a felony, keeping the 2-year maximum prison term.

mi:HB 6282.title: Public employees and officers: ethics; moratorium on former legislators accepting employment with an entity that receives a grant from the utility consumer participation board; provide for. Creates new act.
mi:HB 6282.summary: Bars former legislators, for at least two years after leaving office, from taking jobs with entities that receive utility consumer participation board grants; violations are misdemeanors punishable by up to 90 days in jail, a fine up to $1,000, or both.

mi:HB 6302.title: Education: school districts; requirement to display an American flag in classrooms; provide for. Amends sec. 1347 of 1976 PA 451 (MCL 380.1347).
mi:HB 6302.summary: As passed by the House, changes the school flag rule so a U.S. flag in classrooms where students recite the Pledge of Allegiance must be displayed, hoisted, draped, or placed on a stand or post in a prominent location.

mi:HB 6309.title: Highways: memorial; portion of M-86; designate as the "Casey Rice Memorial Highway". Amends 2001 PA 142 (MCL 250.1001 - 250.2092) by adding sec. 116.
mi:HB 6309.summary: Designates M-86 in Branch County between US-12 and Arbogast Road as the "Casey Rice Memorial Highway."

mi:HR 373.title: A resolution to condemn socialism, the platform of the Democratic Socialists for America, and politicians who espouse socialist views, and to oppose the implementation of socialist policies in the state of Michigan and the United States.
mi:HR 373.summary: Condemns socialism, the platform of the Democratic Socialists for America, and politicians who espouse socialist views, and opposes socialist policies in Michigan and the United States.

mi:SB 102.title: Counties: employees and officers; request for transcript and abstract of paper or record; modify. Amends sec. 1 of 1895 PA 161 (MCL 48.101).
mi:SB 102.summary: Extends the capped-fee electronic records rule for county treasurers to records they possess, and treats a request for both winter and summer tax bill amounts as one request with a $2,000 maximum charge.

mi:SB 1132.title: Military affairs: other; Camp Grayling improvement fund; establish. Amends 1967 PA 150 (MCL 32.501 - 32.851) by adding secs. 388a, 388b, 388c, 388d, 388e & 388f.
mi:SB 1132.summary: Creates a Camp Grayling improvement fund for the site's fees, rents and other revenue, spendable by the Department of Military and Veterans Affairs on appropriation for improvements; authorizes site leases and contracts; and requires an annual report.

mi:SB 1134.title: Retirement: state employees; election process to transfer certain law enforcement officers to the Michigan state police retirement system; provide for. Amends sec. 55 of 1943 PA 240 (MCL 38.55) & adds secs. 50b, 50c, 50d, 64a, 64b & 64c.   TIE BAR WITH: SB 1133'26,  SB 1135'26
mi:SB 1134.summary: Lets state employees' retirement system Tier 2 participants in certain corrections positions, conservation officers, and state police motor carrier and properties security officers elect to join the state police retirement system effective January 2028, with elections due October 15, 2027.

mi:SB 198.title: Occupations: vehicles, dealers, and repair facilities; requirements for automobile dealer data collection; provide for. Creates new act.
mi:SB 198.summary: As introduced, bars vehicle manufacturers and third parties from accessing, sharing or using protected dealer data, including consumer and diagnostic data, without the dealer's written consent, and from limiting dealers' use of it.

mi:SB 217.title: Traffic control: accidents; penalties for moving violation causing physical injury or death to a vulnerable roadway user; enhance. Amends sec. 12e, ch. XVII of 1927 PA 175 (MCL 777.12e).   TIE BAR WITH: SB 0216'25
mi:SB 217.summary: As introduced, adds the new felonies for moving violations that seriously injure or kill vulnerable roadway users, such as pedestrians, to the sentencing guidelines; tied to SB 216.

mi:SB 373.title: Housing: landlord and tenants; limitations on fees charged to tenants; provide for. Amends sec. 3 of 1978 PA 454 (MCL 554.633).
mi:SB 373.summary: As introduced, bars a rental agreement from charging an extra fee on every allowed rent payment method, so an agreement allowing multiple methods must offer at least one without an added charge.

mi:SB 413.title: Health occupations: psychologists; requirements for practice by limited licensed psychologist; modify. Amends secs. 18221, 18223, 18233 & 18237 of 1978 PA 368 (MCL 333.18221 et seq.).
mi:SB 413.summary: Beginning 12 months after enactment, lets limited-license psychologists practice without supervision and requires 2 years of supervised postgraduate experience (3,000 hours; 4,000 for master's degrees granted from August 31, 2027). Adds two limited-license psychologists to the licensing board.

mi:SB 433.title: State agencies (existing): health and human services; educational materials regarding health dangers for youth using high-potency THC and cannabis products; require the department to provide. Amends 1976 PA 451 (MCL 380.1 - 380.1852) by adding sec. 1509.
mi:SB 433.summary: As passed by the House, requires the Department of Health and Human Services to develop, by July 1, 2027, an annually updated notice on the dangers of tobacco, vapor, nicotine, THC cannabis and synthetic hemp products and on THC poisoning, which schools must give parents by October 1 each year from 2027-28.

mi:SB 478.title: Property: conveyance of state property; transfer of certain state-owned property in Livingston County; provide for. Creates land transfer act.
mi:SB 478.summary: Authorizes the State Administrative Board to transfer administrative jurisdiction of about 93 acres in Green Oak Township, Livingston County, from the Department of Corrections to the Department of Military and Veterans Affairs without payment.

mi:SB 569.title: Health facilities: other; fees related to nurse aide and medication aide training and permit programs; modify. Amends secs. 5431, 5841,13104, & 16315 of 1978 PA 368 (MCL 333.5431 et seq.).
mi:SB 569.summary: Moves $1,000,000 of newborn screening fees, $220,000 from the parent participation fund for children with special health care needs, and $100,000 of body art facility license fees into the general fund each year from fiscal 2027 through 2029.

mi:SB 729.title: State finance: authorities; outstanding obligations of the state building authority; provide exception to the limit of. Amends sec. 8 of 1964 PA 183 (MCL 830.418).
mi:SB 729.summary: As introduced, exempts $421.3 million of State Building Authority bonds issued in June 2025 from counting toward the Authority's $2.7 billion cap on outstanding debt.

mi:SB 791.title: Highways: memorial; portion of I-475; designate as the "St. John Street Community Memorial Highway". Amends 2001 PA 142 (MCL 250.1001 - 250.2092) by adding sec. 124.
mi:SB 791.summary: As introduced, designates the portion of I-475 in Genesee County from Hamilton Avenue north to a quarter mile past Stewart Avenue as the "St. John Street Community Memorial Highway."

mi:SB 947.title: Natural resources: inland lakes; dam safety regulations; provide for. Amends and adds (See bill).   TIE BAR WITH: HB 5485'26
mi:SB 947.summary: As introduced, brings dams licensed under the Federal Power Act under state environmental department jurisdiction, raises dam permit fees, increases inspection frequency, and requires a dam registration process.

mi:SB 988.title: Property tax: tax tribunal; number of days to appeal a claim for poverty exemption; modify. Amends sec. 53c of 1893 PA 206 (MCL 211.53c).
mi:SB 988.summary: Extends the deadline to appeal a board of review's denial of a poverty exemption to the Michigan Tax Tribunal from 30 to 35 days after the denial, and treats a mailed appeal as timely if postmarked by the deadline.

mn:HF 1082.title: Public safety; time extended to use appropriations; public safety officer and survivor benefits provided; sale or transfer of law enforcement vehicle, assault of hospital or clinic security guard, and grooming prohibited; crimes of impersonating a peace officer and theft modified; task forces and grant program established; MINNCOR policies modified; domestic violence case process modified; personal information protections provided to public safety officers; criminal penalties provided; reports required; and money appropriated.
mn:HF 1082.summary: Appropriates $1,314,000 for a clearance grant program and two task forces, transfers $12 million to the victims of crime account, and bars selling law enforcement vehicles to the public with police equipment or insignia, along with other public safety provisions.

mn:HF 1141.title: Housing finance and policy bill.
mn:HF 1141.summary: Appropriates $25 million to the Minnesota Housing Finance Agency from its investment earnings, authorizes $100 million in housing infrastructure bonds, and returns tax-forfeited land settlement money to the general fund and appropriates it for family homeless prevention.

mn:HF 1410.title: Correctional and peace officer disciplinary procedures modified.
mn:HF 1410.summary: Adds procedures for questioning correctional officers in discipline cases, including a signed complaint, witness lists, electronic recording, a union representative or attorney present, and damages from agencies that violate them; adjusts related peace officer definitions.

mn:HF 1606.title: Nudification technology access prohibited.
mn:HF 1606.summary: Bars owners of websites and apps from letting users nudify images or videos of identifiable people, or doing so for them, unless the service requires user technical skill; bans advertising such services; lets depicted people sue; allows attorney general penalties up to $500,000 per violation.

mn:HF 1849.title: Term limits provided for governor and lieutenant governor, and constitutional amendment proposed.
mn:HF 1849.summary: Proposes a state constitutional amendment, for the 2026 ballot, limiting a person to being elected governor no more than twice and lieutenant governor no more than twice, counting terms from the 2026 election.

mn:HF 2133.title: Income tax; pass-through entity tax technical correction made.
mn:HF 2133.summary: Corrects the wording of the Minnesota income tax law on the credit for pass-through entity tax paid to another state, changing references from "section" to "subdivision" so the credit's expiration applies to that subdivision.

mn:HF 2358.title: Enhanced criminal penalty provided for violations of coercion crime.
mn:HF 2358.summary: Raises the maximum sentence for coercion by threatening a violation of the law on nonconsensual dissemination of private sexual images to 10 years if a substantial factor in great bodily harm, and 15 years if in the victim's death.

mn:HF 2433.title: Education finance bill.
mn:HF 2433.summary: Requires school districts and charter schools to adopt a policy by June 30, 2027 and implement a local or state anonymous threat reporting system by July 1, 2028; changes fiscal year 2027 compensatory aid; provides grants and appropriates money.

mn:HF 2438.title: Taxation bill; financing and operation of state and local government provided.
mn:HF 2438.summary: Conforms Minnesota's income tax to most changes in federal Public Law 119-21, with exceptions such as a 1% floor on charitable deductions, and makes other state and local tax changes.

mn:HF 2484.title: Bonding bill; spending authorized to acquire and better land and buildings and for other improvements of a capital nature, new programs established and existing programs modified, report required, prior appropriations modified and canceled, and money appropriated.
mn:HF 2484.summary: Appropriates general fund money in fiscal year 2027 for capital improvements to land and buildings, establishes new programs and modifies existing ones, and modifies and cancels prior appropriations.

mn:HF 3067.title: Paraprofessional qualifications clarified.
mn:HF 3067.summary: Treats a paraprofessional who shows the required competencies as meeting federal qualification rules when the employing district or charter school validates it, and requires Department of Education guidance on validation by August 1, 2026.

mn:HF 3155.title: Gift card fraud included in organized retail theft.
mn:HF 3155.summary: Includes gift cards in the organized retail theft law and adds tampering with stolen merchandise or packaging to obtain value to the covered acts.

mn:HF 3298.title: Reimbursement program established for underground petroleum storage tank systems with pressurized single-walled steel piping.
mn:HF 3298.summary: Uses up to $4 million a year from the Petroleum Tank Fund to reimburse underground tank owners for 50% of the cost of replacing single-walled steel piping and equipment; the program expires in 2037.

mn:HF 3404.title: Criminal penalty for impersonating a peace officer increased, crime of impersonating a peace officer while possessing a firearm established, enhanced penalties established, persons presenting as peace officers required to fulfill duty to identify, and criminal penalties established.
mn:HF 3404.summary: Makes impersonating a peace officer a felony (up to 2 years; 10 with a firearm or recent prior), raises penalties for other crimes committed while impersonating, and requires officers to identify their agency, last name and ID number by uniform markings or on request.

mn:HF 3426.title: Environment and natural resources trust fund finance bill.
mn:HF 3426.summary: Appropriates about $102 million in fiscal year 2027 from the Environment and Natural Resources Trust Fund, sets rules for its community grant program, and adds requirements for approving emerging-issues spending.

mn:HF 3453.title: Kratom; legal age to possess kratom established as 21 years of age or older.
mn:HF 3453.summary: Raises from 18 to 21 the age below which selling kratom is a gross misdemeanor and possessing it is a misdemeanor, effective August 1, 2026.

mn:HF 3467.title: Commissioner of veterans affairs allowed to direct agency resources to veterans' initiatives, and reports required.
mn:HF 3467.summary: Lets the commissioner of veterans affairs direct nonmonetary agency resources to initiatives on veterans' food insecurity, homelessness, suicide prevention and similar issues, and requires an annual report each October 15.

mn:HF 3489.title: Licensing boards reporting required, criminal offense of grooming established, criminal penalties provided, and money appropriated.
mn:HF 3489.summary: Creates the felony of grooming a child, extends felony solicitation offenses to people in authority over a minor and to school staff regarding students, requires police to notify licensing boards when a teacher is charged with listed offenses, and appropriates money.

mn:HF 3521.title: Exception to the hospital construction moratorium provided.
mn:HF 3521.summary: Adds an exception to the hospital construction moratorium for a project to add 85 licensed beds at an existing safety net, level I trauma center hospital in Ramsey County.

mn:HF 3522.title: Veterans; standards established for legislatively directed competitive and direct grants, honor guard detail provided, available benefits to veterans of the Secret War in Laos modified, eligibility for burial in state veterans cemeteries modified, Commanders Task Force established, pay for state active service modified, commissioner of veterans affairs allowed to temporarily close veterans homes, reports required, and money appropriated.
mn:HF 3522.summary: Sets standards for legislatively directed veterans grants, extends honor guard funeral payments to more groups, changes Secret War in Laos veteran benefits, state veterans cemetery burial eligibility and state active service pay, creates a Commanders Task Force, and appropriates money.

mn:HF 3544.title: Certain veterans or former members of the armed forces who have forfeited federal benefits made ineligible for state-funded benefits, services, or programs; and environmental hazards information and assistance program for veterans discontinued.
mn:HF 3544.summary: Bars veterans the federal VA has found to have forfeited federal benefits from state-funded veterans benefits and programs, adds a deputy commissioner for administration at the veterans department, and ends the environmental hazards information and assistance program.

mn:HF 3629.title: Program payment withholding provided for credible allegation of fraud, grant management provisions changed, and program integrity reports required.
mn:HF 3629.summary: Replaces agencies' 60-day payment withholding on a preponderance of fraud evidence with withholding during a credible allegation of fraud under investigation, with administrative reconsideration; changes grant rules; requires annual program integrity reports from Human Services and Children, Youth, and Families.

mn:HF 3676.title: Safe at Home program; protections, remedies, and various provisions provided and modified; and criminal penalties established.
mn:HF 3676.summary: Changes the Safe at Home address confidentiality program by barring discrimination against participants, adding a criminal penalty when a violation causes bodily harm, and adjusting legal-proceeding and driver's license address rules.

mn:HF 3709.title: Virtual-currency custody services allowed to be offered and performed.
mn:HF 3709.summary: As passed by the House, allows banks and credit unions to provide virtual-currency custody services if they follow safety-and-soundness and written-policy requirements and give the commissioner 60 days' written notice.

mn:HF 3718.title: Veterinary medicine and veterinary technology practice provisions modified.
mn:HF 3718.summary: Rewrites Minnesota's veterinary practice law, adding definitions for telemedicine, teletriage and the veterinarian-client-patient relationship, and changing rules on veterinary technicians, drug dispensing, record keeping, feed directive drugs, and donated drugs for animals.

mn:HF 3769.title: Multiple levels of substance abuse care provided by the commissioner of corrections clarified in law, and access to mental health unit beds for incarcerated persons expanded.
mn:HF 3769.summary: Requires residential substance use treatment programs in certified state-operated juvenile correctional facilities to meet community treatment program standards, as adult programs already must, and expands incarcerated people's access to mental health unit beds.

mn:HF 3782.title: Chemical irritant used in buildings disclosure required, and commissioner of public safety required to develop a standard form.
mn:HF 3782.summary: Requires peace officers to notify building owners, and occupants of homes or apartments, when chemical irritants are used inside a building, requires agencies to share product information on request, and directs the Department of Public Safety to create a standard notice form.

mn:HF 3785.title: Definitions and registration requirements for motorized bicycles and motorcycles powered by electric motors modified, sellers required to have a dealer license, certain vehicles prohibited from using public roads, and money appropriated.
mn:HF 3785.summary: Defines motorized bicycles with electric motors as over 750 and under 1,500 watts, lets them register as off-highway motorcycles, requires dealer licenses and electrical safety certification for sellers, lowers micromobility device limits to 20 mph and 100 pounds, and appropriates $30,000 for signage.

mn:HF 3825.title: Health occupations; licensing and scope of practice modified for acupuncture and herbal medicine practice, athletic training, mortuary science, social work, dentistry practice, marriage and family therapy, pharmacy practice, physical therapists, and advanced practice registered nurses; registration established for massage therapists and Asian bodywork therapists; licensure established for music therapists; unlicensed practice provisions modified; advisory councils established; civil penalties; reports required; fees imposed; and money appropriated.
mn:HF 3825.summary: As passed by the House, changes licensing and scope of practice for acupuncture, athletic training, mortuary science, social work, dentistry, pharmacy and other health professions; creates registration for massage and Asian bodywork therapists and licensure for music therapists.

mn:HF 3827.title: Grants from Bureau of Criminal Apprehension to local law enforcement clarified as reimbursements, law related to recording of crimes updated, process for determining how certain criminal records are ineligible for sealing established, and court required to provide order for protection for access by law enforcement.
mn:HF 3827.summary: Turns public safety grants to local law enforcement into reimbursements, has the BCA superintendent prescribe the form for crime data, has court administrators make vulnerable adult protection order status available to officers, and requires the BCA to unseal records later found ineligible for expungement.

mn:HF 3875.title: Judiciary policy bill.
mn:HF 3875.summary: Lets district courts post notices on the judicial branch website when no suitable local newspaper exists, limits public-authority notice in dissolutions to cases with children, makes docketed restitution orders last until satisfied, and extends the child protection council's report deadline to December 15, 2026.

mn:HF 3900.title: Permanent school fund investment, management, and distribution policy modified; and constitutional amendment proposed.
mn:HF 3900.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment for the November 2026 ballot letting permanent school fund distributions be set by law instead of limited to interest and dividends; a companion law sets them at 4.5% of the fund's three-year average value.

mn:HF 3908.title: Ignition interlock program license revocation requirements modified, driver's license indicators classified as private data, and technical corrections made.
mn:HF 3908.summary: Changes driver's license rules, including making license indicators and designations private data, barring sharing of autism and mental health designations with federal agencies, and revising impaired-driving and ignition interlock provisions.

mn:HF 3970.title: Remedy to extinguish a joint interest in a contract for deed of a perpetrator of domestic abuse or sexual assault established.
mn:HF 3970.summary: Lets an unmarried person subjected to domestic abuse, sexual assault, sexual extortion or harassment by a contract-for-deed co-party ask a court to end the abuser's interest if the abuser has not lived there for six months and the petitioner made all payments.

mn:HF 4017.title: Unlawful shipment of infectious or pathological waste study required, and money appropriated.
mn:HF 4017.summary: Requires the Pollution Control Agency to submit a study by January 15, 2027 on unlawful shipment of infectious or pathological waste to solid waste facilities, including a survey of waste generators, and appropriates $75,000 for it.

mn:HF 4052.title: Various provisions governing telephone company regulation, facilities and property, pricing plans, service classification, and reporting requirements.
mn:HF 4052.summary: Repeals many state telephone company rate, price and service regulations and requires telephone companies to notify residential customers of the price of all service options available to them.

mn:HF 4063.title: First aid kit requirements on school buses modified, USDOT numbers required for all school buses, and school buses authorized on public roads for training purposes.
mn:HF 4063.summary: Requires anyone providing school transportation with a school bus to apply for a USDOT number, allows school buses to be used on public roads for driver training, and requires first aid kits meeting national school transportation specifications in model year 2027 and newer vehicles.

mn:HF 4074.title: Retirement policy bill.
mn:HF 4074.summary: Changes public pension law, including lower contribution rates and higher postretirement adjustments for correctional service plan members, state aid for certain plans, firefighter relief association rules, and Secure Choice Retirement Program administration.

mn:HF 4075.title: Uniform procedure established for imposition, implementation, and oversight of firearm restrictions resulting from certain criminal convictions and judicial orders.
mn:HF 4075.summary: Creates a uniform process for surrendering firearms in child protection, domestic abuse, assault, harassment and pretrial release cases, and requires petitioners in child protection and domestic abuse cases to identify where the respondent's firearms are located.

mn:HF 4102.title: State Patrol compensation study requirements modified, and volunteer chaplains allowed within the state patrol.
