ok:SB 1286.summary: Requires political subdivisions that held a county-run election since January 1, 2023, and own or lease a facility in or near a precinct lacking a suitable polling place to provide a room free on the county election board secretary's written request.

ok:SB 1303.title: Workers' compensation; transferring property and records. Effective date. Emergency.
ok:SB 1303.summary: Terminates the Advisory Council on Workers' Compensation and transfers its property and records to the Workers' Compensation Commission.

ok:SB 1319.title: Corporation Commission; processes for cities and counties to seek certain reimbursement; fair market value; requiring application to request use of certain funds; creating the Remediation Assistance Revolving Fund. Emergency.
ok:SB 1319.summary: Sets a process for cities and counties to seek reimbursement from a new Remediation Assistance Revolving Fund after buying and removing homes contaminated by oil or brine. The Commission remediates using state plugging funds; the city or county then sells the property and returns proceeds.

ok:SB 1325.title: Protection from Domestic Abuse Act; requiring defendants charged with certain domestic violence offenses to use a Global Positioning System (GPS) device when released on bond. Effective date.
ok:SB 1325.summary: As passed by the Senate, requires defendants charged with domestic abuse by strangulation, with a deadly weapon, or after a prior domestic abuse adjudication to be on GPS monitoring at their own cost to be released on bail. Corrections lists approved GPS programs; the court may let the victim receive proximity alerts.

ok:SB 1326.title: Self-Service Storage Facility Lien Act; permitting electronic delivery and acceptance of rental agreements. Effective date.
ok:SB 1326.summary: Allows self-storage rental agreements to be delivered and accepted electronically, deems payment or continued use acceptance if the occupant does not sign within 30 days, and starts the 15-day wait before disposing of abandoned property from delivery of notice.

ok:SB 1338.title: Education; creating the Education Impact and Innovation Revolving Fund; providing for competitive grants pool; providing for use of grants. Effective date.
ok:SB 1338.summary: As amended, requires the State Department of Education to run competitive grants for proposals to improve education outcomes and creates the Education Impact and Innovation Revolving Fund. The State Board scores and ranks proposals, with identifying information removed, against a department rubric.

ok:SB 1360.title: Mathematics instruction; Oklahoma Math Achievement and Proficiency Act; teacher training; creating the Office of Mathematics Improvement; Director; screening instrument; funding. Effective date. Emergency.
ok:SB 1360.summary: Creates an Office of Mathematics Improvement in the State Department of Education, led by a director focused on K-5 math. Moves to 2027-2028 the year districts must use the statewide screening instrument, and changes how math funds are allocated to districts.

ok:SB 1380.title: Medicaid; requiring certain death record verifications; requiring certain denial or disenrollment of deceased individuals; prohibiting certain payments. Effective date.
ok:SB 1380.summary: Requires the Health Care Authority to check Social Security and state death records before approving Medicaid, deny applications of deceased people, verify enrollee deaths monthly from 2027, disenroll the deceased, stop payments after death and recoup them where allowed. Requires periodic State Auditor reviews.

ok:SB 1390.title: Gross production tax; modifying apportionment of collections for certain fiscal years; modifying apportionment limit. Effective date.
ok:SB 1390.summary: Extends through fiscal year 2032, instead of 2027, the current split of certain gross production tax revenue, one-third each to the tourism capital fund, conservation infrastructure fund and community water infrastructure fund.

ok:SB 1400.title: Sales tax exemption; combining certain exemptions for aircraft maintenance, manufacturing, and parts. Effective date.
ok:SB 1400.summary: Combines the sales tax exemptions for aircraft maintenance and manufacturing facilities with those for aircraft parts, and modifies certain exemptions.

ok:SB 1410.title: Agriculture; requiring operation of an Ag in the Classroom Education Program; requiring development of curriculum for K-12 programs. Effective date.
ok:SB 1410.summary: Requires the Department of Agriculture to run an Ag in the Classroom Education Program with K-12 curriculum, and allows it to give incentives to participating teachers if funding is available.

ok:SB 1425.title: Health care; repealing provisions related to the Health Care Workforce Resources Board. Effective date.
ok:SB 1425.summary: Repeals the Oklahoma Health Care Workers and Educators Assistance Program and the Health Care Workforce Resources Act, which includes the Health Care Workforce Resources Board.

ok:SB 1437.title: Schools; creating the Donald J. Trump Physical Fitness Act. Effective date.
ok:SB 1437.summary: Requires the State Department of Education to set guidelines, including staff training, disability and medical exemptions, and a parent opt-out, for schools to give students the Presidential Fitness Test, which districts must then administer.

ok:SB 1448.title: Oklahoma Consumer Protection Act; modifying exemptions. Effective date.
ok:SB 1448.summary: Changes the Oklahoma Consumer Protection Act exemption for other regulators' oversight to actions required or authorized under specific state or federal laws or regulations they administer; actions regulated under Corporation Commission laws remain exempt.

ok:SB 1451.title: Voter registration; requiring certain information to be included on voter registration applications. Emergency.
ok:SB 1451.summary: Adds a prior-registration question to voter registration applications, treats an application as a request to cancel any prior registration, and requires notice to the other state's election official. Requires an annual report on those notices and cancellations.

ok:SB 1461.title: Oklahoma Educational Television Authority; extending sunset date.
ok:SB 1461.summary: Extends the sunset date of the Oklahoma Educational Television Authority from July 1, 2026 to July 1, 2031 and clarifies language on its appointees.

ok:SB 1489.title: Students; directing compliance with the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act; requiring publication of certain information. Effective date. Emergency.
ok:SB 1489.summary: Adds special education law training to principal certification requirements, lets parents of children with disabilities review records five days before an IEP meeting and bring a person of their choice, and requires dispute-resolution information online.

ok:SB 1502.title: Long-term care; eliminating the Alzheimer-Dementia Disclosure Act Advisory Council. Effective date.
ok:SB 1502.summary: Eliminates the Alzheimer-Dementia Disclosure Act Advisory Council, which advises on state rules for dementia special care disclosures by long-term care facilities.

ok:SB 1531.title: Aerospace, aircraft, and aviation infrastructure; authorizing the Oklahoma Department of Aerospace and Aeronautics to take certain actions. Effective date.
ok:SB 1531.summary: Authorizes the Department of Aerospace and Aeronautics' unmanned aircraft systems and advanced air mobility clearinghouse to invest in publicly owned infrastructure and partner with other states and industry to create regional or technical centers.

ok:SB 1534.title: Corporations; modifying requirements related to charitable organizations and solicitation of charitable contributions; prohibiting certain actions by charitable nonprofit corporations. Effective date.
ok:SB 1534.summary: Requires charitable organizations to list tax ID numbers on Secretary of State registrations, requires charitable nonstock corporation boards to have at least three members, bars loans to or guarantees for directors, and modifies which religious and educational groups are exempt from filing.

ok:SB 1543.title: Driving under the influence; authorizing aggregation of certain offenses; creating felony offense. Effective date.
ok:SB 1543.summary: Allows two or more DUI violations within one year to be aggregated and prosecuted as a single Class C2 felony, exempts certain cases from blood and breath test timing requirements, and repeals duplicate versions of the statute.

ok:SB 1546.title: Education; modifying eligibility under the Equal Opportunity Education Scholarship Act.
ok:SB 1546.summary: As amended, lets scholarship granting organizations and educational improvement grant organizations give capital improvement grants to schools, requires them to report such grants to the Tax Commission, and clarifies that public schools can spend grant money on improving reading and math scores.

ok:SB 1553.title: Medicaid; specifying certain qualifications for appeals; providing for recovery of certain costs. Effective date.
ok:SB 1553.summary: Specifies that a psychologist reviewing a Medicaid appeal meets the specialty requirement if currently licensed, with training and experience in testing for and treating the condition, sufficient to determine whether the service is medically necessary or clinically appropriate.

ok:SB 1555.title: Medicaid home- and community-based services; modifying certain definition. Effective date.
ok:SB 1555.summary: Replaces the IQ-based definition of "individual with intellectual disability" in Oklahoma's Medicaid home- and community-based services law with the Social Security Administration's listing criteria for intellectual disorder, effective November 1, 2026.

ok:SB 1557.title: Applied behavior analysis; transferring licensure powers and duties to the State Board of Examiners of Psychologists; requiring background check. Effective date.
ok:SB 1557.summary: Transfers licensing of behavior analysts and assistant behavior analysts to the State Board of Examiners of Psychologists, requires criminal history checks, and replaces the $100 fee cap with fees covering costs.

ok:SB 1562.title: Hospice; specifying certain penalties; defining term. Effective date.
ok:SB 1562.summary: Adds Health Department discipline and injunction authority for hospice solicitation or paid patient referrals, defines solicitation to include recruiting patients already enrolled in another hospice, and states that advertising and fair-market-value marketing payments are not prohibited.

ok:SB 1572.title: State Commissioner of Health; requiring Commissioner and Department of Mental Health and Substance Abuse Services conduct a feasibility study to gather certain information. Emergency.
ok:SB 1572.summary: Directs the State Commissioner of Health, with the Department of Mental Health and Substance Abuse Services, to study consolidating the two agencies and report to the Governor and legislative leaders by March 1, 2027.

ok:SB 1589.title: Crimes and punishments; modifying scope of certain offense related to gambling. Effective date.
ok:SB 1589.summary: Adds online casino games, and geolocation providers, gaming suppliers, platform providers, promoters and media affiliates who support them, to the felony offense of conducting or supporting gambling games. Takes effect November 1, 2026.

ok:SB 1593.title: Higher education; removing language regarding the promulgation of rules and the presidential search process for the Board of Trustees for Oklahoma State University/Tulsa. Effective date. Emergency.
ok:SB 1593.summary: Removes the requirement that the Oklahoma State University/Tulsa Board of Trustees promulgate certain rules and adopt certain policies, along with the presidential search process language and other outdated language.

ok:SB 1595.title: Motor vehicles; prohibiting certain entities from providing certain recommendations; providing certain exception. Effective date. Emergency.
ok:SB 1595.summary: Bars state agencies and their contractors from recommending for or against a specific commercial driver training school or withholding student grants based on the school chosen, and lets affected schools or students sue.

ok:SB 1614.title: Teachers; modifying requirements of induction program; providing funding sources for program. Effective date. Emergency.
ok:SB 1614.summary: Makes the state teacher induction program state-supported, requiring districts to take part beginning in 2026-27, and allows it to be funded by appropriations, grants and philanthropic or nonprofit contributions.

ok:SB 1618.title: Criminal procedure; creating the Public Protection Act; conditions of release; public safety reports. Effective date.
ok:SB 1618.summary: Lets courts use a pretrial risk-assessment public safety report to help set release conditions, and requires one when the charge is a violent crime. The report cannot be the sole basis to grant or deny release and goes to defense and state counsel on request.

ok:SB 1630.title: Schools; allowing a school district or charter school to count certain day or number of hours toward certain requirement under certain circumstances. Effective date. Emergency.
ok:SB 1630.summary: Lets a school district or charter school count one virtual instruction day (six hours) toward the existing two-day (12-hour) virtual limit when a high school site holds statewide testing with limited space and staffing, if its board approves for non-testing students.

ok:SB 1632.title: Schools; directing career-readiness assessments and assessment-based credentials to be made available to certain students beginning in certain school year. Effective date. Emergency.
ok:SB 1632.summary: Shifts approval of career-readiness assessments and credentials from the Commerce Department to the State Department of Education, removes the funding condition, and makes the assessments available to grades 10 through 12 starting in the 2026-2027 school year.

ok:SB 1633.title: Higher education; removing language providing resident tuition eligibility for certain students. Emergency.
ok:SB 1633.summary: Removes language letting students who cannot document U.S. nationality or lawful immigration status qualify for in-state tuition, language on their eligibility for state scholarships and financial aid, and an exception to the bar on higher education benefits for certain students.

ok:SB 1651.title: State Board of Medical Licensure and Supervision; modifying various provisions related to physicians and allied health professionals. Effective date.
ok:SB 1651.summary: Changes licensing rules for physicians, including a special training license, new rules for international medical graduates and physician emeritus status, and for athletic trainers, music therapists and respiratory care practitioners.

ok:SB 1670.title: Higher education; directing certain model policy established by the Oklahoma State Regents for Higher Education to include certain tiered system of ownership. Effective date. Emergency.
ok:SB 1670.summary: Requires the Regents' technology-development policy to include a tiered system of ownership based on revenue generated, and inventor compensation competitive with similar institutions. Adds aerospace and defense to encouraged areas and requires policy review every seven years.

ok:SB 1679.title: General provisions; creating the Preserving Oklahoma Values Act of 2026. Emergency.
ok:SB 1679.summary: Voids court rulings based on foreign law that violate defined "Judeo-Christian Western rights and values" (due process, speech, religion, privacy and others), and contract terms letting such law govern or set jurisdiction. Excludes tribal law and entities that contract for foreign law.

ok:SB 1684.title: Motor vehicles; requiring certain operators to have certain insurance coverage. Effective date.
ok:SB 1684.summary: Requires operators of highway remediation and cleanup services to carry at least $3 million in liability insurance, with proof submitted to the Department of Environmental Quality when applying for or renewing a license.

ok:SB 1687.title: Driver licenses; adding certain age requirement to qualification for certain license; permitting certain persons to proctor certain examination. Effective date.
ok:SB 1687.summary: Requires Service Oklahoma to authorize third parties, such as school districts, technology centers, colleges and driver training schools, to proctor written driver license exams, and lets certified driver education instructors and designated examiners proctor the knowledge exam.

ok:SB 171.title: State government; commissioning of peace officers; directing the Commission of Public Safety to commission peace officers in conjunction with the President Pro Tempore of the Senate or the Speaker of the Oklahoma House of Representatives. Effective date.
ok:SB 171.summary: Directs the Commissioner of Public Safety to commission up to two members, rather than one, of each chamber's security team as peace officers, with jurisdiction under Title 21, Sections 99 and 99a, effective only during official duties, replacing Capitol-grounds jurisdiction.

ok:SB 1726.title: Higher education; directing certain institutions of higher education to establish certain training program for graduate instructors. Effective date. Emergency.
ok:SB 1726.summary: Requires state higher education institutions that use graduate students as instructors of record to run a training program covering teaching practices, grading, accommodations, academic integrity, and students' First Amendment rights to free speech and viewpoint neutrality.

ok:SB 1734.title: Schools; creating the Oklahoma Responsible Technology in Schools Act; requiring development of guidance for use of artificial intelligence and emerging technologies. Effective date. Emergency.
ok:SB 1734.summary: Creates the Oklahoma Responsible Technology in Schools Act: teachers must review AI output, AI may not be the primary basis for grading or promotion, districts give parents annual disclosure and an opt-out, and the state sets guidance.

ok:SB 1772.title: Motor vehicles; requiring use of lamps and illuminating devices at certain times. Effective date.
ok:SB 1772.summary: Adds windshield wiper use due to inclement weather to the times when vehicles on highways must display lamps and lighting devices, alongside nighttime and low-visibility times, and updates related statutory language.

ok:SB 1775.title: Municipalities; clarifying that penalties for certain municipal ordinances may be equal to penalties in state statute. Emergency.
ok:SB 1775.summary: Bars municipal ordinance penalties above the state penalty for the same offense, and makes any municipal fine above the statutory maximum void and unenforceable to the excess, reduced to the lawful maximum.

ok:SB 1794.title: Mental health; creating the Oklahoma Behavioral Health Vacancy Registry Act; requiring establishment of certain behavioral health vacancy registry; mandating certain reporting. Effective date.
ok:SB 1794.summary: Creates the Oklahoma Behavioral Health Vacancy Registry Act, requiring a registry of available behavioral health beds with a forensic competency module. Covered facilities must report; hospital participation is voluntary. Authorized referral sources can request placements.

ok:SB 1796.title: Foster care; allowing foster parents to use certain caregivers and arrangements for temporary care of foster children; specifying certain time limit on temporary care. Effective date.
ok:SB 1796.summary: Allows foster parents to use approved alternate caregivers, respite care, and informal arrangements for temporary care, requiring approval for care over 72 hours and notice to the Department of Human Services.

ok:SB 1806.title: Foster care; directing the Department of Human Services to implement certain extension of foster care services. Effective date. Emergency.
ok:SB 1806.summary: Directs the Department of Human Services to offer voluntary extended foster care services until age 21 to qualified individuals who are in school, in job programs, working 80 hours a month, or unable due to treatment.

ok:SB 1810.title: Human trafficking; authorizing Attorney General to enter into agreements for services for victims of human trafficking; requiring certification of certain shelters and programs. Effective date.
ok:SB 1810.summary: Allows the Attorney General to contract for services for human trafficking victims, requires Attorney General certification of trafficking shelters and programs, makes certain victim information confidential, and makes expert testimony on trafficking's effects on victims admissible in court.

ok:SB 1827.title: Governmental Tort Claims Act; modifying definitions. Effective date.
ok:SB 1827.summary: Expands the Governmental Tort Claims Act definition of public trust to include the university hospitals trust and any sole-member nonprofit corporation of it, or nonprofit subsidiary of such a corporation.

ok:SB 1832.title: Income tax; reauthorizing certain income tax refund donations. Effective date. Emergency.
ok:SB 1832.summary: Reauthorizes the income tax refund donation checkoff for the Veterans Affairs Department's Indigent Veteran Burial Program and its Equipment and Capital Improvement Program.

ok:SB 1859.title: Oklahoma State Bureau of Investigation; creating the Cyber Crime Fraud Unit; revolving fund. Effective date. Emergency.
ok:SB 1859.summary: Creates a Cyber Crime and Fraud Unit in the State Bureau of Investigation to investigate cyber-enabled crime, financial fraud and digital evidence cases, on request of a district attorney, law enforcement agency or authorized state officer, or at the Governor's direction. Creates a revolving fund.

ok:SB 1876.title: Service of process; modifying persons that may be appointed as agent. Effective date.
ok:SB 1876.summary: Changes who may be appointed as agent for service of process on foreign insurers, changes how appointments can be revoked, requires agent information to be given to the Insurance Commissioner, and allows alternate service in certain circumstances.

ok:SB 1877.title: State government; directing submission of certain reports to utilize certain centralized filing system; directing the Office of the Secretary of State to create and maintain certain centralized filing system. Effective date.
ok:SB 1877.summary: Directs state agencies in agriculture, courts, criminal justice, children's services and many other areas to submit required reports through a centralized state filing system, and removes some obsolete reports.

ok:SB 1894.title: Teachers; professional development programs; changing maximum number of professional development hours. Effective date. Emergency.
ok:SB 1894.summary: As passed by the Senate, removes the 150-hour limit on professional development or training that may be required of classroom teachers during any five-year period.

ok:SB 1916.title: Insurance Department; creating certain division within the Insurance Department;  establishing powers for certain conservator; allowing contacts. Effective date.
ok:SB 1916.summary: Creates a division within the Insurance Department to handle supervisions, conservatorships and receiverships of troubled insurers, with existing cases moved by January 1, 2028. Sets powers for supervisors and conservators, and limits disclosure of certain related records.

ok:SB 1946.title: Alcoholic beverages; decreasing alcohol license fee; allowing sale of certain sample spirits at certain events; removing certain production limits for distilleries. Effective date.
ok:SB 1946.summary: Raises from one to two the noncontiguous locations where a distiller may sell its spirits, allows them anywhere in the state rather than the same county, and allows sampling at public events. Areas used for on-premises consumption count as distillery premises.

ok:SB 1948.title: Fireworks; creating the Rocket's Red Glare Act; removing requirement to sell fireworks within certain time frame; prohibiting counties from restricting certain firework display under certain circumstances. Emergency.
ok:SB 1948.summary: Creates the Rocket's Red Glare Act: removes a retail fireworks sales time-frame requirement, bars counties from prohibiting private noncommercial outdoor displays when no burn ban or red flag warning applies, and removes a prohibition on certain skyrockets.

ok:SB 1983.title: Foster care; requiring the Department of Human Services to provide certain data to resource family partners. Effective date.
ok:SB 1983.summary: Requires the Department of Human Services to give private foster care placement agencies monthly aggregated, de-identified data on children awaiting placement, foster parent demographics, placement shortages, disruptions, separated siblings and distant placements.

ok:SB 1989.title: Oklahoma College Savings Plan; expanding options for making contributions to a 529 Savings Plan. Effective date.
ok:SB 1989.summary: Allows contributions to Oklahoma College Savings Plan accounts to be made by cash or by digital peer-to-peer and other digital payment networks.

ok:SB 2.title: Wind energy; providing setback requirements for certain affected counties; waiver; referral of question to eligible voters; zoning; construction; exemptions; database.
ok:SB 2.summary: As proposed by conference committee, bars commercial wind turbines within 2.5 times tip height of a dwelling or 1.5 times tip height of a nonparticipating property line unless the owner waives in writing; exempts small systems and projects with majority site control.

ok:SB 2011.title: Assault and battery; modifying scope of certain offenses. Effective date.
ok:SB 2011.summary: Adds contracted employees of county detention facilities to the staff covered by felony assault and battery offenses committed by people in Office of Juvenile Affairs custody, and makes technical corrections to criminal statutes.

ok:SB 2045.title: Schools; Grow Your Own Educator Program; eligible school district; funds; alternative certification pathway. Emergency.
ok:SB 2045.summary: Expands the Grow Your Own Educator Program to school staff completing an alternative teacher certification pathway and removes references to matching funds.

ok:SB 206.title: Emergency medical services; declaring emergency medical services to be essential services for certain purpose. Emergency.
ok:SB 206.summary: Treats emergency medical services from ambulance services managed by a municipality, county, ambulance district, tribal entity or other public entity as essential services, solely for federal funding eligibility.

ok:SB 2063.title: Entrepreneurial experience; enacting the Oklahoma Youth Entrepreneurs Promotion and Development Act of 2026. Effective date.
ok:SB 2063.summary: Exempts the first $1,000 of annual business income, and sales by businesses with under $1,000 in revenue, from state taxes for sole proprietorships run by people under 18, and exempts them from business licensing for up to 90 days a year.

ok:SB 2071.title: Agriculture; Oklahoma Milk and Milk Products Act; clarifying jurisdictional authority of dairy inspection and grading programs. Effective date.
ok:SB 2071.summary: Updates the Oklahoma Milk and Milk Products Act: changes definitions (including goats to hooved mammals), raises per-100-pound milk fees from one cent to two cents, and clarifies jurisdiction of dairy inspection and grading programs.

ok:SB 2084.title: Governmental Tort Claims Act; limiting settlement awards for wrongful termination claims; providing for inclusion of certain damages. Effective date.
ok:SB 2084.summary: Caps total settlements, arbitration awards, and judgments in state-law wrongful termination claims by faculty at state higher education institutions at two years of the faculty member's base pay and benefits, excluding earned retirement contributions and accrued wages or leave.

ok:SB 2104.title: Trusts; modifying requirements related to management and enforceability of trusts. Effective date.
ok:SB 2104.summary: Changes trust law: makes no-contest clauses enforceable unless the challenger proves just cause and good faith, and lets trustees obtain nonjudicial settlement of accounts after notice, with 60 days for beneficiaries to object.

ok:SB 2110.title: Agriculture; allowing sale of ungraded eggs in certain locations. Effective date.
ok:SB 2110.summary: Limits Oklahoma producers selling ungraded eggs from their own flocks directly to consumers, on or off the farm, to 150 dozen per month; they may sell graded eggs if they comply with grading rules. Effective November 1, 2026.

ok:SB 2180.title: Foreign lobbying; creating the Foreign Principal Lobbying Oversight Act. Effective date.
ok:SB 2180.summary: Requires paid agents lobbying for foreign governments, political parties or foreign-controlled businesses to register with the Secretary of State within 15 days, report changes, and face a misdemeanor and $500 fine for willful or knowing violations.

ok:SB 2182.title: Civil remedies; creating the Uniform Civil Remedies for Unauthorized Disclosure of Intimate Images Act. Effective date.
ok:SB 2182.summary: Creates a civil lawsuit for an identifiable person harmed by intentional or threatened disclosure of a private intimate image without consent, with damages, attorney fees and injunctive relief available and a four-year filing deadline.

ok:SB 237.title: Ad valorem tax; exemption for manufacturing facilities; defining battery energy storage system; exemption; applications. Effective date.
ok:SB 237.summary: Bars battery energy storage systems from the five-year property tax exemption for manufacturing facilities, and solar power generators from qualifying starting January 5, 2028, with no new applications from January 5, 2029. Defines battery energy storage system.

ok:SB 248.title: Tourism; Oklahoma Tourism and Recreation Department Revolving Fund; properties; funds appropriated; creating the Real Property Proceeds Revolving Fund; funds appropriated; interest. Effective date.
ok:SB 248.summary: Creates a Real Property Proceeds Revolving Fund for the Tourism and Recreation Department, holding money from selling or leasing department land (except concession leases) for maintenance and capital projects, not employee pay or transfers to other agencies.

ok:SB 259.title: Water and water rights; establishing procedures for permitting, monitoring, and reporting of groundwater use. Effective date.
ok:SB 259.summary: Requires the Water Resources Board to audit usage reports, investigate waste complaints and impose progressive fines for overuse. Treats groundwater use for data-center evaporative cooling as waste, issuing permits only for low-consumption, recirculating cooling systems.

ok:SB 382.title: Commercial driver licenses; prohibiting issuance to certain individuals; persons not to be licensed; Service Oklahoma to make certain verification. Effective date.
ok:SB 382.summary: As amended by the House, bars Service Oklahoma from issuing a commercial driver license to an applicant on the methamphetamine offender registry, and requires it to check by data match or other means that applicants are not listed.

ok:SB 423.title: Medical records; access; eliminating certain health care provider duties; authorizing certain fees. Effective date.
ok:SB 423.summary: Allows cost-based fees when patients request their records and raises the base fee for attorney, insurer and subpoena requests from $20 to up to $25. Raises the electronic-records fee cap from $200 to $270. Bars covered entities from using health information beyond what HIPAA allows.

ok:SB 504.title: Marriage; imposing age restriction on eligibility to marry; removing exceptions. Effective date.
ok:SB 504.summary: Bars marriage and marriage licenses for anyone under 18 by removing the exceptions that allowed it with parental consent or in other circumstances.

ok:SB 514.title: Schools; student eligibility; virtual charter school students; Oklahoma Secondary School Activities Association (OSSAA) activities; policies. Effective date.
ok:SB 514.summary: Lets school districts adopt policies allowing charter, virtual charter and otherwise-educated students to join their extracurricular activities, and bars public schools from joining an athletic association that excludes such students.

ok:SB 540.title: Professions and occupations; enacting the Dentist and Dental Hygienist Compact and authorizing the Governor to enter into Compact with certain jurisdictions. Effective date.
ok:SB 540.summary: Enacts the Dentist and Dental Hygienist Compact and directs the Governor to enter it, letting dentists and dental hygienists licensed in one participating state obtain a compact privilege to practice in other participating states.

ok:SB 563.title: County planning commission; personnel; chair of the board; composition of board. Effective date. Emergency.
ok:SB 563.summary: Makes the county commission chair or designee a member of the county planning commission, sets two-year terms, and requires county boards of adjustment to have three, five, or seven appointed resident property owners.

ok:SB 604.title: Motor vehicles; definitions; merging multiple versions of statues; termination, cancellation, or nonrenewal of a franchise; repealer. Effective date.
ok:SB 604.summary: As amended by the House, merges duplicate versions of two motor vehicle statutes, on definitions and on franchise termination, cancellation or nonrenewal, into single versions and repeals the older versions.

ok:SB 633.title: Children; Children's Code;  enacting Leo's Law; fentanyl testing; child endangerment; appropriating funds. Effective date.
ok:SB 633.summary: Enacts Leo's Law: requires the Department of Human Services to seek consent for drug screening, including fentanyl testing, in certain child welfare cases, creates a fentanyl testing revolving fund, and expands the child endangerment offense.

ok:SB 65.title: Substance abuse services; authorizing the possession, acquisition, distribution and administration of emergency opioid antagonists and adulterant test strips by any person. Effective date. Emergency.
ok:SB 65.summary: Allows any person to possess, obtain, distribute and administer emergency opioid antagonists, and provides criminal and civil immunity for doing so.

ok:SB 650.title: Public finance; cabinet secretary approval for salary increases in excess of specified percentage; limitation; rules; employee categories. Effective date. Emergency.
ok:SB 650.summary: Requires cabinet secretary approval for executive branch salary increases above 10 percent in a fiscal year, caps bonuses at 10 percent of base salary, and requires agencies to set maximum bonuses and performance measures by rule. Exempts agency heads and some professional positions.

ok:SB 667.title: Chiropractors; requiring use of licensure portals; modifying certain licensing requirements; modifying requirements for notification of disapproval. Effective date.
ok:SB 667.summary: Requires chiropractic license applicants to use the Board's online portal and show a Doctor of Chiropractic degree from an accredited program, requires written reasons when a relocation application is disapproved, and repeals chiropractic claims consultant registration.

ok:SB 710.title: Teacher preparation; establishment of TeachForwardOK; allowing Commission for Educational Quality and Accountability to select more than one applicant under certain circumstances. Emergency.
ok:SB 710.summary: Lets the Commission for Educational Quality and Accountability select more than one approved teacher education program to receive a monetary award under the TeachForwardOK pilot program, if funds are sufficient.

ok:SB 740.title: Child sexual abuse; creating the Cindy Clemishire Act; creating Trey's Law. Effective date.
ok:SB 740.summary: As amended by the House, voids settlement terms concealing details of child sexual abuse or exploitation claims, keeps victim-identifying information confidential, allows prosecuting sexual crimes against children at any time, and excuses health professionals from reporting minor-to-minor incidents revealed in medical histories absent coercion, exploitation, threat or intimidation.

ok:SB 893.title: Property and critical infrastructure; creating the Military Installation and Critical Infrastructure Protection Act of 2025. Effective date.
ok:SB 893.summary: Bars foreign principals from foreign adversary countries from owning or acquiring agricultural land, or controlling real property within 10 miles of military installations or critical infrastructure. Requires divestiture within 180 days and registration within 60 days, with a national security agreement exception.

ok:SB 904.title: Gender transition procedures; prohibiting certain use of public funds and state facilities; providing criminal penalty. Emergency.
ok:SB 904.summary: Bars use of state funds, including Medicaid, and state facilities for gender transition procedures (surgeries, puberty blockers, cross-sex hormones) for minors and adults. State officers or employees who intentionally violate it commit a misdemeanor.

ok:SJR 50.title: Constitutional amendment; Medicaid funding.
ok:SJR 50.summary: Refers to voters a constitutional amendment ending the state's duty to cover low-income adults under Medicaid if the federal match falls below 90 percent, and repealing Article XXV-A Sections 1-4, replacing them with statutes, if the federal match is modified.

ok:SJR 52.title: Joint resolution; approving certain proposed permanent rules of the Oklahoma Health Care Authority.
ok:SJR 52.summary: Approves 20 proposed permanent rules of the Oklahoma Health Care Authority that meet the definition of major rules and directs the Secretary of State to distribute copies of the resolution.

or:HB 4004.title: Relating to natural resources; and prescribing an effective date.
or:HB 4004.summary: Changes natural resource laws, including waiving certain forestland assessment back taxes when disqualification results from insects or disease, allowing Water Resources Department time extensions for water right permit holders, and modifying engineer requirements.

or:HB 4005.title: Relating to Water Professionals Appreciation Week; and prescribing an effective date.
or:HB 4005.summary: Designates the first Saturday of October through the following Sunday each year as Water Professionals Appreciation Week.

or:HB 4007.title: Relating to transportation; and prescribing an effective date.
or:HB 4007.summary: Defines "powered micromobility device" (up to 28 mph, under 100 pounds), applies bicycle rules to riders, lets local governments restrict them on bike lanes and sidewalks, extends youth helmet rules to them, and creates offenses for selling uncertified batteries or impostor e-bikes.

or:HB 4012.title: Relating to labor contractors; and prescribing an effective date.
or:HB 4012.summary: Directs the Construction Contractors Board and the Bureau of Labor and Industries to run a targeted assessment initiative on unlicensed labor contractors at construction sites and report by October 1, 2027.

or:HB 4013.title: Relating to labor standards.
or:HB 4013.summary: Clarifies which federal rules the Bureau of Labor and Industries must follow when adopting rules on the hours minors may work.

or:HB 4016.title: Relating to tax compliance; and prescribing an effective date.
or:HB 4016.summary: Requires public contractors to certify and maintain tax compliance as a condition of a public contract starting January 1, 2027, and directs the Secretary of State to study collecting compliance information through business registration.

or:HB 4017.title: Relating to use of campaign contributions; and declaring an emergency.
or:HB 4017.summary: Allows candidates and officeholders' campaign committees to spend contributions on specified security expenses, and lets them convert certain security items to personal use after leaving office without it counting as a gift.

or:HB 4018.title: Relating to elections; and declaring an emergency.
or:HB 4018.summary: Changes campaign finance law, including in-kind contribution rules and disclosure by organizations making political communications, and lets corporations and labor unions run separate segregated funds, registered as political committees, financed only by individuals' contributions.

or:HB 4020.title: Relating to permits; and prescribing an effective date.
or:HB 4020.summary: Requires the departments of Environmental Quality, State Lands, Energy, and Geology and Mineral Industries to cite legal authority when denying permits, give applicants a guide to contesting denials, and develop a permit-timeliness performance measure by 2029.

or:HB 4022.title: Relating to children's literacy.
or:HB 4022.summary: Creates the Oregon Imagination Library Program, run by the Department of Early Learning and Care, to provide a free book each month to eligible children, with a dedicated account for funding.

or:HB 4024.title: Relating to speculative ticket sales; and prescribing an effective date.
or:HB 4024.summary: Bars ticket resellers from offering or reselling an admission ticket unless they have it or have written authorization to obtain it from the operator or seller.

or:HB 4025.title: Relating to the residential rates of public utilities; and prescribing an effective date.
or:HB 4025.summary: Allows residential rate increases for public utilities other than electric and gas utilities to take effect from November 1 to March 31.

or:HB 4027.title: Relating to the Bureau of Labor and Industries; and prescribing an effective date.
or:HB 4027.summary: Directs the Department of Consumer and Business Services to set an assessment rate funding a new BOLI Expenses Fund with a 12-month reserve, and raises the cap on the prevailing wage fee paid by public agencies.

or:HB 4031.title: Relating to the siting of renewable energy facilities; and prescribing an effective date.
or:HB 4031.summary: Exempts certain renewable energy facilities from needing an Energy Facility Siting Council site certificate if they qualify for federal tax credits, are in service by 2030, and file a local land use application by December 31, 2028.

or:HB 4034.title: Relating to animal rescue entities.
or:HB 4034.summary: Changes animal rescue entity law: only those keeping 10 or more animals for over two consecutive business days need a license, the State Department of Agriculture replaces the State Veterinarian as enforcer, and the department sets record-keeping and audit rules.

or:HB 4036.title: Relating to affordable housing; and declaring an emergency.
or:HB 4036.summary: Creates the Housing Opportunity, Longevity and Durability Fund, using state bond proceeds to preserve at-risk affordable housing, and requires a December 1, 2026 report on barriers to affordable housing production.

or:HB 4037.title: Relating to housing; and prescribing an effective date.
or:HB 4037.summary: Changes several housing laws, including loan terms for city and county affordable housing programs, limits on plan review for housing of two or fewer units, and an approval process for housing meeting clear and objective standards.

or:HB 4039.title: Relating to medical assistance; and declaring an emergency.
or:HB 4039.summary: Requires the Oregon Health Authority to develop a transparent, data-driven process for setting capitation rates for coordinated care organizations.

or:HB 4041.title: Relating to public safety; and declaring an emergency.
or:HB 4041.summary: Changes criminal laws: narrows which license suspensions support criminal driving-while-suspended charges, sets felony fleeing-police sentencing categories by prior convictions and injury, sets a 120-day deadline for nonunanimous-verdict post-conviction petitions, and adds court review of releases from sentence-computation errors.

or:HB 4043.title: Relating to courts.
or:HB 4043.summary: Authorizes the State Treasurer to issue bonds to renovate or expand courthouses, and requires community mental health directors to notify the court within two judicial days if a defendant found unfit to proceed is not complying with restoration services.

or:HB 4045.title: Relating to search warrant response time limits; and declaring an emergency.
or:HB 4045.summary: Requires social media platforms to respond to search warrants for records within 72 hours, and other communications providers within five business days, when the investigation concerns stalking or domestic violence.

or:HB 4047.title: Relating to rural emergency hospitals; and prescribing an effective date.
or:HB 4047.summary: Requires the Oregon Health Authority to adopt rules and procedures letting a hospital apply for a license as a rural emergency hospital.

or:HB 4052.title: Relating to a tax credit for de novo banks; and prescribing an effective date.
or:HB 4052.summary: Creates a corporate excise tax credit for newly chartered Oregon banks, up to $1 million a year for three consecutive tax years, limited to tax owed, with unused credit carried forward up to three years.

or:HB 4060.title: Relating to fluorescent lamps; and declaring an emergency.
or:HB 4060.summary: Delays until January 1, 2030 a ban on selling certain fluorescent lamps to buyers with facilities over one million square feet, and exempts residential and long term care facilities from submitting lamp replacement plans.

or:HB 4066.title: Relating to education; and declaring an emergency.
or:HB 4066.summary: Changes education laws, including barring the student member of the OHSU board from collective bargaining matters affecting students, allowing education service district board stipends, and having Portland State University report on a farmworker labor standards study.

or:HB 4069.title: Relating to the safety of behavioral health workers; and prescribing an effective date.
or:HB 4069.summary: Requires behavioral health employers to implement a written safety policy or plan for the physical safety of the people working for them.

or:HB 4070.title: Relating to health care; and prescribing an effective date.
or:HB 4070.summary: Requires the Oregon Health Authority and coordinated care organizations to apply behavioral health treatment limits no more stringently than medical and surgical limits in Medicaid, and changes quality review and telehealth reimbursement rules.

or:HB 4072.title: Relating to arraignment; and prescribing an effective date.
or:HB 4072.summary: Excludes normal business hours when the court is closed, in addition to holidays, Saturdays and Sundays, from the 96-hour arraignment deadline for defendants not in custody.

or:HB 4075.title: Relating to hospital finance; and declaring an emergency.
or:HB 4075.summary: Requires the State Treasurer to guarantee an eligible rural hospital loan for cash shortages or debt refinancing by April 1, 2027, with up to $44 million from the Unclaimed Property and Estates Fund available to cover the guarantee.

or:HB 4076.title: Relating to energy; and prescribing an effective date.
or:HB 4076.summary: Requires the Energy Facility Siting Council to treat the 'reasons justify an exception' standard as met for energy facilities using an existing facility's surplus grid interconnection with no transmission lines over two miles; lets local governments apply similar reasoning to renewable facility farmland exceptions.

or:HB 4077.title: Relating to the securitization of a public utility's insurance program; and prescribing an effective date.
or:HB 4077.summary: Allows a public utility, with Public Utility Commission approval, to issue bonds and securitize debt for costs of a self-insurance or captive insurance program.

or:HB 4079.title: Relating to policies for when federal immigration authorities enter public education property; and prescribing an effective date.
or:HB 4079.summary: Requires school district boards and public higher education governing boards to adopt policies for notifying students, employees and (for K-12) parents when federal immigration authorities are confirmed on school property or campus for immigration enforcement, effective September 30, 2026.

or:HB 4082.title: Relating to housing for older persons; and prescribing an effective date.
or:HB 4082.summary: Lets cities and Metro add sites to urban growth boundaries for manufactured dwelling parks or housing for older persons, capped at 100 acres for cities of 25,000 or more and 50 acres for smaller cities.

or:HB 4083.title: Relating to behavioral health care providers; and prescribing an effective date.
or:HB 4083.summary: Requires the Oregon Health Authority to adopt a uniform behavioral health provider credentialing process and electronic system by June 30, 2027, bars coordinated care organizations from adding credentialing requirements, and allows supervision across different license types.

or:HB 4084.title: Relating to economic development; and prescribing an effective date.
or:HB 4084.summary: Creates a Joint Permitting Council to run a fast-track permit program, has agencies publish permit catalogs, updates enterprise zone rules and restricts their use for data centers, and modifies the new-jobs tax credit.

or:HB 4088.title: Relating to health; and declaring an emergency.
or:HB 4088.summary: Bars public bodies from assisting federal or other-state investigations of reproductive or gender-affirming care lawful in Oregon, bars the Governor from extraditing people charged elsewhere over it, makes certain records confidential, and limits discipline of direct entry midwives in specified cases.

or:HB 4089.title: Relating to criminal offenses related to work.
or:HB 4089.summary: Expands the crime of theft of services to include partial payments, and makes knowingly contracting with an unlicensed labor contractor a crime punishable by up to 364 days in jail and a $6,250 fine.

or:HB 4097.title: Relating to the Oregon Ocean Science Trust.
or:HB 4097.summary: Authorizes the Oregon Ocean Science Trust to create and maintain a tax-exempt 501(c)(3) entity to advance the trust's mission.

or:HB 4099.title: Relating to a task force on veterans in crisis; and prescribing an effective date.
or:HB 4099.summary: Creates the Task Force on Responding to Veterans in Crisis to propose a crisis response team of at least two trained people in each county, with funding, training and law enforcement data-system changes, reporting by September 15, 2026.

or:HB 4100.title: Relating to bulk fuel terminals; and declaring an emergency.
or:HB 4100.summary: Requires owners or operators of bulk oil and liquid fuel terminals to obtain a certificate of financial responsibility from the Department of Environmental Quality and preempts stricter local financial assurance requirements.

or:HB 4102.title: Relating to Department of Environmental Quality regulatory processes; and prescribing an effective date.
or:HB 4102.summary: Modifies the Department of Environmental Quality's authority to enter agreements with regulated entities to expedite or enhance a regulatory process.

or:HB 4107.title: Relating to urgent care centers.
or:HB 4107.summary: Requires urgent care centers to publish specified information, offer specified services, and generally have at least one licensed health care provider on site during operating hours.

or:HB 4108.title: Relating to annexation of land noncontiguous to a city.
or:HB 4108.summary: Lets the City of Eugene annex noncontiguous land without a hearing or vote when all owners petition and the land is inside the urban growth boundary, planned for residential or mixed use, connected to water, wastewater and stormwater services, and accessible by public road.

or:HB 4111.title: Relating to immigration-related practices; and prescribing an effective date.
or:HB 4111.summary: Makes a party's or witness's immigration status inadmissible in civil cases, with exceptions, bars employers from retaliating against employees who update work authorization information, and adds immigration status to the law enforcement profiling definition.

or:HB 4114.title: Relating to law enforcement operations; and declaring an emergency.
or:HB 4114.summary: Lets property owners and occupants sue an individual who, under color of law, enters property without a court-issued warrant or recognized exception, except people suable under 42 U.S.C. 1983; prevailing plaintiffs get attorney fees.

or:HB 4115.title: Relating to health care providers; and prescribing an effective date.
or:HB 4115.summary: Makes certain caregiver criminal records checks last three years and portable across care settings, and requires coordinated care organizations to reimburse behavioral health providers back to their Medicaid enrollment application date.

or:HB 4116.title: Relating to consumer finance loans; and prescribing an effective date.
or:HB 4116.summary: Declares that Oregon does not want a 1980 federal law amendment (section 521 of DIDMCA) to apply to consumer finance loans made in the state, and specifies who the state's consumer finance laws cover and what a license application must include.

or:HB 4120.title: Relating to smoking policies in residential tenancies.
or:HB 4120.summary: Lets landlords ban smoking of lit tobacco in units and interior common areas on 180 days’ notice, for existing tenants in attached units, if a posted smoking area is provided; excludes accessible units and waits until fixed terms end.

or:HB 4121.title: Relating to emergency management.
or:HB 4121.summary: Creates an authority to coordinate emergency management, requires state agencies to designate emergency management liaisons, changes Resilience Hub requirements, and establishes grant programs for emergencies.

or:HB 4124.title: Relating to the state post-secondary education system; and declaring an emergency.
or:HB 4124.summary: Directs the Higher Education Coordinating Commission to study Oregon's post-secondary education system, with a preliminary report due October 1, 2026 and a final report due April 1, 2027.

or:HB 4130.title: Relating to farm use.
or:HB 4130.summary: Counts land under farm-product and biofuel processing facilities, plus adjacent land used with them, as farm use for special property tax assessment, on application to the county assessor by April 1.

or:HB 4132.title: Relating to veterans; and prescribing an effective date.
or:HB 4132.summary: Changes veterans laws, including setting director qualifications, creating a suicide prevention and workforce grant program, raising the Veteran Educational Bridge Grant cap from $5,000 to $10,000, and ordering a veterans' treatment court access study.

or:HB 4134.title: Relating to funding for natural resource matters; prescribing an effective date; and providing for revenue raising that requires approval by a three-fifths majority.
or:HB 4134.summary: Raises the state transient lodging tax rate from 1.5 percent to 2.75 percent for charges on or after January 1, 2027, directs how the added revenue is distributed, and renames a wildlife subaccount.

or:HB 4137.title: Relating to the transfer of interest in motor vehicles.
or:HB 4137.summary: Lets a vehicle's previous owner notify the court that they transferred their interest, and are not liable for a traffic citation, instead of making a first appearance.

or:HB 4138.title: Relating to limitations on the actions of public employees; and declaring an emergency.
or:HB 4138.summary: Requires on-duty officers, including federal and out-of-state, to display a name or ID number, agency name and badge, and bars facial coverings with exceptions. Bars public employees from knowingly aiding federal or out-of-state agencies in actions based on protected conduct, class status or unlawful searches.

or:HB 4144.title: Relating to batteries.
or:HB 4144.summary: Requires battery producers to join a producer responsibility organization and run a battery collection and recycling program, with the Department of Environmental Quality enforcing it through a new fund and civil penalties.

or:HB 4145.title: Relating to firearms; and declaring an emergency.
or:HB 4145.summary: Delays the start of Ballot Measure 114's firearm permit-to-purchase rules and large-capacity magazine ban from March 15, 2026 to January 1, 2028.

or:HB 4148.title: Relating to local taxation; and prescribing an effective date.
or:HB 4148.summary: Lets local lodging tax revenue fund resiliency grants for small restaurants and lodgings, and changes the required split from at least 70 percent tourism and up to 30 percent local services to at least 50 percent and up to 50 percent.

or:HB 4151.title: Relating to initiating a false report.
or:HB 4151.summary: Makes a false report a Class C felony, up to five years and a $125,000 fine, if it intentionally causes an enhanced law enforcement response and recklessly causes serious injury or death; removes mandatory minimum jail terms for false reports involving SWAT deployment.

or:HB 4153.title: Relating to farm stores.
or:HB 4153.summary: Allows farm stores selling the operation's own farm products as a permitted use on exclusive farm use and mixed farm-forest land, limited to 10,000 square feet of enclosed space and minimum tract and farm-use acreage, with agri-tourism activities.

or:HB 4157.title: Relating to hearsay; and prescribing an effective date.
or:HB 4157.summary: Makes certain hearsay statements about specified sex crimes admissible in evidence even if the person who made them is available to testify.

or:HB 4159.title: Relating to the Oregon Government Ethics Commission.
or:HB 4159.summary: Requires at least one Oregon Government Ethics Commission member to have local government experience, and provides that attorney-client privilege is not waived when someone gives the commission information about an ethics complaint.

or:HB 4160.title: Relating to procedures for medical emergencies in schools; and prescribing an effective date.
or:HB 4160.summary: Requires schools to have a cardiac emergency response plan, including automated external defibrillator requirements, as part of their medical emergency procedures, starting July 1, 2027.

or:HB 4161.title: Relating to use of official position or office; and declaring an emergency.
or:HB 4161.summary: Exempts from the ban on using office for financial gain food and drinks a public body provides at meetings or official events, and merchandise from a public body costing up to $100 a calendar year.

or:HB 4177.title: Relating to public meetings; and prescribing an effective date.
or:HB 4177.summary: Restates the ban on a governing body quorum using serial communications to deliberate outside public meetings, lists exempt communications, shifts notice and recording duties from governing bodies to public bodies, and changes how violations can be cured.

or:HB 4178.title: Relating to rounding procedures in transactions; and declaring an emergency.
or:HB 4178.summary: Allows some places of public accommodation to round in-person transaction totals to the nearest five cents under a posted policy, with an exception for customers paying exact change.

or:HB 4179.title: Relating to entities created by the Oregon Health and Science University.
or:HB 4179.summary: Allows Oregon Health and Science University to create a nonprofit corporation for clinical care if the university is a corporate member, and treats physicians, naturopathic physicians and dentists providing patient care for it as acting within state employment for liability purposes.

or:HB 5203.title: Relating to state financial administration; and declaring an emergency.
or:HB 5203.summary: Approves new or increased fees set by state agencies and boards, including a $125 licensing predetermination petition fee for counselors and psychologists and a $25 annual psilocybin worker permit.

or:HB 5204.title: Relating to state financial administration; and declaring an emergency.
or:HB 5204.summary: Adjusts the 2025-27 state budget by changing General Fund appropriations and agency spending limits, such as raising by $4.4 million the limit for State Data Center charges and out-of-state tax reporting contracts.

or:SB 1501.title: Relating to the Moda Center; and declaring an emergency.
or:SB 1501.summary: Lets the state negotiate a joint authority to own the Moda Center, creates an Oregon Arena Fund, and states intent to issue $365 million in debt. Moves Rose Quarter income tax withholding to the fund after conditions, including a Trail Blazers sale and 20-year lease.

or:SB 1502.title: Relating to proposed legislative measures to be filed by the Secretary of State; and prescribing an effective date.
or:SB 1502.summary: Directs the Secretary of State to file a proposed bill for the 2027 session setting out the Secretary's recommended changes to campaign finance limits and reporting requirements.

or:SB 1504.title: Relating to the administration of epinephrine.
or:SB 1504.summary: Replaces "autoinjectable" with "premeasured dose" epinephrine, which can be given by autoinjector, intranasal device or another method set by rule, in school self-administration policies, liability protections and allergy training.

or:SB 1507.title: Relating to revenue; and prescribing an effective date.
or:SB 1507.summary: Updates Oregon's link to the federal tax code, raises the earned income tax credit percentage, disconnects from federal deductions for auto loan interest and bonus depreciation, and creates a new-jobs tax credit for 2026 through 2031.

or:SB 1509.title: Relating to electors of President and Vice President of the United States; and prescribing an effective date.
or:SB 1509.summary: Sets registration and party-affiliation requirements for presidential elector candidates, and has the Secretary of State invalidate an elector's ballot cast contrary to the pledge, declare the office vacant, and have remaining electors fill it.

or:SB 1510.title: Relating to taxation; and prescribing an effective date.
or:SB 1510.summary: Makes technical changes to tax laws, including extending the pass-through business alternative income tax through 2027, expanding the film production credit to commercials, and extending the property tax exemption for cargo containers.

or:SB 1511.title: Relating to the estate tax; prescribing an effective date.
or:SB 1511.summary: Replaces the $1 million estate tax exclusion with a $2.5 million deduction, phases in tax above it, raises the filing threshold, and adjusts rates, for decedents dying on or after January 1, 2027.

or:SB 1512.title: Relating to workforce development.
or:SB 1512.summary: Expands the goals of the Prosperity 10,000 workforce program and requires the Higher Education Coordinating Commission to award grants to local workforce development boards to administer it.

or:SB 1513.title: Relating to real estate professionals; and declaring an emergency.
or:SB 1513.summary: Delays until July 1, 2027, the rule barring real estate teams from using "realty" or "real estate" in their names.

or:SB 1515.title: Relating to wrongful convictions; and declaring an emergency.
or:SB 1515.summary: Changes the process for wrongful-conviction compensation petitions and creates, until January 2, 2031, a post-conviction relief process for convictions based on specified discredited forensic science.

or:SB 1516.title: Relating to public safety; and declaring an emergency.
or:SB 1516.summary: Limits law enforcement use of license plate readers to listed purposes, caps most data retention at 30 days, lets people sue vendors for intentional or grossly negligent misuse, and says standing pretrial release orders do not limit a magistrate's release decision.

or:SB 1517.title: Relating to civil litigation; and declaring an emergency.
or:SB 1517.summary: Allows operators of sport, fitness and recreation activities to require participants, or parents of minors, to sign releases of ordinary-negligence injury claims. Releases cannot cover gross negligence, safety equipment maintenance, abuse, or vehicle use.

or:SB 1519.title: Relating to total disability.
or:SB 1519.summary: Sets temporary and permanent total disability pay, for injuries on or after Jan. 1, 2027, at 75 percent of wages up to 75 percent of the average weekly wage plus 65 percent of wages above that, capped at 133 percent of the average.

or:SB 1521.title: Relating to local requirements to develop affordable housing.
or:SB 1521.summary: Bars Portland-area cities and counties from enforcing affordable-unit requirements on multiunit developments unless they first calculate developers' expected losses and offset them; applies to rentals from 2028 and all housing from 2029.

or:SB 1523.title: Relating to electronic access to residential tenancies; and prescribing an effective date.
or:SB 1523.summary: Requires landlords to offer an alternative to tenant portals on request, bars requiring rent payment by portal, card or electronic means, and changes the processing fees landlords may charge for credit or debit card or portal payments.

or:SB 1527.title: Relating to health care.
or:SB 1527.summary: Bars cost-sharing for cervical cancer screenings and follow-up examinations in certain private health insurance and in Oregon Educators Benefit Board and Public Employees' Benefit Board coverage.

or:SB 1532.title: Relating to services for vulnerable persons; and declaring an emergency.
or:SB 1532.summary: Changes laws on long term care facilities and developmental disability services, including limits on license conditions after immediate-jeopardy findings, a model consent form for room cameras, and a differentiated rate model for live-in direct support professionals.

or:SB 1533.title: Relating to the rights of children in care; and declaring an emergency.
or:SB 1533.summary: Changes the Oregon Foster Children's Bill of Rights and Sibling Bill of Rights, and requires the Department of Human Services to tell parents and guardians that its representatives cannot give them legal advice.

or:SB 1535.title: Relating to child care; and prescribing an effective date.
or:SB 1535.summary: Lets the Early Learning Council change the priority given to families receiving temporary assistance in the Employment Related Day Care subsidy program, and creates a work group, ending in 2029, on child care provider liability insurance.

or:SB 1538.title: Relating to conduct of public education; and prescribing an effective date.
or:SB 1538.summary: Prohibits discrimination in education based on immigration or citizenship status, with limited exceptions, and adds requirements for Attorney General model policies on immigration enforcement at public schools; districts must give employees the model policies. Takes effect July 1, 2026.

or:SB 1544.title: Relating to transportation; and prescribing an effective date.
or:SB 1544.summary: Ends the requirement that motor vehicle dismantlers get local government approval to renew certificates, and adds intergovernmental entities serving tribes to the definition of public transportation 'qualified entity'.

or:SB 1546.title: Relating to artificial intelligence companions.
or:SB 1546.summary: Requires operators of AI companion platforms to notify users they are interacting with artificial output when a reasonable person might think it is a human, and to maintain a protocol for detecting suicidal or self-harm ideation, including crisis lifeline referral.

or:SB 1547.title: Relating to licensed behavioral health and wellness practitioners; and prescribing an effective date.
or:SB 1547.summary: Authorizes the Board of Psychology to license behavioral health and wellness practitioners, defines their practice, bars use of the title without a license, and requires them to report certain types of abuse.

or:SB 1551.title: Relating to fire hardening of residential properties; and prescribing an effective date.
or:SB 1551.summary: Voids recorded-document provisions that bar fire-hardened building materials or removal of non-fire-hardened ones, and planned-community rules that effectively prohibit such materials. An owner’s application is deemed approved unless the association denies it or requests modifications in writing within 90 days.

or:SB 1556.title: Relating to representation of persons in the magistrate division of the Oregon Tax Court; and prescribing an effective date.
or:SB 1556.summary: Consolidates the statutes on who may represent parties before the Oregon Tax Court's magistrate division, for proceedings started on or after January 1, 2027.

or:SB 1561.title: Relating to restoration of dwellings damaged by involuntary causes.
or:SB 1561.summary: Requires local governments to approve applications to restore or replace dwellings damaged or destroyed by natural or other involuntary events if criteria are met, including no more than 25 percent added floor area; approvals are not land use decisions.

or:SB 1565.title: Relating to snowmobiles; and prescribing an effective date.
or:SB 1565.summary: Raises the snowmobile registration and renewal fees from $10 to $30.

or:SB 1567.title: Relating to mixed income housing; and prescribing an effective date.
or:SB 1567.summary: Directs the Housing and Community Services Department to create a below-market loan program for mixed income housing, with $20 million moved from the Housing Project Revolving Loan Fund; initial rules are due by January 1, 2027.

or:SB 1570.title: Relating to protections in health care facilities; and prescribing an effective date.
or:SB 1570.summary: Requires hospitals to adopt policies for law enforcement arrivals and designate non-public areas; requires hospitals and federally qualified health centers to treat immigration status as protected health information and not disclose it for law enforcement unless law or a court order requires.

or:SB 1573.title: Relating to syringe service programs.
or:SB 1573.summary: As introduced, bars syringe service programs from operating mobile or temporary locations within 2,000 feet of a school or licensed child care facility, and lets any person sue a violating program for damages.

or:SB 1575.title: Relating to hospice licensure; and declaring an emergency.
or:SB 1575.summary: Adds requirements for initial hospice licenses, bars people excluded from Medicare or Medicaid or found liable for fraud from owning a hospice, and bars most new hospice licenses until state rulemaking is complete.

or:SB 1585.title: Relating to matching grants for cities; and prescribing an effective date.
or:SB 1585.summary: Caps the cash match that cities of 20,000 or fewer residents must provide for certain state matching grants, including school-area safety projects, at 3% to 12% of project costs by population, and lets them spend grants on planning and engineering.

or:SB 1587.title: Relating to data brokers; and prescribing an effective date.
or:SB 1587.summary: Bars public bodies from giving personal information to data brokers unless the broker attests it will not be passed to anyone who will use it for federal immigration enforcement, with exceptions for public records law and court orders.

or:SB 1590.title: Relating to public lands; and declaring an emergency.
or:SB 1590.summary: Prohibits public bodies from assisting the federal government with privatizing certain federally owned lands; the prohibition expires January 2, 2032.

or:SB 1594.title: Relating to immigration; and declaring an emergency.
or:SB 1594.summary: Directs the Department of Justice to consult the Office of Immigrant and Refugee Advancement when developing or updating model policies that limit immigration enforcement at public facilities.

or:SB 1596.title: Relating to play-based learning.
or:SB 1596.summary: Directs the State Board of Education to allow play-based learning to count as instructional time for students in kindergarten through grade five.

or:SB 1597.title: Relating to energy generation; prescribing an effective date.
or:SB 1597.summary: Requires electric utilities to disclose to customers, and energy facility developers to disclose to the utility and public, the costs of storing nuclear waste produced in generating electricity.

or:SB 1598.title: Relating to access to health services; and declaring an emergency.
or:SB 1598.summary: Requires certain health plans to cover preventive services under federal rules as of June 30, 2025, plus immunizations the Public Health Officer recommends, and lets the Officer issue standing prescription orders for disease control.

or:SB 1601.title: Relating to state financial administration; and declaring an emergency.
or:SB 1601.summary: Makes budget-related law changes, including extending the deadline to classify existing sex offender registrants from December 1, 2026 to June 30, 2030, removing the cap on lottery transfers to the County Fair Account, and transferring certain funds to the General Fund.

or:SB 5701.title: Relating to state financial administration; and declaring an emergency.
or:SB 5701.summary: Changes the amounts of state bonds authorized for 2025-27, including raising LIFT affordable rental housing bonds to about $543.8 million, and authorizes bonds or certificates of participation for Moda Center capital improvements.

or:SB 5702.title: Relating to state financial administration; and declaring an emergency.
or:SB 5702.summary: Sets spending limits for state capital construction projects, including $365 million for Moda Center improvements and $540 million for the LIFT affordable rental housing program, and extends some project approval expiration dates.

or:SB 5703.title: Relating to state financial administration; and declaring an emergency.
or:SB 5703.summary: Adjusts 2025-27 lottery and criminal fine account allocations to several agencies, including lowering the State School Fund amount from $606.5 million to $584.2 million and raising amounts for business development operations and the Regional Solutions Program.

or:SCR 209.title: Establishing deadlines for presession-filed legislative measures for the 2027 regular session of the Eighty-fourth Legislative Assembly.
or:SCR 209.summary: Sets deadlines for presession-filed measures for the 2027 session: draft requests due September 11, 2026, drafts delivered by December 1, and submission for introduction by December 11, 2026.

pa:HB 1604.title: An Act amending Title 53 (Municipalities Generally) of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes, in employees, providing for mandatory firearms training for certain officers.
pa:HB 1604.summary: Requires police officers in a second class A county (population 565,000 to 600,000) to complete certified in-service firearms training, including simulation, at least four times a year; instructors and agency chiefs keep records, and noncompliant officers go on administrative leave.

pa:HB 2542.title: An Act amending the act of June 3, 1937 (P.L.1333, No.320), known as the Pennsylvania Election Code,  in returns of primaries and elections, further providing for appeals to court from decisions of the county board and for Secretary of the Commonwealth to tabulate, compute and canvass returns; and, in recounts and contests, further providing for entry and effect of decision and providing for appeal.
pa:HB 2542.summary: Requires courts to decide county-board appeals and election contests within seven days of filing, allows a one-day appeal to the Supreme Court, sets a fifth-Tuesday deadline for certifying general election results, and requires notice to legislative leaders seven days ahead if it may be missed.

ri:HB 7002.title: AN ACT RELATING TO BUSINESSES AND PROFESSIONS -- BOARD OF MEDICAL LICENSURE AND DISCIPLINE
ri:HB 7002.summary: As introduced, bars healthcare providers and health plans from denying payment of a medical bill solely because it arose from a third-party claim.

ri:HB 7020.title: AN ACT RELATING TO BUSINESSES AND PROFESSIONS -- VETERINARY PRACTICE
ri:HB 7020.summary: Allows a veterinarian to establish a client-patient relationship through live audio-video means, if licensed in Rhode Island and with client consent, and requires keeping documentation for at least one year.

ri:HB 7046.title: AN ACT RELATING TO TAXATION -- PROPERTY SUBJECT TO TAXATION
ri:HB 7046.summary: Exempts the real and tangible personal property of Blithewold, Inc., at 101 Ferry Road in Bristol, from taxation.

ri:HB 7064.title: AN ACT RELATING TO BUSINESS AND PROFESSIONS -- MENTAL HEALTH COUNSELORS AND MARRIAGE AND FAMILY THERAPISTS
ri:HB 7064.summary: Changes the direct client contact hours required to license marriage and family therapists and associates, and allows licensure without an exam for therapists licensed in another state for a year or more.

ri:HB 7122.title: AN ACT RELATING TO TAXATION -- PROPERTY SUBJECT TO TAXATION
ri:HB 7122.summary: Exempts the real and tangible personal property of Community MusicWorks in Providence from taxation, retroactive to December 31, 2025.

ri:HB 7183.title: AN ACT RELATING TO HEALTH AND SAFETY -- BUILDING BENCHMARKING AND REPORTING ACT OF 2026
ri:HB 7183.summary: Requires owners of residential and nonresidential buildings and campuses of 25,000 or more gross square feet to report annual energy use, starting May 2028 for 50,000 or more and May 2030 for smaller ones; the Office of Energy Resources publishes it.

ri:HB 7298.title: AN ACT RELATING TO TAXATION -- LEVY AND ASSESSMENT OF LOCAL TAXES
ri:HB 7298.summary: Lets the town of Tiverton set different property tax rates for different classes of property, using an annual assessor's list of valuations and each class's share of the tax levy.

ri:HB 7332.title: AN ACT RELATING TO PUBLIC UTILITIES AND CARRIERS -- DUTIES OF UTILITIES AND CARRIERS
ri:HB 7332.summary: Requires every licensed public utility to keep a customer service operation physically located in Rhode Island, reasonably staffed to handle inquiries and accept bill payments.

ri:HB 7349.title: AN ACT RELATING TO BEHAVIORAL HEALTHCARE, DEVELOPMENTAL DISABILITIES AND HOSPITALS -- OVERSIGHT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TECHNOLOGY IN MENTAL HEALTH CARE ACT
ri:HB 7349.summary: Bars licensed therapists from using AI to make independent therapeutic decisions or set treatment plans, requires written patient consent for certain AI use in recorded sessions, and limits offering therapy, including internet-based AI therapy, to licensed providers.

ri:HB 7350.title: AN ACT RELATING TO COMMERCIAL LAW--GENERAL REGULATORY PROVISIONS -- ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE COMPANION MODELS
ri:HB 7350.summary: Requires AI companion operators to have protocols for users who express suicidal thoughts or harm to others, referring them to crisis services, and to tell users at the start and every three hours they are not talking to a person. Penalties reach $15,000 daily.

ri:HB 7360.title: AN ACT RELATING TO CRIMINAL PROCEDURE -- PROTECT OUR COURTS ACT
ri:HB 7360.summary: Exempts people attending court as a party or potential witness, or with a family member who is one, from civil arrest absent a judicial warrant or order; allows civil suits, including by the attorney general; lets the chief justice set courthouse arrest rules.

ri:HB 7437.title: AN ACT RELATING TO MOTOR AND OTHER VEHICLES -- AUTOMATED TRAFFIC VIOLATION MONETARY SYSTEMS
ri:HB 7437.summary: As amended, extends the sunset of "Don't Block the Box" traffic cameras (up to three intersections per municipality) from January 15, 2027 to January 15, 2030, and limits use and sharing of camera images and data.

ri:HB 7475.title: AN ACT RELATING TO PUBLIC FINANCE -- RHODE ISLAND SECURE CHOICE RETIREMENT SAVINGS PROGRAM ACT
ri:HB 7475.summary: As introduced, makes technical changes to the state's Secure Choice retirement savings program for private-sector workers, described as necessary for continued administration and partnership with other states.
