ri:HB 7477.title: AN ACT RELATING TO CORPORATIONS, ASSOCIATIONS AND PARTNERSHIPS -- UNIFORM PARTNERSHIP ACT -- THE RHODE ISLAND LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY ACT
ri:HB 7477.summary: Replaces Rhode Island's limited liability company act with a newer model act, updating rules on forming, dissolving, merging and converting LLCs and removing statutory apparent authority for members and managers. Most provisions take effect January 1, 2028.

ri:HB 7494.title: AN ACT RELATING TO ELECTIONS -- MAIL BALLOTS
ri:HB 7494.summary: Requires the Board of Elections to provide a public observation area for mail ballot processing, sets a tiered signature-review process by two designees and supervising staff, and requires a driver's license, state ID or last four Social Security digits on mail ballot applications.

ri:HB 7547.title: AN ACT RELATING TO CRIMINAL PROCEDURE -- CRIMINAL INJURIES COMPENSATION
ri:HB 7547.summary: Lets stalking victims recover relocation and home-modification costs from the crime victim compensation program, and removes larceny and certain sex-offense categories from the list of compensable offenses.

ri:HB 7571.title: AN ACT RELATING TO MOTOR AND OTHER VEHICLES -- REGISTRATION OF VEHICLES
ri:HB 7571.summary: Creates a special vehicle registration plate for the Friends of the Historic Narragansett Towers, a nonprofit, which the Division of Motor Vehicles may issue.

ri:HB 7606.title: AN ACT RELATING TO COMMERCIAL LAW -- GENERAL REGULATORY PROVISIONS -- LIBRARY EBOOK CONTRACTS
ri:HB 7606.summary: Bars publisher e-book and audiobook license terms that restrict libraries from lending, setting loan periods or making preservation copies. Takes effect once the attorney general publishes notice that four other states, with 10 million people combined, have similar laws.

ri:HB 7638.title: AN ACT RELATING TO MOTOR AND OTHER VEHICLES -- RIGHT-OF-WAY
ri:HB 7638.summary: Amends the pedestrian right-of-way law to reference the schedule of violations for adjudicating traffic offenses.

ri:HB 7653.title: AN ACT RELATING TO CRIMINAL PROCEDURE -- DOMESTIC VIOLENCE PREVENTION ACT
ri:HB 7653.summary: Requires law enforcement agencies to file domestic violence and sexual assault reporting forms electronically, expands the information on the forms, and sets submission monthly or as soon as practicable.

ri:HB 7654.title: AN ACT RELATING TO PROPERTY -- MORTGAGE FORECLOSURE AND SALE
ri:HB 7654.summary: As amended, requires foreclosure sale notices to mortgagors to be sent by first-class mail and an overnight delivery service instead of certified mail, and extends servicemember foreclosure protections from nine months to one year after active duty.

ri:HB 7656.title: AN ACT RELATING TO PUBLIC OFFICERS AND EMPLOYEES -- RHODE ISLAND PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PENSION REVOCATION AND REDUCTION ACT
ri:HB 7656.summary: Lets the state retirement board revoke or reduce a public employee's pension if the person is convicted of, or pleads guilty or no contest to, a felony sex crime related to their public office or job.

ri:HB 7677.title: AN ACT RELATING TO WATERS AND NAVIGATION -- COASTAL RESOURCES MANAGEMENT COUNCIL
ri:HB 7677.summary: Provides that the legislature negotiates on the state's behalf for all activities in, on and over state submerged land extending beyond 25 acres, amending Coastal Resources Management Council laws.

ri:HB 7780.title: AN ACT RELATING TO MOTOR AND OTHER VEHICLES -- REGISTRATION OF VEHICLES
ri:HB 7780.summary: Creates a special registration plate for the Rhode Island Hockey Hall of Fame.

ri:HB 7840.title: AN ACT RELATING TO BUSINESSES AND PROFESSIONS -- REAL ESTATE BROKERS AND SALESPERSONS
ri:HB 7840.summary: Requires anyone in the business of buying, selling or assigning an equitable interest in real estate without taking legal title to be licensed as a real estate broker or salesperson and follow disclosure and cancellation rules, starting January 1, 2027.

ri:HB 7869.title: AN ACT RELATING TO MOTOR AND OTHER VEHICLES -- SIZE, WEIGHT, AND LOAD LIMITS
ri:HB 7869.summary: Updates size, weight and load rules for commercial and specialized vehicles.

ri:HB 7879.title: AN ACT RELATING TO PUBLIC UTILITIES AND CARRIERS -- THERMAL ENERGY NETWORK AND JOBS ACT
ri:HB 7879.summary: Requires a public utility to identify sites and start at least two feasibility studies of thermal energy networks, and creates a 12-member task force to advise on the results.

ri:HB 7923.title: AN ACT RELATING TO FOOD AND DRUGS -- UNIFORM CONTROLLED SUBSTANCES ACT
ri:HB 7923.summary: Removes specific opioid dosage requirements from the Uniform Controlled Substances Act, updates it to current standards of professional practice, and repeals the chapter on intractable pain treatment.

ri:HB 7960.title: AN ACT RELATING TO LABOR AND LABOR RELATIONS -- PAYMENT OF WAGES
ri:HB 7960.summary: Replaces the 30-day deadlines for scheduling and deciding wage-law hearings before the Department of Labor and Training with a "reasonable and timely" standard, not to exceed 180 days.

ri:HB 7989.title: AN ACT RELATING TO MOTOR AND OTHER VEHICLES -- REGISTRATION OF VEHICLES
ri:HB 7989.summary: Exempts vehicles sold without a manufacturer-provided front plate bracket from displaying a front registration plate, if the rear plate is attached and the second plate is carried in the vehicle and shown on an officer's request.

ri:HB 8001.title: AN ACT RELATING TO HEALTH AND SAFETY -- STATE BUILDING CODE -- ADMINISTRATION AND ENFORCEMENT
ri:HB 8001.summary: Lets municipalities, by emergency declaration after severe weather or a disaster, suspend local zoning and building approvals to build SAFE Units, temporary housing for people experiencing homelessness, which follow set standards instead of the state building code; requires reports to the governor and legislative leaders.

ri:HB 8025.title: AN ACT RELATING TO TAXATION -- PROPERTY SUBJECT TO TAXATION
ri:HB 8025.summary: Allows Tiverton to authorize, by ordinance, a real estate tax credit for seniors over age 65.

ri:HB 8026.title: AN ACT RELATING TO TAXATION --  PROPERTY SUBJECT TO TAXATION
ri:HB 8026.summary: Raises Tiverton's minimum tax credit for totally disabled veterans from $200 to $400 and extends it to their unmarried widows and widowers.

ri:HB 8028.title: AN ACT RELATING TO TOWNS AND CITIES -- DAM MANAGEMENT DISTRICTS
ri:HB 8028.summary: Lets Burrillville exempt from taxation, by ordinance, the lake bed and dam property of Wilson's Reservoir; requires dam management district fees there be collected like taxes; extends the district's civil-liability immunity to the lake bed.

ri:HB 8046.title: AN ACT RELATING TO COURTS AND CIVIL PROCEDURE--PROCEDURE GENERALLY -- FEES
ri:HB 8046.summary: Sets one $70 fee for sheriffs, town sergeants and constables to serve all writs, citations and subpoenas, replacing the separate $100 fee for writs of replevin and out-of-state papers.

ri:HB 8060.title: AN ACT RELATING TO CRIMINAL OFFENSES -- IMPERSONATION AND IDENTITY FRAUD
ri:HB 8060.summary: Makes it a crime to knowingly impersonate an entity to facilitate fraud, and adds "digital forgery," meaning creating or distributing a deceptive fake image or voice recording of a real person or entity without consent to facilitate fraud.

ri:HB 8104.title: AN ACT RELATING TO PROPERTY -- MORTGAGES OF REAL PROPERTY
ri:HB 8104.summary: Limits mortgage prepayment rules to mortgages on owner-occupied properties with one to four dwelling units.

ri:HB 8128.title: AN ACT RELATING TO BUSINESSES AND PROFESSIONS -- PUBLIC ACCOUNTANCY
ri:HB 8128.summary: Updates Rhode Island's public accountancy law to match the 9th edition of the Uniform Accountancy Act issued in July 2025 by NASBA (the state accountancy boards' national association) and the AICPA.

ri:HB 8232.title: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE FORMATION OF A REGIONAL SCHOOL DISTRICT EMBRACING THE TOWNS OF FOSTER AND GLOCESTER
ri:HB 8232.summary: Changes the date of the Foster-Glocester regional school district's financial meeting to March 24, 2026.

ri:HB 8247.title: AN ACT RELATING TO COURTS AND CIVIL PROCEDURE -- COURTS -- SUPERIOR COURT
ri:HB 8247.summary: Renames the Superior Court's "drug court" magistrate and program as the "recovery court."

ri:HB 8294.title: AN ACT RELATING TO PROPERTY -- ABANDONED PROPERTY
ri:HB 8294.summary: Makes energy storage systems a by-right zoning use on abandoned properties in court receivership and on previously contaminated sites, with a 5 megawatt cap on the receivership-property systems, and lets courts give sale priority to buyers who install one.

ri:HB 8297.title: AN ACT RELATING TO STATE AFFAIRS AND GOVERNMENT -- ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEDURES
ri:HB 8297.summary: Replaces the periodic refiling of state agency rules with a confirmation and attestation system showing rules remain active, and repeals the existing refiling section.

ri:HB 8333.title: AN ACT RELATING TO MOTOR AND OTHER VEHICLES -- REGISTRATION OF VEHICLES
ri:HB 8333.summary: Allows the Division of Motor Vehicles to issue a special registration plate for the Dominican Independence and Heritage Award Committee of RI, a nonprofit. Takes effect six months after passage.

ri:HB 8348.title: AN ACT RELATING TO TAXATION --  PROPERTY SUBJECT TO TAXATION
ri:HB 8348.summary: Exempts from property tax the property of the nonprofit Mount St. Rita Health Centre in Cumberland, effective as of December 31, 2025.

ri:HB 8400.title: AN ACT RELATING TO STATE AFFAIRS AND GOVERNMENT -- QUONSET DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION
ri:HB 8400.summary: Bars the Quonset Development Corporation from allowing any thermal waste conversion facility, such as pyrolysis, in the Quonset Point/Davisville Industrial Park until June 1, 2027, except for activity already lawfully underway.

ri:HB 8436.title: AN ACT RELATING TO TAXATION-PROPERTY SUBJECT TO TAXATION -- GLOCESTER -- EXEMPTION OF ELDERLY AND DISABLED PERSONS
ri:HB 8436.summary: Authorizes Glocester to add a non-compounding CPI adjustment, without an income test, to its property tax exemption for elderly and disabled residents.

ri:HB 8437.title: AN ACT RELATING TO TAXATION -- PROPERTY SUBJECT TO TAXATION
ri:HB 8437.summary: Changes several Cranston property tax exemptions, including those for veterans, seniors, people with disabilities and legally blind residents, into tax credits capped at set amounts (for example, $182.90 a year for veterans), adjusted every three years by up to the CPI.

ri:HB 8483.title: AN ACT RELATING TO ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES -- RETAIL LICENSES
ri:HB 8483.summary: Allows the issuance of a Class BV alcohol retail license for the property at 1814 Broad Street in Cranston.

ri:HB 8484.title: AN ACT RELATING TO TAXATION -- PROPERTY SUBJECT TO TAXATION
ri:HB 8484.summary: Exempts the real and tangible personal property of Amos House from taxation as long as it remains a 501(c)(3) tax-exempt corporation.

ri:HB 8488.title: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE TOWN OF PORTSMOUTH TO ISSUE NOT TO EXCEED $41,000,000 GENERAL OBLIGATION BONDS, NOTES AND OTHER EVIDENCES OF INDEBTEDNESS TO FINANCE THE CONSTRUCTION, ADDITIONS, RENOVATION, IMPROVEMENT, ALTERATION, REPAIR, FURNISHING AND EQUIPPING OF SCHOOLS AND SCHOOL FACILITIES THROUGHOUT THE TOWN
ri:HB 8488.summary: Authorizes the town of Portsmouth to issue up to $41 million in bonds and notes for school construction and renovation. Most provisions take effect on voter approval; state aid requires Department of Education project approval.

ri:HB 8506.title: AN ACT RELATING TO TOWNS AND CITIES -- RELATING TO CENTRAL FALLS PENSION PLAN
ri:HB 8506.summary: Lowers contributions by active Central Falls firefighters and police officers to the city pension plan from 11.7% to 10% of salary or compensation.

ri:HB 8509.title: AN ACT RELATING TO SOLEMNIZATION OF MARRIAGES
ri:HB 8509.summary: Authorizes Joseph Couto to perform the marriage of two named individuals in Tiverton on or about August 2, 2026.

ri:HB 8527.title: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE CHARIHO REGIONAL SCHOOL DISTRICT TO FINANCE THE CONSTRUCTION, FURNISHING AND EQUIPPING OF AN ELEMENTARY SCHOOL SERVING THE TOWNS OF CHARLESTOWN, RICHMOND AND HOPKINTON, CONSISTING OF ONE OR MORE BUILDINGS ON A SINGLE CAMPUS, AND IMPROVEMENTS AT THE SWITCH ROAD CAMPUS INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, COSTS OF LAND ACQUISITION, DEMOLITION, DESIGN, HEALTH AND SAFETY PROJECTS, PLAYGROUNDS, LANDSCAPING, PAVING, AND ALL EXPENSES INCIDENTAL THERETO, BY THE ISSUANCE OF NOT MORE THAN $116,000,000 BONDS AND/OR NOTES THEREFOR, SUBJECT TO APPROVAL OF STATE HOUSING AID AT A REIMBURSEMENT RATE OR STATE SHARE RATIO OF NOT LESS THAN 61% AT THE TIME OF ISSUANCE, WHICH RATE OR RATIO MAY INCREASE TO 65% AT PROJECT COMPLETION
ri:HB 8527.summary: Authorizes the Chariho Regional School District to issue up to $116 million in bonds or notes for a new elementary school and Switch Road campus improvements, contingent on state aid of at least 61% and voter approval.

ri:HB 8546.title: AN ACT REGARDING MOTIONS AT THE TOWN OF SCITUATE ANNUAL FINANCIAL TOWN MEETING
ri:HB 8546.summary: As amended, requires notice signed by ten electors by May 15, and posted in the warrant or online seven days ahead, for Scituate town meeting motions changing a recommended appropriation by $10,000 or more. Takes effect only if voters approve it in November 2026.

ri:HB 8558.title: AN ACT RELATING TO TOWNS AND CITIES -- GENERAL POWERS -- CITY OF WARWICK
ri:HB 8558.summary: Lets the city of Warwick sell the property at 34 Warwick Lake Avenue despite the state limits on selling donated public-use land, in order to clear the property's title.

ri:HB 8580.title: AN ACT RELATING TO THE NORTH TIVERTON FIRE DISTRICT
ri:HB 8580.summary: Reduces the number of tax assessors for the North Tiverton Fire District from six to four, after voluntary resignations, following the 2026 annual meeting. Takes effect upon approval by district electors.

ri:HB 8582.title: AN ACT RELATING TO INSURANCE -- PHARMACY FREEDOM OF CHOICE--FAIR COMPETITION AND PRACTICES
ri:HB 8582.summary: Imposes duties, transparency and accountability requirements on pharmacy benefit managers and their services, effective January 1, 2027.

ri:HB 8586.title: AN ACT RELATING TO HIGHWAYS -- RHODE ISLAND TURNPIKE AND BRIDGE AUTHORITY
ri:HB 8586.summary: Lets vehicle rental and leasing companies use a rental agreement as prima facie evidence that the renter was the driver in toll violation cases, and exempts them from registration penalties for out-of-state toll violations.

ri:HB 8588.title: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE CITY OF PAWTUCKET TO PROVIDE FOR THE PLANNING, EVALUATION, DESIGN, CONSTRUCTION, EQUIPPING AND RECONSTRUCTION OF SANITARY SEWERS AND STORM SEWERS IN THE CITY AND AUTHORIZING THE FINANCING THEREOF, INCLUDING THE ISSUE OF NOT MORE THAN $4,000,000 BONDS AND NOTES THEREFOR, TO FUND THE CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM FOR THE TWO FISCAL YEARS 2028 AND 2029
ri:HB 8588.summary: Authorizes Pawtucket to issue up to $4,000,000 in general obligation bonds and notes for sanitary and storm sewers. Requires approval by city voters.

ri:HB 8589.title: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE CITY OF PAWTUCKET TO PROVIDE FOR THE RENOVATION, CONSTRUCTION, RECONSTRUCTION AND EQUIPPING OF PUBLIC RECREATION FACILITIES IN THE CITY INCLUDING LAND ACQUISITION AND AUTHORIZING THE FINANCING THEREOF, INCLUDING THE ISSUE OF NOT MORE THAN $2,000,000 BONDS AND NOTES THEREFOR, TO FUND THE CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM FOR THE TWO FISCAL YEARS 2028 AND 2029
ri:HB 8589.summary: Authorizes Pawtucket to issue up to $2,000,000 in general obligation bonds and notes for public recreation facilities, including land acquisition. Requires approval by city voters.

ri:HB 8590.title: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE CITY OF PAWTUCKET TO PROVIDE FOR THE CONSTRUCTION, RENOVATION, IMPROVEMENT, REPAIR, ALTERATION, FURNISHING AND EQUIPPING OF PUBLIC BUILDINGS IN THE CITY AND AUTHORIZING THE FINANCING THEREOF, INCLUDING THE ISSUE OF NOT MORE THAN $5,000,000 BONDS AND NOTES THEREFOR, TO FUND THE CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM FOR THE TWO FISCAL YEARS 2028 AND 2029
ri:HB 8590.summary: Authorizes Pawtucket to issue up to $5,000,000 in general obligation bonds and notes for constructing, renovating and equipping public buildings. Requires approval by city voters.

ri:HB 8591.title: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE CITY OF PAWTUCKET TO PROVIDE FOR THE CONSTRUCTION, RECONSTRUCTION, REPAIR AND EQUIPPING OF BRIDGES AND ALL COSTS INCIDENTAL OR RELATED THERETO AND AUTHORIZING THE FINANCING THEREOF, INCLUDING THE ISSUE OF NOT MORE THAN $2,000,000 BONDS AND NOTES THEREFOR, TO FUND THE CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM FOR  THE TWO FISCAL YEARS 2028 AND 2029
ri:HB 8591.summary: Authorizes Pawtucket to issue up to $2,000,000 in general obligation bonds and notes for constructing, repairing and equipping bridges. Requires approval by city voters.

ri:HB 8592.title: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE CITY OF PAWTUCKET TO PROVIDE FOR THE DESIGN, CONSTRUCTION, RECONSTRUCTION, REPAIR AND EQUIPPING OF STREETS, SIDEWALKS AND OTHER TRANSPORTATION INFRASTRUCTURE IMPROVEMENTS INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, DRAINAGE AND LANDSCAPING AND AUTHORIZING THE FINANCING THEREOF, INCLUDING THE ISSUE OF NOT MORE THAN $2,000,000 BONDS AND NOTES THEREFOR, TO FUND THE CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM FOR THE TWO FISCAL YEARS 2028 AND 2029
ri:HB 8592.summary: Authorizes Pawtucket to issue up to $2,000,000 in general obligation bonds and notes for streets, sidewalks, drainage and landscaping. Requires approval by city voters.

ri:HB 8593.title: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE CITY OF PAWTUCKET TO PROVIDE FOR THE  IMPROVEMENT AND REPLACEMENT OF ROAD SAFETY INFRASTRUCTURE  AND TRAFFIC CONTROL DEVICES IN THE CITY OF PAWTUCKET AND AUTHORIZING THE FINANCING THEREOF, INCLUDING THE ISSUE OF NOT MORE THAN $2,500,000 BONDS AND NOTES THEREFOR, TO FUND THE CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM FOR THE TWO FISCAL YEARS 2028 AND 2029
ri:HB 8593.summary: Authorizes Pawtucket to issue up to $2,500,000 in general obligation bonds and notes for road safety infrastructure and traffic control devices. Requires approval by city voters.

ri:HB 8594.title: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE CITY OF PAWTUCKET TO PROVIDE FOR THE REPAVING OF STREETS IN THE CITY AND AUTHORIZING THE FINANCING THEREOF, INCLUDING THE ISSUE OF NOT MORE THAN $3,000,000 BONDS AND NOTES THEREFOR, TO FUND THE CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM FOR THE TWO FISCAL YEARS 2028 AND 2029
ri:HB 8594.summary: Authorizes Pawtucket to issue up to $3,000,000 in general obligation bonds and notes for repaving city streets. Requires approval by city voters.

ri:HB 8602.title: AN ACT RELATING TO SOLEMNIZATION OF MARRIAGES
ri:HB 8602.summary: Allows a named individual to perform a marriage ceremony in Narragansett on or about September 27, 2026.

ri:HB 8611.title: AN ACT RELATING TO TAXATION -- TAXATION OF BANKS
ri:HB 8611.summary: Changes how banks' income is apportioned and allocated for state tax purposes, for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2025.

ri:HB 8620.title: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE CITY OF CRANSTON TO FINANCE THE REPAIR, CONSTRUCTION AND REHABILITATION OF STORM DRAINS AND DRAINAGE IMPROVEMENTS, AND THE REMEDIATION AND MITIGATION OF DRAINAGE AND FLOODING PROBLEMS, BY THE ISSUANCE OF NOT MORE THAN $4,000,000 GENERAL OBLIGATION BONDS AND NOTES THEREFOR
ri:HB 8620.summary: Authorizes Cranston to issue up to $4,000,000 in general obligation bonds and notes for storm drains, drainage improvements, and flooding mitigation. Requires approval by city voters.

ri:HB 8621.title: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE CITY OF CRANSTON TO FINANCE THE ACQUISITION, DEMOLITION, CONSTRUCTION, IMPROVEMENT, RENOVATION, REPAIR, ALTERATION, FURNISHING AND EQUIPPING OF PUBLIC BUILDINGS IN THE CITY BY THE ISSUANCE OF NOT MORE THAN $2,000,000 GENERAL OBLIGATION BONDS AND NOTES THEREFOR
ri:HB 8621.summary: Authorizes Cranston to issue up to $2,000,000 in general obligation bonds and notes to acquire, demolish, construct, renovate and equip public buildings. Requires approval by city voters.

ri:HB 8623.title: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE CITY OF CRANSTON TO FINANCE THE DESIGN, CONSTRUCTION, REPAIR, REHABILITATION AND IMPROVEMENT OF STREETS, SIDEWALKS AND BRIDGES IN THE CITY INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, PAVING, DRAINAGE, TRAFFIC CONTROL DEVICES, ROAD MAINTENANCE EQUIPMENT, SAFETY IMPROVEMENTS AND LANDSCAPING AND ALL COSTS INCIDENTAL OR RELATED THERETO BY THE ISSUANCE OF NOT MORE THAN $8,000,000 GENERAL OBLIGATION BONDS AND NOTES THEREFOR
ri:HB 8623.summary: Authorizes Cranston to issue up to $8,000,000 in general obligation bonds and notes for streets, sidewalks and bridges, including paving, drainage, traffic control devices and safety improvements. Requires approval by city voters.

ri:HB 8624.title: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE CITY OF CRANSTON TO FINANCE THE ACQUISITION, IMPROVEMENT, RENOVATION AND REPAIR OF FIRE AND PUBLIC SAFETY EQUIPMENT BY THE ISSUANCE OF NOT MORE THAN $8,000,000 GENERAL OBLIGATION BONDS AND NOTES THEREFOR
ri:HB 8624.summary: Authorizes Cranston to issue up to $8,000,000 in general obligation bonds and notes to acquire, improve, renovate and repair fire and public safety equipment. Requires approval by city voters.

ri:HB 8625.title: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE CITY OF CRANSTON TO ISSUE NOT TO EXCEED $25,000,000 GENERAL OBLIGATION BONDS, NOTES AND OTHER EVIDENCES OF INDEBTEDNESS TO FINANCE THE PURCHASE AND/OR ACQUISITION OF LAND AND BUILDINGS, CONSTRUCTION, RENOVATION, IMPROVEMENT, ALTERATION, REPAIR, LANDSCAPING, FURNISHING AND EQUIPPING OF SCHOOLS AND SCHOOL FACILITIES THROUGHOUT THE CITY
ri:HB 8625.summary: Authorizes Cranston to issue up to $25,000,000 in general obligation bonds and notes for school land, buildings, construction and renovation. State aid reimbursement requires approval of the projects by the Department of Education. Requires voter approval.

ri:HB 8627.title: AN ACT RELATING TO SOLEMNIZATION OF MARRIAGES
ri:HB 8627.summary: Allows a named individual to perform a marriage ceremony in Narragansett on or about September 25, 2026.

ri:HR 7031.title: JOINT RESOLUTION CREATING A SPECIAL LEGISLATIVE COMMISSION TO STUDY SAFE STAFFING RATIOS IN HOSPITALS
ri:HR 7031.summary: Creates a 15-member special legislative commission to study safe staffing ratios in hospitals, reporting by September 1, 2027 and expiring January 30, 2028.

ri:HR 7579.title: JOINT RESOLUTION REPEALING RHODE ISLAND'S RATIFICATION OF THE CORWIN AMENDMENT
ri:HR 7579.summary: Repeals Rhode Island's earlier ratification of the Corwin Amendment, a proposed 1861 U.S. constitutional amendment barring changes that would let Congress abolish or interfere with states' domestic institutions, including slavery.

ri:HR 8605.title: JOINT RESOLUTION MAKING AN APPROPRIATION TO PAY CERTAIN CLAIMS
ri:HR 8605.summary: Appropriates $6,280.12 from the state treasury for fiscal 2027 to pay nine claims of $150 to $1,209.45 each, mostly for vehicle damage from roadway defects or debris.

ri:SB 2974.title: AN ACT RELATING TO MOTOR AND OTHER VEHICLES -- RIGHT-OF-WAY
ri:SB 2974.summary: Makes the fine for violating pedestrian right-of-way laws subject to the state's schedule of traffic violation fines.

ri:SB 2975.title: AN ACT RELATING TO COURTS AND CIVIL PROCEDURE-- PROCEDURE IN PARTICULAR ACTION -- SMALL CLAIMS AND CONSUMER CLAIMS
ri:SB 2975.summary: Raises the small claims entry fee from $55 to $75, sets a $75 appeal filing fee, and raises the compulsory counterclaim limit from $2,500 to $5,000 to match the small claims limit. Takes effect January 1, 2027.

ri:SB 3075.title: AN ACT RELATING TO FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS  -- LICENSED ACTIVITIES
ri:SB 3075.summary: Requires nonbank mortgage servicers with 2,000 or more one-to-four unit loans, operating in two or more states, to meet capital, liquidity, board oversight, audit and risk management standards.

ri:SB 3086.title: AN ACT RELATING TO PUBLIC FINANCE -- RHODE ISLAND SECURE CHOICE RETIREMENT SAVINGS PROGRAM ACT
ri:SB 3086.summary: As introduced, makes technical changes to the state's Secure Choice retirement savings program for private-sector workers, described as necessary for continued administration and partnership with other states.

ri:SB 3290.title: AN ACT RELATING TO COURTS AND CIVIL PROCEDURE--COURTS -- SUPERIOR COURT
ri:SB 3290.summary: Creates a separate domestic violence calendar in the Superior Court for hearing and deciding felony domestic violence cases.

ri:SB 3321.title: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE CITY OF PAWTUCKET TO PROVIDE FOR THE RENOVATION, CONSTRUCTION, RECONSTRUCTION AND EQUIPPING OF PUBLIC RECREATION FACILITIES IN THE CITY INCLUDING LAND ACQUISITION AND AUTHORIZING THE FINANCING THEREOF, INCLUDING THE ISSUE OF NOT MORE THAN $2,000,000 BONDS AND NOTES THEREFOR, TO FUND THE CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM FOR THE TWO FISCAL YEARS 2028 AND 2029
ri:SB 3321.summary: As introduced, authorizes Pawtucket to issue up to $2,000,000 in bonds and notes to renovate, build and equip public recreation facilities, including land acquisition; most provisions take effect only if city voters approve.

ri:SB 3359.title: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE CITY OF CRANSTON TO FINANCE THE DESIGN, CONSTRUCTION, REPAIR, REHABILITATION AND IMPROVEMENT OF STREETS, SIDEWALKS AND BRIDGES IN THE CITY INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, PAVING, DRAINAGE, TRAFFIC CONTROL DEVICES, ROAD MAINTENANCE EQUIPMENT, SAFETY IMPROVEMENTS AND LANDSCAPING AND ALL COSTS INCIDENTAL OR RELATED THERETO BY THE ISSUANCE OF NOT MORE THAN $8,000,000 GENERAL OBLIGATION BONDS AND NOTES THEREFOR
ri:SB 3359.summary: As introduced, authorizes Cranston to issue up to $8,000,000 in general obligation bonds and temporary notes for street, sidewalk and bridge work, including paving, drainage, traffic controls and equipment; most provisions take effect only if city voters approve.

ri:SB 3361.title: AN ACT RELATING TO PROPERTY -- MORTGAGE FORECLOSURE AND SALE
ri:SB 3361.summary: As amended, requires foreclosure sale notices to mortgagors to be sent by first-class mail and an overnight delivery service instead of certified mail, and extends servicemember foreclosure protections from nine months to one year after active duty.

sc:H 3020.title: Status Offenses
sc:H 3020.summary: Removes playing a pinball machine from the list of status offenses for minors and repeals the law that prohibits minors from playing pinball machines.

sc:H 3021.title: Small Business Regulatory Freedom Act
sc:H 3021.summary: Requires the legislature to approve, by joint resolution, state regulations estimated to cost $1 million or more over five years, directs courts to review agency interpretations of statutes and regulations without deference, and sets periodic Legislative Audit Council reviews of agency regulations.

sc:H 3335.title: Designation of representation in magistrates court
sc:H 3335.summary: Lets a housing authority designate an employee to represent it in magistrates court, as corporations and partnerships may now, without that person being treated as practicing law without a license.

sc:H 3387.title: Unlawful occupants of property
sc:H 3387.summary: Creates a court petition process for owners to remove unlawful occupants from a residential dwelling, with an immediate ex parte removal order and a hearing within 24 hours, and makes unlawfully occupying a residential dwelling a felony called criminal mischief.

sc:H 3924.title: Hemp-derived ingestible
sc:H 3924.summary: Sets up licensing and regulation of hemp-derived beverages and chewables under the Department of Revenue, with a 10 milligram per serving THC cap, a minimum sales age of 21, and excise taxes.

sc:H 4069.title: Patient-Friendly Billing
sc:H 4069.summary: Requires hospitals and other healthcare facilities, starting January 1, 2027, to give patients an itemized bill in plain language electronically, and in writing on request, showing the amount the facility says is owed.

sc:H 4382.title: Nonprescription Ephedrine Products
sc:H 4382.summary: Requires makers of nonprescription ephedrine and pseudoephedrine products to pay monthly fees, starting October 1, 2026, to the administrator of the real-time sales-tracking system, and sets a penalty for noncompliance.

sc:H 4476.title: SC-Bahamas Trade Commission
sc:H 4476.summary: Creates a 15-member South Carolina-Bahamas Trade Commission, appointed by the Speaker, the Senate President and the Governor, to advance trade and investment between South Carolina and The Bahamas.

sc:H 4635.title: Physical Fitness Services
sc:H 4635.summary: Allows fitness facilities to send automatic-renewal notices electronically, by means specified in the contract, as well as in writing, and requires the notice no later than ten days before the initial contract expires.

sc:H 5093.title: Gross proceeds
sc:H 5093.summary: Excludes from sales-tax gross proceeds amounts governments pay for the Emergency Services IP Network used for Next Generation 911, and insurance charges bought with a taxed product. Exempts chamber of commerce admissions from the admissions tax.

sc:H 5126.title: Budget
sc:H 5126.summary: Appropriates money and provides revenues for the ordinary expenses of state government for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2026, regulates how those funds are spent, and sets other provisions for operating state government that year.

sc:H 5127.title: Capital Reserve Fund, appropriations
sc:H 5127.summary: Appropriates Capital Reserve Fund money for fiscal year 2025-26: $175 million for the MUSC cancer hospital, about $139.6 million for bridge modernization, and $72.8 million for FEMA disaster match. Unspent funds carry forward.

sc:H 5164.title: Hospitals
sc:H 5164.summary: Allows hospitals to place patient beds in hallways and exit routes during a defined "justified emergency," such as a declared disaster or full emergency department; also requires hospitals and surgical centers to adopt surgical smoke exposure policies from July 2027, later for some.

sc:H 5261.title: Alcohol Server Training
sc:H 5261.summary: Extends the deadline for alcohol server training required under state law to May 1, 2026.

sc:H 5473.title: Fishing
sc:H 5473.summary: Bans fishing at any time on the J. Foster Jeffords Causeway across Forest Lake on Knollwood Road in Florence County. Violators face a fine of up to $25 or up to 30 days in jail.

sc:H 5537.title: Dillon National Guard Armory
sc:H 5537.summary: Directs state agencies to transfer ownership of National Guard armories in Dillon County to the City of Dillon, in Timmonsville to the City of Timmonsville, and in Barnwell to Barnwell County.

sc:S 1005.title: Judicial Salaries
sc:S 1005.summary: Raises family court judges' salaries from 92.5 to 95 percent of an Associate Justice's salary, the same percentage as circuit court judges.

sc:S 1011.title: Barnwell National Guard Armory
sc:S 1011.summary: Directs state agencies to transfer ownership of the National Guard armory at 10233 Marlboro Avenue in Barnwell to Barnwell County.

sc:S 1043.title: Civil Air Patrol Leave Act
sc:S 1043.summary: Creates the Civil Air Patrol Leave Act, requiring public and private employers to give employees who are Civil Air Patrol members at least 30 days of leave per year for emergency service operations, with anti-discrimination and benefit protections.

sc:S 1062.title: A JOINT RESOLUTION TO APPROVE REGULATIONS OF THE STATE COMMISSION ON HIGHER EDUCATION, RELATING TO DETERMINATION OF RATES OF TUITION AND FEES, DESIGNATED AS
sc:S 1062.summary: Approves the State Commission on Higher Education's Regulation Document No. 5443, covering the determination of tuition and fee rates, including the residency rules for charging in-state rates.

sc:S 11.title: Paid Family Leave Eligible State Employee
sc:S 11.summary: Changes the definition of "eligible state employee" for paid parental leave to any state, higher education or technical college employee in a position eligible to earn annual leave.

sc:S 136.title: Dismissal of pending gun possession charges
sc:S 136.summary: Requires the state to dismiss and expunge pending unlawful handgun possession charges from before the 2024 constitutional carry law, waiting until related charges from the same facts are resolved, and bars using the dismissal as a basis for civil suits over the arrest.

sc:S 238.title: Sine Die
sc:S 238.summary: Moves from March 31 to March 10 the House budget third-reading deadline that triggers an automatic extension of the session, lets leaders recall members until the first Thursday in June for budget business, and pauses the 120-day regulation review.

sc:S 325.title: Department of Consumer Affairs
sc:S 325.summary: Moves the Department of Consumer Affairs into the executive branch and replaces its governing commission with an administrator appointed by the Governor with Senate consent.

sc:S 52.title: Driving under the influence
sc:S 52.summary: Revises DUI laws: permits both fines and jail, requires victim impact panels, creates second-degree felony DUI and felony reckless driving offenses, sets a one-year license suspension for a first test refusal, and allows ignition interlock devices during suspensions.

sc:S 623.title: Georgetown County Building Requirements
sc:S 623.summary: Exempts Georgetown County from building requirements for properties in or affected by the limit of moderate wave action line, letting it enforce AE flood standards instead; repealed when the next such line is adopted.

sc:S 688.title: DEW UI Tax Code
sc:S 688.summary: Changes how South Carolina calculates employer unemployment insurance tax rates, adding a trust fund solvency target and surcharge, and removes the caps on penalties for failing to file reports or pay contributions on time.

sc:S 695.title: Unauthorized Fees for Claim Assistance
sc:S 695.summary: Enacts the Safeguarding American Veterans' Benefits Act, setting limits on compensation for helping with veterans' benefit claims, requiring written terms, and setting penalties for violations.

sc:S 779.title: Legislative Expense Allowance
sc:S 779.summary: Gives each member of the General Assembly a $1,000 monthly legislative expense allowance, retroactive to July 1, 2025, prorated for vacated seats and denied to members convicted of, or pleading guilty or no contest to, a felony during the fiscal year.

sc:S 823.title: Child Welfare
sc:S 823.summary: Requires family courts, on a party's motion or the court's own initiative, to consider no-contact or supervised-contact orders between the child and biological parents or relatives when terminating parental rights or finalizing adoptions, and to state written findings if declining.

sc:S 829.title: Joint System Governance
sc:S 829.summary: Changes how joint water and sewer authorities are formed and run, including how commissioners are appointed, how members join or withdraw, how bonds are issued by a governor-appointed commission, and automatic contract extensions tied to bond terms.

sc:S 851.title: Protection from Financial Exploitation
sc:S 851.summary: Lets financial institutions, other than broker-dealers and investment advisers, decline or hold transactions on reasonable belief of financial exploitation of someone 55 or older or a vulnerable adult; holds end after 30 business days (55 if investigators request an extension).

sc:S 853.title: Abandoned Buildings Tax Credit
sc:S 853.summary: Changes the Abandoned Buildings tax credit by not requiring prior income-producing use, clarifying notice-of-intent timing, barring use of the credits as loan collateral, and dropping a certification for state-owned sites.

sc:S 857.title: Contingent Deferred Annuities
sc:S 857.summary: Defines "contingent deferred annuity" in state insurance law, exempts it from certain nonforfeiture provisions for individual deferred annuities, and lets the Department of Insurance set separate nonforfeiture benefit rules.

sc:S 858.title: Foster Care
sc:S 858.summary: Renames the division the Foster Care Review Division, limits holdover board service to 180 days, shifts local review board appointment and removal from the Governor to the division director, and has the department provide local board meeting help and training.

sc:S 895.title: Rural Emergency Hospitals
sc:S 895.summary: Adds hospitals that convert to Rural Emergency Hospitals under federal rules to the state licensing law's definition of a "hospital."

sc:S 922.title: Appointments
sc:S 922.summary: Changes the Governor's interim appointment power, requires Senate consent for State Election Commission members serving terms matching the Governor's, ties cabinet agency directors' terms to the appointing Governor, and removes Senate confirmation for many boards and commissions.

sc:S 961.title: Red drum, saltwater fish, deer hunting
sc:S 961.summary: Lowers the red drum daily limit from two to one per person (six to two per boat) and changes the legal size from 15-23 to 18-25 inches. Requires non-offset, non-stainless circle hooks for hook-and-line fishing with natural bait on 4/0 or larger hooks.

sc:S 996.title: Fingerprint Background Checks Update
sc:S 996.summary: Limits the fingerprint background check to volunteers and contractor employees who provide Department of Social Services-related services and have direct unsupervised contact with a child in its custody, removing the separate category for any person with such contact.

sd:HB 1001.title: provide for prescribed burning of state-owned land by a person owning adjoining land and to declare an emergency.
sd:HB 1001.summary: Lets a landowner burn adjoining state-owned land along the Missouri River together with their own land, with written state consent. The landowner must provide fire suppression resources and assumes liability; the state is immune from damage claims.

sd:HB 1006.title: create a taskforce to study the creation of Indian medicaid managed care entities in the state.
sd:HB 1006.summary: Creates a taskforce of tribal, state, legislative, federal and health industry representatives to study Indian Medicaid managed care entities in South Dakota, supported by the Department of Social Services, reporting to the Governor by December 1, 2028.

sd:HB 1007.title: amend the definition of law enforcement officer to include tribal law enforcement officers.
sd:HB 1007.summary: Adds officers, prosecutors and employees of an Indian tribe who assist in enforcing state criminal or traffic laws, or in preventing, detecting or prosecuting a crime committed in South Dakota, to the definition of law enforcement officer.

sd:HB 1017.title: permit the board of a school district to require that certain students receive instruction in alternative settings.
sd:HB 1017.summary: As amended, allows a school board to assign a student to an alternative instruction setting for aggressive or violent behavior that disrupts the school or affects safety, and requires annual reporting of assignments to the Department of Education, with data released only anonymized and aggregated.

sd:HB 1027.title: update certain citations to federal regulations regarding pipeline safety inspections.
sd:HB 1027.summary: Updates the federal pipeline safety regulations and statutes that South Dakota's pipeline safety law adopts or references from versions in effect January 1, 2023 to those in effect January 1, 2026, and rewords several definitions.

sd:HB 1038.title: allow the Public Utilities Commission to assess actual costs to data centers that are customers of public utilities.
sd:HB 1038.summary: Lets the Public Utilities Commission charge actual processing costs to data centers with peak demand of 10 megawatts or more when it reviews their electric service contracts, with the money deposited in the commission's gross receipts tax fund.

sd:HB 1040.title: revise the child support obligation schedule.
sd:HB 1040.summary: Replaces the child support obligation schedule with updated amounts, raises the self-support reserve from $871 to $1,148 per month, and sets at least the minimum base obligation for a noncustodial parent incarcerated over 180 days.

sd:HB 1045.title: revise certain provisions related to child support.
sd:HB 1045.summary: Changes child support rules: sets minimum-wage-times-1,820-hours as the floor for imputed income; continues a parent's order after release from over 180 days' incarceration until modification is requested; lets referees email notices with consent and file hearing exhibits on objections.

sd:HB 1046.title: authorize the Department of Corrections to demolish the Pierre Minimum Center, to make an appropriation therefor, and to declare an emergency.
sd:HB 1046.summary: Authorizes the Department of Corrections to demolish the Pierre Minimum Center and appropriates $682,825 from the general fund for the demolition and site restoration.

sd:HB 1048.title: make an appropriation for the expansion of broadband infrastructure and to declare an emergency.
sd:HB 1048.summary: Appropriates $87 million in federal fund spending authority to the Governor's Office of Economic Development for broadband infrastructure grants under the federal BEAD program.

sd:HB 1049.title: protect electric infrastructure in this state.
sd:HB 1049.summary: Bars prohibited entities under state law, and non-U.S. citizens who are citizens of countries listed there, from owning, operating or controlling electric facilities; requires divestiture within one year of acquisition; lets the Public Utilities Commission seek court-ordered forfeiture.

sd:HB 1051.title: revise property tax levies for school districts and to revise the state aid to general and special education formulas.
sd:HB 1051.summary: Sets school district general fund property tax levy caps for taxes payable in 2027 and later, including $4.867 per thousand dollars of valuation generally, and revises state aid for general and special education.

sd:HB 1056.title: require that the Department of Social Services submit a federal waiver request to exclude soft drinks from the supplemental nutrition assistance program.
sd:HB 1056.summary: Requires the Department of Social Services to seek a federal waiver by September 1, 2026 excluding soft drinks from SNAP-eligible foods, repeating yearly until approved. Soft drinks mean sweetened nonalcoholic beverages, excluding milk, milk substitutes, and certain juices.

sd:HB 1062.title: revise a provision related to aggravated assault.
sd:HB 1062.summary: Rewrites the aggravated assault statute in "no person may" form, removes subsections already deleted, and extends the menacing offense to a physical object realistically simulating a deadly weapon. Aggravated assault remains a Class 3 felony.

sd:HB 1066.title: revise a provision related to theft by a contractor, subcontractor, or supplier.
sd:HB 1066.summary: Rewrites South Dakota's contractor theft law: a contractor, subcontractor or supplier who, with intent to defraud, uses entrusted property for anything other than paying labor, skill or materials for the improvement commits theft, with no $500 threshold.

sd:HB 1077.title: consider a cultivated-protein food product to be adulterated food.
sd:HB 1077.summary: Adds cultivated-protein food products, defined as foods resembling animal tissue made by growing animal cells in vitro, to the foods deemed adulterated under South Dakota food law.

sd:HB 1082.title: establish parameters for the reimbursement of school districts that provide free or reduced-price meals to students.
sd:HB 1082.summary: Bars school districts from charging students eligible for reduced-price meals under the federal lunch and breakfast programs, and has the state Department of Education reimburse districts the difference between the free and reduced-price meal rates for those meals.

sd:HB 1084.title: amend provisions pertaining to the public availability of information contained in certain records.
sd:HB 1084.summary: Bars public inspection of home addresses, phone numbers and personal e-mails in county and statewide voter files, including the historical archive, for current or retired state and federal judges and law enforcement officers; their city and county of residence stay public.

sd:HB 1089.title: modify the distributions of revenues collected from severance taxation on new permits.
sd:HB 1089.summary: Sets the precious-metals severance tax split for permits issued on or after July 1, 2026 at 80 percent to the general fund and 20 percent to the county, without the $1 million county cap that applies to earlier permits.

sd:HB 1092.title: update provisions pertaining to open records.
sd:HB 1092.summary: Updates wording of the records exempt from open records law, including the Gaming Commission’s name, federal law citations, and the security-information exemption’s “including” to “specific to”; other exemptions are largely restated.

sd:HB 1095.title: modify provisions pertaining to the submission of a nominating petition.
sd:HB 1095.summary: Moves petition filing deadlines to the third Tuesday of March (June elections) or August (November elections) for municipal and school board candidates, and to the third Tuesday of March for primary and convention-delegate petitions; also sets petition circulation start dates and candidate withdrawal deadlines.

sd:HB 1096.title: allow for the direct creation of a limited liability limited partnership.
sd:HB 1096.summary: Allows a limited liability limited partnership to be formed directly by filing a certificate with the secretary of state, instead of only by an existing limited partnership filing a statement of qualification. Takes effect January 1, 2027.

sd:HB 1099.title: reschedule the pharmaceutical composition of crystalline polymorph psilocybin in a drug product approved by the Food and Drug Administration as a Schedule IV controlled substance.
sd:HB 1099.summary: Moves the pharmaceutical composition of crystalline polymorph psilocybin in an FDA-approved drug product from Schedule I to Schedule IV of state controlled substances.

sd:HB 1101.title: prohibit an insurer from declining or limiting life, disability, or long-term care insurance policies based solely on an individual's status as a living organ donor.
sd:HB 1101.summary: Bars insurers from declining, limiting, or otherwise discriminating in life, disability, or long-term care insurance solely because a person is a living organ donor.

sd:HB 1102.title: reschedule the date for filing certain annual reports.
sd:HB 1102.summary: As passed by the House, sets the annual report due date for limited liability companies and limited liability partnerships at January 31 each year, effective January 1, 2027.

sd:HB 1106.title: revise the terms of county extension board members.
sd:HB 1106.summary: Limits county extension boards to five or seven members, instead of five to seven, and sets staggered terms of one to three years instead of one-year terms.

sd:HB 1107.title: modify restrictions on lands for certain public purposes.
sd:HB 1107.summary: Adds a court option to modify a grantor's restrictions on land held for religious, educational, charitable or public purposes when the purpose has become impractical, and allows sale proceeds to be reinvested in any manner consistent with that purpose, not only other land.

sd:HB 1108.title: require the sealing of court files upon dismissal or denial of a petition for a protection order.
sd:HB 1108.summary: Requires clerks to seal stalking and domestic abuse protection order petitions dismissed without a hearing, requires courts to seal denied petitions found baseless and harassing, frivolous or abusive, and applies dismissal sealing retroactively to electronic court records.

sd:HB 1111.title: modify the requirements for obtaining an agricultural processor's lien.
sd:HB 1111.summary: Changes the farm-machinery processing lien, effective July 1, 2027: lienholders file a financing statement electronically with the secretary of state within 60 days of finishing the work, instead of filing with the register of deeds, and give the customer a copy.

sd:HB 1119.title: modify provisions regarding directors serving on a farm mutual insurer’s board.
sd:HB 1119.summary: Raises the maximum number of directors of a farm mutual insurer from eleven to fifteen, and lets a director be a member of the insurer or of one of its affiliates.

sd:HB 1126.title: revise a provision related to driving under the influence.
sd:HB 1126.summary: Lowers from six to five the number of DUI convictions within fifteen years that requires a mandatory minimum six-year state prison sentence for an aggravated DUI offense.

sd:HB 1130.title: amend permissible uses of a school district's capital outlay fund.
sd:HB 1130.summary: Rewrites the list of allowed uses of a school district's capital outlay fund as a numbered list and adds payment of the district's property insurance premiums.

sd:HB 1134.title: make an appropriation for the economic development prosperity of South Dakota.
sd:HB 1134.summary: Appropriates $101 from the state general fund for the economic development prosperity of South Dakota, effective June 30, 2026.

sd:HB 1135.title: make an appropriation to enhance the economic health of South Dakota.
sd:HB 1135.summary: Appropriates $101 from the state general fund to enhance the economic health of South Dakota, effective June 30, 2026.

sd:HB 1138.title: require the licensure of non-medical home care agencies, and to provide a penalty therefor.
sd:HB 1138.summary: Requires non-medical home care agencies to be licensed by the Department of Health (fee up to $100, one-year license), with aide training and background checks, and makes operating without a license a Class 1 misdemeanor.

sd:HB 1140.title: permit a court to impose as a condition of probation, or parole in certain circumstances, treatment at a nonprofit entity awarded an alternative care program grant.
sd:HB 1140.summary: Lets a court, with the defendant's consent, require participation in a program at a nonprofit holding an alternative care program grant as a condition of probation or suspended sentence, if the program has availability and the application is completed before sentencing.

sd:HB 1143.title: authorize the possession and self-administration of diabetes medications by a student on school property and at school-related events and activities.
sd:HB 1143.summary: Allows students to possess and self-administer diabetes medications and use related equipment and supplies at school and school events, with parent authorization and a health care provider's written statement.

sd:HB 1146.title: adopt the physician assistant licensure compact.
sd:HB 1146.summary: Adopts the Physician Assistant Licensure Compact, letting physician assistants holding a qualifying license in a participating state obtain a privilege to practice in South Dakota, with state boards keeping power to discipline.

sd:HB 1148.title: adopt the respiratory care interstate compact.
sd:HB 1148.summary: Adopts the Respiratory Care Interstate Compact, letting respiratory therapists licensed in member states practice in South Dakota, and requires fingerprint-based state and federal background checks for respiratory care practitioner license applicants.

sd:HB 1149.title: adopt the athletic trainer licensure compact.
sd:HB 1149.summary: Adopts the Athletic Trainer Compact, letting licensed athletic trainers from member states practice in South Dakota, and requires a fingerprint-based background check, paid by the trainer, for those seeking compact participation.

sd:HB 1160.title: repeal the medical marijuana oversight committee.
sd:HB 1160.summary: Repeals the legislative oversight committee on the state's medical marijuana program, including its membership, chair rules, and its duty to meet twice a year and make recommendations.

sd:HB 1162.title: add certain substances to Schedule I of the controlled substances schedule.
sd:HB 1162.summary: Adds phenibut and tianeptine to the list of Schedule I controlled substances.

sd:HB 1164.title: establish the crime of fraudulent assisted reproduction and provide a penalty and civil liability therefor.
sd:HB 1164.summary: Makes it a Class 5 felony for a licensed health care provider to use donor material, or the provider's own, in assisted reproduction without the patient's written consent, and lets patients, children and donors sue.

sd:HB 1169.title: classify medetomidine as a Schedule III controlled substance and establish permissible uses.
sd:HB 1169.summary: Classifies medetomidine as a Schedule III controlled substance, with exceptions for approved animal drugs, veterinary use, manufacturing for animal drugs, and pharmacy or veterinary compounding.

sd:HB 1175.title: revise provisions related to Division of Criminal Investigation cooperation with Indian tribes.
sd:HB 1175.summary: Extends from the Sisseton-Wahpeton Sioux Tribe to any Indian tribe the Division of Criminal Investigation's ability to obtain national criminal history records on people seeking or serving in listed tribal positions, such as council members, judges, gaming licensees, and foster parents.

sd:HB 1176.title: clarify bond or pre-trial release upon sobriety program participation.
sd:HB 1176.summary: Bars jailing a defendant or revoking bond for not paying 24/7 sobriety program costs unless a court finds they can pay, puts the burden on the defendant to show non-willful nonpayment, and lets the sobriety fund reimburse counties.

sd:HB 1180.title: ensure the validity of non-compete agreements in the context of jointly owned business entities.
sd:HB 1180.summary: Lets owners of a business entity agree, in governing documents or a sale contract, to a non-compete barring a former owner from the same type of business in the entity's geographic area for up to three years after transfer.

sd:HB 1184.title: define man and woman throughout the state.
sd:HB 1184.summary: Defines male and female by the type of reproductive system an individual naturally has or would have, defines man, woman, boy, girl, mother, father and sex, and applies the definitions to state and local government laws, rules and policies.

sd:HB 1187.title: add coaches to the list of mandatory reporters of child abuse or neglect.
sd:HB 1187.summary: Adds coaches of school activities to the people required to report suspected child abuse or neglect.

sd:HB 1188.title: limit the liability of law enforcement officers and others when removing a disabled vehicle from a highway, a right of way, or public waters.
sd:HB 1188.summary: Lets highway patrol, transportation department, sheriff and peace officers arrange removal of disabled vehicles and spilled cargo, makes the owner liable for costs, and shields them from damages absent gross negligence or willful misconduct.

sd:HB 1189.title: establish a greater tire weight limit for a mobile crane moving on any highway in this state.
sd:HB 1189.summary: Sets a higher tire weight limit of 650 pounds per inch of tire width for axles on permitted mobile cranes with a boom, compared with 600 or 500 pounds for other axles. Defines a mobile crane.

sd:HB 1193.title: modify the provisions for a refund of taxes to disabled veterans and surviving spouses under certain property tax relief programs.
sd:HB 1193.summary: Specifies that county commissioners may abate or refund property taxes for up to the previous four years for disabled veterans and surviving spouses who qualify for the $200,000 exemption but missed an application deadline.

sd:HB 1194.title: clarify authority for the Cosmetology Commission to credit work experience for educational hours for certain out-of-state licensure applicants, and to require the commission to promulgate rules therefor.
sd:HB 1194.summary: Requires the Cosmetology Commission to credit post-licensure work experience toward education hours, at two work hours per education hour and up to half the required hours, for applicants whose out-of-state licenses are not equivalent to a South Dakota license.

sd:HB 1197.title: revise a provision related to the venue of adoption proceedings.
sd:HB 1197.summary: Lets adoption petitions be filed in the county where the adopting parent lives, the agency with custody of the child is located, or the child was born or lives, instead of only the child's or adopting parent's county of residence.

sd:HB 1199.title: address prior authorization and reporting requirements by utilization review organizations and health carriers.
sd:HB 1199.summary: Requires health insurers and utilization review organizations to report annually on prior authorization approvals, denials and decision times, and to drop prior authorization requirements for services that are routinely approved.

sd:HB 1200.title: make an appropriation for victim services provided by nonprofit organizations.
sd:HB 1200.summary: Appropriates general fund money to the Department of Public Safety for grants to nonprofits assisting abused or neglected children and victims of domestic violence, sexual assault or trafficking, for services such as emergency lodging, licensed counseling, crisis lines and child advocacy centers.

sd:HB 1209.title: require employment verification eligibility through the e-verify program and to provide a penalty therefor.
sd:HB 1209.summary: Requires employers with more than 50 employees to verify new hires through E-Verify within 20 days, and lets the attorney general seek a $2,000 civil penalty per violation when federal agencies confirm knowing employment of an unauthorized worker.

sd:HB 1215.title: authorize counties and municipalities to issue a license for a cigar bar.
sd:HB 1215.summary: Lets counties and municipalities license cigar bars on the premises of certain alcohol-licensed establishments that have a humidor, enclosed ventilated space, and at least 10 percent of income from cigars, and allows only cigars to be smoked there.

sd:HB 1219.title: require the provision of interpreter or translator services for parties to an administrative contested case.
sd:HB 1219.summary: Requires the agency to appoint and pay an interpreter or translator for a party or witness who needs one in an administrative contested case, and lets the prevailing party recover other interpreter or translator costs.

sd:HB 1220.title: regulate the sale of nicotine products, and to provide a penalty therefor.
sd:HB 1220.summary: Requires nicotine product distributors to hold a Department of Revenue license ($1,000 fee), limits retailers to buying from licensed distributors, sets age-21 verification for direct shipments to consumers, and makes unlicensed sales a Class 1 misdemeanor.

sd:HB 1232.title: establish principles for a state agency to consider when formulating or implementing a program that has the potential of affecting tribal members on a reservation.
sd:HB 1232.summary: Establishes principles for state agencies developing or running programs that could affect tribal members on a reservation, including cooperation, respect for tribal sovereignty, early communication with tribal officials, and accountability.

sd:HB 1233.title: modify provisions for a tax collection agreement with an Indian tribe.
sd:HB 1233.summary: Specifies that state tax collection agreements with Indian tribes may cover sales and use taxes as applied to out-of-state sellers (chapter 10-64) and marketplace providers (chapter 10-65).

sd:HB 1234.title: revise provisions related to serving a subpoena in a contested case.
sd:HB 1234.summary: Lets attorneys of record issue subpoenas in agency contested cases. Requires notice and a copy of a document subpoena to go to all parties first. Lets the hearing examiner or judge quash an unreasonable subpoena or condition denial on advance payment of costs.

sd:HB 1238.title: protect financial institutions taking action to prevent the financial exploitation of consenting, senior, or vulnerable adults.
sd:HB 1238.summary: Allows financial institutions to delay or refuse transactions, hold withdrawals, and block account changes when they reasonably suspect financial exploitation of a consenting, senior (65+), or vulnerable adult, and to notify third parties. Grants immunity from liability for acting or not acting.

sd:HB 1241.title: modify the requirements for public notice of a hearing prior to a vote to impose an excess tax levy, and to modify requirements to refer an excess tax levy of a school district to a vote.
sd:HB 1241.summary: As amended, requires school and other taxing districts to publish notice at least 21 days before voting on an excess tax levy; sets the school-levy referral petition at 5% of voters or 2,500, whichever is less; requires ballots to state years and maximum total dollars.

sd:HB 1244.title: repeal the special donations fund and make an appropriation to the Department of Education for the provision of a grant to support the Jobs for America's Graduates-South Dakota program.
sd:HB 1244.summary: Appropriates $500,000 to the Department of Education for a grant supporting Jobs for America's Graduates programs in schools, and moves money in the special donation fund to the general fund and repeals that fund.

sd:HB 1245.title: authorize municipalities to establish a local funding mechanism for capital improvement projects.
sd:HB 1245.summary: Lets municipalities impose a temporary gross receipts tax of up to 1 percent for capital projects, if a five-member capital improvement board approves and 60 percent of voters voting approve; revenue goes to a special capital outlay fund.

sd:HB 1249.title: amend provisions pertaining to the School Finance Accountability Board, and the process by which a recommendation of the board is approved.
sd:HB 1249.summary: Lets the School Finance Accountability Board itself waive a district's state aid reduction for excess cash balances or its teacher-pay penalty for special circumstances, replacing legislative committee review of recommended waivers. Waivers may be conditioned on three years of compliance.

sd:HB 1250.title: revise the types of community-based providers for purposes of state funded services.
sd:HB 1250.summary: Adds critical access hospitals and federally qualified health centers to the community-based provider types covered by the chapter on state-funded services.

sd:HB 1253.title: adjust the assessment methodology for owner-occupied single-family dwellings and nonagricultural property.
sd:HB 1253.summary: As amended, directs county equalization directors to annually adjust assessed value of owner-occupied single-family homes and nonagricultural property to the average of the most recent eight years' market values, dropping the highest and lowest. The adjustment may not raise taxes on agricultural property.

sd:HB 1254.title: exempt any soil amendment used exclusively for agricultural purposes from sales tax.
sd:HB 1254.summary: Exempts soil amendments from sales tax when 500 pounds or more of one product is sold in a single sale for exclusively agricultural use.

sd:HB 1257.title: amend the definition of an abortion.
sd:HB 1257.summary: Excludes from the legal definition of abortion treatment of a miscarriage or ectopic pregnancy, removal of a deceased unborn child, accidental death from medical treatment, and procedures to save the life or preserve the health of the unborn child. Defines "miscarriage."

sd:HB 1258.title: require that a property tax bill provide access to a state website providing property tax information.
sd:HB 1258.summary: Requires county property tax bills to include a QR code and web address linking to a Department of Revenue website on property taxes and tax relief programs, plus a notice that more information is available there.

sd:HB 1260.title: authorize the establishment of municipal property tax rebate programs.
sd:HB 1260.summary: Allows a municipality to establish by ordinance a program giving rebates of municipal property taxes to owners of owner-occupied single-family homes, and requires it to pay rebates to applicants who meet the ordinance's criteria.

sd:HB 1262.title: make an appropriation for a non-residential, school-based, therapeutic services facility in Brown County and to declare an emergency.
sd:HB 1262.summary: Appropriates $2 million to the Department of Education for a grant to a nonprofit to acquire, renovate and equip a non-residential, school-based therapeutic services facility for students in an alternative setting.

sd:HB 1263.title: eliminate an exclusion from the definition of an agricultural equipment dealer.
sd:HB 1263.summary: Removes the exclusion for dealers whose principal business is selling off-road construction equipment from the statutory definition of dealer for agricultural equipment.

sd:HB 1264.title: eliminate the Agricultural Land Assessment Implementation and Oversight Advisory Task Force, and to provide that the Department of Revenue receive the submission of recommendations and provide a report on agricultural value.
sd:HB 1264.summary: Repeals the Agricultural Land Assessment Implementation and Oversight Advisory Task Force, removes its review role, and requires the Department of Revenue to report annually by March 1 to the tax committees on agricultural income-value data.

sd:HB 1265.title: authorize the salvage of certain bird eggs.
sd:HB 1265.summary: Allows salvage of eggs of certain protected birds by people holding a federal migratory bird special purpose salvage permit, except eggs of birds whose taking is always prohibited.

sd:HB 1274.title: prohibit the dispensing, distribution, sale, or advertisement of certain articles or things for purposes of an unlawful abortion and provide a criminal and civil penalty therefor.
sd:HB 1274.summary: Makes it a Class 6 felony to knowingly dispense, distribute, sell or advertise items for an unlawful abortion, and lets the attorney general seek civil penalties up to $10,000 per violation, plus injunctions.

sd:HB 1279.title: permit technical college employees to join the state health plan.
sd:HB 1279.summary: Allows technical colleges to join the state employee health plan on terms agreed with the human resources commissioner. The employing local education agency pays at least the state's usual employer contribution. Covers permanent employees scheduled 20+ hours a week. Takes effect July 1, 2027.

sd:HB 1286.title: amend the process by which moneys are distributed from the employer's investment in South Dakota's future fund.
sd:HB 1286.summary: Requires business applicants to the employer's investment in South Dakota's future fund to submit business plans and all awardees to sign public agreements. Awards reimburse only actual costs; awards over $1 million need itemized invoices. Makes grant reports annual, to more legislative committees.

sd:HB 1292.title: limit the ability of a health carrier to recoup, recover, or retroactively deny previously paid claims.
sd:HB 1292.summary: Limits health carriers to recouping or retroactively denying paid claims within 18 months of payment, with written notice of the reason. Exceptions include fraud, waste or abuse, Medicare, Medicaid, workers' compensation and self-insured ERISA plans. Applies to services from July 1, 2026.

sd:HB 1298.title: prohibit the electronic publication of certain information about a judicial officer or law enforcement officer and provide a penalty therefor.
sd:HB 1298.summary: Makes it a Class 6 felony to electronically publish a judicial or law enforcement officer's home address, date of birth, or Social Security number, without consent and with intent to place the officer or immediate family in reasonable fear of death or great bodily injury.

sd:HB 1299.title: permit the use of biological filtration systems in water recreational facilities located in certain lodging establishments.
sd:HB 1299.summary: Lets lodging establishments with 15 or fewer rooms apply for a one-year permit (fee up to $50) to use a biological filtration system in a water recreational facility, with annual inspections and permit revocation on a failed inspection.

sd:HB 1300.title: except victims of human trafficking or domestic abuse from certain clemency notice requirements.
sd:HB 1300.summary: Exempts clemency applicants who are victims of human trafficking or domestic abuse from the newspaper-publication notice requirement if they and two listed professionals, such as police or counselors, submit affidavits, including that the applicant's safety is at risk. Victim-notification rights are unchanged.

sd:HB 1302.title: address issues facing South Dakota.
sd:HB 1302.summary: States that the Legislature shall address issues facing South Dakota. As introduced, the bill contains no other provisions.

sd:HB 1311.title: require the reporting of funding given by certain persons and governments to institutions under the control of the Board of Regents and the South Dakota Board of Technical Education.
sd:HB 1311.summary: Requires the Board of Regents and the Board of Technical Education to report annually any funding received from sources in China, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Russia or Venezuela, including amounts, purposes and sources.

sd:HB 1320.title: revise a provision related to service of process for boards of county commissioners.
sd:HB 1320.summary: Changes how an appeal of a county commission decision starts: written notice may be served on any county auditor or commissioner, the county's state's attorney, or a person the board designates by resolution.

sd:HB 1323.title: modify the requirements to refer an ordinance or resolution to the voters of a political subdivision.
sd:HB 1323.summary: As amended, changes how voters refer county, municipal and school district decisions to a public vote: petitions need signatures of 5 percent of registered voters or 2,500, whichever is fewer, and certain county and municipal decisions cannot be referred.

sd:HB 1326.title: appropriate money for the ordinary expenses of the legislative, judicial, and executive departments of the state, the current expenses of state institutions, interest on the public debt, and common schools.
sd:HB 1326.summary: Appropriates money for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2027, for the ordinary expenses of state government's legislative, judicial and executive departments, state institutions, interest on the public debt, and common schools, with amounts set by budget unit.

sd:SB 100.title: revise provisions related to trusts.
sd:SB 100.summary: Revises trust law: lets a trustee, unless the trust bars it, pay a trustor's income tax on trust income; sets rules on when gifts and distributions count as advancements; and limits an attorney's duties to others when advising a fiduciary.

sd:SB 101.title: amend provisions pertaining to the duties of presidential electors.
sd:SB 101.summary: Requires presidential electors to pledge to vote for their party's nominees and for the state's winning ticket, unless a nominee withdraws, dies or is disabled; vacates the seat and voids the ballot if an elector votes otherwise or casts a blank ballot.

sd:SB 102.title: modify the distribution of gaming revenues.
sd:SB 102.summary: Changes the split of remaining gaming proceeds to 25 percent general fund, 3.3 percent other Lawrence County municipalities, 0.7 percent certain school districts and 71 percent Deadwood, replacing 70/10/10/10, and drops the $6.8 million Deadwood threshold.

sd:SB 106.title: modify the amount required to be set aside for extraordinary expenses incurred in providing special education programs.
sd:SB 106.summary: Raises the annual special education set-aside for extraordinary expenses from $4 million to $5 million beginning July 1, 2026; unspent funds do not revert if the total reserved in a year stays at or below $5.5 million.

sd:SB 111.title: require that social media companies provide collected personal data of a user at the user's request and maintain transparent interoperability interfaces.
sd:SB 111.summary: Requires social media services with over 100 million monthly users to give users a portable copy of their personal data on request and to provide interoperability interfaces, including export of a user's social graph.

sd:SB 113.title: increase the penalty for preventing practice of religion.
sd:SB 113.summary: Raises the penalty for using threat or violence to intentionally prevent another person from performing a lawful religious act from a Class 1 misdemeanor to a Class 6 felony.

sd:SB 114.title: provide for the publication of ballot images and the cast vote record of automatic tabulating equipment.
sd:SB 114.summary: Makes cast vote records and ballot images from automatic vote tabulators public records, but bars release of any that show when or in what order ballots were cast, contain unredacted voter-identifying information, or come from precincts with under 100 ballots unless redacted and combined.

sd:SB 119.title: create the capitol restoration fund and to transfer moneys thereto.
sd:SB 119.summary: Creates the capitol restoration fund for restoring and improving the state capitol, and transfers $1.1 million into it from the public buildings fund. Spending requires a special legislative appropriation.

sd:SB 120.title: make an appropriation for the economic development of South Dakota.
sd:SB 120.summary: Appropriates $101 from the state general fund for the economic development of South Dakota, effective June 30, 2026.

sd:SB 121.title: transfer moneys and make an appropriation for the replacement of the Richmond Lake dam and spillway and to declare an emergency.
sd:SB 121.summary: Transfers $8.2 million from the unclaimed property trust fund to the general fund and appropriates the same amount to replace the Richmond Lake dam and spillway.

sd:SB 122.title: establish the crime of failure to summon aid for a suicide attempt and provide a penalty therefor.
sd:SB 122.summary: Makes it a Class 1 misdemeanor to be present at a suicide attempt, know of it, and intentionally fail to summon help, with defenses for reasonable fear of harm, belief aid was summoned, or being under 18.

sd:SB 124.title: temporarily prohibit the manufacture, sale, and distribution of any product containing cell-cultured protein, and to provide a penalty therefor.
sd:SB 124.summary: Bans selling, making or distributing products containing cell-cultured protein from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2031, enforced by inspections, stop-sale orders and seizure; violations are a Class 2 misdemeanor.

sd:SB 125.title: establish the homeowner tax reduction fund.
sd:SB 125.summary: Creates a homeowner tax reduction fund in the state treasury, run by the Department of Revenue, to provide property tax relief for owner-occupied single-family homes; interest stays in the fund and money cannot move to the general fund.

sd:SB 130.title: make an appropriation for roadway and related infrastructure improvements required because of construction activity at Ellsworth Air Force Base and to declare an emergency.
sd:SB 130.summary: Appropriates $8 million from the general fund to the South Dakota Ellsworth Development Authority for roadway and related infrastructure improvements needed because of construction on Ellsworth Air Force Base, with administrative costs capped at 3 percent.

sd:SB 131.title: revise the season in which a nonprofit organization may host a special pheasant hunt for disabled veterans and Purple Heart recipients.
sd:SB 131.summary: Changes the season for a nonprofit's special pheasant hunt for disabled veterans and Purple Heart recipients from before or during the regular pheasant season to the private shooting preserve season, and revises the "disabled veteran" definition.

sd:SB 133.title: provide additional legislative oversight of rulemaking.
sd:SB 133.summary: Requires state agencies to prepare a regulatory impact analysis, including whether a rule is a major rule, before proposing permanent rules, and revises rulemaking procedures and the Interim Rules Review Committee's duties.

sd:SB 134.title: restrict deference to a state agency's interpretation of a state statute, administrative rule, or policy.
sd:SB 134.summary: As introduced, bars courts and administrative hearing officers from deferring to a state agency's interpretation of a statute, rule or policy, requiring them to interpret its meaning independently.

sd:SB 135.title: protect residents from increased utility costs and utility shortages caused by data centers and clarify authority to regulate data centers.
sd:SB 135.summary: Requires electric providers to set separate service terms making data centers of 10 megawatts or more reimburse their attributable costs, requires water-use notices before operating, and preserves local authority to regulate data centers.

sd:SB 136.title: make an appropriation for grants to support the purchase of personal protective equipment by volunteer fire departments and to declare an emergency.
sd:SB 136.summary: Appropriates $5,000,000 from the general fund to the Department of Public Safety for grants to buy firefighter protective equipment for fire departments that are at least 70 percent volunteer, awarding applications in order received and prioritizing greatest need; unspent funds revert after June 30, 2030.

sd:SB 137.title: establish procedures for anti-SLAPP actions to protect the exercise of a person's constitutional rights, including freedom of speech.
sd:SB 137.summary: Creates anti-SLAPP procedures: a person sued over speech, petition or government-proceeding communications may file a special motion to dismiss within 60 days, pausing discovery; costs and attorney fees are available. Excludes suits against governments, some government enforcement actions, and claims against sellers.

sd:SB 138.title: revise the time within which a recount for a school board election must be completed.
sd:SB 138.summary: Changes how school board election recount boards are appointed, with the secretary of state naming the extra member if candidates do not agree, and requires recounts to finish before the board's annual meeting.

sd:SB 14.title: modify provisions related to the practice of pharmacy.
sd:SB 14.summary: Defines pharmacist-in-charge and lets a non-pharmacist owner hold a pharmacy license by delegating to one. Allows owners to change that designation. Allows pharmacies to deliver prescriptions through remote drop sites supervised by the pharmacist-in-charge.

sd:SB 15.title: create the Developmental Disability Service Delivery Committee.
sd:SB 15.summary: Creates a nine-member Developmental Disability Service Delivery Committee to examine Medicaid waiver programs for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities, including streamlining provider reviews, and report to the Legislative Research Council's executive board each December 31.

sd:SB 151.title: require the publication of the results of an election for precinct committeeman or committeewoman and to declare an emergency.
sd:SB 151.summary: Requires county auditors to send the secretary of state the names and primary election results of precinct committeeman and committeewoman candidates, including those elected without opposition, and requires the secretary of state to post them online.

sd:SB 153.title: prohibit certain restrictions in employment contracts for community services providers.
sd:SB 153.summary: Makes contract provisions entered into on or after July 1, 2026 voidable if they bar a community services provider from working with people with developmental disabilities after employment ends, except sale-of-practice terms and client-solicitation limits.

sd:SB 154.title: clarify the eligibility of multiple garages or structures to be classified as owner-occupied.
sd:SB 154.summary: Includes all garages and ancillary structures used with a home, and the land beneath them, in the owner-occupied single-family dwelling property tax classification.

sd:SB 159.title: revise requirements pertaining to the minimum age for marriage.
