tn:SB 1915.summary: Adds counties and cities to those verifying public-benefit applicants' lawful presence; requires government entities to report unlawfully present recipients to the state immigration enforcement division, with a Class A misdemeanor for intentional failure; lets the attorney general withhold state funds from noncomplying localities.

tn:SB 1992.title: Criminal Offenses - As enacted, creates a Class E felony offense when a person, for the purpose of deriving a pecuniary benefit, engages in conduct intended to influence the occurrence or nonoccurrence of an event while the person, or another acting in active concert with the person, is a party to a contract traded on a prediction-market by which the person will derive such pecuniary benefit directly from the settlement of that contract based on the occurrence or a nonoccurrence of the event. - Amends TCA Title 39.
tn:SB 1992.summary: Creates a Class E felony for a person who holds a prediction-market contract and acts to influence whether an event occurs in order to profit from that contract.

tn:SB 2040.title: Pharmacy, Pharmacists - As enacted, enacts the "Freedom, Access, and Integrity in Registered Pharmacy (FAIR Rx) Act." - Amends TCA Title 63.
tn:SB 2040.summary: Enacts the FAIR Rx Act: from July 1, 2028, bars owning or controlling (over 5%) a pharmacy together with both a health insurer and a pharmacy benefits manager, with civil penalties up to $10,000 per violation. Exempts orphan and limited-distribution drugs.

tn:SB 2055.title: Local Education Agencies - As enacted, requires LEAs and public charter schools to allow a private pay provider who is under contract with a parent or legal guardian of a student with autism spectrum disorder or developmental delays who is enrolled in the LEA or public charter school, access to the student during the school day to provide the student with private pay services in educational settings as long as the educational settings in which private pay services are provided do not conflict with the student's educational placement; makes other related changes. - Amends TCA Title 49; Title 68 and Title 71.
tn:SB 2055.summary: Requires public school districts and charter schools to let a parent-hired private provider give a student with autism or developmental delays applied behavior analysis on school grounds during the school day, coordinated with the student's IEP team.

tn:SB 2085.title: Victims' Rights - As enacted, authorizes a court clerk to increase the victims assistance assessment from $45 to $125, with the first $15 of each assessment being paid to the court clerk for processing and handling and the remaining amount being transmitted to the county in which the offense occurred for the exclusive use of the victims assistance program previously designated by the county legislative body. - Amends TCA Section 40-24-109.
tn:SB 2085.summary: Sets the victims assistance assessment on defendants who plead or are found guilty at $125, up from $45. Clerks keep the first $15 for processing and send $110 to the county's victims assistance program.

tn:SB 2136.title: Gambling - As enacted, clarifies that gambling, the operation or possession of gambling devices, and the operation, conducting, or commercial promoting of online sweepstakes games and other forms of online or app-based gambling are unlawful and a violation of  the Tennessee Consumer Protection Act; expands the authority of the sports wagering council to investigate illegal gambling and gaming activity; expands the investigative authority of the attorney general to investigate unlawful activity within the purview of the attorney general. - Amends TCA Title 4; Title 4, Chapter 49; Title 8, Chapter 6, Part 4; Title 40, Chapter 2 and Title 47.
tn:SB 2136.summary: Declares gambling, gambling devices and online sweepstakes games unlawful (lawful licensed games excepted) and a Consumer Protection Act violation; lets the attorney general demand information in investigations of unlawful acts, and the sports wagering council investigate non-licensees.

tn:SB 2145.title: Orders of Protection - As enacted, allows a person to file a petition for a lifetime order of protection against a person who was convicted of certain offenses in another jurisdiction; provides that venue for such a petition is in the county where the respondent resides or, if the respondent is not a resident of this state, the county where the petitioner resides. - Amends TCA Title 36 and Title 39.
tn:SB 2145.summary: Lets a victim seek a lifetime order of protection against an offender convicted in another state of a comparable felony assaultive, homicide, kidnapping or sexual offense, filed in the respondent's county or, if the respondent lives out of state, the petitioner's county.

tn:SB 2162.title: Open Meetings - As enacted, authorizes a governing body to conduct an executive session for the purpose of interviewing applicants for employment as director-level staff of the body without providing public notice of such session. - Amends TCA Title 8.
tn:SB 2162.summary: As enacted, allows a governing body to hold a closed executive session, without public notice, to interview applicants for director-level staff jobs. Deliberation and votes must occur in an open, noticed meeting.

tn:SB 2213.title: Public Utilities - As enacted, requires a utility to provide material that is required for construction of utility infrastructure for the customer's or approved contractor's use at the same price as the utility paid for the material, if such material is available only from the utility; authorizes a customer or approved contractor installing utility infrastructure to install street lights; prohibits a utility from requiring a customer or approved contractor from installing street lights; prohibits certain fees for inspections and review of plans and designs from exceeding a combined total of 10% of the proposed cost of the project. - Amends TCA Title 7; Title 13, Chapter 7; Title 65 and Title 68.
tn:SB 2213.summary: As enacted, requires a utility to sell a customer or approved contractor building utility infrastructure any required material available only from the utility at the utility's cost; bars requiring street lights; and caps combined plan review and inspection fees at 10% of project cost.

tn:SB 2221.title: TennCare - As enacted, extends the ground ambulance service annual assessment to June 30, 2027; changes the penalty imposed by the bureau on an ambulance provider for each day an assessment remains unpaid from $50 per calendar day to 5 percent of the principal amount owed per month for each month. - Amends TCA Title 71, Chapter 5, Part 15.
tn:SB 2221.summary: Extends the ground ambulance service assessment to June 30, 2027, and changes the penalty for unpaid assessments from $50 per day to 5 percent of the principal owed per month.

tn:SB 2228.title: Education - As enacted, makes various revisions to education law, including, but not limited to, prohibiting parents from using funds deposited in a participating student's IEA to make contributions to an achieving a better life experience account for purposes of the ABLE Act, and requiring the Title VI coordinator for a LEA or public charter school to investigate certain complaints of antisemitic discrimination and harassment reported to the LEA or public charter school before formally reporting the incidents and complaints to the Title VI coordinator designated by the department of education. - Amends TCA Title 4, Chapter 29; Title 5, Chapter 21; Title 8, Chapter 50, Part 8; Title 49, Chapter 10, Part 1; Title 49, Chapter 10, Part 14; Title 49, Chapter 11, Part 1; Title 49, Chapter 11, Part 8; Title 49, Chapter 13; Title 49, Chapter 15, Part 1; Title 49, Chapter 16, Part 2; Title 49, Chapter 17; Section 49-2-203; Title 49, Chapter 3, Part 1; Title 49, Chapter 5, Part 4; Title 49, Chapter 50, Part 10; Title 49, Chapter 50, Part 16; Title 49, Chapter 50, Part 18; Title 49, Chapter 6, Part 10; Title 49, Chapter 6, Part 15; Title 49, Chapter 6, Part 22; Title 49, Chapter 6, Part 23; Title 49, Chapter 6, Part 30; Title 49, Chapter 6, Part 34; Title 49, Chapter 6, Part 42; Title 49, Chapter 6, Part 81; Title 49, Chapter 1, Part 2; Title 49, Chapter 1, Part 3 and Section 68-204-110.
tn:SB 2228.summary: As enacted, makes various education law changes, including barring parents from using student individualized education account (IEA) funds for ABLE account contributions and requiring local Title VI coordinators to investigate certain antisemitic discrimination and harassment complaints before reporting them to the state coordinator.

tn:SB 2237.title: Local Government, General - As enacted, requires a local government responsible for reviewing a development application, development plan, or a site inspection submitted by a developer for the purpose of developing real property in this state, within 60 business days of the submission, to approve the application, plan, or site inspection or add the submission to the next available agenda of either the planning commission or the governing body; makes other related changes. - Amends TCA Title 7.
tn:SB 2237.summary: As enacted, requires local governments to approve a development application or put it on an agenda within 60 business days, or send a deficiency report or information request within 30; if they do none, the submission is deemed approved.

tn:SB 2265.title: Criminal Offenses - As enacted, makes various changes relative to the offense of organized retail crime. - Amends TCA Title 18; Title 38, Chapter 6, Part 1 and Title 39.
tn:SB 2265.summary: Changes the organized retail crime offense: adds a 30-day mandatory minimum sentence when a firearm, ammunition or anti-theft device is used or possessed, extends the value-aggregation period from 90 to 180 days, and covers use of masks or missing, altered, fake or temporary license plates.

tn:SB 2283.title: Tourism - As enacted, requires revenue that is received by a municipality and that is used to fund a destination marketing entity engaged in tourism promotion on behalf of the municipality be released to the destination marketing entity no later than 120 days after the municipality approves its final budget. - Amends TCA Title 5; Title 6; Title 7 and Title 67.
tn:SB 2283.summary: Requires municipalities to release hotel tax revenue they use to fund a destination marketing entity to that entity within 120 days after approving their final budget.

tn:SB 2293.title: Tobacco, Tobacco Products - As enacted, expands the definition of "consumable material" to include natural and synthetic liquid nicotine solutions and liquid nicotine analogues for purposes of the taxation of vapor products containing such material; requires the alcoholic beverage commission to issue the fines for the offense of selling or offering for sale a vapor product for retail sale in this state to anyone under 21. - Amends TCA Title 39, Chapter 17; Title 43; Title 57 and Title 67, Chapter 4, Part 10.
tn:SB 2293.summary: Expands the vapor product tax definition of consumable material to include natural and synthetic liquid nicotine solutions and liquid nicotine analogues, and specifies that the alcoholic beverage commission issues fines for selling vapor products to anyone under 21.

tn:SB 2317.title: Education - As enacted, requires the department of education to implement a pilot program to evaluate whether administering fewer district- and state-mandated assessments results in students achieving greater academic success; adds an additional method by which a student who is not proficient in ELA, as determined by the student's achieving a performance level rating of “approaching” on the ELA portion of the student's most recent TCAP test, may be promoted. - Amends TCA Title 49.
tn:SB 2317.summary: As enacted, requires the Department of Education to run a pilot with up to ten eligible local education agencies testing whether fewer state and district assessments help students, limiting tests for K-8 students above the 40th percentile on screeners in 2027-2029.

tn:SB 2318.title: Schools, Charter - As enacted, allows private postsecondary institutions, including those that are religiously affiliated, to operate a public charter school; allows such institutions to apply to the local board of education or directly to the Tennessee public charter school commission to open a public charter school and to give an enrollment preference to children of the institution's employees or members of its governing body in the same manner afforded to public institutions of higher education. - Amends TCA Title 49.
tn:SB 2318.summary: Allows regionally accredited private colleges and universities with a Tennessee campus, including religiously affiliated ones, to sponsor and establish public charter schools; nonpublic K-12 schools may not establish them.

tn:SB 2338.title: Fire Prevention and Investigation - As enacted, requires the commissioner of commerce and insurance to fulfill certain duties for the volunteer firefighter vehicle grant program, which is established to annually provide grants to select volunteer fire departments to assist with local match requirements for federal grants to purchase vehicles. - Amends TCA Title 68.
tn:SB 2338.summary: Creates a volunteer firefighter vehicle grant program giving volunteer fire departments grants toward the local match for federal vehicle-purchase grants, with stated intent to fund it with $1 million in fiscal year 2026-27.

tn:SB 2367.title: County Government - As enacted, applies the Neighborhood Preservation Act to Tipton County; authorizes Montgomery County and Tipton County to participate in the Tennessee Local Land Bank Program. - Amends TCA Title 5 and Title 13.
tn:SB 2367.summary: Applies the Neighborhood Preservation Act to Tipton County and lets Montgomery and Tipton counties participate in the Tennessee Local Land Bank Program.

tn:SB 2410.title: Housing - As enacted, establishes the community workforce housing innovation pilot program to be administered by the Tennessee housing development agency; authorizes the agency to provide loans to an applicant for construction or rehabilitation of workforce housing in each of the three grand divisions; requires the housing to be affordable to natural persons or families who meet certain criteria. - Amends TCA Title 7, Chapter 53; Title 13; Title 48, Chapter 101, Part 3; Title 56 and Title 67.
tn:SB 2410.summary: Creates a pilot program in which the Tennessee housing development agency makes loans to build or rehabilitate workforce housing for households earning 80 to 150 percent of area median income, with at least one project in each grand division.

tn:SB 2419.title: Fireworks - As enacted, requires a person who offers sparkling devices for sale and who does not hold a fireworks permit to register each location at which the person offers such devices for sale with the state fire marshal; makes other related changes. - Amends TCA Title 68.
tn:SB 2419.summary: Requires sellers of sparkling devices without a fireworks permit to register each sales location with the state fire marshal for $25, expiring December 31, and applies fireworks age, location, and county sales rules to sparkling devices.

tn:SB 2431.title: Health Care - As enacted, makes various changes to health-related laws, including, but not limited to, requiring the commissioner of health to prescribe conditions under which processed and verified claims data found on the UB-92 form are made available to the public; revising law relative to critical access hospitals, and revising law relative to certificates of need. - Amends TCA Title 33; Title 63 and Title 68.
tn:SB 2431.summary: Makes health law changes, including directing the health commissioner to set conditions for releasing hospital and surgery center claims data to the public, revising critical access hospital rules, and requiring diagnostic centers and PET providers to be accredited by a CMS-approved organization.

tn:SB 2452.title: Alcoholic Beverages - As enacted, authorizes the consumption of alcoholic beverages and beer on the premises of a temporary special event zone located in Davidson County, subject to certain requirements. - Amends TCA Title 7 and Title 57.
tn:SB 2452.summary: Allows drinking alcoholic beverages and beer outside licensed premises within a temporary special event zone in a metropolitan-government county of over 500,000 residents, only for events approved under a zone ordinance and in event-designed to-go cups.

tn:SB 2461.title: Hospitals and Health Care Facilities - As enacted, requires each fertility clinic operating in this state to obtain a certificate from the department of health to perform assisted reproductive technology services. - Amends TCA Title 4; Title 29; Title 36; Title 63 and Title 68.
tn:SB 2461.summary: Requires fertility clinics to hold a Department of Health certificate, renewed every two years, with proof of Society for Assisted Reproductive Technology membership or an approved equivalent, a plan to transfer embryos if the clinic closes, and a passed lab inspection.

tn:SB 2468.title: Criminal Offenses - As enacted, makes revisions to law relative to offenses occurring at a house of worship. - Amends TCA Title 29 and Title 39.
tn:SB 2468.summary: Adds a fine of at least twice the damages for vandalism at a house of worship. Makes it a Class E felony (Class C for repeat offenses) to use force, threats, or obstruction against worshippers there or to damage the property, and allows civil suits.

tn:SB 2473.title: Regional Authorities and Special Districts - As enacted, vacates the present board of commissioners of each existing authority for metropolitan and regional airports and reconstitutes a new governing body; makes related changes. - Amends TCA Title 4; Title 7 and Title 42.
tn:SB 2473.summary: Vacates the boards of existing airport authorities and replaces them with nine-member boards (twelve for certain regional authorities) appointed by the governor, the House and Senate speakers and the creating city, with staggered terms and a bar on members with financial interests in an airport.

tn:SB 2504.title: Natural Disasters - As enacted, enacts the "Local Disaster Displacement Tax Relief Act." - Amends TCA Title 7, Chapter 4; Title 58 and Title 67, Chapter 4.
tn:SB 2504.summary: Lets a county under a declared emergency authorize hotel operators and short-term rental marketplaces to waive hotel occupancy taxes, or reimburse taxes paid, for residents displaced from their homes, for up to 14 days.

tn:SB 2509.title: Children - As enacted, enacts the "Tennessee Child Care Red Tape Reduction Act." - Amends TCA Title 13, Chapter 7 and Title 71, Chapter 3.
tn:SB 2509.summary: Requires local governments to give child care agency permit applications the same priority as affordable housing applications, assigned for review within five business days, and makes the state fire marshal the only fire safety inspector for child care licensure.

tn:SB 2528.title: Recreational Areas - As enacted, expands the purposes for which monies from the Ocoee River recreation and economic development fund may be expended by the Ocoee River recreation and economic development fund board; replaces the park manager member of the board with the director of the division of state parks. - Amends TCA Title 4, Chapter 3, Part 10 and Title 11, Chapter 8.
tn:SB 2528.summary: Expands the permitted uses of money in the Ocoee River recreation and economic development fund and replaces the park manager seat on the fund's board with the director of the division of state parks.

tn:SB 254.title: Criminal Procedure - As enacted, requires a defendant who is ordered to wear a transdermal monitoring device or alternative device, including other alternative alcohol or drug monitoring device, or global positioning monitoring device, as a condition of pretrial release, and who has not been determined by the court to be indigent, to pay all fees associated with the installation, monitoring, maintenance, and operation of the device. - Amends TCA Title 38; Title 39; Title 40 and Title 55.
tn:SB 254.summary: Requires a defendant ordered to wear an alcohol, drug or GPS monitoring device as a condition of pretrial release, and not found indigent, to pay all fees for installing, monitoring, maintaining and operating it.

tn:SB 2557.title: Insurance, Health, Accident - As enacted, authorizes a health insurance entity to offer a short-term limited-duration plan and hospital indemnity coverage on the marketplace. - Amends TCA Title 3; Title 4; Title 5; Title 6; Title 7; Title 8; Title 10; Title 12; Title 29; Title 35; Title 36; Title 37; Title 39; Title 40; Title 41; Title 42; Title 45; Title 47; Title 49; Title 50; Title 52; Title 53; Title 56; Title 58; Title 63; Title 67; Title 68 and Title 71.
tn:SB 2557.summary: As enacted, allows health insurers to offer short-term limited-duration plans, with a deductible up to $10,000 and a $1 million per-person maximum benefit, and tiered hospital indemnity coverage on Tennessee's federal insurance marketplace.

tn:SB 2614.title: County Government - As enacted, authorizes a county legislative body operating under the County Purchasing Law of 1957 to set the compensation for the director of accounts and budgets. - Amends TCA Title 5 and Title 8.
tn:SB 2614.summary: Lets a county legislative body operating under the County Purchasing Law of 1957 set the pay of the county's director of accounts and budgets.

tn:SB 2633.title: Taxes - As enacted, adds to the definition of a "qualified public use facility" as used in the Local Tourism Development Zone Business Tax Act a mixed-use development containing a performance venue with a seating capacity of at least 2,500; authorizes a municipality or public authority that has financed a qualified public use facility within a tourism development zone and that qualifies for an allocation of sales tax revenue from within that zone under the Convention Center and Tourism Development Financing Act of 1998 and under other provisions of sales tax law to use the revenue for purposes authorized in the act or other law. - Amends TCA Title 7 and Title 67.
tn:SB 2633.summary: Revises the tourism development zone "qualified public use facility" definition to cover mixed-use developments with a 2,500-seat performance venue or a 10-field sports facility at $200 million or more, and apportions certain venue sales tax revenue to retire its original debt.

tn:SB 2640.title: DUI Offenses - As enacted, clarifies present law regarding the revocation of a person's driver license for an implied consent violation. - Amends TCA Section 55-10-407.
tn:SB 2640.summary: Sets the driver license suspension for refusing an implied consent test at one year and six months for anyone with no prior DUI conviction, rather than one year in some cases; takes effect January 1, 2027.

tn:SB 2646.title: Industrial Development - As enacted, revises law relative to industrial development corporations. - Amends TCA Title 7 and Title 48.
tn:SB 2646.summary: As enacted, lets an industrial development corporation's board initiate a merger, and changes approval steps for payments in lieu of taxes: letters of support or notice to local chief executives, with legislative body approval in some cases.

tn:SB 2658.title: Utilities, Utility Districts - As enacted, authorizes, during a state of emergency that is based on a natural emergency, an emergency utility worker to travel upon public roads and enter areas subject to curfew or restricted access orders when such access is necessary to perform emergency utilities restoration activities; provides that an emergency utility worker, and the emergency utility worker's employer, are immune from civil liability for injury, death, or property damage resulting from an act or omission of the emergency utility worker committed in good faith while engaged in emergency utilities restoration activities during a state of emergency declared that is based on a natural emergency. - Amends TCA Title 4; Title 29; Title 39 and Title 58.
tn:SB 2658.summary: Lets emergency utility workers travel public roads and enter curfew or restricted areas to restore service during a governor-declared natural emergency, gives them and employers immunity for good-faith acts except willful misconduct or gross negligence, and adds them to assault-on-first-responder law.

tn:SB 539.title: Taxes, Real Property - As enacted, establishes the process for property tax assessment and valuation of multi-unit rental housing that receives a federal, state, or local incentive based on low-income renter restrictions. - Amends TCA Title 7; Title 13; Title 48; Title 49; Title 67 and Title 68.
tn:SB 539.summary: Sets how multi-unit rental housing with government-restricted, low-income rents is valued for property tax: net operating income, adjusted for restricted rents, excluding housing tax credits. Applies to projects developed on or after July 1, 2026, where a local government adopts it.

tn:SB 599.title: State Government - As enacted, terminates the James K. Polk Memorial Association and requires the Tennessee historical commission to enter into good faith negotiations for the purchase and transfer of the James K. Polk Home in Columbia.  - Amends TCA Title 4.
tn:SB 599.summary: Ends the James K. Polk Memorial Association and directs the Tennessee Historical Commission to negotiate in good faith to buy the James K. Polk Home in Columbia, hold title, and report annually.

tn:SB 677.title: Education, Dept. of - As enacted, requires the department to provide at least one professional development course that provides asynchronous instruction on the use of artificial intelligence in the classroom and that is made available, at no cost, to teachers in grades 6-12; requires such teachers to complete at least one department-approved professional development course on the use of artificial intelligence in the classroom by the later of August 1, 2028, or within two years of becoming licensed as a teacher in this state. - Amends TCA Title 49.
tn:SB 677.summary: Requires the education department to offer a free online course on using artificial intelligence in the classroom, and requires grade 6-12 teachers to complete an approved course by August 1, 2028 or within two years of licensure, whichever is later.

tn:SB 821.title: Education, Curriculum - As enacted, establishes a pilot program that provides grants to local education agencies to advance substance abuse and violence prevention programs. - Amends TCA Title 49.
tn:SB 821.summary: Creates a three-year pilot giving grants of up to $13,300 to three local school systems for substance abuse and violence prevention instruction in grades 3-12, with annual effectiveness reports to state departments and legislative committees.

tn:SB 879.title: Human Services, Dept. of - As enacted, requires the commissioner to provide the commissioner of correction with a form application for food assistance for use by inmates who are preparing for release. - Amends TCA Title 71, Chapter 5, Part 3.
tn:SB 879.summary: As enacted, requires the human services commissioner to give the correction commissioner a food assistance application for inmates preparing for release, with an option to decline. Requires the correction department to distribute and collect forms and report annually.

tx:HB 1.title: Relating to youth camp emergency plans and preparedness; authorizing penalties.
tx:HB 1.summary: Requires youth camps to adopt state-approved emergency plans, install weather-alert radios and warning systems, follow campground safety rules, and meet minimum camper-to-counselor ratios set by rule.

tx:HB 16.title: Relating to the operation and administration of and practices and procedures related to proceedings in the judicial branch of state government, including court security, court documents and arrest warrants, document delivery, juvenile boards, constitutional amendment election challenges, record retention, youth diversion, court-ordered mental health services, the powers of the Texas Supreme Court, jurors, and the special prosecution unit; increasing a criminal penalty; authorizing fees.
tx:HB 16.summary: Creates new district courts, revises court administration, juvenile boards, jurors, youth diversion and court-ordered mental health services, and raises penalties for harassing a court employee (Class A misdemeanor) or judge (state jail felony).

tx:HB 18.title: Relating to a restriction on the acceptance of political contributions and the making of certain political expenditures by a member of the legislature and certain political committees during certain periods in which a member is absent from a legislative session; authorizing a civil penalty.
tx:HB 18.summary: As amended, bars a legislator, and a specific-purpose committee or caucus supporting them, from accepting over the per diem from one contributor or paying travel, food or lodging costs during an unexcused out-of-state absence after arrest warrants issue. Civil penalty up to $5,000.

tx:HB 192.title: Relating to the funding of law enforcement agencies in certain counties.
tx:HB 192.summary: Expands the voter-approval requirement for law enforcement funding cuts in counties over 3.3 million people to cover budget amendments and reallocation of unspent funds or position funding, and bars those counties from moving sheriff and constable appropriations to general revenue or restricting their use.

tx:HB 20.title: Relating to measures to prevent and reduce fraudulent charitable solicitations and theft during declared disasters, including establishing a designation program for disaster relief nonprofit organizations and financial institutions; creating a criminal offense; increasing a criminal penalty.
tx:HB 20.summary: Creates a secretary of state program for political subdivisions to designate a nonprofit or financial institution to accept disaster relief donations, makes fraudulent disaster solicitation a felony, and lets prevailing donors or donees recover 300 percent of donations collected plus attorney's fees.

tx:HB 22.title: Relating to the authority of the comptroller to provide funding for the deployment and operation of certain emergency communication equipment.
tx:HB 22.summary: Expands uses of the state broadband infrastructure fund to pay for early warning and emergency notification systems and interoperable emergency communication equipment, including operating costs.

tx:HB 23.title: Relating to the exemption from ad valorem taxation of property owned by certain nonprofit corporations, located in a populous county, and used to promote agriculture, support youth, and provide educational support in the community.
tx:HB 23.summary: Exempts from property tax real and personal property owned by certain nonprofits in counties of 3.3 million or more that promote agriculture, support youth and provide educational support.

tx:HB 25.title: Relating to a pharmacist's authority to dispense ivermectin without a prescription.
tx:HB 25.summary: Allows pharmacists to dispense ivermectin without a prescription under Board of Pharmacy protocols, shields a pharmacist acting in a reasonably prudent manner from criminal liability and professional discipline, and lets the Texas State Board of Pharmacy adopt rules.

tx:HB 26.title: Relating to contracting with law enforcement agencies in certain counties.
tx:HB 26.summary: Allows sheriffs and constables in counties of more than 3.3 million people to contract with local governments, property owners' associations or landowners to provide law enforcement services, without county commissioners court approval.

tx:HB 265.title: Relating to governmental oversight of youth camps, including youth camp rules, duties, and the advisory committee.
tx:HB 265.summary: Changes youth camp law: makes the advisory committee 11 members with set expertise, requires annual criminal and sex-offender checks for adult staff and volunteers with unsupervised camper contact and CPR and first aid training for adult staff, and repeals waiver provisions.

tx:HB 27.title: Relating to a groundwater study of certain aquifers underlying the territory of the Neches and Trinity Valleys Groundwater Conservation District by the Texas Water Development Board before the issuance of permits or permit amendments by the district.
tx:HB 27.summary: Requires the Texas Water Development Board to study the effects of groundwater pumping on aquifers under the Neches and Trinity Valleys district and report. Pauses new district permits to produce and export groundwater until 270 days after the report is due.

tx:HB 4.title: Relating to the composition of the districts for the election of members of the United States House of Representatives from the State of Texas.
tx:HB 4.summary: Replaces the 2021 map of Texas's U.S. House districts with the map in plan PLANC2333, with one member elected from each district.

tx:HB 7.title: Relating to prohibitions on the manufacture and provision of abortion-inducing drugs, including the jurisdiction of and effect of certain judgments by courts within and outside this state with respect to the manufacture and provision of those drugs, and to protections from certain counteractions under the laws of other states and jurisdictions; authorizing qui tam actions.
tx:HB 7.summary: Bars manufacturing or distributing abortion-inducing drugs in Texas, and mailing, delivering, prescribing or providing them to or from any person or location in Texas, with exceptions. Only private persons may enforce it, through qui tam civil actions.

tx:HB 8.title: Relating to public school accountability and transparency, including the implementation of an instructionally supportive assessment program and the adoption and administration of assessment instruments in public schools, indicators of achievement, public school performance ratings, and interventions and sanctions under the public school accountability system, a grant program for school district local accountability plans, and actions challenging Texas Education Agency decisions related to public school accountability.
tx:HB 8.summary: Replaces STAAR testing with an instructionally supportive assessment program by 2027-2028, changes how school performance ratings are determined, and limits legal challenges to Texas Education Agency accountability decisions, including a nine-month deadline to sue over rules.

tx:HCR 13.title: Urging the federal government to take immediate action to curb the spread of the New World screwworm in Texas.
tx:HCR 13.summary: Urges the federal government to act against the New World screwworm, including working with Mexico, expediting the planned control facility at Moore Air Force Base, and speeding FDA approval of treatments and EPA approval of pesticides.

tx:HR 128.title: Amending the House Rules of Procedure to authorize additional constitutionally compliant, proportional penalties for members absent without leave for purpose of impeding the action of the House that do not unfairly impair members' representative functions.
tx:HR 128.summary: Raises the daily fine for members absent without leave to impede the House from $500 to three times the legislative per diem; adds operating-budget forfeiture, loss of chair posts after two days and seniority cuts after three, unless the House excuses.

tx:HR 174.title: Suspending limitations on conference committee jurisdiction, S.B. No. 5.
tx:HR 174.summary: Suspends House rules so the conference committee on Senate Bill 5 can add camp-safety funding for the Department of State Health Services, contingent on S.B. 1 ($2.59 million stabilization fund, $2.48 million general revenue), and an immediate effective date.

tx:HR 177.title: Creating a general investigating committee on disaster response.
tx:HR 177.summary: Creates a five-member House investigating committee on disaster response to examine the 2025 flooding disasters, including causes, preparedness and response resources, and coordination among local, state and federal agencies, with general investigating committee powers.

tx:SB 1.title: Relating to campground and youth camp safety.
tx:SB 1.summary: Bars licensing youth camps with floodplain cabins, with exceptions; requires campgrounds to put roof-access ladders in floodplain cabins and keep evacuation plans; requires youth camps to follow campground rules plus emergency plans, weather radios and warning systems.

tx:SB 10.title: Relating to the calculation of the voter-approval tax rate for certain taxing units.
tx:SB 10.summary: Under the conference committee report, lowers the voter-approval property tax rate multiplier from 1.035 to 1.025 for taxing units other than special taxing units and cities or counties under 75,000 people.

tx:SB 11.title: Relating to an affirmative defense to prosecution for certain victims of trafficking of persons or compelling prostitution.
tx:SB 11.summary: Creates an affirmative defense to prosecution for trafficking or compelling-prostitution victims whose charged conduct resulted directly from force, fraud or coercion, excluding certain serious offenses unless the person is charged only as a party.

tx:SB 12.title: Relating to the duty of the attorney general to prosecute criminal offenses prescribed by the election laws of this state.
tx:SB 12.summary: Gives the attorney general jurisdiction to prosecute Election Code crimes, and requires law enforcement to send the attorney general probable-cause reports and local prosecutors to provide requested investigation information.

tx:SB 14.title: Relating to the provision by a political subdivision of credits against impact fees to builders and developers for certain water conservation and reuse projects.
tx:SB 14.summary: Requires cities and other political subdivisions to give builders and developers a credit against water and wastewater impact fees for facilities, systems or products that conserve or reuse water.

tx:SB 16.title: Relating to real property theft and real property fraud; establishing recording requirements for certain documents concerning real property; creating the criminal offenses of real property theft and real property fraud and establishing a statute of limitations, restitution, and certain procedures with respect to those offenses.
tx:SB 16.summary: Creates the felonies of real property theft and real property fraud, with higher penalties for elderly, disabled or nonprofit owners and homesteads, adds restitution and recording procedures, and sets a 10-year limitations period for both.

tx:SB 18.title: Relating to an exemption from the requirement to obtain a permit from the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality for certain dams or reservoirs operated and maintained for the purposes of erosion, floodwater, and sediment control.
tx:SB 18.summary: Exempts districts and authorities that serve as federal Natural Resources Conservation Service local sponsors from needing a state permit to build or maintain dams or reservoirs of up to 200 acre-feet for flood and erosion control on their land, or to divert water for repairs.

tx:SB 3.title: Relating to outdoor warning sirens in flash flood-prone areas.
tx:SB 3.summary: Requires cities and counties to install, operate and test outdoor warning sirens in flood-prone areas covered by the July 2025 Hill Country flood declaration that a state board identifies, and creates a governor's grant program for installation costs.

tx:SB 5.title: Relating to making supplemental appropriations for disaster relief and preparedness and giving direction and adjustment authority regarding those appropriations.
tx:SB 5.summary: Appropriates $200 million from the economic stabilization fund for disaster response and federal matching, $50 million for local flood siren and gauge grants in 30 counties, and $28 million for forecasting grants, plus contingent camp safety funding.

tx:SB 8.title: Relating to the designation and use of certain spaces and facilities according to sex; authorizing a civil penalty and a private civil right of action.
tx:SB 8.summary: Tables an amendment that would strike the bill's provisions barring courts from blocking its enforcement or certifying classes, and making parties who seek such court orders pay the other side's costs and attorney fees.

us:H.J.Res. 72.title: Relating to a national emergency by the President on February 1, 2025
us:H.J.Res. 72.summary: Terminates the national emergency declared by the President on February 1, 2025 in Executive Order 14193, under the National Emergencies Act.

us:H.R. 1834.title: Breaking the Gridlock Act
us:H.R. 1834.summary: Extends the enhanced premium tax credit for health insurance marketplace coverage, including for households above 400 percent of the poverty line, for tax years 2026 through 2028.

us:H.R. 33.title: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to provide special rules for the taxation of certain residents of Taiwan with income from sources within the United States
us:H.R. 33.summary: Creates special U.S. tax rules for qualified residents of Taiwan, replacing the 30 percent rate on certain U.S.-source interest, dividends and royalties with 10 percent, or 10 to 15 percent for dividends.

us:H.R. 4275.title: Coast Guard Authorization Act
us:H.R. 4275.summary: Authorizes funding and personnel levels for the Coast Guard and changes its organization, acquisition oversight, shipping and navigation, oil pollution response, and sexual assault response rules.

us:H.R. 6703.title: Lower Health Care Premiums for All Americans Act
us:H.R. 6703.summary: Allows employer groups to form association health plans, changes treatment of stop-loss insurance and health reimbursement arrangements, adds oversight of pharmacy benefit managers, and funds cost-sharing reduction payments from 2027.

us:H.Res. 1142.title: Providing for disposition of the Senate amendment to the bill (H.R. 7147) Department of Homeland Security Appropriations Act, 2026
us:H.Res. 1142.summary: Provides for the House to concur in the Senate amendment to H.R. 7147, further consolidated appropriations for fiscal year 2026, with an amendment consisting of the text of Rules Committee Print 119-21.

us:H.Res. 1299.title: Providing for the concurrence by the House in the Senate amendment to H.R. 6644, with amendment
us:H.Res. 1299.summary: Has the House concur in the Senate amendment to H.R. 6644 with a House amendment, the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, covering housing supply, manufactured housing, community banks, limits on large investors buying single-family homes, and a Federal Reserve digital currency ban through 2030.

us:H.Res. 1399.title: Directing the Committee on Ethics to preserve and publicly release records relating to monetary settlements involving acts of sexual harassment
us:H.Res. 1399.summary: Directs the House Ethics Committee and Office of Congressional Workplace Rights to publish, within 60 days, a list of Members who were subjects of reviews involving sexual harassment that led to taxpayer-funded payments, with amounts, plus aggregate settlement totals.

us:H.Res. 488.title: Denouncing the antisemitic terrorist attack in Boulder, Colorado
us:H.Res. 488.summary: Condemns the June 2025 Boulder, Colorado attack, affirms the need for communication between state, local and federal law enforcement, and thanks law enforcement officers including ICE personnel.

us:H.Res. 566.title: On Agreeing to the Amendment
us:H.Res. 566.summary: Amends the House rule for considering the Senate amendment to H.R. 1 to add that the previous question is considered ordered on the motion to concur, without intervening motion; the rule also sets one hour of debate.

us:H.Res. 888.title: Censuring and condemning Delegate Stacey Plaskett and removing her from the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence for conduct that reflects discreditably on the House of Representatives for colluding with convicted felony sex offender Jeffrey Epstein during a congressional hearing
us:H.Res. 888.summary: As introduced, censures Delegate Stacey Plaskett over alleged coordination with Jeffrey Epstein during a February 2019 hearing, removes her from the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, and directs the Ethics Committee to investigate.

us:S.J.Res. 82.title: S. J. Res. 82; A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Office of the Secretary of the Department of Health and Human Services relating to "Policy on Adhering to the Text of the Administrative Procedure Act".
us:S.J.Res. 82.summary: Nullifies the Department of Health and Human Services rule that rescinds the department's policy of using public notice-and-comment rulemaking beyond what the Administrative Procedure Act requires (the Richardson Waiver).

us:S.Res. 412.title: S.Res. 412; An executive resolution authorizing the en bloc consideration in Executive Session of certain nominations on the Executive Calendar.
us:S.Res. 412.summary: Allows the Senate to move to consider 108 named executive nominations together in a single vote, instead of one at a time.

us:S.Res. 532.title: S.Res. 532; An executive resolution authorizing the en bloc consideration in Executive Session of certain nominations on the Executive Calendar.
us:S.Res. 532.summary: Allows the Senate to move to consider 97 named executive nominations together in a single vote, instead of one at a time.

ut:HB 101.title: Firearm Background Check Amendments
ut:HB 101.summary: Exempts sales of National Firearms Act firearms from the state criminal background check within 30 days after ATF approves the transfer application, and clarifies that transfers of firearms to a federal firearms licensee need no state background check.

ut:HB 102.title: Victim Privacy Amendments
ut:HB 102.summary: Lets a crime victim request that initials replace the victim's name in publicly available criminal justice documents, while requiring entities to give the name in response to a court order.

ut:HB 103.title: Underage Marriage Amendments
ut:HB 103.summary: Creates third-degree felonies for an adult unlawfully marrying a minor, transporting a Utah minor out of state for a marriage invalid in Utah, and traveling out of state to marry a minor; prosecution allowed until 15 years after the minor turns 18.

ut:HB 110.title: Offender Modifications
ut:HB 110.summary: Lets courts order Adult Probation and Parole to supervise class B misdemeanants it agrees to supervise, adds parole-board considerations after revoked paroles, and sets waiting periods of 10 or 20 years before pardon consideration for registered sex offenders.

ut:HB 111.title: Wildlife Amendments
ut:HB 111.summary: Changes wildlife laws, including creating a Poaching Mitigation Fund from restitution money, providing for grizzly bear management, and changing definitions, fees and limits for guides and outfitters.

ut:HB 113.title: Emergency Reporting Abuse Amendments
ut:HB 113.summary: Expands the offense of emergency reporting abuse to cover contacting 911 when the caller knows or should know no emergency or crime exists, and adds new penalties.

ut:HB 118.title: Driver Training Schools for Commercial Driver License Amendments
ut:HB 118.summary: Requires commercial driver license applicants to sign a form attesting to their English language ability, and requires reporting on commercial driver training schools.

ut:HB 122.title: Pregnant and Postpartum Inmate Amendments
ut:HB 122.summary: Requires prisons and jails to report numbers of pregnant inmates and inmate parents, sets a 12-week postpartum period, bars restraints then without an individualized security finding, and extends social worker and postpartum care access to 12 weeks.

ut:HB 123.title: Sex, Kidnap, and Child Abuse Offender Registration Amendments
ut:HB 123.summary: Clarifies that anyone who committed an offense in another jurisdiction that would require registration on Utah's Sex, Kidnap, and Child Abuse Offender Registry must register in Utah.

ut:HB 125.title: Department of Natural Resources Related Modifications Amendments
ut:HB 125.summary: Changes Department of Natural Resources laws on invasive-species rules for boats, water rights records, secondary water metering loans, and the duties and board of the Utah Geological Survey.

ut:HB 128.title: Traffic Amendments
ut:HB 128.summary: Removes the requirement to signal a turn while driving through a roundabout.

ut:HB 134.title: Offender Transfer Amendments
ut:HB 134.summary: Changes the fee for people on probation or parole seeking transfer to another state, requires Adult Probation and Parole supervision before transfer, and requires arrest warrants for out-of-state supervisees to be entered in the national crime database.

ut:HB 136.title: Unlicensed Driver Amendments
ut:HB 136.summary: Changes when police must impound vehicles driven without a valid license, permit or driving privilege card, modifies related fees and penalties, and changes administrative license suspension rules.

ut:HB 137.title: Violent Crime Clearance Rate Amendments
ut:HB 137.summary: Creates the Violent Crime Clearance Rate Fund, administered by the State Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice, to award grants to law enforcement agencies for solving violent crimes.

ut:HB 139.title: Female Genital Mutilation Amendments
ut:HB 139.summary: Repeals the Department of Health and Human Services' duty to run a community education program on female genital mutilation and removes the statute of limitations for prosecuting the offense.

ut:HB 153.title: Law Enforcement Officer Employment Amendments
ut:HB 153.summary: Requires municipalities, before discharging, demoting or suspending over two days a law enforcement officer, to notify the officer of the allegations, allow at least two business days for a written reply, and give an opportunity to be heard.

ut:HB 158.title: Unlawful Tracking Amendments
ut:HB 158.summary: Renames and broadens the tracking offense to cover tracking devices placed on personal property and tracking applications, including use after consent is revoked, and requires statutory damages if a victim elects them.

ut:HB 16.title: Solar Power Plant Amendments
ut:HB 16.summary: Sets state incentive eligibility based on land characteristics for utility-scale solar plants, reduces incentives on certain protected farmland, and requires wildlife consultation, decommissioning plans with financial assurance, and a permit process with site plan approval.

ut:HB 164.title: Health Care Patient Reporting to the Division of Professional Licensing
ut:HB 164.summary: Requires health care providers who receive a report of possible unprofessional or unlawful conduct to explain how to report to the Division of Professional Licensing, and makes patient nondisclosure clauses valid only if the division's model notice was given first.

ut:HB 178.title: School Zone Speeding Amendments
ut:HB 178.summary: Removes the provision for compensatory service observing a crossing guard as a penalty for a speeding conviction in a school zone.

ut:HB 179.title: Milk Amendments
ut:HB 179.summary: Sets rules for raw milk and raw milk products, including labeling, foodborne illness outbreaks, cease and desist orders, penalties, and an exemption from certain dairy regulations.

ut:HB 185.title: Carbon Credit Amendments
ut:HB 185.summary: Creates the Carbon Credit Litigation Fund, requires state entities that sell or exchange carbon credits to report, and requires the state auditor to report on those sales to a legislative appropriations subcommittee.

ut:HB 187.title: Water Amendments
ut:HB 187.summary: Exempts certain lower-basin water rights of water conservancy districts from abandonment or forfeiture for nonuse and prohibits certain instream flow change applications related to the lower Colorado River basin.

ut:HB 190.title: Child Care Business Tax Credit
ut:HB 190.summary: Expands the employer-provided child care income tax credit to off-site child care facilities, increases the credit for certain small employers, and removes the requirement to have claimed a construction credit first.

ut:HB 192.title: Vehicle Inspection Fee Amendments
ut:HB 192.summary: Removes the statutory cap on labor fees that safety inspection stations may charge and allows a reasonable fee for safety inspections.

ut:HB 195.title: Precious Metals Amendments
ut:HB 195.summary: Requires the state treasurer to continue a precious metals study for two more years and to seek proposals for a precious metals-backed electronic payment system, with annual reports to a legislative committee.

ut:HB 2.title: New Fiscal Year Supplemental Appropriations
ut:HB 2.summary: Adjusts fiscal year 2027 appropriations for state agencies, higher education and other purposes, authorizes full-time employment levels for internal service funds, and includes intent language.

ut:HB 204.title: Higher Education Student Belief Accommodation
ut:HB 204.summary: Broadens the requirement that higher education institutions reasonably accommodate students' sincerely held religious and conscience beliefs, adds notification and review steps, and requires the Board of Higher Education to adopt policies.

ut:HB 209.title: Voting Amendments
ut:HB 209.summary: Sets a process for election officers to find a registered voter is not a citizen, barring them from voting unless they successfully dispute it; from November 1, 2026, voters not giving proof of citizenship may vote only in federal races.

ut:HB 214.title: Firearms Liability Amendments
ut:HB 214.summary: Narrows the exceptions to limits on civil claims against firearm and accessory sellers, manufacturers and trade associations, requires claims to plead facts with particularity, awards fees to defendants who win dismissal, and bars local governments from imposing civil liability for criminal misuse.

ut:HB 217.title: Stolen Vehicle Amendments
ut:HB 217.summary: Bars local governments from restricting a person's ability to report a vehicle theft and sets when they must accept reports of stolen vehicles subject to a rental agreement.

ut:HB 220.title: Public Safety Data Amendments
ut:HB 220.summary: Moves several public safety data reports, including on attempted firearm purchases and sexual assaults in detention, from an interim committee to the State Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice's public safety portal, and requires colleges to report student housing crime data.

ut:HB 221.title: Coercion Amendments
ut:HB 221.summary: Creates the offense of aiding or encouraging suicide, splits sexual extortion and aggravated sexual extortion into separate offenses, makes them eligible as domestic violence offenses, and requires mandatory fines for these convictions.

ut:HB 230.title: Offender Amendments
ut:HB 230.summary: Requires county jails to help certain inmates obtain a current driver license or ID, Corrections to provide post-incarceration housing information and an attorney communication portal, and treatment programs to share drug test results with supervising officers.

ut:HB 238.title: Utah Energy Generation and Transmission Planning
ut:HB 238.summary: Requires the Public Service Commission to participate in regional transmission organizations where Utah utilities are members, allows it to contract for market analysis, requires annual reports to the Legislature, and requires community clean energy program notices to include a simple opt-out.

ut:HB 24.title: Criminal Penalty Amendments
ut:HB 24.summary: Reduces speeding 21 to 29 mph in a school zone and careless driving from class C misdemeanors to infractions, and merges the offenses of driving without vehicle security and failing to carry proof of it.

ut:HB 240.title: Carbon Dioxide System Amendments
ut:HB 240.summary: Requires licensing of businesses that service carbon dioxide systems and certification of most individuals who do so, through the state fire marshal, with rules and fees set by the Utah Fire Prevention Board.

ut:HB 243.title: Gambling Revisions
ut:HB 243.summary: Clarifies that a proposition bet falls within the legal definition of gambling.

ut:HB 247.title: Great Salt Lake Related Amendments
ut:HB 247.summary: Changes the brine shrimp royalty tax rate, sends its revenue to the Sovereign Lands Management Account in certain cases, adjusts severance tax calculations for Great Salt Lake extraction operators, and deposits certain judgment and settlement proceeds into that account.

ut:HB 250.title: Utah Retirement Plan Exchange
ut:HB 250.summary: Directs the state treasurer's office to run a public online exchange where eligible private employers can compare and choose retirement plans, with a listing process for plan providers and annual provider reports.

ut:HB 251.title: Diligence Claims Water Amendments
ut:HB 251.summary: Creates a rebuttable presumption of a right to use certain water tied to a homestead parcel, sets how it can be rebutted, and clarifies how diligence claims are submitted.

ut:HB 259.title: Parental Access to Children's Medical Records Amendments
ut:HB 259.summary: Gives parents the right to access a child's medical record, requires health care facilities and electronic record vendors to provide parental access unless exceptions apply, and lets the attorney general bring enforcement actions.

ut:HB 261.title: Electronic Information Privacy Act Amendments
ut:HB 261.summary: Changes rules for law enforcement access to electronic information, makes the act's procedures the only permitted methods, bars using third parties to get data the agency could not get directly, and applies evidence exclusion rules to violations.

ut:HB 269.title: Ambulance Provider Payment Amendments
ut:HB 269.summary: Adjusts Medicaid ambulance rates, lets the Bureau of Emergency Medical Services adjust the base rate yearly, includes medicine costs in the base rate, and repeals sunset dates.

ut:HB 270.title: Healthcare Worker Post-Employment Amendments
ut:HB 270.summary: Makes void non-compete agreements between employers and healthcare workers, and voids certain nonsolicitation agreements between a person and a healthcare worker.

ut:HB 271.title: Multi-Agency Joint Strike Force Modifications
ut:HB 271.summary: Adds metal theft to the crimes addressed by the multi-agency joint strike force and requires an annual report on catalytic converter thefts and arrests to the Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice.

ut:HB 274.title: Sentencing Amendments
ut:HB 274.summary: Changes Sentencing Commission membership, directs it to weigh set objectives and to revise adult guidelines for certain offenses before November 1, 2026, and changes what courts must consider at sentencing.

ut:HB 276.title: Artificial Intelligence Modifications
ut:HB 276.summary: Bars generation services and platforms from distributing counterfeit intimate images without verified consent, creates civil liability, and requires large platforms to preserve content provenance data and AI providers to include disclosures in AI-generated content.

ut:HB 284.title: Murder Offense Amendments
ut:HB 284.summary: Clarifies that murder committed with depraved indifference to human life does not require specific intent to kill a particular person.

ut:HB 289.title: Child Sexual Abuse Material Amendments
ut:HB 289.summary: Creates offenses for possessing or distributing AI-generated "apparent" child sexual abuse material depicting realistic minors, and for producing or distributing obscene child sexual abuse material, and removes artificially generated material from the existing definition.

ut:HB 290.title: Child Tax Credit Amendments
ut:HB 290.summary: Raises the income thresholds at which the individual income tax credit for child dependents phases out.

ut:HB 291.title: Security and Land Restriction Amendments
ut:HB 291.summary: Lowers the ownership percentage at which an entity counts as a restricted foreign entity, has Public Safety send letters requiring proof within 30 days that an entity is not one, and allows daily fines for nonresponse.

ut:HB 296.title: Water Commitment Amendments
ut:HB 296.summary: Allows a water provider's conservation plan to include a commitment of available water to uses on the Great Salt Lake.

ut:HB 3.title: Appropriations Adjustments
ut:HB 3.summary: Adjusts state appropriations for fiscal years 2026 and 2027, increasing and decreasing budgets for state agencies, public and higher education, and funding bills with fiscal impact passed in the 2026 session.

ut:HB 30.title: Wildlife Management Area Amendments
ut:HB 30.summary: Replaces the hunting or fishing license requirement for wildlife management area access with conditions including an approved educational video, creates a Wildlife Management Area Stewardship Fund, and allows voluntary contributions and volunteer labor.

ut:HB 301.title: Drug Recodification
ut:HB 301.summary: Reorganizes and clarifies Utah laws on drugs, moving certain drug offenses from the occupations and professions title into the criminal code and updating cross references.

ut:HB 303.title: Family Court Amendments
ut:HB 303.summary: Sets factors courts weigh in awarding costs and fees in family law cases, provides a process for ordering mental health treatment in custody cases, and lets courts consider evidence of coercive control in custody and parent-time decisions.

ut:HB 307.title: Attorney Fees Amendments
ut:HB 307.summary: Changes the standard for mandatory civil attorney fee awards to claims, defenses or motions that are frivolous or lack a reasonable basis and were brought to harass, delay or abuse the process, and restates trial de novo fee awards in the same terms.

ut:HB 308.title: Homeless Services Amendments
ut:HB 308.summary: Changes homeless services law, including duties of the Office of Homeless Services, letting providers temporarily exceed a congregate shelter's bed limit under conditions, and changing local tax revenue distributions for shelters.

ut:HB 311.title: Elections Study
ut:HB 311.summary: Directs Utah Valley University institutes to study the security of in-person versus mail voting and best practices for requiring ID at ballot drop boxes, and present findings to a legislative committee.

ut:HB 312.title: School Curriculum and Standards Modifications
ut:HB 312.summary: Changes K-12 social studies requirements, including instruction on self-governance and founding documents, teaching constitutional government and U.S. history each as two semester courses, and regular elementary social studies instruction, implemented by July 1, 2031.

ut:HB 313.title: Landscaper Certification Amendments
ut:HB 313.summary: Requires the Division of Professional Licensing to identify a specialty contractor that may do landscape work and sets continuing education requirements for licensees who do landscape work.

ut:HB 314.title: Firearm Purchase Amendments
ut:HB 314.summary: Removes the requirement that licensed firearm dealers use a Bureau of Criminal Identification form for sales and extends how long the bureau may keep background check records from 20 to 30 days.

ut:HB 318.title: Agency Fee Amendments
ut:HB 318.summary: Requires internal service fund agencies and fee agencies to give rate and fee data to the governor's budget office and legislative fiscal analyst before charging, and to report actual costs and revenue annually.

ut:HB 323.title: Solar Panel Disposal Amendments
ut:HB 323.summary: Requires solar retailers to disclose solar panel disposal rules, creates a Solar Panel Waste Restricted Account funded by assessments and a distributed generation fee, and from July 1, 2028 allows rules requiring hazardous waste analysis and proper disposal of solar panels.

ut:HB 325.title: Government Records Classification Amendments
ut:HB 325.summary: Classifies as public any record of a government entity's receipt or spending of funds, such as budgets, vouchers, grants and vendor payments, and makes private records that reveal whether a taxpayer receives a property tax exemption or relief.

ut:HB 329.title: State Employee Maternity and Leave Amendments
ut:HB 329.summary: Raises state employee postpartum recovery leave from three to six weeks, adds six weeks of paid leave for adopting a child under six, and creates a separate four-week paid foster leave.

ut:HB 331.title: Criminal Offenses Modifications
ut:HB 331.summary: Renames threat of terrorism as terrorism and extends it to completed acts, and creates offenses of unlawfully advancing foreign organizations and governments, concealing identity while committing an offense in public, and depriving religious rights, with a civil action.

ut:HB 337.title: Nicotine Product Tax Amendments
ut:HB 337.summary: Raises taxes on cigarettes, e-cigarettes and nontherapeutic nicotine devices, replaces weight-based rates on alternative nicotine products with per-pouch or percentage-of-price rates, and imposes a one-time inventory tax on cigarettes.

ut:HB 339.title: Street Medicine Amendments
ut:HB 339.summary: Requires the Department of Health and Human Services to develop a guide for street medicine providers and allows those providers to dispense and administer long-acting injectables.

ut:HB 34.title: Victim Rights Amendments
ut:HB 34.summary: Directs the Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice's executive director to designate a coordinator for victim rights committees, changes the complaint process, and requires criminal justice agencies to give the coordinator their policy for handling victim-rights complaints.

ut:HB 348.title: Dedicated Water Amendments
ut:HB 348.summary: Changes how dedicated water applications are filed and approved, bars separating them from the underlying water right, and addresses instream flow, agricultural land, state engineer reporting and lapsing of applications.

ut:HB 354.title: Rescue Tracking Equipment Offense Amendments
ut:HB 354.summary: Makes it a class B misdemeanor to destroy or impede the function of public-place rescue tracking equipment, or to interact with it knowing a false report of an emergency will result.

ut:HB 361.title: Elections Provisions Amendments
ut:HB 361.summary: Changes election procedures, including candidate nickname rules, notice requirements, declaration of candidacy periods, and, from January 1, 2027, barring a county clerk's name from ballots and return envelopes unless the clerk is a candidate.

ut:HB 369.title: Agriculture and Food Amendments
ut:HB 369.summary: Updates Department of Agriculture and Food provisions, including creating a weights and measures account, removing tattoos and the brisket as livestock brand marks and locations, letting the commissioner remove conservation district board members, and repealing farm name registration.

ut:HB 37.title: Used Oil Management Act Amendments
ut:HB 37.summary: Increases the recycling fee on lubricating oil sales beginning July 1, 2026, lets the division set the fee from July 1, 2027, and allows grant funds to pay permitted transporters in curbside used oil collection.

ut:HB 370.title: Sex Offender Oversight Amendments
ut:HB 370.summary: Requires a monitoring program for sex offenders who cannot provide a residential address, creates penalties for noncompliance, and sets duties for local law enforcement and Adult Probation and Parole, including arrest warrant procedures.

ut:HB 376.title: Land Management Funding Amendments
ut:HB 376.summary: Establishes the Utah Forest Restoration Institute with Utah State University, funds it, and has it research forest and watershed health, coordinate restoration funding with the Watershed Restoration Initiative, and monitor project results.

ut:HB 378.title: Fugitive Dust Mitigation Amendments
ut:HB 378.summary: Lets the Division of Air Quality charge aggregate operations a compliance fee for fugitive dust, lets the Air Quality Board set the amount by rule from July 1, 2028, and requires public signage at fugitive dust facilities.

ut:HB 381.title: Electric Mobility Device Amendments
ut:HB 381.summary: Bans drinking alcohol while riding an electric-assisted bicycle, requires riders under 21 to wear helmets on certain electric devices on highways, lets officers hold a minor's electric vehicle for a parent, and creates a safety course.

ut:HB 382.title: Uniform Assignment for Benefit of Creditors Amendments
ut:HB 382.summary: Enacts the Uniform Assignment for Benefit of Creditors Act, setting rules for assignees, creditor claims, distribution priority and court oversight, and repeals the existing assignment for benefit of creditors code.

ut:HB 384.title: Executive Branch Agency Amendments
ut:HB 384.summary: Clarifies that the Office of Data Privacy and oversight of state accounting and payroll sit within the Department of Government Operations, and replaces the Division of Finance director's audit of all claims with oversight of internal controls.

ut:HB 385.title: Specialized Product Sales Amendments
ut:HB 385.summary: Creates a Department of Agriculture license for specialized product retailers, requires ownership disclosure, limits e-cigarette advertising locations, and makes negligent sales of tobacco or nicotine to minors a crime.

ut:HB 389.title: Cannabis Amendments
ut:HB 389.summary: Requires industrial hemp retailers to check that buyers are 21, moves the medical cannabis program from the health department to the Department of Agriculture and Food, and lets medical cannabis pharmacies sell low-THC products.

ut:HB 401.title: Geothermal Study Amendments
ut:HB 401.summary: Directs Utah State University to study the geological and environmental impacts of geothermal energy development in the state and report to a legislative interim committee.

ut:HB 404.title: Sex-Designated Housing Amendments
ut:HB 404.summary: Lets landlords limit occupancy of single-sex housing to people of the designated biological sex and provides that doing so is not unlawful discrimination under the Utah Fair Housing Act.

ut:HB 408.title: Data Sharing Amendments
ut:HB 408.summary: Requires social media platforms to share user data in real time when users move to another platform, lets users choose which data to transfer, and requires consent before others' comments are included.

ut:HB 41.title: Construction and Fire Codes Amendments
ut:HB 41.summary: Updates the State Construction Code to current wildland-urban interface standards, delays the annual fee on high-risk wildland-urban interface property, and requires the division to share its wildfire risk mapping tool and respond to county-recommended changes.

ut:HB 410.title: Water Leasing Amendments
ut:HB 410.summary: Creates a Great Salt Lake Preservation Program and Board to lease water for the lake, sets the leasing process, and makes program appropriations nonlapsing.

ut:HB 412.title: Energy Development Planning Amendments
ut:HB 412.summary: Requires local governments to consult the Division of Wildlife Resources before approving utility-scale solar and wind power plants, sets the consultation requirements, and gives the division rulemaking authority.

ut:HB 416.title: First Responder Health Modifications
ut:HB 416.summary: Creates the Firefighter Cancer Benefit Trust Fund with a board of trustees and changes the amount of insurance premiums tax revenue transferred to the Utah State Retirement Office for certain firefighter retirement programs.

ut:HB 419.title: Environmental Legal Action Amendments
ut:HB 419.summary: Expands the definition of environmental action, which carries bond requirements, to include judicial review of certain permits issued by the Division of Oil, Gas, and Mining.

ut:HB 420.title: Municipal Office Vacancy Modifications
ut:HB 420.summary: Changes how vacancies in municipal offices are filled and how ties are broken in votes of a municipal legislative body.

ut:HB 423.title: Hit and Run and DUI Offense Amendments
ut:HB 423.summary: Increases penalties for leaving the scene of an accident for people previously convicted of that offense or DUI, creates mitigation for a negative chemical test, and changes DUI license hearing deadlines.

ut:HB 425.title: Local Government Fees Amendments
ut:HB 425.summary: Bars cities from charging the general public fees for broadband or public safety service, and towns for public safety, with exceptions; lets municipalities and counties impose transportation utility fees under set procedures, subject to referendum.

ut:HB 429.title: Special Districts Amendments
ut:HB 429.summary: Sets processes for a first-class county to withdraw from a first responder district and for a first-class county or municipality in it to withdraw from a garbage disposal district, including feasibility studies, hearings, and a freeze on the district's new debt.

ut:HB 436.title: Moderate Income Housing Infrastructure Amendments
ut:HB 436.summary: Changes what municipalities must report on moderate income housing for 2026 and gives the Transportation Commission priority consideration for certain projects where new residential units grow 2.5% or more.

ut:HB 437.title: Environmental Permitting Amendments
ut:HB 437.summary: Lets the Department of Environmental Quality and the Division of Oil, Gas, and Mining make rules for expedited review of eligible permits by certified qualified reviewers, with maximum review times, followed by a technical review and final decision.

ut:HB 447.title: Tobacco Amendments
ut:HB 447.summary: Allows remote retail sales of cigars and pipe tobacco by phone, mail or internet, with licensing, bonding and taxation of remote sellers and a criminal penalty for noncompliance.

ut:HB 448.title: Utah Schools for the Deaf and Blind Amendments
ut:HB 448.summary: Changes the mission, governance and funding relationship of the Utah Schools for the Deaf and the Blind, including how its superintendent is appointed, the State Board of Education's role, student counts and facilities.

ut:HB 454.title: Public Assistance Fraud Amendments
ut:HB 454.summary: Amends criminal provisions on obtaining public assistance, creates an offense of fraud by a person facilitating an inaccurate public assistance application, and adds it to the list of pattern of unlawful activity offenses.

ut:HB 457.title: County Governance Modifications
ut:HB 457.summary: Requires certain unincorporated islands in second-class counties to be annexed automatically by a bordering municipality unless local legislative bodies exempt them, with county notice required.

ut:HB 462.title: School Bus Internet Access
ut:HB 462.summary: Creates a grant program for rural school districts to install and operate internet connectivity on school buses, with priority criteria, long-term operation commitments and State Board of Education rules.

ut:HB 471.title: Social Services Amendments
ut:HB 471.summary: Changes Medicaid and SNAP rules, including work requirements, citizenship and verification standards, disenrollment after death or leaving the state, and limits on retroactive Medicaid eligibility, and adds reporting requirements.

ut:HB 473.title: Colorado River Authority Amendments
ut:HB 473.summary: Moves the Colorado River Authority of Utah from the governor's office to the Department of Natural Resources, changes its membership and appointment process, expands its powers, and repeals the Colorado River Authority Restricted Account.

ut:HB 474.title: Uniform Commercial Code Modifications
ut:HB 474.summary: Updates the Uniform Commercial Code, including replacing "writing" with "record," and adding rules on controllable electronic records, electronic documents of title, and security interests in related collateral.

ut:HB 475.title: Development Planning and Coordination Amendments
ut:HB 475.summary: Renames the Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity as the Governor's Office of Economic Development, changes the executive director's duties, and creates an Economic Development Council with reporting requirements.

ut:HB 48.title: Criminal and Juvenile Justice Changes
ut:HB 48.summary: Defines recidivism terms and changes the rules for provisionally housing a minor tried as an adult for aggravated murder in a secure care facility, including letting a prosecutor file a motion with the Board of Pardons and Parole.

ut:HB 481.title: Transportation Modifications
ut:HB 481.summary: Repeals the clean vehicle program, changes how standard and special group license plates are designed and issued, changes road usage charge rates, and allows flexible distribution timing for class B and C road funds.

ut:HB 492.title: Transportation, Infrastructure, and Housing Amendments
ut:HB 492.summary: Creates a State Housing Infrastructure Partnership Fund and board to lend to local governments for infrastructure that facilitates housing, and changes affordable housing infrastructure grant rules.

ut:HB 495.title: Capital Felony Case Amendments
ut:HB 495.summary: Changes procedures in death penalty cases, including appointing appellate counsel after a death sentence, rules for deciding intellectual disability, appeals of those rulings, stays of execution, and competency-to-be-executed petitions.

ut:HB 496.title: Forestry and Fire Amendments
ut:HB 496.summary: Gives the Division of Forestry, Fire, and State Lands enforcement and investigatory powers over wildland fires and heritage trees, and changes use of money from forest management cooperative agreements.

ut:HB 507.title: State Coordination of Regional and Local Economic Development Projects Amendments
ut:HB 507.summary: Bars local governments from giving incentives to large-load data centers with exceptions, creates a State Reinvestment Restricted Account and an optional county energy excise tax, and ends creation of certain reinvestment zones after January 1, 2028.

ut:HB 508.title: State Facilities Modifications
ut:HB 508.summary: Raises from $100,000 to $1.5 million the project cost for which a state entity may directly supervise facility construction, and changes capital project funding request steps, including for higher education.

ut:HB 509.title: Wetlands Study Amendments
ut:HB 509.summary: Directs the Department of Natural Resources to study wetlands in first- and second-class counties, report recommendations to a legislative committee, and restores its duty to publish wetlands land use permits.

ut:HB 51.title: Adoption Amendments
ut:HB 51.summary: Changes adoption rules for child-placing agencies, including licensing, advertising, reporting and disclosures, clarifies permissible payments and fees, and addresses birth parent consent revocation, therapy and transportation of birth mothers to Utah.

ut:HB 514.title: Utah Energy Council Amendments
ut:HB 514.summary: Creates the Utah Energy Infrastructure Service District, a state political subdivision that can own and operate energy facilities and issue revenue bonds, and expands the Utah Energy Council from five to seven members.

ut:HB 52.title: Tribal Endorsement of Utah Driver License Amendments
ut:HB 52.summary: Allows driver license and ID card applicants to request a "Federally Recognized Tribal Member" notation showing enrollment in a federally recognized tribe, without naming the specific tribe.

ut:HB 520.title: Higher Education Student Housing Study
ut:HB 520.summary: Requires a governor's office employee, with the commissioner of higher education, to study how higher education student housing affects surrounding communities and report to the Higher Education Appropriations Subcommittee.

ut:HB 536.title: Criminal Conduct on Public Lands Amendments
